# TriTrack — Development Plan

**Maintained by:** the planning session (Opus, via Cowork). This file is the
interface between planning and implementation — Claude Code reads it
directly out of this repo; nothing here should require copy-pasting a
prompt from one tool into the other.

**If you're Claude Code reading this:** see `CLAUDE.md` at the repo root
for the full convention (when to check this file, how to update task
status, where to log newly discovered scope, model selection). The short
version: find your task below, follow its spec, update its `Status` when
done, and log anything unplanned you find under that phase's
"Discovered Scope" rather than doing it silently.

**If you're the planning session reading this later:** this is the
authoritative record of what's been decided, what's in flight, and what's
still just an idea. Update task status directly from `git log`/`git diff`
against this repo rather than trusting the user's memory of what Claude
Code did — verify before marking anything Done.

---

## How to use this document

**Task results travel through `CLAUDE_DOCS/TASK_COMMS.md` (added 2026-08-29).** Every
task ends by appending its two action lists there — one for the planning session, one
for Michael — so that nothing has to be retyped from one Claude window into the other,
and so an action item does not live only in a chat log. `CLAUDE.md`'s "Reporting
results" section carries the rules, including the one that matters most: **a task with
nothing to ask still writes an entry saying so**, because a missing entry and an empty
one are otherwise the same thing.


- **Status values:** `Not started` · `In progress` · `Blocked (reason)` · `Done`
- **Model:** recommended model for the task, with a one-line reason. Tasks
  invoked via a matching `.claude/commands/<task-id>.md` file have this
  pinned automatically in that file's frontmatter — running `/<task-id>`
  in Claude Code needs no manual `/model` switch. Ad hoc work should still
  follow the recommendation here.
- **Task IDs** are `phase.task`, e.g. `3.1`. A command file for task `3.1`,
  if one exists, lives at `.claude/commands/3-1-<short-name>.md`.
- **Every command file for a remediation task must name the class the
  finding belongs to and enumerate every other site where that class could
  occur, with a verdict per site** (fixed / verified unaffected / open —
  needs its own task) — see "Fix the Class, Not the Instance" in
  `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md`. A brief that hands over only a
  reproduction, with no "where else could this shape live?" instruction, is
  an incomplete brief regardless of how the implementing session executes
  it. This binds the planning session writing the file as much as the
  session that implements it — task 10.66.
- Historical phases (0 through the current on-disk state) are summarized
  from git history for orientation, not re-litigated here — see
  `git log --oneline` for the real record. Active planning starts at the
  first phase below with tasks in it.

## Phase 4 — Tag Color Coding

**Goal:** each tag gets a user-assignable color (auto-assigned by default) so
tags are easy to visually distinguish in the Tag Database, Observation Log,
tag selector, and Main Map. Independent of Phase 3 — can be done in any order
relative to it, including first.

**Decisions locked in (2026-07-28, see design docs for full detail):**
- Color stored as `color_hex`, format `"#RRGGBB"`, validated
  `^#[A-Fa-f0-9]{6}$` on manual entry and CSV import.
- Auto-assigned round-robin from a curated colorblind-safe palette when a
  tag is created; user can override via a swatch picker, with an "advanced"
  collapsed custom-hex field for exact values.
- **Default palette** (Okabe-Ito based + extensions, 12 colors — spot-check
  actual on-device contrast against the map basemaps before finalizing,
  this list is a starting point not gospel):
  `#E69F00` orange · `#56B4E9` sky blue · `#009E73` bluish green ·
  `#D55E00` vermillion · `#0072B2` blue · `#CC79A7` reddish purple ·
  `#C9A227` gold *(darker than pure Okabe-Ito yellow for contrast/legibility
  as a filled marker)* · `#E4298C` magenta · `#017374` teal ·
  `#8B4513` brown · `#4D4D4D` dark gray *(not pure black — avoids reading as
  default UI text/icon color)* · `#6B8E23` olive
- **Main Map: per-tag color replaces the old fixed type-based colors** for
  bearing rays, estimated positions, and actual tag locations (previously
  fixed blue/darker-blue/green). Viewshed overlay is unchanged (stays fixed
  light blue — it isn't tag-specific). Shape stays the required redundant
  non-color cue (circle+line+wedge for rays, ellipse for estimates, distinct
  marker for actual locations) — this was already an open item independent
  of this feature; don't skip it.
- Map legend becomes tag-keyed (swatch + tag name, only tags with currently
  visible elements) instead of the old fixed element-type legend.

See `TriTrack_Design_Document.md` ("Map Layer Color Coding", "Map Furniture")
and `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md` (`Tags` schema, "Display Conventions")
for the full updated spec — those are the documents of record; this plan
just breaks the work into tasks.

### Task 4.1 — Schema, model, repository, palette/auto-assign logic
**Status:** Done
**Model:** Sonnet — additive schema change with a clear default, no
sync/merge/auth/algorithm work involved.
**Depends on:** nothing (first task, unblocks 4.2–4.5)

- Add `color_hex TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '<first palette color>'` to `Tags`
  via a real migration: bump `PRAGMA user_version` and `schema_version`
  (see existing migration pattern in `data/db/`), backfill any pre-existing
  rows with round-robin palette colors rather than leaving them all on the
  same default.
- Add `colorHex` to the `Tag` freezed model; regenerate `.freezed.dart`/
  `.g.dart` via `build_runner`.
- Add a small `TagColorPalette` utility (or provider) holding the 12-color
  list above and an "assign next unused color for this project's tags"
  function — used both on tag creation and on migration backfill, so the
  logic lives in one place.
- Repository create/update methods accept and persist `colorHex`; validate
  format server-side (repository layer) as well as in the UI, per the
  project's existing "bound-check on both manual entry and CSV import"
  convention.
- **Acceptance criteria:** existing tests still pass; new unit tests cover
  the migration backfill (existing tags get distinct colors, not all the
  same), the validation regex (reject malformed hex), and the
  next-unused-color assignment logic (round-robins, doesn't just always
  return the first palette color).

### Task 4.2 — Tag creation/edit UI
**Status:** Done
**Model:** Sonnet
**Depends on:** 4.1

- Add a color swatch picker to the tag add/edit form (Tag Database
  Management screen): 12 palette swatches, large touch targets (48x48pt,

  `DesignTokens.minTouchTarget` constant is 44.0, not 48.0; use 48 for

  not just a highlight color — non-color cue).
- Add a collapsed "advanced" row (matching the existing antenna-type/
  receiver-gain collapsible-advanced pattern already used elsewhere) with a
  manual hex text entry, validated live, that overrides the palette
  selection if used.
- New tags default to the next auto-assigned palette color (from 4.1)
  before the user touches anything; editing an existing tag shows its
  current color.
- **Acceptance criteria:** creating a tag without touching the color field
  still gets a valid, distinct `color_hex` persisted; manually picking a
  swatch or entering a custom hex overrides it correctly; invalid custom

### Discovered Scope

- **4.1 touched more call sites than expected.** `Tag.colorHex` is a
  required field, so every place that constructs a `Tag(...)` had to be
  updated to compile: the observation-sharing quick-add, Project Setup's
  quick-add-tag dialog, Observation Logging's quick-add-tag dialog + its
  "add new tag" sentinel, the Tag Database edit form, and CSV import. Only
  the three *repository-backed* creation flows (observation sharing
  quick-add, Project Setup quick-add, Observation Logging quick-add) got a
  real auto-assigned color via `TagRepository.nextColorHex()` — matching
  the "auto-assigned round-robin ... when a tag is created" decision.
  Two sites were placeholder-only pending their own tasks, marked with
  `// TODO(4.x)` comments in the code:
  - Tag Database's add/edit form (`tag_database_screen.dart`) — **resolved
    by 4.2** (swatch picker + auto-assign wiring now in place; TODO removed).
  - CSV import (`tag_csv_import.dart`) — still a placeholder, pending 4.5
    (parse/validate a `color_hex` column, fall back to auto-assign on
    missing/invalid values).
- `TagColorPalette.colors[0]` is not a valid Dart constant expression
  (index operator isn't constant-foldable), so a separate
  `TagColorPalette.defaultColor` constant was added for contexts needing a
  compile-time-constant default (e.g. test fixture default parameters).
- **4.2: the app's touch-target constant is `DesignTokens.minTouchTarget =
  44.0`, not 48.0** as this plan's task 4.2 entry stated. Implemented the
  swatches at 48x48 anyway (the plan's explicit number, and it only
  exceeds the app minimum) rather than silently reconciling down to 44 —
  flagging here in case the planning session wants either this plan doc's
  "48x48pt... existing standard" phrasing corrected, or the app-wide
  constant bumped to match. Non-blocking either way.
- **4.2 widget-testing gotchas worth knowing before 4.3/4.4's UI tests**
  (all hit while testing `_TagEditDialog`'s async dialog-open → fill →
  save flow — a pattern this repo's widget tests hadn't exercised before):
  - A tap whose `onPressed` does real (uncached) DB I/O — e.g.
    `TagRepository.nextColorHex()`, a fresh `rawQuery` every call, or the
    eventual `tagRepo.insert`/`update` after a dialog closes — must itself
    run *inside* `tester.runAsync()`'s real zone from the very first
    `tester.tap()` call, and every later interaction with that same async
    chain (filling fields, tapping Save, reading the result back out)
    needs to stay inside that same `runAsync` block. Splitting the tap and
    the wait across separate `runAsync` calls does not work — the async
    chain's zone is fixed at the point it started.
  - Any provider a screen reads for the first time only at save-time
    (e.g. `currentUserProvider`, `deviceIdProvider`) should be
    pre-resolved in the test's setup alongside the providers already
    watched at open-time — otherwise a fixed real-time delay before
    asserting persistence is an unreliable guess (`currentUserProvider`
    itself does a fresh DB query/user-creation on an uncached first read).
  - `pumpAndSettle()` while a `TextField` has focus can spin forever (the
    blinking cursor's timer keeps scheduling new frames) — set
    `EditableText.debugDeterministicCursor = true` in `setUp()` for any
    test that types into a field and then calls `pumpAndSettle()`, and
    still prefer a plain `pump()` over `pumpAndSettle()` immediately after
    `enterText`.
  - The dialog's content column overflows the default 800x600 test
    surface; swatches/toggles below the fold fail their hit test even
    though they're rendered — bump `tester.view.physicalSize` before
    pumping a screen with a tall dialog.
- **4.3: new shared `TagColorSwatch` widget** (`lib/widgets/tag_color_swatch.dart`)
  — a small filled circle rendering a `colorHex` value, used by all three
  4.3 call sites. `_TagEditDialog`'s own palette-picker swatch (`_Swatch`
  in `tag_database_screen.dart`, from 4.2) was left as-is rather than
  refactored onto this shared widget — it needs the larger 48x48 tap
  target, selection ring, and check-icon overlay the picker requires,
  which don't fit `TagColorSwatch`'s plain small-dot job. Worth
  reconciling later if a fourth need for a *large, selectable* swatch
  shows up, but not before.
- **4.3: `WheelPicker<T>` gained an optional `leadingBuilder: Widget?
  Function(T item)?`** (`lib/widgets/wheel_picker.dart`) so a small leading
  widget (here, a `TagColorSwatch`) can sit next to the label text,
  fading with selection distance the same as the label. Returning null
  for a given item (used for the "add new tag" sentinel) renders that
  item with no leading — existing `WheelPicker` call sites that don't
  pass `leadingBuilder` are unaffected (still label-only, no `Row`).
- **4.3 did not touch two other tag-referencing spots**, left for a future
  task/judgment call since the plan named only the three above:
  - `_NonDetectionTile` in `log_screen.dart` — a "no signal" row lists
    *multiple* tags (`tagIdsListenedFor`), so a single leading swatch
    doesn't map 1:1; would need a small stack/row of swatches instead of
    the single-swatch treatment used elsewhere.
  - The "no signal" tag multi-select `CheckboxListTile` list and the
    `WheelPicker<Tag>` in `position_estimation_screen.dart`'s tag-picker
    bottom sheet (both in Observation Logging/Position Estimation) — not
    named in this task's spec (only "the tag-selector scroll wheel" in
    Observation Logging was), but same-shaped and easy to extend with
    `leadingBuilder`/a `TagColorSwatch` leading now that both exist.
- **4.4 confirmed rendering-only, no viewshed/algorithm coupling.**
  `map_screen.dart`'s `_mapDataProvider` already carried `tag_id` on every
  observation/estimate/location row; the only new data-layer work was
  adding `colorHex` to the private `_TagRow` (mirrors `Tag.colorHex`) and
  threading it through. `TagColorSwatch`'s hex-parsing was extracted into
  a new top-level `tagColorFromHex(String)` (`lib/widgets/tag_color_swatch.dart`)
  so both the swatch widget and the map's per-element coloring share one
  parser. Viewshed's fixed color and the estimate-ellipse/observer-circle/
  bearing-wedge/actual-location shape cues were all already implemented
  pre-4.4 (circle vs. square distinguishes estimates from actual
  locations) — nothing there needed building, only re-pointing colors at
  `tag.colorHex` via a new `_tagColor(tagId, tagNames, fallback)` helper
  that falls back to the old fixed token if a tag lookup misses (dangling/
  unlinked tag_id), rather than crashing.
- **4.4: the map's fixed 4-row legend became a computed `_legendRows()`**
  — tag rows are gathered from whichever of rays/estimates/tag-locations
  are currently toggled on, respect the same per-tag visibility filter and
  time window the map layers themselves use, sorted alphabetically by tag
  name; the "Viewshed" row is appended only when `_viewshedIsRendered()`
  (a new getter factoring out the `OverlayImageLayer`'s own visibility
  check, so the two can never disagree) is true. The legend card itself
  (`MapLegendCard`) needed no changes — it already took a generic
  `List<(Color, String)>`. The legend is now hidden entirely (not just
  empty) when `legendRows` is empty, a small UX call not explicitly
  spec'd; flagging in case the planning session wants an explicit
  "nothing visible" row instead.
- **4.4 has no automated test coverage on `map_screen.dart` itself** —
  consistent with this file having *no* prior test file at all (unlike
  every other 4.x screen touched so far), almost certainly because of its
  live GPS stream / viewshed computation / real tile-layer dependencies,
  the same class of widget-testing friction documented under 4.2's
  bullet above. Coverage added instead: a `tagColorFromHex` unit test
  (exact-color-distinctness assertion, since that's the one new pure
  function underpinning all the per-element coloring) plus `flutter
  analyze` + full-suite regression. If real coverage of
  `_legendRows`/`_tagColor`/`_viewshedIsRendered` is wanted later, it'd
  need either exposing them (dropping the leading underscore) for a
  logic-only unit test, or a first real widget-test harness for
  `MapScreen` — worth scoping as its own task rather than folding into
  4.4 or a future 4.x task silently.
- **4.5's spec assumed a "tag CSV export" already existed to add a column
  to — it didn't.** Searched the codebase and both design docs
  thoroughly: the only existing tag-related CSV feature is *import* (bulk
  roster import, `TagCsvImport`/`tag_database_screen.dart`'s "Bulk import
  CSV" button). The Data Export screen's "Export CSV" exports
  *observations*/*non-detections* (with tag name/frequency looked up
  inline for spreadsheet convenience), not a standalone tag roster. Since
  the task's acceptance criteria explicitly require an export→import
  round-trip, building a minimal `TagCsvExport` (new file, mirrors the
  existing `ObservationCsv`/`NonDetectionCsv` pure-formatter pattern) was
  the smallest reasonable judgment call rather than leaving the
  acceptance criteria untestable — flagging this discrepancy for the
  planning session rather than silently treating it as pre-existing.
  Wired a new "Export tags CSV" download-icon button into
  `TagDatabaseScreen`'s app bar, next to the existing import button.
- **4.5: CSV round-robin for auto-assigned colors is index-based, not
  DB-count-based.** `TagCsvImport.preview()` is deliberately DB-free (a
  pure parse/validate step, per its own docs) so it can't call
  `TagRepository.nextColorHex()`'s live-count logic the way 4.1's UI
  auto-assign paths do. Instead, `preview()` keeps an in-memory counter
  incremented once per row that actually needed an auto-assigned color
  (valid explicit `color_hex` values don't consume a slot), giving
  distinct colors across one import batch without touching the database.
  This means a CSV import's auto-assigned colors aren't coordinated with
  colors already used by existing tags in the project — acceptable given
  the "distinct within the batch" acceptance criterion, but worth knowing
  if a future task wants cross-batch/global distinctness too.
- **Post-4.4 bug fix: editing a tag's color in Tag Database didn't update
  the Main Map live** (user report, 2026-07-29) — it updated in the Log
  screen but not the map. Root cause: `_mapDataProvider` (map_screen.dart)
  resolves each tag's name/color once via `tagRepo.findById` inside its
  own one-shot `FutureProvider` body and bakes it into `_TagRow`, rather
  than watching `allTagsProvider`; it only refetches when the shared
  `recordingsRevisionProvider` counter bumps (previously bumped only by
  observation/estimate/tag-location CRUD, never by tag edits).
  `tag_database_screen.dart`'s `_showEditDialog` and `_importCsv` now also
  call `ref.read(recordingsRevisionProvider.notifier).bump()` alongside
  their existing `ref.invalidate(allTagsProvider)`, and the provider's doc
  comment was updated to mention tag edits as a trigger. No new dedicated
  test added (matches 4.4's existing gap: `map_screen.dart` has no test
  harness at all) — verified by code inspection/reasoning only; flagging
  in case a future task wants to build the first widget-test harness for
  `MapScreen` and add regression coverage for this specific path.
- **Post-4.4 UX change: uncertainty wedges are now their own independent
  map layer** (user request, 2026-07-29), not tied to the "Bearings"
  toggle — a new `_showWedges` bool (default on) gates the wedge
  `PolygonLayer` instead of `_showRays`, with its own "Uncertainty
  wedges" row in the Layers & Filters sheet (right after "Bearings").
  `_legendRows()` was updated to count a tag as visible if *either*
  `_showRays` or `_showWedges` is on. Wedge opacity was also bumped up
  (fill 0.12→0.2 baseline, 0.22→0.35 highlighted, 0.04→0.08 dimmed;
  border 0.3→0.45, 0.08→0.14 dimmed) per explicit feedback that they read
  as too transparent. Exact opacity values were a judgment call (user
  said "a bit less transparent," not exact numbers) — revisit if still
  off.
- **4.6: `_TagSwatchStack` was promoted to a shared public widget,
  `TagColorSwatchStack`** (`lib/widgets/tag_color_swatch.dart`), rather
  than staying a private class local to `log_screen.dart` — needed so it
  could be unit-tested at all (a private class in one file's library
  can't be referenced from an external test file), and it's generic
  enough (overlapping-circle stack with a "+N" overflow cap) that another
  future multi-tag row could reuse it directly instead of re-deriving the
  same layout math.
- **4.6 acceptance criteria fully met**: `_NonDetectionTile` now shows a
  `TagColorSwatchStack` (leading) built from `tagIdsListenedFor`'s
  resolved colors; the no-signal `CheckboxListTile` multi-select list
  (Observation Logging) gets a `TagColorSwatch` via its `secondary` slot
  (the control already occupies `leading`); Position Estimation's
  `WheelPicker<Tag>` tag-picker bottom sheet gets one via the existing
  `leadingBuilder` API from 4.3 — no `WheelPicker` API changes needed,
  confirming 4.3's extension point was sufficient for every subsequent
  single-tag-per-row case. Every tag-referencing row/list in the app now
  shows a color swatch.
- **4.7: confirmed narrow scope, no ripple.** Re-ran
  `grep -rn "minTouchTarget" lib/` after the change — still only the
  `DesignTokens` definition itself and this one new `_ColorSwatchGrid`
  reference; nothing else in the app consumes the constant, so there was
  genuinely nothing else to reconcile. Added one assertion (to the
  existing "new tag defaults to..." widget test) checking a swatch's
  `Container.constraints` against `DesignTokens.minTouchTarget` directly,
  so a future hardcoded-literal regression fails a test instead of only
  a doc-comment mismatch.

## Phase 5 — Desktop (macOS) Support

**Goal:** make the macOS build actually usable. It currently compiles and
launches but is functionally broken in three ways, all discovered by
planning-session audit (2026-07-29) rather than by running it: the sandbox
blocks outbound network *and* location, the location usage-description
string was never filled in (crash risk, not just denial), and
`flutter_compass`/`sensors_plus` have no macOS implementation — with the
current `.value`-only stream listeners silently swallowing the resulting
errors, so the user sees dashes and dead buttons with no explanation.

Independent of Phase 3 and Phase 4. Not a field-deployment target — macOS
is a desk/analysis and development-convenience target (the Position
Estimation screen is already fully compass-independent and works there).

**Decisions locked in (2026-07-29):**
- **Compass-unavailable detection is capability-based, not platform-based**
  — a null `FlutterCompass.events` or an errored sensor stream means "no
  compass," on any platform. This deliberately also covers a tablet with
  no magnetometer and a phone with failed hardware; it is a behavior
  change on mobile (those cases currently show silent dashes), which is
  considered an improvement, not a regression.
- **Manual bearing entry stays magnetic-only.** No magnetic/true-north
  frame toggle. The UI must make it unmistakable that the expected input
  is a magnetic bearing from north. *(An earlier draft of this phase
  proposed a user-selectable magnetic/true frame toggle; that was
  reconsidered and dropped — it would have introduced bidirectional
  declination conversion and the exact sign-convention/circular-math trap
  flagged as a "critical bug class" in `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md`,
  for little field benefit. Keeping one frame keeps the stored
  magnetic/true pair unambiguous about which value was observed.)*
- **Position-picker fallback centering is the project extent** (`Projects`
  already stores `bbox_min/max_lat/lon`), with an explicit user-visible
  notice that the map was centered on the project extent rather than on a
  real position fix. Falls back to a wide view only if the project has no
  bbox set.

**Model note for this phase: all Sonnet.** This is config, capability
detection, input validation, and UI-state work — no algorithm,
sign-convention, or sync/merge correctness risk. Task 5.3 would have been
Opus under the earlier magnetic/true-toggle design (bidirectional
declination conversion across the 0/360 boundary); the magnetic-only
decision removed that risk. If any task turns out to require touching the
sensor-fusion math in `compass_controller.dart`'s `_recompute()` (as
opposed to its stream-listening/availability plumbing), stop and flag it
for a model re-review rather than proceeding.

### Task 5.1 — macOS sandbox entitlements + location usage description
**Status:** Done (2026-07-30)
**Model:** Sonnet — pure platform config, no Dart logic.
**Depends on:** nothing

- `macos/Runner/DebugProfile.entitlements` **and**
  `macos/Runner/Release.entitlements`: add
  `com.apple.security.network.client` (`true`). Without it a sandboxed
  macOS app cannot make outbound connections at all — map tiles,
  elevation/DEM fetches, and every `http` call fail silently. Note
  `network.server` is currently in the Debug profile only (that's for
  Flutter's dev tooling and is correct as-is); `network.client` belongs in
  both.
- Same two files: add `com.apple.security.personal-information.location`
  (`true`). Sandboxed macOS apps need this for Core Location even though
  `geolocator_apple` *is* registered for macOS.
- `macos/Runner/Info.plist`: add `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription`
  with a real user-facing string (it's currently the stock `flutter
  create` template with no location keys at all). On macOS, requesting
  location authorization with no usage-description string present can hard
  crash rather than merely being denied. Match the wording style of the
  existing iOS `Info.plist` entry for consistency.
- **Acceptance criteria:** `flutter run -d macos` launches; the Main Map
  loads online tiles; requesting location either prompts or is cleanly
  denied without crashing; `flutter analyze`/`flutter test` unaffected.
  Verify the tile load specifically — that's the entitlement most likely
  to be silently wrong.

### Task 5.2 — Capability-based "compass unavailable" state
**Status:** Done (2026-07-30) — see Discovered Scope for a deviation from
the original null/error-only design, needed once the actual plugin
behavior turned out not to match the plan's assumption.
**Model:** Sonnet — availability plumbing and UI state, not sensor-fusion
math. See the phase-level model note.
**Depends on:** nothing (independent of 5.1)

Today `compass_provider.dart:14-16` throws a `StateError` when
`FlutterCompass.events` is null, and *nothing catches it*;
`compass_controller.dart` listens with `.value`-only callbacks that
silently ignore `AsyncError`. Result on macOS: `CompassReading.initial`
forever, dashes in the UI, disabled POINT/RANGE buttons, no explanation.

- Add a single source of truth for compass availability (e.g. a
  `compassAvailableProvider`) derived from the capability check — null
  event stream or errored sensor stream ⇒ unavailable. Do **not** gate
  this on `Platform.is*`.
- **Compass screen** (`lib/features/compass/screens/compass_screen.dart`):
  when unavailable, replace the dial/readouts with a clear explanatory
  empty state — "No compass available on this device" plus a sentence
  saying bearings can still be entered manually on the Record screen, and
  a button routing there. Don't render a dead dial with dashes.
- **Record screen** (`observation_logging_screen.dart`): when unavailable,
  make manual entry the obvious path rather than a small unlabeled `✎`
  glyph — surface a visible affordance/label, and have the bearing entry
  sheet open with the **Manual entry** tab preselected (it currently
  defaults to `_manualTab = false`, i.e. Compass). The POINT/RANGE buttons
  should read as unavailable-with-reason, not merely greyed out.
- Leave the interference-warning path alone — `CompassReading.initial`
  deliberately reports `InterferenceLevel.none`/0 µT so no spurious
  warning banner appears, which is still correct when there's no sensor.
- **Acceptance criteria:** on macOS the Compass screen shows the
  explanatory state (not dashes) and the Record screen leads the user to
  manual entry with the manual tab preselected; on iOS/Android with a
  working compass nothing changes; a simulated null/errored compass stream
  produces the unavailable state rather than a silent dead UI.

### Task 5.3 — Manual bearing entry: explicit magnetic framing + input constraints
**Status:** Done (2026-07-30)
**Model:** Sonnet — input validation and copy. No declination conversion
involved (see the magnetic-only decision above).
**Depends on:** nothing

In `lib/features/observations/widgets/bearing_entry_sheet.dart`:

- Make the magnetic-only expectation unmistakable, not just a field label.
  The current `labelText: 'Bearing (° from magnetic north)'` is easy to
  miss; add clearer supporting copy (helper text / short note in the
  manual tab) stating the value must be a **magnetic** bearing measured
  clockwise from magnetic north, and that the app computes true north from
  it automatically using the position and date.
- **Fix the silent-failure validation bug.** Current behavior at
  `bearing_entry_sheet.dart:259-261` is
  `if (value == null || value < 0 || value > 360) return;` — the "USE THIS
  BEARING" button does *nothing at all* on invalid input, with no message.
  Replace with a visible inline error.
- Constrain the input to `>= 0` and `< 360`: use an input formatter so a
  minus sign can't be typed at all (digits and a single decimal point
  only), plus validation that rejects `>= 360` with an inline message, and
  normalize an entered `360` to `0`. *(The alternative — silently
  wrapping negatives, e.g. `-10` → `350` — was considered; explicit
  rejection is preferred here since a typed negative in the field is more
  likely a typo than an intended wrap, and silent correction of a bearing
  is exactly the kind of quiet error this project's conventions warn
  about. If a future field trial says otherwise, revisit.)*
- Keep manual entry's existing `captureMethod == null` semantics and the
  uncertainty slider unchanged.
- **Acceptance criteria:** typing a valid bearing works as before; invalid
  input (empty, non-numeric, `>= 360`) shows a clear inline error instead
  of a dead button; a minus sign cannot be entered; `360` is accepted and
  stored as `0`; the magnetic-bearing expectation is stated visibly in the
  manual tab, not only in the field label. Add widget tests for the
  boundary cases (`0`, `359.9`, `360`, empty, non-numeric).

### Task 5.4 — Position picker usable with no GPS fix
**Status:** Done (2026-07-30)
**Model:** Sonnet — flow/layout fix reusing the existing WMM and pin code.
**Depends on:** nothing (but pairs naturally with 5.1's location entitlement)

`record_position_preview_screen.dart:121-125` dead-ends at
`_WaitingForGps` when there is no manual pin *and* no GPS fix, so a first
pin can never be placed — while the Record screen's save-blocked snackbar
(`observation_logging_screen.dart:451-459`) tells the user to "use manual
pin instead." That's a closed loop, and it's the normal state on a desktop
with no location fix.

- Replace the `_WaitingForGps` dead end with a usable map: center on the
  active project's extent (`bbox_min/max_lat/lon`) when there's no fix and
  no pin; fall back to a wide/zoomed-out view only if the project has no
  bbox.
- **Show an explicit, user-visible notice** that the map is centered on
  the project extent and is **not** a position fix — a persistent banner
  or inline note on the picker (not a transient snackbar that can be
  missed), so a pin placed from this state is never mistaken for a
  GPS-derived position. Keep the existing "Use GPS" affordance available
  for when a fix does arrive.
- Once a pin is placed, the existing behavior (bearing ray + uncertainty
  wedge preview, drag-to-adjust, declination computed at the pinned
  position via the existing WMM path) should work unchanged — this task
  is about reaching that state, not changing it.
- **Note the enum-semantics wrinkle, but do not change it here:**
  `PositionSource.manualPin` is dead code; tapped pins are currently
  stored as `manualEntry`. Leave as-is for this task and flag under
  Discovered Scope — renaming/repurposing touches stored data semantics
  and CSV/sharing payloads, which deserves its own task rather than a
  drive-by change.
- **Acceptance criteria:** with no GPS fix and no existing pin, the picker
  opens on the project extent with a visible "not a position fix" notice
  and a pin can be placed, dragged, and used; the Record screen can then
  save that observation; behavior with a live GPS fix is unchanged; a
  project with no bbox still opens something usable.

### Task 5.5 — Test coverage for the no-compass / no-GPS paths
**Status:** Done (2026-07-30)
**Model:** Sonnet
**Depends on:** 5.2, 5.3, 5.4

There is currently **no** test anywhere for a missing compass or an
errored sensor stream (`test/compass/` holds pure-math unit tests only),
and none for the no-GPS position-picker path.

- Unit/widget tests for `compassAvailableProvider` (or whatever 5.2
  introduces): null stream ⇒ unavailable, errored stream ⇒ unavailable,
  healthy stream ⇒ available.
- Widget test: Compass screen renders the explanatory unavailable state
  rather than a dial when compass is unavailable.
- Widget test: bearing entry sheet opens on the Manual tab when compass is
  unavailable, and on Compass when it's available.
- Widget test: position picker with no GPS and no pin renders a usable map
  plus the project-extent notice (not `_WaitingForGps`).
- Reuse the widget-test techniques already documented under Phase 4's
  Discovered Scope (`runAsync` zone rules, `debugDeterministicCursor`,
  `tester.view.physicalSize` for tall dialogs) — those were hard-won and
  apply directly here.
- **Acceptance criteria:** all four areas covered; `flutter analyze` and
  the full `flutter test` suite pass.

### Discovered Scope

- **New Project save hangs indefinitely on macOS (first run, no existing
  user/project).** Found while verifying 5.1's tile-load acceptance
  criterion: `ProjectSetupScreen._save()` (`project_setup_screen.dart:276`)
  calls through `currentUserProvider` (`app_context_provider.dart:22`),
  which auto-creates the first-run local "Field User". On a fresh macOS
  debug build the Save button's spinner never resolves (confirmed hung
  15+ minutes, then reproduced again on a second fresh launch) — no
  crash, no sandbox-denial log entries, no outbound network attempt
  observed (so it isn't the entitlement fix), and the window stays
  responsive, meaning some awaited `Future` in that provider chain (or
  the `deviceIdProvider`/`activeUserIdProvider` `SharedPreferencesAsync`
  path it depends on) never completes on first run on this platform. Not
  reproduced/ruled out on iOS/Android.
- **The "Set extent on map" / "Use current location" button row
  (`project_setup_screen.dart:153-174`) does not render at all on
  macOS**, independent of the hang above — the form jumps straight from
  the extent preview box to the Save button with zero space for that
  `Row`, confirmed across two fresh launches and reproducible clicks at
  its expected position hitting whatever is underneath instead. Not
  investigated further (no Dart logic changes in this task's scope);
  worth a look alongside the save hang since both sit in the same
  screen.
- Both of the above **blocked a full visual confirmation of online tile
  rendering** for 5.1: the normal path (New Project → Save → Main Map)
  hangs, and the fallback path (extent-picker mini-map from this same
  form) has no reachable entry point in the current build. What *is*
  confirmed for 5.1: `codesign -d --entitlements` shows both
  `com.apple.security.network.client` and
  `com.apple.security.personal-information.location` embedded in the
  built app; `flutter run -d macos` launches and stayed open 15+ minutes
  with zero sandbox-denial entries in the unified log; a Core Location
  authorization request was observed going out (TCC IPC) with no crash,
  consistent with the Info.plist usage-description fix. Recommend a
  follow-up task to fix the save hang and missing button row, then
  re-verify tile rendering visually on the Main Map.
- **5.2's planned "null event stream or errored sensor stream" detection
  doesn't actually happen in practice — `compassAvailableProvider` needed
  a timeout fallback, not just an error check.** `flutter_compass` 0.8.1's
  `FlutterCompass.events` getter is unconditionally non-null (only
  `kIsWeb` gets a special-cased `Stream.empty()`; every other platform,
  supported or not, gets a real `EventChannel.receiveBroadcastStream()`).
  And on a platform with no registered platform-side handler for that
  channel (macOS — `flutter_compass` has no `macos/` implementation) the
  stream doesn't error either: the engine's `listen` invocation gets a
  null reply, and `EventChannel`'s controller treats a null reply as
  "nothing to do" rather than an error. Net effect: the stream just sits
  forever with no data and no error — confirmed live on macOS, where the
  Compass screen showed the live dial (dashes) indefinitely with
  `compassAvailableProvider` reporting available, before the fix below.
  `compass_provider.dart:14-16`'s `events == null` check is therefore
  dead code on every real platform (kept anyway as defense-in-depth for a
  future plugin version change), and a bare `hasError` check on
  `compassHeadingProvider` is not suffient on its own.
  `CompassAvailable` (now a `Notifier<bool>`, not a plain function) adds:
  no non-null heading within `compassAvailabilityTimeout` (2s) of first
  watching ⇒ unavailable, latching `true` permanently once one real
  heading arrives so a momentary calibration blip can't flip it back.
  This is still capability-based (never `Platform.is*`) and, per
  `CompassEvent.heading`'s own nullable contract, is arguably a *more*
  faithful implementation of "a tablet with no magnetometer" than the
  original error-only design — a real device with no compass hardware
  exhibits the identical symptom (heading always null, no error), so a
  pure error check would have missed that case on real hardware too, not
  just on macOS. Verified live: Compass screen showed the dial for the
  first ~2s on a fresh macOS launch, then switched to the "No compass
  available" empty state; "Go to Record" correctly routed to the Record
  tab. The Record screen's compass-unavailable affordance (manual-entry
  button, POINT/RANGE tooltip, sheet opening on the Manual tab) could
  **not** be visually verified on macOS — it only renders with an active
  project, and project creation is blocked by the save-hang bug above;
  verified by code review only (call sites, types, `flutter analyze`)
  pending 5.5's dedicated widget-test coverage.
- **5.3: manual bearing entry sheet also couldn't be visually verified live
  on macOS**, for the same reason as 5.2's Record-screen affordance — it's
  only reachable from the Record tab's bearing capture UI, which needs an
  active project (blocked by the save-hang bug above). Verification instead
  relied on the widget tests the task itself calls for (added at
  `test/features/observations/bearing_entry_sheet_test.dart`, 9 cases:
  framing copy present, empty/non-numeric/`>360` each show their own inline
  error and leave the sheet open, `0`/`359.9`/`360` all accepted (`360`
  normalized to `0.0`), a typed `-10` renders as `10` (minus stripped by the
  input formatter), and typing after an error clears it) plus
  `flutter analyze`/`flutter test` (352/352 passing).
- **5.4 got a real interactive pass on macOS after all**, by working around
  the save-hang bug rather than waiting on a fix for it: inserted a project
  (with a bbox around Flagstaff, AZ) and a tag directly via `sqlite3` into
  the app's local dev database
  (`~/Library/Containers/edu.nau.tritrack/Data/Library/Application
  Support/edu.nau.tritrack/tri_track.db`) and set
  `active_project_id` via `defaults write edu.nau.tritrack`, entirely
  bypassing `ProjectSetupScreen._save()`. Confirmed live: the picker opens
  centered on the project extent with the "📍 No GPS fix — map centered on
  the project area, not your position" banner and no marker; tapping the
  map drops a pin, the banner switches to the existing "✋ Manual position"
  state with lat/lon and a "Use GPS" affordance; back on the Record screen
  the position line shows `<lat>, <lon> · manual`; setting a manual bearing
  and saving produced a real `Observations` row
  (`position_source = 'manual_entry'`, confirmed by query) — the full loop
  the task's acceptance criteria describes. Test fixtures were deleted
  again afterward to leave the local dev database as found. Also confirmed
  live, as a bonus: 5.2's "No compass on this device" copy and 5.3's
  magnetic-framing note both render correctly in this same flow.
- **Confirmed via that same live pass:** `Observations.position_source`
  for a pin placed on this picker is written as `manual_entry`, not
  `manual_pin` — exactly the enum-semantics wrinkle 5.4's task entry
  flagged in advance. `PositionSource.manualPin` remains unused dead code.
  Left alone per the task's explicit instruction; still needs its own task
  if it's ever worth reconciling (touches CSV/sharing payload semantics).
- **5.5 found a new widget-test gotcha worth adding to the Phase 4
  `runAsync` rules: it's not just *when a tap happens* that's zone-sensitive
  — a bare `container.listen(...)` call is too.** `container.listen`
  synchronously kicks off the target provider's build the instant it's
  called; for an autoDispose provider backed by real `sqflite_common_ffi`
  I/O (e.g. `projectActiveTagsProvider`, `observationFormProvider`), calling
  `listen` *before* entering `tester.runAsync` starts that provider's
  underlying Future chain in the fake-async zone, and it then never
  resolves — even though every other read in the test correctly happens
  inside `runAsync`. Two new test files
  (`test/features/observations/observation_logging_screen_test.dart`,
  `record_position_preview_screen_test.dart`) hung indefinitely (10+
  minutes, no exception, no output) until the fix: move every
  `container.listen(...)` call for a non-keepAlive provider to *inside* the
  same `runAsync` block as the rest of that provider's reads. Also hit
  again in both new files: a bare `MaterialApp()` in a test harness needs
  `theme: AppTheme.light()` or any screen touching
  `Theme.of(context).extension<TriTrackColors>()!` null-check-crashes —
  already known from 5.3's `bearing_entry_sheet_test.dart` but worth
  restating since it recurred immediately in the next two test files.
- Added, per this task's acceptance criteria: `compassAvailableProvider`
  unit tests (`test/core/providers/compass_provider_test.dart`, 5 cases:
  construction-throw, stream-error, healthy-stream, timeout-when-silent,
  and the latch-stays-true-after-going-silent-again case); a Compass-screen
  widget test for the unavailable empty state
  (`test/features/compass/compass_screen_test.dart`); an
  `observation_logging_screen_test.dart` covering the bearing sheet opening
  on Compass vs. Manual entry depending on live compass availability (the
  actual `_BearingCaptureBlock` wiring, not just `showBearingEntrySheet`'s
  parameter in isolation); and `record_position_preview_screen_test.dart`
  covering the no-fix/no-pin extent-centered map, a no-bbox project
  fallback, and tap-to-place-pin switching to the manual-position banner.
  `flutter analyze` clean; full suite 363/363 passing.
- **Bug found and fixed post-5.5 (2026-07-30): tapping "SAVE OBSERVATION"
  on macOS silently did nothing.** Not the 5.1 save-hang bug above — that
  one didn't reproduce on re-investigation (`currentUserProvider` resolved
  normally this session). The real cause: `ObservationLoggingScreen._save()`
  (`observation_logging_screen.dart`) built the saved row's `tag_id` from
  `draft.tagId` (the persisted draft state) rather than from `tag`, the
  screen's own already-validated `selectedTag`. `draft.tagId` can be
  non-null but stale — pointing at a tag that's since gone inactive or been
  deleted — and `_buildForm`'s `selectedTag` fallback only corrected the
  *displayed* selection in that case, silently leaving the persisted
  `draft.tagId` wrong (its self-healing `postFrameCallback` only fired when
  `draft.tagId` was null, not merely invalid). Saving then hit
  `Observations.tag_id`'s foreign key and threw — inside a bare `try/finally`
  with no `catch`, so the exception surfaced only as an unhandled exception
  in the console; the button just silently reset. Fixed two ways: (1)
  `_save` now always uses `tag.tagId` (not `draft.tagId`) to build tag-scoped
  observations/non-detections; (2) `_buildForm`'s reconciliation now also
  fires when `draft.tagId` is non-null but absent from the project's active
  tags, not just when it's null, so the persisted draft self-heals instead
  of staying wrong indefinitely; (3) added a `catch` to `_save` that surfaces
  failures via a SnackBar instead of failing silently. Reproduced live via
  `flutter run -d macos` (a stale tag id had been left behind by earlier
  Phase 5 manual `sqlite3` DB seeding) and confirmed fixed the same way.
  Regression test added: `observation_logging_screen_test.dart` now also
  covers saving with a stale `draft.tagId`, asserting the row lands with the
  currently-valid tag. That test needed its own new zone workarounds beyond
  5.5's: `_save`'s WMM-declination branch calls `rootBundle.loadString`,
  which the test's mocked binary messenger only answers on the *fake*-async
  zone — the opposite problem from the sqflite/`SharedPreferencesAsync`
  calls elsewhere in the same method, which only resolve in the *real* zone
  inside `runAsync`. Worked around by pre-setting a manual declination
  override (skips the WMM/`rootBundle` branch entirely) rather than trying
  to satisfy both zones in one call. Also needed `accelerometerReadingProvider`
  /`magnetometerReadingProvider`/`gpsPositionProvider` overridden to empty
  streams — `CompassController` listens to all three, and their real
  `sensors_plus`/`geolocator` platform channels (no test-time implementation)
  only actually throw once something drives the real event loop, which
  didn't happen in any earlier test in this file. `flutter analyze` clean;
  full suite 364/364 passing.
- **Bug found and fixed post-5.5 (2026-07-30): double-clicking the position
  picker map (`record_position_preview_screen.dart`, used by both the
  bearing-capture "Preview / set position on map" flow and the no-GPS path
  5.4 added) zoomed in and blanked the map.** This screen's whole purpose is
  tap-to-place-a-pin, but `MapOptions.interactionOptions` never overrode
  `flags`, so flutter_map's default `InteractiveFlag.all` — which includes
  `doubleTapZoom` — stayed active. Two quick taps to adjust a pin twice got
  reinterpreted as "zoom in here," and zooming past the tile source's
  usable range left the map blank. Fixed by setting `flags: InteractiveFlag.all
  & ~InteractiveFlag.doubleTapZoom & ~InteractiveFlag.doubleTapDragZoom` on
  both `MapOptions` in this file (`_buildNoFixMap` and `_buildMap`), leaving
  pan/pinch-zoom/scroll-wheel-zoom/rotate untouched. Verified live via
  `flutter run -d macos`: double-clicking now just places the pin twice at
  the same zoom level, no zoom, no blank map. **Not yet applied to**
  `position_estimation_screen.dart`, which has the same
  tap-to-place-a-point pattern and the same unoverridden `interactionOptions`
  — likely the same latent bug, but out of scope for this fix since it
  wasn't reported; worth its own task if confirmed. `flutter analyze` clean;
  full suite still 364/364 (no new test — no widget-test coverage exists yet
  for flutter_map gesture-flag behavior in this codebase).
- **Follow-up UX request (2026-07-31): desktop map pan/zoom should follow the
  Google Maps convention** — click-drag to pan, pinch or two-finger trackpad
  scroll to zoom — instead of flutter_map's touch-first default, which
  applies a plain two-finger trackpad scroll (no pinch) as a pan. Confirmed
  the position-picker's double-tap-zoom fix above didn't touch this; it's a
  separate gesture path. Root cause: on macOS, a trackpad's two-finger
  scroll and its pinch gesture arrive as the *same* engine event
  (`PointerPanZoomUpdateEvent`) — flutter_map's `ScaleGestureRecognizer`
  reads the translation component of that event as a pan whenever
  `InteractiveFlag.pinchMove` is enabled (the default), with no flag to
  redirect a scale-less scroll into a zoom instead. Fixed with a new shared
  helper, `lib/features/map/services/desktop_map_gestures.dart`:
  `mapInteractionFlags()` drops `pinchMove` on desktop (macOS/Windows/Linux;
  gated by `isDesktopMapPlatform`, untouched on iOS/Android) so trackpad
  scroll stops panning, and a new `DesktopTrackpadZoom` wrapper widget
  listens for that same raw `PointerPanZoomUpdateEvent` one level above each
  `FlutterMap` and converts a near-1.0-`scale` (i.e. not an actual pinch)
  two-finger scroll into a zoom around the cursor — same
  velocity/`focusedZoomCenter` math flutter_map's own scroll-wheel-zoom
  already uses, so trackpad and external-mouse-wheel zooming feel identical.
  Applied to all four map screens (user confirmed "all map screens," desktop
  only): `map_screen.dart`, `offline_data_map_screen.dart`,
  `position_estimation_screen.dart`, `record_position_preview_screen.dart`
  (which also folded its existing double-tap-zoom-disable into
  `mapInteractionFlags(doubleTapZoom: false)` rather than a hand-rolled bitmask).
  Verified live via `flutter run -d macos`: click-drag-to-pan confirmed
  working (screenshotted before/after a simulated drag). **Two-finger
  trackpad scroll-to-zoom itself was not verified live** — `cliclick` (the
  tool used for macOS UI automation this session) has no way to synthesize a
  trackpad pan/zoom gesture, only clicks/drags/moves — so this needs the
  user's own hands-on check on real trackpad hardware. `flutter analyze`
  clean; full suite still 364/364 (no new automated test — flutter_map
  gesture-flag/pointer-event behavior isn't covered by this codebase's
  widget-test harness, same gap noted above).
- **User-reported follow-up (2026-07-31): fast two-finger scroll-to-zoom
  above "transitioned to a pan" right at release.** Root cause: flutter_map's
  fling-on-release (`_handleScaleEnd` in its gesture viewer) is gated only by
  `InteractiveFlag.flingAnimation`, not by `pinchMove`/`pinchZoom` — so even
  with `pinchMove` disabled (stopping the *live* pan), a release with enough
  velocity still kicked off flutter_map's own momentum **pan** animation,
  independent of and right after `DesktopTrackpadZoom`'s zoom. Fixed by also
  dropping `InteractiveFlag.flingAnimation` in `mapInteractionFlags()` on
  desktop — this removes momentum from click-drag panning too, not just
  scroll-zooming, which matches the Google Maps desktop convention this task
  is chasing (no inertia either way on desktop). `flutter analyze` clean;
  full suite 364/364.

## Phase 6 — Observation Identity & Provenance

**Why this exists.** Started as "clean up the dead `PositionSource.manualPin`
enum value," but auditing that turned up a genuine data-integrity bug in the
sharing path that should be fixed *before* the Phase 3 server exists.

**The bug.** When a shared observation is saved
(`observation_sharing_screen.dart:224-245`), the receiving device creates a
**brand-new** observation: fresh `Uuid().v4()`, `userId` = the *receiving*
user, `SyncMeta.initial` with the receiving device as origin, and the real
observer's identity demoted to a notes string ("Shared by Alice"). So Alice's
original and Bob's saved copy are two rows with **different primary keys**.
At sync time nothing recognizes them as the same observation — last-write-wins
never fires, because they aren't in conflict. The result is silent
duplication, not a resolvable conflict.

That is worse here than in a generic app: the Lenth MLE treats duplicated
bearings as independent confirmations, so a double-counted bearing *tightens*
the confidence ellipse. The output is a more confident, wronger fix — the
exact "confident but wrong" failure class the degenerate-geometry guards
exist to prevent. The payload also carries no `position_accuracy_m`, so a
relayed observation loses the accuracy that should down-weight it.

**Decisions locked in (2026-07-30):**
- **The measurer owns the record.** A saved shared observation must be a
  *faithful replica* of the original, not a new observation.
- **Preserve the original `observation_id`** so both copies converge to one
  row under existing revision/`updated_at` LWW logic.
- **Observer identity travels as normalized email**, matching the documented
  cross-device identity anchor in `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md` ("treat
  email (normalized, lowercased) as the cross-device identity anchor for
  dedup on import/merge"). The receiving device dedupes/creates a local
  `Users` row keyed by that email.
- **Privacy caveat, accepted:** share payloads travel over consumer
  messaging apps, so the payload will contain a team member's email address.
  Acceptable within a research team; noted here because a forwarded payload
  discloses it downstream. If this becomes a concern, revisit — do not
  quietly change the identity anchor, since that's load-bearing for merge.
- **Fixing this now, before the server** — every share-save today is a
  latent duplicate that would otherwise need server-side reconciliation
  later.
- **Existing rows: forward-only, no data migration.** Current DB contents
  are development/test data; new writes use corrected values, existing rows
  stay as-is.
- **Share-payload `position_accuracy_m`/`position_source` are now in scope
  here** (they were previously deferred as a separate task) because faithful
  replication requires them.

**Model note:** 6.1 is Sonnet (isolated relabel). 6.2 and 6.3 are **Opus** —
cross-device identity, primary-key semantics, and merge/LWW correctness,
squarely the category `CLAUDE.md` reserves for Opus. A subtle error here
produces silent duplication or data loss that won't surface until a real
multi-device sync.

### Task 6.1 — Correct the pin `PositionSource` mislabel
**Status:** Done
**Model:** Sonnet — isolated relabel, no schema or merge semantics.
**Depends on:** nothing

- `observation_logging_screen.dart:451` writes
  `PositionSource.manualEntry` when the user has placed a map pin. Change to
  `PositionSource.manualPin` (currently dead code — zero production writes).
- Leave `observation_sharing_screen.dart:233`'s `manualEntry` **alone** for
  now; 6.3 replaces it with the original observation's real
  `position_source`.
- Confirm the intended semantics are documented in
  `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md`'s schema section: `gps_fix` = this
  device's GPS; `manual_pin` = user placed/dragged a point on the map;
  `manual_entry` = typed coordinates (deliberately unimplemented — see
  `List_of_fixes_needed.rtf`: "no one wants to manually enter a lat/lon").
  Update that doc if it doesn't already say this clearly.
- **Acceptance criteria:** placing a pin stores `manual_pin`; GPS-derived
  positions still store `gps_fix`; no data migration attempted; CSV export
  and `RowValidator` need no change (both already enumerate all three
  values); `flutter analyze`/`flutter test` pass.

### Task 6.2 — Share payload v2: carry identity, provenance, and sync clock
**Status:** Done
**Model:** **Opus** — wire-format versioning plus identity/merge semantics.
**Depends on:** nothing (6.3 depends on this)

`lib/data/sharing/observation_share.dart` currently encodes `'v': 1` inside
a `TT1:`+base64 envelope, and `decode` already documents itself as handling
"current-or-older-version" payloads — so a v2 is a natural extension, but
the v1 path must keep working.

Add to the payload:
- `observation_id` — the original UUID (the key to replica convergence).
- `observer_user_id` **and** `observer_email` (normalized/lowercased), plus
  the existing `observer_name`. **Both** the id and email are needed:
  carrying only the email means the receiver invents a different local
  `user_id` for the same person, so the replicated observation's `user_id`
  would differ between Alice's copy and Bob's — reintroducing a conflict on
  the very row we're trying to converge. Carrying the original `user_id`
  lets the receiver create the local `Users` row with the *same* id, while
  email remains the dedup key.
- `position_source` and `position_accuracy_m` — the original values.
- The original **sync clock**: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `revision`,
  `last_modified_by`, `origin_device_id`. **This matters for correctness,
  not just tidiness:** if the replica were written with `SyncMeta.initial`
  (revision 1, `updated_at` = now), Bob's copy could look *newer* than
  Alice's original and overwrite her later edits on merge. Copying her clock
  makes it a true replica, so `MergeResolver`'s revision→`updated_at`
  ordering behaves correctly.

Also:
- Bump to `'v': 2`. Keep decoding v1 payloads: they lack identity fields, so
  a v1 payload cannot produce a faithful replica — decode must surface that
  clearly (e.g. a nullable identity block on `SharedObservation`) so 6.3 can
  fall back to today's new-observation behavior *with a visible warning*
  rather than silently pretending it replicated.
- Decide and document whether the envelope prefix stays `TT1:` (a format
  marker) or becomes `TT2:`. Recommendation: keep `TT1:` as the app marker
  and rely on the inner `v` field for versioning, so older builds still
  recognize the envelope enough to give a useful "payload is newer than this
  app" error rather than "not a Tri Track payload" — but call this out
  explicitly either way.
- Keep bound-checking every ingested field (existing `decode` discipline),
  including validating `position_source` against the enum and rejecting
  malformed emails/UUIDs rather than trusting the sender.

**Acceptance criteria:** v2 round-trips all new fields; a v1 payload still
decodes and is clearly marked as identity-less; a v2 payload from a
hypothetical newer version fails with a helpful message; malformed/hostile
field values are rejected, not written through; unit tests cover v1→v2
compatibility both directions.

### Task 6.3 — Replica import: preserve identity instead of creating a new row
**Status:** Done
**Model:** **Opus** — primary-key/upsert semantics and cross-device identity.
**Depends on:** 6.2

Rewrite the save path in `observation_sharing_screen.dart` so a saved shared
observation is a replica:

- Use the payload's `observation_id` as the primary key — do **not** mint a
  new UUID.
- Resolve the observer: look up a local `Users` row by normalized
  (lowercased, trimmed) email; if absent, create one using the payload's
  `observer_user_id` and name. If a row already exists with that email but a
  *different* `user_id`, prefer the existing local row and record the
  discrepancy — do not create a duplicate user or silently rewrite ids.
- Write the observation with the original `user_id`, `position_source`,
  `position_accuracy_m`, and the original sync clock from 6.2.
- **Handle the already-have-this-row case.** The same payload may be pasted
  twice, or Bob may already hold that observation from a server sync. Do not
  let this throw on a PK conflict. Reuse **`MergeResolver`**
  (`lib/data/sync/merge_resolver.dart`) — it already implements exactly the
  revision→`updated_at` LWW ordering needed — rather than hand-rolling a
  comparison. Incoming newer ⇒ update; incoming same-or-older ⇒ keep local
  and tell the user it was already present, don't silently no-op.
- Drop the "Shared by X" notes-prefix hack **only** for v2 replicas (the
  observer is now properly attributed via `user_id`); keep it for the v1
  fallback path, where attribution genuinely can't be preserved.
- v1 fallback: today's behavior (new UUID, receiver-owned,
  `PositionSource.manualEntry`) but with a **visible warning** that
  provenance can't be preserved and the record may duplicate the original.
- **Note a consequence to verify, not fix here:** preserving the original
  `user_id` means the existing permission model ("only the observation's
  creator can edit") makes the replica read-only to the receiving user.
  That's the desired outcome, but confirm the edit UI degrades gracefully
  (disabled/explained, not a crash or a silently failing save).

**Acceptance criteria:** saving a v2 shared observation produces a row whose
`observation_id`, `user_id`, `position_source`, `position_accuracy_m`, and
sync clock all match the sender's; pasting the same payload twice does not
duplicate or throw; an older incoming revision does not clobber a newer local
row; a local `Users` row is created/deduped by normalized email; the v1 path
still works and warns; the replica is not editable by the receiving user and
that's surfaced clearly.

### Task 6.4 — Tests for identity preservation and merge convergence
**Status:** Done
**Model:** Sonnet — the correctness properties are specified in 6.2/6.3;
this is writing them out as tests.
**Depends on:** 6.2, 6.3

- Round-trip: encode → decode → save reproduces the original row's identity
  fields and sync clock exactly.
- Idempotence: saving the same payload twice yields one row.
- LWW: incoming older revision doesn't overwrite a newer local row; incoming
  newer does.
- Email dedup: two payloads from the same observer with differently-cased
  emails resolve to one local `Users` row.
- Mismatched-id case: existing local user with same email but different
  `user_id` prefers the local row and doesn't duplicate.
- v1 compatibility: decodes, falls back, warns.
- Rejection: malformed email/UUID/`position_source` in a payload is refused.
- **The duplication regression itself:** a test asserting that two devices
  saving the same shared observation converge to one row — the specific bug
  this phase exists to fix. Without this, the fix can silently regress.
- **Acceptance criteria:** all of the above covered; `flutter analyze` and
  the full suite pass.

### Discovered Scope

- **`deleted_at` is deliberately not on the wire (6.2).** The plan named five
  sync-clock fields; `SyncMeta` has six. Only live observations are shareable
  (Log lists live rows), so the replica's tombstone is always null and the
  wire format omits it. Consequence to keep in mind: a share payload can never
  propagate a *deletion*. If Phase 3 ever wants share-based deletes, that's a
  v3 field, not a bug fix.
- **Id validation is "opaque id"-shaped, not strict UUID (6.2).** The plan said
  "rejecting malformed emails/UUIDs." Enforcing UUID-v4 would reject the test
  fixtures' `obs-1`/`user-1` ids and any future id scheme, so `decode` bounds
  ids as `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` instead — which still rejects the hostile
  shape (quotes, SQL/path punctuation, whitespace, absurd lengths) that matters
  for values written straight into PK/FK columns. Revisit only if a stronger
  guarantee is actually needed.
- **`ObservationShare.encode` now asserts `observer.userId ==
  observation.userId` (6.2).** v2 attributes the record to the passed
  `observer`, so handing it the *sharing* user rather than the *author* would
  misattribute the replica on every receiving device. The one production call
  site (`log_screen.dart:_share`) already passes the author. Worth a real
  runtime guard rather than an assert if a second call site ever appears.
- **Follow-up for 6.3, not done here:** the paste screen's preview shows
  nothing about whether a payload is replicable. 6.3 needs to surface
  `SharedObservation.canReplicate == false` in the UI (the "provenance can't be
  preserved" warning), and `_PreviewCard` is where that belongs.
  **Resolved in 6.3** — warning now renders below the preview card, before
  saving, so the user can decline.
- **The save path moved out of the screen into
  `lib/data/sharing/shared_observation_importer.dart` (6.3).** Identity
  resolution, the `MergeResolver` upsert, and the v1 fallback are not
  screen concerns and were untestable there. The screen now only maps the
  returned `SharedObservationImportOutcome` to user-facing wording.
- **Replica writes deliberately bypass the repository layer (6.3).**
  `BaseRepository.updateById` bumps `revision` and touches `updated_at` — correct
  for a local edit, corrupting for a replica, whose whole point is to carry the
  *sender's* clock. The importer takes a `DatabaseExecutor` and does raw
  table writes inside one transaction, same as `ProjectMerger._upsert`. Any
  future replica-style write must do the same; consider promoting a shared
  `upsertPreservingClock` helper if a third call site appears.
- **`Users` rows for a newly-seen observer get `SyncMeta.initial` (6.3).** The
  v2 payload carries a clock for the *observation*, not for the observer's user
  row, so the local `Users` row is stamped as originating on the receiving
  device — which is honest, since it did. Consequence: two devices that
  independently receive Alice's payload create `Users` rows with the same
  `user_id` but different clocks. Harmless under LWW (the columns agree), but
  if user-row provenance ever matters, the payload would need a user clock too.
- **No `Project_Memberships` row is created for a replicated observer (6.3).**
  The Log resolves observer names by `user_id` directly, not through
  membership, so names display correctly without one. Flagging it because a
  future membership-gated view (or a per-project roster UI) would show the
  observation without its observer listed as a project participant.
- **A tombstoned local row reports "already have this, nothing changed" (6.3).**
  No-resurrection is correct and tested — an older incoming payload cannot
  clear a newer local tombstone — but the message doesn't say the local copy is
  deleted. Minor wording gap, not a data-integrity one. Worth a distinct
  outcome if it confuses anyone in the field.
- **6.4 landed as three additions rather than a new omnibus test file**, since
  6.3's own tests already carried most of the listed properties (as noted
  above): a new `test/data/sharing/identity_round_trip_test.dart` for the two
  properties that only show up across a full device round-trip (encode →
  decode → save → re-export with identity/clock intact, and the duplication
  regression run through the *real* `ProjectMerger` across three independent
  in-memory databases rather than the importer's own upsert path — the two
  devices genuinely never see each other's data until the merge step); a
  `test/features/more/log_screen_test.dart` addition confirming a replica
  (observer ≠ current user) renders Share but not Edit/Delete, and the
  contrasting case for an own observation; and a
  `test/features/more/observation_sharing_screen_test.dart` addition
  confirming the v1 "provenance can't be preserved" warning actually renders
  in the preview, not just that `canReplicate` is false at the model layer.
- **The populated-Log-list widget-test technique flagged as fragile in
  `log_screen_test.dart`'s existing header comment (tap-triggered async DB
  writes don't resolve within `pumpAndSettle()`) does not apply to a
  render-only assertion.** `historyDataProvider` pre-resolved via
  `tester.runAsync` before `pumpWidget` (same treatment as
  `localTagsProvider`/`allTagsProvider` elsewhere), plus overriding
  `currentUserProvider`/`currentProjectProvider` directly instead of routing
  through `SharedPreferences`-backed `activeUserIdProvider`/
  `activeProjectIdProvider`, was enough — no tap involved, so the gotcha
  about a tap's async chain needing to share `runAsync`'s zone never comes up.
  Worth reusing this pattern (pre-resolve + direct provider override) for any
  future Log-list render-only assertion; the tap-triggered-write gotcha still
  stands for anything that clicks a button and then checks DB/UI state.

## Phase 7 — Local User Identity (no server)

**Why this exists.** A planning-session audit (2026-07-31) found the app has
**no user-facing identity surface at all**: no login, no profile, no account
screen, no way to see or change who you are. Every install silently
auto-creates a hard-coded `Field User` with a *random placeholder email*
(`app_context_provider.dart:40`):

```dart
email: 'field-user-${const Uuid().v4()}@local.tritrack',
```

**That one line disables the entire cross-device identity system.** Email is
the documented cross-device identity anchor, and the machinery that depends
on it is fully built and tested — `ProjectMerger._buildUserRemap`
(`project_merger.dart:110-178`) does proper two-phase normalized-email
remapping, `SharedObservationImporter._resolveObserver` mirrors it exactly,
and the result even surfaces in the UI ("Users matched to local accounts:
N", `data_export_screen.dart:225`). But because every install mints a unique
random email, **no two devices ever match**: the remap always comes back
empty, and merging two field devices' backups accumulates another "Field
User" row instead of deduping. Phase 6's replica import inherits the same
problem — it resolves observers correctly in code and will never match anyone
in practice.

So the highest-leverage change is small: **make name and email real and
user-supplied.** The merge engine, audit columns, observer filter, and CSV
attribution are all already written against that anchor and start working the
moment it carries meaning.

**Scope boundary — identity, not authentication.** This phase gives the app a
truthful answer to "who is using this device," offline, with no server.
It deliberately does **not** attempt authentication (passwords, tokens,
sessions, verification) — nothing here proves a user is who they claim.
Auth only becomes meaningful with the Phase 3 server and is a genuinely
different problem; building a login-shaped screen now would be theater that
needs reworking later. Any UI copy in this phase must not imply verification.

**Field usage context (confirmed 2026-07-31):** one device per person. A
small team has person A record from their device and person B from theirs —
which is precisely why the server matters and why cross-device identity has
to be right *before* it lands.

**Decisions locked in (2026-07-31):**
- **First-run identity capture is non-skippable.** Justification: it happens
  exactly once, at install time, which is never in the field — you install
  before you leave. It also ties into the existing pre-trip checklist
  concept. (This does cut against the app's fast-path instincts; noted
  deliberately, and revisit if field experience says otherwise.)
- **Existing installs must be migrated, not just new ones.** Devices already
  carrying a `@local.tritrack` placeholder (including the developer's own
  test iPhone and macOS build) must be prompted to complete their profile,
  or they stay permanently unmergeable.
- **Prior emails are retained** in a new `User_Emails` table, and used as a
  *lower-confidence* match in merge — see Task 7.3 for the full rationale
  and the guardrail this needs.
- **No `UNIQUE` constraint on `Users.email`.** Both merge paths deliberately
  tolerate duplicate emails and handle them defensively
  (`_preferredLocalUserId`); a UNIQUE constraint would convert a survivable
  merge into a hard failure. Continue normalizing on comparison (already
  implemented in `UserRepository.normalizeEmail`) and storing as entered for
  display.

### Task 7.1 — First-run identity capture + placeholder migration
**Status:** Done (2026-07-31)
**Model:** Sonnet — form, validation, and routing; no merge or auth semantics.
**Depends on:** nothing

- New identity setup screen: first name, last name, email. Validate email
  format (a reasonable RFC-ish check, not a strict parser) and require all
  three non-empty. Large touch targets per `DesignTokens.minTouchTarget`.
- **Non-skippable gate:** route to it before the app is usable when no real
  identity exists. Wire it into the existing splash → `/map` flow
  (`splash_screen.dart`) rather than bolting on a second launch path.
- **Placeholder migration:** treat a user whose email matches the
  `@local.tritrack` placeholder pattern as "identity not yet set" and route
  to the same screen, pre-filling nothing (the `Field User` name is not worth
  keeping). This is what fixes already-installed devices.
- Update the existing user row in place — **do not create a new one.** The
  existing `user_id` is referenced by every observation, tag, and project
  already recorded on that device; minting a new user would orphan all of it.
  Change `first_name`/`last_name`/`email` on the existing row via
  `UserRepository.update` (currently dead code — this is its first production
  caller).
- UI copy must not imply verification (see the scope boundary above): this is
  "who is using this device," not a login.
- **Acceptance criteria:** a fresh install cannot reach the map without
  entering identity; a device with a `@local.tritrack` placeholder is
  prompted on next launch and, after completing it, retains its original
  `user_id` with all prior records still attributed to it; malformed emails
  are rejected inline; a device with a real identity already set launches
  straight to the map with no prompt.

### Task 7.2 — Profile screen (view/edit identity)
**Status:** Done (2026-07-31)
**Model:** Sonnet
**Depends on:** 7.1, 7.3 (needs `User_Emails` to record the prior address)

- New profile screen under **More** (add the tile — More currently has eight
  and none of them is identity), showing the current user and allowing
  first/last name and email edits.
- **Email changes must record the previous address** into `User_Emails`
  (7.3) before writing the new one, and must warn the user explicitly that
  backups already exported and payloads already shared carry the old address.
- Name-only edits need no warning — names aren't an identity anchor.
- **Acceptance criteria:** name/email edits persist and are reflected
  everywhere the user is displayed; an email change writes a `User_Emails`
  row for the old address and shows the warning; the user's `user_id` never
  changes; validation matches 7.1's.

### Task 7.3 — `User_Emails` table + prior-email matching in merge
**Status:** Done (2026-07-31)
**Model:** **Opus** — touches merge/dedup identity resolution, where a subtle
error silently merges two different people or splits one person in two.
**Depends on:** nothing (7.2 depends on this)

**Why retain prior emails at all.** `user_id` is stable per device, so an
email change never breaks *local* attribution — it only matters when matching
one human across two devices with independently generated `user_id`s. That
case is real and already present: the developer runs both an iPhone and a
macOS build, which are two devices, two `user_id`s, one person. If an email
is changed on one and not the other, the merge silently produces a duplicate
user. Retaining prior addresses closes that gap and gives a traceable audit
trail of identity changes.

- New `User_Emails` table (schema **v5** — next after v4's tag colors):
  `user_email_id` (UUID PK), `user_id` (FK to Users), `email`,
  `recorded_at`, plus the standard sync columns per the Global Data
  Conventions. Register it in `sync_tables.dart` with
  `userColumns: ['user_id', 'last_modified_by']` so it flows through backup
  and merge like every other table, and place it in FK-safe order after
  `Users`.
- Extend the matching in **both** `ProjectMerger._buildUserRemap` and
  `SharedObservationImporter._resolveObserver` to consider prior emails —
  they must stay behaviorally identical (they already document that intent:
  *"Matches ProjectMerger's rule so the two paths never disagree"*).
- **Required guardrail — match precedence.** A current↔current email match
  must always win over any prior-email match. Prior-email matching is
  strictly a fallback. **The hazard being guarded against:** a shared or
  reassigned institutional address (e.g. a lab account like
  `wildlifelab@nau.edu` passed from a graduating student to a new one) would,
  under naive prior-email matching, merge two genuinely different people into
  one. Never let a prior-email match override a current-email match, and
  never merge on a prior↔prior match alone.
- **Report prior-email matches distinctly** in `MergeReport` (e.g. separately
  from `usersDeduped`) and surface them in the merge summary UI, so a match
  made via a historical address is visible to the user rather than silent.
- **Acceptance criteria:** two devices whose users share a *current* email
  dedupe as before (no regression); two devices where one user changed email
  and the other still holds the old one dedupe via the prior address and are
  reported as such; a current-email match is never overridden by a
  prior-email match; a prior↔prior-only overlap does **not** merge; the new
  table round-trips through export/import; migration v5 applies cleanly to a
  v4 database.

### Task 7.4 — Harden the identity plumbing
**Status:** Done (2026-07-31)
**Model:** Sonnet — targeted bug fixes with clear expected behavior.
**Depends on:** 7.1

Three concrete defects found in the audit:

- **Silent second-user creation.** `currentUser`
  (`app_context_provider.dart:16-46`) mints a brand-new user with a fresh
  random email if `active_user_id` survives in SharedPreferences but the row
  doesn't — DB file replaced, or the row tombstoned by a merge (`findById`
  excludes tombstones by default). All prior attribution is orphaned with no
  reconciliation path. Detect this case explicitly: prefer recovering the
  tombstoned/renamed row over creating a new identity, and if a new one truly
  must be created, surface it to the user rather than doing it silently.
- **NULL `last_modified_by` on insert.** The auto-created user row
  (`app_context_provider.dart:41`) omits `modifiedBy`, as does the inline
  "Add new tag" path (`observation_logging_screen.dart:1318,1325`, creating a
  Tag and a ProjectTag). `SyncMeta.initial` takes it optionally, so these
  write NULL. Populate it consistently.
- **`UserRepository` dead methods.** `findAll` and `findByEmail` have no
  production callers (the importer re-implements the lookup with a raw
  `txn.query`). Either route callers through them or delete them — don't
  leave a third divergent copy of email lookup, given 7.3 is adding
  prior-email logic that must not fragment.
- **Acceptance criteria:** the prefs/row-mismatch case recovers the existing
  identity where possible and never silently creates a second one; no insert
  path leaves `last_modified_by` NULL; exactly one implementation of
  email-based user lookup exists after this task.

### Task 7.5 — Surface the current user
**Status:** Done (2026-07-31)
**Model:** Sonnet
**Depends on:** 7.1

- Show who you are: at minimum a header/row on the **More** screen. Nothing
  in the app currently displays the current user as "you" — names appear only
  as read-only observer attribution on other people's records.
- Add an **"identity configured"** row to the pre-trip checklist
  (`pretrip_checklist_screen.dart`), consistent with the existing live-status

- **Acceptance criteria:** the current user's name and email are visible

### Task 7.6 — Tests
**Status:** Done (2026-07-31)
**Model:** Sonnet
**Depends on:** 7.1–7.5

- First-run gate: fresh install can't bypass identity capture.
- Placeholder migration: `@local.tritrack` user is prompted; after
  completion, `user_id` is unchanged and prior records stay attributed.
- Prefs/row-mismatch recovery (7.4).
- **The regression that matters most:** two devices with real emails actually

- Prior-email matching: the fallback works, precedence holds, prior↔prior

- **Acceptance criteria:** all of the above covered; `flutter analyze` and
