### Task 11.159 — A row pushed at revision 2^62 wins every merge forever
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-05. The server detects and records; it refuses nothing.**
**The burst was measured first, and it killed the candidate remedy.**
`test/data/sync/offline_revision_burst_test.dart` prints five findings on every run: fifty offline
edits to one row arrive as **one row advanced by fifty** (the push offers current state, never an
edit log); fifty edits spread over fifty rows arrive as fifty rows advanced by one; a batch limit
bounds how many *rows* a push carries and cannot bound how far one row has moved; the share/import
path admits `revision: 3999000000` and pushes it verbatim; and **a first push of a row the server
has never seen is an insert, so a bound on the increment is not merely loose there — it is never
consulted at all.** The pin is cheapest exactly where a delta cannot see it.
**Refuse-versus-detect, with the asymmetry stated:** refusing wrongly strands an irreplaceable
field record behind a red bar nobody can clear, and noticing wrongly costs one row in a
server-only table. **And a ceiling cannot be both safe and effective** — `revision: 1000000` pins
an observation exactly as permanently as `2^62` does, so a bound high enough that no honest row
trips it does not prevent the pin, and one low enough to prevent it is a lifetime guess. So:
detection. `server/lib/src/sync/revision_plausibility.dart` asks not *"is this number too big"*
but **"could this many edits have been made in the time the row itself claims they took"**,
answered from the row's own `created_at`/`updated_at` span, leaving one parameter bounded by what
a person can physically do rather than by a guess about a record. `revision_anomalies` is a
**server-only table** (no `latestSchemaVersion` bump, no client change), **one row per affected
record rather than one per push**, read by `GET /diagnostics/revision-anomalies`. A pin that
**predates** the detection is caught by its other door: a push that loses last-write-wins to a
stored row whose own revision is unexplainable is recorded too, which is also the moment it starts
costing somebody a correction. **The §4 question is answered in `TriTrack_Security_Model.md`
§4.30: the pin is an accepted risk of write access; the silence was not.** **Watched red both
ways** — with the classifier gutted (7 unit cases), with the recording removed (3 integration
cases), and with a refusal spliced in, which fails the half of each test that asserts the row is
still *stored*. 916 server tests, 358 sync tests, 2240 app tests pass.
**Two things this does not do, said plainly:** a pin below the detected rate is still available to
somebody already trusted with writes (it is an instrument, not a control), and the count is
visible only through the diagnostics console, which is off by default — putting it in
`scripts/operator_status.sh` is in Discovered Scope.
**Below the line by reachability — not through the app, and it needs
somebody who already has write access — and above it by permanence:** the row is pinned silently
and no honest edit can ever overtake it.
**Model:** **Opus, high.** **The obvious remedy is wrong and 11.158 said so.** What makes this hard
is that the safe answer has to be derived from state rather than chosen as a number.
**Depends on:** 11.158, Done, which gave `revision` a floor and flagged the ceiling rather than
guessing at one.

**The finding, in 11.158's own words.** *"A negative revision is self-defeating (the row loses every
merge), which is why the floor was cheap. A very large one is the opposite — a row pushed at
revision 2^62 wins last-write-wins permanently and no honest edit can ever overtake it."*

> **It flagged this rather than proposing a number, and that was correct.** Any ceiling is a guess
> about how many times a row gets edited over its life, **and guessing low strands a row instead** —
> which is a worse failure than the one being fixed.

- **A candidate the planning session offers, to be evaluated and not adopted: bound the *increment*,
  not the value.** The server knows the row's current revision. Refusing a push whose revision
  exceeds *current + N* is **not a guess about a row's lifetime**; it is a guess about a single
  jump, derived from state the server already holds. **A ceiling has to anticipate years. A delta
  only has to anticipate one push.**
- **What would falsify that candidate, and it must be checked first: a device that has been offline
  for a long time.** If fifty edits made offline arrive as one push at *current + 50*, then N is not
  small, and if edits can batch without bound then the delta is a ceiling wearing a different hat.
  **Measure how a real offline burst arrives before designing anything.** Say what you measured.
- **A third option exists and may be the right one: do not refuse, detect.** An implausible jump
  that is recorded and surfaced costs nothing to a legitimate device and is not a guess at all.
  **Refusing wrongly strands data; noticing wrongly costs a line in a log.** Weigh that asymmetry
  explicitly rather than defaulting to a refusal because the last three tasks shipped refusals.
- **Say whether this belongs in `TriTrack_Security_Model.md` §4.** A member permanently pinning a
  row is a data-integrity shape available to somebody already trusted with writes; **it may be an
  accepted risk of that trust rather than a defect.** Either answer is fine written down; neither is
  fine assumed.
- **A client bug is the likelier cause than malice** — an uninitialised value, an overflow, a bad
  import — and **that is an argument for detection over refusal**, because the person holding the
  broken client is not an attacker and stranding their data helps nobody.
- **Watch it fail:** whatever ships, a row pushed at an absurd revision must produce the chosen
  outcome — refused, or recorded and visible — and the check must go red without it.

- **Acceptance:** how an offline burst actually arrives is measured and reported; refuse-versus-
  detect is decided with the asymmetry stated; the §4 question is answered either way; nothing
  strands a legitimate row; and the failing case was watched.


### Task 11.160 — Saving your name and changing tab redraws the app in the middle of drawing it
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-04.** Fixed in **one place — the tab shell's branch container**.
`app_router.dart` now builds the shell with the plain `StatefulShellRoute` constructor and its own
`keepHiddenBranchesResumed`, which is go_router 17.3.0's own `_IndexedStackedRouteBranchContainer`
with one thing removed: a hidden branch keeps `TickerMode` **enabled**. It is still `Offstage`, so
it is not painted, and `IndexedStack` still keeps every visited branch mounted. **riverpod 3 pauses
a `ref.watch` subscription whenever its branch is ticker-muted**, which is what turns an
invalidation into a recomputation *owed* rather than done — and the debt is settled at the instant
a tab is shown again, synchronously, from inside `_TickerModeState.didChangeDependencies`, i.e.
during the build phase. **The three call sites were rejected and the rejection is measured, not
argued:** the new test asserts that `container.invalidate(currentUserProvider)` raises nothing at
all, and that the fault arrives 300 ms later with the tab change — there is nothing a call site can
do at the moment it invalidates. **The standing deadlock facts were re-checked and two of the three
do not apply here**; in particular `ArrivalRefresh`'s settle-first guard is not the remedy, because
nothing is mid-build when the invalidation happens. `test/routing/tab_switch_after_invalidate_test.dart`
runs both transitions 11.145 named plus a check that the app's own route table uses the new
container; **all three were watched going red.** One unrelated red was repaired on the way:
`app_shell_harness_default_test.dart` anchors its derivation on the literal
`StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack(` and refused, correctly, to derive from nothing. **Cost, stated
rather than hidden:** a mounted-but-hidden tab now keeps its provider subscriptions live and its
tickers running. 2213 app tests pass. **Above the line.** It is on a path a person takes — Profile, save, next
tab — **it needs no server and no sync round**, and a release build does not complain, it simply
performs the thing the debug build objects to.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** Finding it is done. **Deciding *where* the holding pattern belongs —
`currentUserProvider`'s three invalidation sites, or the shell itself — is the work**, and it is
the same kind of decision task 11.153 got right by choosing one place rather than five.
**Depends on:** 11.145, Done, which found it while deriving something else and deliberately did not
fix it.

**The finding, measured rather than reasoned.** Editing a name or email on the **Profile** screen
and then tapping another tab raises *"setState() or markNeedsBuild() called during build."*
**Reproduced three times on an iPhone 17 Pro Max simulator (iOS 26.5) under `integration_test`, on
the same two transitions each run.** A bare `container.invalidate(currentUserProvider)` — which a
Profile save does, and so do identity setup and sign-in — followed by a tab switch is the whole
recipe. **No server is involved and no sync round is involved.**

> **It is not the defect task 11.145 was about and nothing in that task closes it.** It does not go
> through the four provider chains. **The entry point is `TickerMode` toggling**, which is what
> `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack` does on every tab change — so **no source check can model it**,
> and the derived guard 11.145 built will not see it either.

- **The full stack, the reproduction recipe and a starting point are in Phase 11's Discovered
  Scope. Read them; do not re-derive them.**
- **Fix it in one place, not at three call sites.** `currentUserProvider` is invalidated by a
  Profile save, by identity setup and by sign-in. **Three patched call sites is a hand-kept list**,
  which is the defect class this project has hit most often. **The shell is the other candidate and
  may be the right one** — say which you chose and why the other was rejected.
- **Say what a person actually sees on a release build, or say that you could not find out.**
  11.145 was explicit that it did not measure this and would not guess. **It may well be
  invisible.** *"I could not tell"* is an acceptable answer; a confident sentence covering a guess
  is not.
- **`TickerMode` means the standing deadlock facts may not apply.** `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md`
  records three outcomes for invalidating a mid-build provider and that deferring to a later
  event-loop turn does not help. **Check whether that holds here before relying on it** — this
  arrives by a different door.
- **Watch it fail:** the reproduction must be an automated case that goes red today, on the
  transitions 11.145 named.

- **Acceptance:** the write no longer lands mid-build; the fix is in one place with the rejected
  alternative named; what a release build shows is stated or explicitly unknown; and the failing
  case was watched.


### Task 11.161 — Tabs you are not looking at now keep their sensors running, and nobody chose that
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-04.** The set was derived rather than taken from 11.160's three examples,
and it disagrees with two of them. `test/routing/hidden_tab_liveness_test.dart` boots the real app
once, snapshots what is alive on the Map tab, opens every tab, comes back, and snapshots again;
anything in the second and not the first is held by a tab nobody is looking at. **Before the fix
that was five providers — the OS heading, the magnetometer, the accelerometer, the compass
controller and the availability check — plus one ticker that started when the Compass tab was first
shown and never stopped.** 11.160's dial was right; **its progress spinner was not** — three
spinners appeared only while the derivation ran under the fake clock, where a screen's database
future never resolves, and vanish with real time available. **One thing nobody had named turned up:
the compass controller listens to GPS for declination**, so the Compass tab held the GPS stream too.
**The decision:** the compass is paused when neither the Compass nor the Record tab is on screen
(and the pre-trip checklist likewise, inside More), through `lib/routing/tab_visibility.dart` — the
shell says which branch is on screen and the screens drop the *watch*, which is an ordinary rebuild
rather than the silent `TickerMode` pause that caused 11.160. **Resume cost: one sensor sample**, the
dial reading 0° with no bubble level until it lands, as on a cold start. **GPS is deliberately not
paused on a tab change** — re-acquiring a fix is a person standing still — and stays on the existing
backgrounded rule, which is extended rather than duplicated in `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md`'s
*Performance & Battery*. `CompassEverHeard` was added so a pause does not put a working compass back
on availability probation. The failing case was watched red with the gate neutered, and the source
guard was watched red with the idiom broken. **11.160's reproduction still passes**, and the battery
saving itself is unmeasured — it needs release-checklist item F1.
**Above the line, and it is a cost this project accepted on purpose two
days ago without measuring it.** The app is for a person carrying a phone through a field day.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** Pausing a stream is easy. **Deciding which streams may be paused
without breaking the thing that pausing them broke is the work**, and getting it wrong reintroduces
task 11.160.
**Depends on:** 11.160, Done, which introduced this deliberately and said so.

**The finding, from 11.160's own report.** Its fix keeps a hidden tab's branch alive, so **a tab you
are not looking at keeps its provider subscriptions live and its animations ticking.** Concretely:
**the compass sensor stream stays subscribed for the rest of the run once either the Compass or the
Record tab has been visited** — both watch `compassControllerProvider` — the compass dial keeps
animating, and a progress spinner on a hidden tab keeps asking for frames. **11.160 could not
measure the battery cost and said so.**

> **The reason it was accepted is good and should not be overturned casually:** *muting a sensor
> should be a decision the app makes on purpose, not a side effect of a framework noticing a widget
> is off-screen.* **That accident is what produced task 11.160's defect.** So this task does not
> restore the accident — **it replaces it with a decision.**

- **This project already has a stated requirement about exactly this**, in `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md`
  under *Performance & Battery*: pause GPS, viewshed computation and other background processes when
  the app is backgrounded, **except downloads in progress.** **A hidden tab is not the same as a
  backgrounded app** — say whether the same reasoning applies, and if the answer is yes, extend the
  rule rather than writing a second one beside it.
- **Enumerate what actually stays live on a hidden tab.** Not the three things 11.160 happened to
  name — **derive the set.** The instruments exist: `ProviderObserver`'s `didAddProvider` on a
  fresh container gives a provider's read-set, and `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md` records it under
  *A Provider's Read-Set Can Be Derived at Run Time*. **A hand-listed three is this project's
  most-repeated defect.**
- **Pause explicitly and say what each pause costs when the tab comes back.** A compass that has to
  re-acquire is a person waiting; a spinner that stopped is nothing. **The cost of resuming is the
  thing that decides which streams are worth pausing**, and it is not the same for all of them.
- **Do not reintroduce 11.160.** Its fix works because the branch stays mounted. **If a pause
  requires unmounting or disposing, it is the wrong pause** — check that the reproduction 11.160
  automated still passes.
- **The battery number itself needs a field day and nobody here can take it.** Release-checklist
  item F1 already asks Michael for that measurement. **Say what this task changed in terms he could
  notice** — which sensors, when they stop, and what he would see if the answer is wrong.
- **Watch it fail:** a test that asserts a named stream is not subscribed while its tab is hidden,
  red against today's code.

- **Acceptance:** what stays live is derived rather than listed; each pause is explicit with its
  resume cost stated; the *Performance & Battery* rule is extended rather than duplicated; 11.160's
  reproduction still passes; and the failing case was watched.


### Task 11.162 — Three downloads and a warning already put that map under its own floor
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-04.** The floor is now a box in the layout rather than a number checked
afterwards. `offline_data_map_screen.dart`'s overlays used to be four independent `Positioned`
children, each correctly sized and none of them added up; they are now one column — top controls,
then a `SizedBox` of `kOfflineMapClearBandFloor` (96) that nothing may be laid out in, then the
bottom furniture in whatever is left. **What yields is the download cards, because they are the
only furniture here whose number a person chooses**, and they yield by scrolling rather than by
being capped: all three are in the tree, the newest and the warning band are what you see, and a
scroll reaches the oldest. Measured across all eight required states at the default text size (the
band with 0/1/2/3 cards, warning down: **371, 278, 177, 96**; warning up: **315, 222, 121, 96** —
it was **76** and **20** before). The whole iOS text ladder holds at 96 through AX4. **AX5 is the
one state it cannot hold and it is named in the test with the cause: the coverage legend alone is
632 logical pixels against the map area's 531**, so it covers the map whatever the downloads do —
switching the legend off restores 96, and the legend is task 11.149's territory, not this screen's
layout. Watched red twice: once against the unfixed screen, and once with the reserve deliberately
set to zero (12 of 20 tests fail). Two live overflows were found and fixed on the way — the legend
pushed the map buttons off the right edge from **xxLarge** once it shared a row with them, and its
own rows striped above AX1 **before this task touched anything**. New file
`test/features/more/offline_data_map_space_budget_test.dart`; 2235 app tests pass.

**Was:** Above the line, and unusually a defect that exists at the default
text size — every other screen-space finding in this phase needed an accessibility setting.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** Trimming is easy. **Deciding what a screen gives up while somebody is
actively using it — three downloads running is the pre-trip flow, not an edge case — is the work.**
**Depends on:** 11.157, Done-declined, which measured it while measuring something else.
**Read 11.109 and 11.126 first:** both exist because somebody added one justified thing to a screen
without measuring the sum, and this is what that looks like when the sum is already over.

**The finding, measured by 11.157 and not caused by it.** On the Offline Data Map, with **three
downloads running and the tiles-not-arriving band up**, the clear map band is **71 logical pixels
against the project's 96-pixel floor** — **with nothing from that task added.**

> **This is reachable on an ordinary evening before a field trip.** Queueing several regions is the
> pre-trip flow the screen exists for, and the tiles-not-arriving band appears exactly when the
> connection at camp is poor. **The two conditions are correlated, not independent.**

- **Decide what yields, and say it once.** Job cards that collapse to a single line with a count,
  cards that scroll inside a fixed height, a band that stands down while a download is running —
  **the choice matters less than that it is made in one place and stated with its reason.**
- **The floor is task 11.110's and it has already been narrowed once**, by task 11.148, to say it
  governs the default text size only. **This finding is at the default text size, so that
  narrowing does not help here** — do not read it as cover.
- **Measure the sum, not the change.** The instruments exist and must not be rebuilt:
  `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md`, *The Text-Size Instruments That Already Exist* — the overflow
  collector names the offending widget, and the ladder prints the body height at each stop.
  **Report the band with zero, one, two and three job cards, with the band up and down.**
- **Do not solve it by capping downloads.** Three concurrent downloads is a thing a person chose;
  **the screen's job is to show them, not to prevent them.**
- **Watch it fail:** an assertion that the clear band holds its floor with three job cards and the
  warning up. **It must go red today.**

- **Acceptance:** the band holds its floor in the three-cards-plus-warning case, or the states where
  it cannot are named with what a person sees there; the remedy is one decision in one place with
  its reason; the sum is measured across the card counts; and the failing case was watched.


### Task 11.163 — The server notices a pinned row and the command Michael runs does not ask
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-05.** `scripts/operator_status.sh` now asks a fourth question,
`_question_pinned_rows`, on the same `docker compose exec postgres psql` path question 3 already
uses — counting `revision_anomalies` (task 11.159's register) and separately counting rows whose
`observed_as = 'blocking'`, the ones caught only because a later push lost to them. The header,
the `_boundary` text, the `_identity` text and the summary block all now say "four questions."
**The exit status is unchanged by design and the file says so three times** — in the header (the
new §4.30 paragraph), in `_question_pinned_rows`'s own comment, and beside the `$ALL` calculation,
which never includes `$PINNED_ROWS_VERDICT`. `server/test/security/operator_status_test.dart`
gained a fourth-question group (35 tests total, all passing) including a live-exit test:
`status(pins: 'found')` still exits 0. **Watched both ways against a real stack**, not just the
stub: brought up `postgres`+`server` with `docker compose up -d --build`, ran the command clean,
inserted a synthetic row directly into `revision_anomalies`, re-ran and saw it named ("Rows
carrying an unexplainable revision: 1", exit stayed governed by the other three questions, not
this one), deleted the row, re-ran and saw the clean sentence again. Stack torn down afterward
(`docker compose down -v`).

**Original status, retained below for record:** Not started. **Above the line, and it is small.**
Task 11.159 built a detector whose output is currently readable only through a console that is
off by default.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** The change is one function on an existing seam. **The care is in a
489-line script and a 542-line test that asserts several of its sentences.**
**Depends on:** 11.159, Done, which built the detector and said plainly that nobody would look.

**The finding, in 11.159's own words.** The server records every row carrying a `revision` no honest
edit can overtake. **The only way to read that record is `GET /diagnostics/revision-anomalies` — a
console §4.10 keeps off by default.** `scripts/operator_status.sh` asks three questions and knows
nothing about this one.

> **This project's oldest rule is that a check which cannot distinguish success from its own failure
> is not a check. A detector nobody reads is the next station along that line.** 11.159 was right
> not to widen its own scope into a 489-line script; it is right that this closes the loop.

- **The seam already exists — use it, do not invent one.** A fourth `_question_` function on the same
  `docker compose exec postgres psql` path question 3 already uses.
- **Three things change besides the function, and missing one leaves the script lying about itself:**
  the header's *"three questions"*, the summary block, and
  `server/test/security/operator_status_test.dart`, which asserts several of those sentences.
  **A script that says it asks three questions and asks four is a document describing code it does
  not match.**
- **Say what the answer looks like when there is nothing to report**, and make that the common case
  reading well. **An operator command whose clean state is noisy trains somebody to skim it.**
- **Do not make it fail.** A pinned row is an accepted risk under §4.30, recorded rather than
  refused. **This question reports; it does not change the command's exit status** — say so in the
  script where somebody would otherwise add it.
- **Watch it fail:** plant a pinned row, run the command, see it named. Then remove it and see the
  question report clean.

- **Acceptance:** the command asks four questions and says so everywhere it counts them; the clean
  case reads well; the exit status is unchanged and that is stated in the file; and both the
  reporting and the clean case were watched.


### Task 11.164 — A viewer at the largest text size still sees what looks like a crash
**Status:** **Done, 2026-09-05.** The cheap question was the whole answer: the viewer's lock
sentence held no control, only an explanation, so it moved out of the pinned "Draft autosaves" /
Save bar (`observation_logging_screen.dart`) and into the scrolling form, right where it used to

moved. Watched red first: with the ladder's viewer ceiling manually raised to AX5 in
`record_screen_space_budget_test.dart`, the unmodified screen struck a 32-pixel `RenderFlex`
overflow with a 0px form viewport at AX5 for a viewer, before any production code changed. After the

full suite (2263 tests) is green. **Model:** Sonnet, medium — as planned.
**Depends on:** 11.149, Done, which fixed the shell and left this deliberately because it is the
screen's layout rather than the shell's.

**The finding, from 11.149's own report.** After the shell was bounded, the Record screen is clean

> **A viewer is somebody on the project who can look but not record.** They have done nothing

> they need it. **What they get is a screen that looks broken, on the one screen whose whole job is

- **The obvious question first, because it may be the whole answer: does that sentence need to be

### Task 11.165 — Every budget written for a child of a `Column` is a comment, not a constraint
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-05.** The set was derived rather than listed: a brace-matching scan of
`lib/` found **138 `Column`s and 591 direct children**, and two passes over them — one for a height
bound written at the *call site*, one for a child whose own widget class carries bound vocabulary —
plus a hand read of all four `SPACE BUDGET` headers. **Eleven distinct budgets exist. Nine are
enforced, one is out of the class and reported as a note, and exactly one was inoperative.** The
inoperative one is the Record screen's pinned SAVE bar: rule 3 of that file's budget says the bar
"is a note and one button, and it stays that", and **nothing could refuse a line added to it** — the
bar is a non-flex child of a `Column`, so it took what it wanted and the scrolling form got the
remainder. Measured with both shell banners live on a 6.1-inch phone, the bar takes **86 logical
pixels of a 570-pixel body at the default text size and 222 of 533 at AX5 (42%)**, and before task
11.149 fixed the shell it took 222 against a body of 56, leaving the form a viewport of **zero**.
It is now laid out inside `kRecordPinnedBarShare` (half the body); the Save button is served from
that budget first and **never sheds**, and the "Draft autosaves" note stands down whole if what is
left cannot hold it. **Nothing a person sees moved** — the bound binds at no text size today
(form/bar heights are identical at all nine stops). 11.149's render object was lifted out of
`shell_banner.dart` into `lib/widgets/budgeted_column.dart` as `BudgetedColumn`, so the remedy is
copied rather than re-invented and there is one of it; it gained a `layoutOrder`, because *the order
things are read in and the order they may be taken away in are different questions*. Watched
refusing three ways: with the bound removed, a 560-pixel surface at AX5 gave the bar 222 pixels
against a 154-pixel form with the note still drawn; with it in place the note stands down; and an
experimental 120-pixel block added to the bar was **capped at exactly 267 of 533 pixels** instead of
reaching 342. **One near-miss worth recording:** the first version of the note measured
`preferredLineHeight` and set `maxLines: 1` — and "Draft autosaves" wraps to two lines at the
accessibility sizes, so the widget written to prevent a silent clip introduced one. It was caught by
the existing ladder going red at six stops. 2273 tests pass. **Out of scope and named, not fixed:**
the Main Map's 96-pixel clear-band floor is enforced by a test assertion and not by its layout — the
same shape as what task 11.162 made structural on the Offline Data Map — but it is a `Stack`, not a
`Column`, so it is a different task.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** Finding the shape is mechanical. **Deciding which of them actually
matter, rather than converting every `Column` in the app into a render object, is the work.**
**Depends on:** 11.149, Done, which found the class by writing one of these bounds and measuring it
do nothing.

**The finding, and 11.149 caught it on itself.** A Flutter `Column` hands every non-flex child
**unbounded** height, so a child cannot discover how much room the parent has. **11.149 wrote the
bound "the banners get at most a quarter of the frame" first, and measured it doing nothing at
all.** It is now enforced by a small render object that lays each banner into what the budget has
left. **The Offline Data Map's top row was a second instance of the same shape.**

> **Two found by accident, in two different files, in one task.** That is the signature of a class
> rather than a coincidence — and every instance is **silent**: the bound reads as enforced, the
> tests pass, and nothing says no until a widget grows.

- **Enumerate, do not guess.** Find where a size budget is expressed for a child of a `Column` and
  **say for each whether anything enforces it.** A hand-listed few is this project's most-repeated
  defect; **derive the set if you can, and if you cannot, say what your enumeration cannot see.**
- **Do not convert everything.** Most `Column` children have no budget and need none. **The
  deliverable is knowing which budgets are inoperative**, not a refactor.
- **The two already fixed are the worked examples** — the shell's banner bound and the Offline Data
  Map's top row. **Copy their remedy rather than inventing a third.**
- **Rank what you find by what a person would see.** A silently-unenforced bound on furniture nobody
  looks at is a note; one on a screen's subject is a defect.
- **Watch it fail:** for anything you change, the bound must be watched refusing something it
  previously allowed.

- **Acceptance:** the set is derived or its horizon stated; each instance has a verdict — enforced,
  inoperative-and-fixed, or inoperative-and-harmless-with-a-reason; nothing was converted that
  needed no budget; and each fix was watched refusing.


### Task 11.166 — What the budget sweep could not reach: the width axis, and a floor in a `Stack`
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-05.** **The width axis has seven budgets and every one of them can be
refused — zero inoperative.** 11.165's scan was recovered and both axes now live in
`scripts/derive_space_budgets.py`, which reproduces 11.165's numbers exactly (138 `Column`s, 591
children) and finds **75 `Row`s and 213 direct children, 69 of them flex or spread**; three passes —
a bound at the call site (2 hits), a child class carrying budget vocabulary (5), and a budget
written only as prose (21 comment blocks, 5 of them about width) — resolve to seven distinct sites.
All seven are enforced by a `Flexible`, an `Expanded`, a `FittedBox`, or a `ConstrainedBox` taking
its width from a `LayoutBuilder`; the eighth candidate, `shell_banner.dart`'s `minWidth`, is a 44pt
touch-target floor and out of the class. **The ranking argument was sound and the answer is still
zero**, and the reason is visible in the sites themselves: every horizontal overflow in this
project's history was fixed by *flexing the child*, which is enforcement — the width axis has been
swept five times already, one defect at a time, by tasks 11.102, 11.133, 11.147, 11.149 and 11.162.
**Part two is a reasoned decline on the layout half and a fix on the other half.** The Main Map's
floor stays an assertion, because **a budget can only say no by taking something away and this
screen has nothing it may take** — every overlay is a licence condition, a control, or a warning
about state, and a warning withdrawn silently is worse than the failure being prevented. That is
now written into the file's SPACE BUDGET as a decision. **What was made structural instead is the
check's own scope, and it was already wrong:** both map budget tests measured a hand-written list
of overlay keys, and the Main Map's legend card has no key and was in neither list — so the floor
was asserted only for the state where somebody has the legend switched off, and a missing overlay
makes the band read *larger*. `clearBandOverStack` derives the set from the `Stack`'s own children,
refuses to report a band if it derives none, and was **watched refusing**: an injected 160-pixel
unkeyed overlay took the derived band from 229 to 85 and went red where the hand list did not move
at all. **Two corrections to this entry's own premises**, both measured: the floor does **not** hold
at every text size — 229/191/152/134/102 up to AX1, then 30 at AX2 and 8 at AX5, which the test has
recorded all along — and the tightest state on the ordinary slider is **105 against 96, nine
pixels**, with tiles failing on a new project. The Offline Data Map keeps its hand list, with the
reason written beside it: its overlays live inside one `Positioned.fill`, so the derivation would
report zero there — loudly, not silently. 2274 tests pass.
**Discovered, not fixed:** `log_screen.dart`'s three `SizedBox(width: 52)` sort/filter labels are a
fixed width with growing text in it; measured in isolation the word wraps and the box reaches 102
logical pixels tall at 2.0× and 306 at 3.0× in `flutter_test`'s font. A fixed size is never
inoperative — it pays on the other axis instead — so it is a different class and wants its own
task.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** The width half is the same derivation 11.165 already wrote, on the other
axis. **The Main Map half is a design question and is the part that needs judgement.**
**Depends on:** 11.165, Done, which swept the height axis and stated both of these as its own
horizon rather than leaving them to be discovered.

**Two halves, merged because they are the same sentence — a budget nothing can refuse — and because
they are both what one task declared it could not see.**

#### Part one — the width axis, and the reason to expect something here

**A `Row` hands a non-flex child unbounded *width* for exactly the reason a `Column` hands it
unbounded height.** 11.165 swept height only, because both worked examples were on that axis. It
found **one inoperative budget in eleven.**

> **The ranking argument, from this project's own history: almost every overflow anybody has
> actually seen in TriTrack has been horizontal.** The Navigate row (11.133, and five wrong causes
> before it), the tag-name width (11.102), the Position controls row running off by 36 to 137
> pixels, the coverage legend's labels, the map buttons pushed off the right edge. **The height
> sweep found one. The width axis is where the symptoms have been.**

- **Reuse 11.165's derivation rather than writing a third one.** It scanned two ways — a bound
  written at the call site, and a child whose own widget class carries budget vocabulary — plus a
  hand read of every `SPACE BUDGET` header. **Point it at `Row` and report the same shape of
  answer: how many, how many enforced, and what the enumeration cannot see.**
- **Say the count even if it is zero.** *Zero measured* is a result; *zero assumed* is not.

#### Part two — the Main Map's clear band, where the remedy from 11.162 does not apply

Its 96-pixel floor is enforced by an assertion in `map_screen_space_budget_test.dart` **and by
nothing in the layout** — the shape task 11.162 made structural on the Offline Data Map.
**11.165 was right to leave it: the Main Map is a `Stack`, not a `Column`, so a `SizedBox` reserve
is not the remedy and the design question is real.**

- **This is a note, not a defect. The floor holds at every text size today**, and the task must not
  report otherwise.
- **The question is what would say no**, per the rule 11.149 established: a number in a test and a
  number the layout enforces are different strengths, and only the second survives somebody adding
  a widget. **On a `Stack` that may mean something other than a reserve** — say what, or say that
  the assertion is the honest ceiling here and why.
- **Declining part two in writing is a legitimate outcome**, with the reason. **Declining part one
  is not** — it is a derivation, and the answer is a number.

- **Acceptance:** the width axis is derived with a count and a stated horizon; every inoperative
  width budget has a verdict; the Main Map floor is made structural or the reason it cannot be is
  written down; and anything changed was watched refusing something it previously allowed.

ambient text scale**, with the text forced to a single line (`softWrap: false`) — the label now
grows sideways, into the same row's own horizontal `SingleChildScrollView`, instead of wrapping and
growing the box downward. **The decision:** grow sideways rather than truncate, become an icon, or
move into a menu — the row already scrolls horizontally for the chips, so giving the label the same
room costs nothing a person would notice, and unlike truncation it never hides which control they're
looking at. **The alignment question:** all three instances (two `Sort` bars — team and personal —
and one `Filter` bar) call the same width computation, so "Filter" and the "Sort" label stacked
directly under it stay pinned to the same left edge at every scale, not just the default — this is
now asserted, not assumed. **The row, not just the label in isolation:** measured on both tabs, at
all twelve stops of the iOS text-size ladder; it holds clean at every one, ordinary slider and
accessibility sizes alike — no truncation was needed.
**One real bug found and fixed on the way, of the class this project keeps finding:** the first
version measured the label with a bare `TextStyle`, not merged onto the ambient
`DefaultTextStyle` the way `Text` itself renders it (task 11.148's exact rule) — it silently
clipped "Filter" to half its height starting at AX2, caught by the new test before this entry was
written. Fixed by measuring with `DefaultTextStyle.of(context).style.merge(_style)`.
**Watched failing:** `test/features/more/log_screen_sort_filter_label_test.dart` was run against
the pre-fix code and failed — 318 logical pixels tall at AX5 against an under-60px ceiling, in the
same shape as 11.166's 306px isolation measurement — then passed once the fix was restored. 36
new tests, all passing; the full pre-existing `log_screen_test.dart` suite (already covering this
screen) still passes unchanged.
**Discovered, not fixed — out of scope for this task:** `log_screen.dart`'s own `TabBar` (`Tab(text:
'Log', ...)` / `Tab(text: 'Team', ...)`) overflows its fixed-height `Column` by about a pixel from
AX3 upward — a pre-existing defect, unrelated to the sort/filter labels, in a different row. The new
test explicitly silences overflow that doesn't trace back to the widget under test so this doesn't
mask a real regression there, but it is not fixed here. **Ask the planning session to give this its
own task** (a `TabBar` label overflowing at large accessibility text sizes) rather than leaving it
to be rediscovered.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** One row of three labels. **The judgement is what a sort control looks
like when its label no longer fits beside it**, which is small but is a decision.
**Depends on:** 11.166, Done, which measured it while sweeping something else and correctly said it
was not that sweep's class.

**The finding, measured by 11.166.** `log_screen.dart` has three `SizedBox(width: 52)` sort/filter
labels. **The width is fixed and the text inside it grows.** Measured in isolation at a phone's
width: the word wraps and the box reaches **102 logical pixels tall at 2.0× and 306 at 3.0×.** In
`flutter_test`'s font, which is about twice Roboto's width — **so on a device it begins higher up
the ladder, not lower.**

> **This is not the class tasks 11.165 and 11.166 swept, and the distinction is the useful part.**
> A budget that nothing enforces is *inoperative* — it never binds. **A fixed size always binds.**
> What it does instead is **pay on the other axis, silently**: the width holds, and the height goes
> wherever the wrapped text sends it.

- **Decide what a sort control does when its label will not fit beside it.** Wrap and grow, truncate
  with the full text elsewhere, become an icon with the label underneath, or move into a menu — **any
  of these is defensible; pick one and write the reason.**
- **Look at what the same row does at the same sizes**, not just the three boxes. 11.166 measured
  them **in isolation**, which is the right first measurement and not the whole one. **Report the
  row.**
- **Do not simply remove the fixed width.** It is presumably there to keep the three controls
  aligned; **say what alignment you are preserving, or say that it did not matter and how you
  checked.**
- **Watch it fail:** an assertion on that row at the text sizes where it breaks, red today.

- **Acceptance:** the row holds at every stop on the ordinary slider; the accessibility sizes are
  either held or named with what a person sees; the alignment question is answered either way; and
  the failing case was watched.

### Task 11.171 — Seven controls that live inside a caller which could stop calling them, and a runner nothing scopes
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-06.** **Four of the seven guarded, three left with a measured reason.**
The four are `gate-instruments.yml`'s `GATE_SMOKE_SELFTEST=1` step (item 7), `build-check.yml`'s two
merged-manifest inspections (item 6), `verify_c3_cleartext_defaults_stack.sh`'s call to the check it
exists for (item 4), and `run_offline_suite.sh`'s W-6 port probe (item 5) — all four as new groups in
`server/test/security/shipped_defaults_test.dart`, copying task 11.127's shape, no new instrument.
**The three left are items 1–3, `gate_smoke_test.sh`'s `--selftest` line and its two
`run_detection_proof` calls, and the reason is a measurement rather than a budget.** That file
already derives `DERIVED_WIRE` on every invocation and fails if any wire-speaking `scripts/*.py`
instrument is not run; measured 2026-09-06, **that derivation covers 11 of the 22 lines in the file
that run something.** The other 11 unguarded lines include `backup_restore_drill`,
`verify_deployment_refusal_matrix`, `verify_i1_source_identity` and the bare
`verify_instrument_unchecked_returns` as well as the three named — so **naming three of eleven in a
Dart test would assert that a detection proof matters more than the drill it is a proof about**, and
would put the list in a different file from the derivation that already answers the question for the
other half. The repair is to widen `DERIVED_WIRE` to the shell instruments inside
`gate_smoke_test.sh` — one change rather than eleven assertions — and it needs its own task.
**Part two is done and paid for:** `run_e2e_tests.sh` now writes a JSON report and runs
`assert_suite_scope.py --no-skips` over `test/e2e`, its verdict exits the script, and the run ledger
records a scope failure as red rather than green. **Verified by two real end-to-end runs** (2026-09-06,
both green, 16 of 16 files and 75 tests with none skipped) and **watched going red** by running the
suite with `--run-skipped` dropped: `flutter test` printed "All tests skipped." and **exited 0**, and
the scope check refused it by name. It is now the fourth entry in 11.127's derived caller set.
All eleven sabotages were watched producing the right red.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** Mechanical individually. **The judgement is which of the seven are
worth guarding and which are noise**, and a sweep that guards everything is worse than the gap.
**Depends on:** 11.127, Done, which surveyed twelve call sites and closed one.

**Two halves, merged because they are the same file and the same sentence — a check whose
*invocation* nothing guards.**

#### Part one — the seven, listed by name in Phase 11's Discovered Scope

Task 11.127 closed `assert_suite_scope.py`'s three callers and left the rest. **Two of the seven are
the detection proofs task 11.125 added to `gate_smoke_test.sh` — one line each.** One is
`gate-instruments.yml`'s `GATE_SMOKE_SELFTEST=1` step, **which is the abort proof for all eleven
wire-speaking instruments** — delete that line and eleven instruments lose their only evidence at
once.

- **Rank before guarding.** The `GATE_SMOKE_SELFTEST=1` step covers eleven instruments and is
  obviously worth it; a one-line proof covering one thing may not be. **Say which you guarded and
  why the others were left.**
- **Copy the shape 11.127 used**, which is `shipped_defaults_test.dart`'s group. **Do not invent a
  fourth instrument for this.**

#### Part two — `run_e2e_tests.sh`, which is the fourth caller

It runs `flutter test test/e2e --tags e2e --run-skipped` with **nothing asserting what the run
reached.** **Drop `--run-skipped` and the default tag skip takes every test out: the command prints
*"All tests skipped."* and exits 0** — and the run ledger that script keeps would record it as a
green run.

- **`assert_suite_scope.py --no-skips` is the remedy and it already exists.** This is the fourth
  caller it should have had.
- **11.127 did not do it because it changes a script Michael runs by hand and needs a full e2e run
  to verify.** **That verification is this task's cost and must actually be paid** — a scope check
  added without a real run is the thing it is guarding against.

- **Acceptance:** each of the seven has a verdict, guarded or left with a reason; `run_e2e_tests.sh`
  asserts its scope and was verified by a real e2e run; nothing new was invented where

### Task 11.172 — The gate derives half of itself, and the other half includes two whole drills
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-05.** **22 of the 22 lines in `gate_smoke_test.sh` that run something
are now derived** — up from 11. The predicate had to be added, as the entry warned: every `*.sh`
and `*.py` under `scripts/` (48 files) carries exactly one `# gate-instrument:` line naming what
this gate runs it as, or `none - <reason>`, and **a file carrying neither fails the run.** It is
opt-*out*, which is the only direction where forgetting is caught: 19 files declare the 22 names,
29 declare themselves out with a reason. Three properties beyond "the name is listed": the command
that ran under a name **must mention the file claiming it** (a declaration checked against the act,
not against its own wording); a name must be claimed by exactly one file; and **deriving nothing
fails**, with checks 2-4 short-circuited so a broken scan reports one finding rather than 22.
A new `GATE_SMOKE_COVERAGE_ONLY=1` mode records what the file would run, runs both derivations, and
runs **nothing else** — no Docker, no stack, no control — so the derivation can be watched failing
in about a second instead of only inside a twenty-minute gate; it says "NOTHING WAS RUN" in those
words. **31 sabotages, each producing the intended red and no other**: all 22 run lines deleted one
at a time, plus a missing declaration, a duplicated one, `none` with no reason, `none` with a
two-word reason, a drill declared out while still run, a renamed declaration, a name run by a
different script, an empty scan, and every declaration lost at once. Also fixed on the way: the
existing wire derivation's failures could not fail a `GATE_SMOKE_SELFTEST=1` run, because
`FAILED_ANY` is always 1 in that mode by design — both derivations now report through one flag that
the self-test reads.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** Widening a derivation is small. **Finding a predicate the shell
instruments share is not, and the honest expectation is that you will have to add one rather than
find one.**
**Depends on:** 11.171, Done, which measured this and correctly refused to guard three of eleven
from outside.

**The finding, measured rather than assumed.** `gate_smoke_test.sh` already derives which
wire-speaking Python instruments must run and **refuses an empty derivation** — good, and it is
**11 of the 22 lines in that file that run something.** The other eleven are the shell instruments
and the detection proofs. **Delete any one of those lines and the gate is green having stopped
running it.**

> **Two of the eleven are whole drills rather than proofs: `backup_restore_drill` and
> `verify_deployment_refusal_matrix`.** The first is the one that says a backup can actually be
> restored. **Michael's beta scheduler failed silently from 31 August and was found by somebody
> asking, not by anything telling him** — that is the cost of this class already paid once.

- **The repair belongs inside `gate_smoke_test.sh`, not in a test naming a subset from outside.**
  11.171 explains why and its reasoning stands: **naming three of eleven elsewhere would assert that
  a detection proof matters more than the drill it is a proof about**, and would split one file's
  answer across two files.
- **Expect to add the predicate, not to find it.** The Python instruments are derivable because they
  share an import. **The shell ones have no common anything** — 11.171 says so plainly. A marker
  comment, a naming convention, a manifest the script reads: **any is fine; inventing one is the
  task, and it must be something a new instrument cannot silently omit.**
- **Keep the property the existing derivation already has: it refuses an empty result.** Whatever
  the widened version derives, **deriving zero must be a failure**, per the rule task 11.160
  established.
- **Watch it fail, once per line if that is what it takes.** 11.171 ran **eleven sabotages, each
  producing the intended failure and no other.** That is the standard this task inherits.

- **Acceptance:** every line in `gate_smoke_test.sh` that runs something is either derived or
  declared with a reason; deriving nothing fails; each new coverage was watched going red; and the
  count of covered lines is reported against the count of lines that run something.


### Task 11.173 — The question "is the gate still running everything" costs a second and is asked nightly
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-05.** `GATE_SMOKE_COVERAGE_ONLY=1` now runs on every push and every pull
request, as a second job — `gate-coverage` — in `.github/workflows/server-suite.yml`. **It is in
that workflow rather than in `gate-instruments.yml` because that one is path-filtered**
(`server/**`, `packages/**`, `scripts/**`, `proxy/**`, the compose files), so a commit deleting a
`run_instrument` line while touching nothing else would not start it; `server-suite.yml` has a bare
`push:`, and it is also the workflow that runs the guard on the new step, so the step and its guard
go red in the same run. **The guard is a new group in
`server/test/security/shipped_defaults_test.dart`** — the same file and the same shape task 11.171
used for `GATE_SMOKE_SELFTEST=1`, not a fourth instrument. It asserts 11.171's four things (exactly
one step sets the variable; that step runs `scripts/gate_smoke_test.sh`; the script still implements
the variable; the events in the step's `if:` are declared triggers) **plus two this task needed**:
that the hosting workflow's `push:` trigger has *no* `paths:` filter — "every push" is the whole of
what was added and a `paths:` line would silently undo it — and that the run's own output cannot
read as a gate result. **Which workflow hosts the step is derived, not named**, and an empty
derivation fails with its own sentence. **Cost: 1.35 s on a Mac, 195 ms in a bare `ubuntu:24.04`
container with no Docker, Python or network** — which is also how it was shown to need nothing but
bash, grep and the checkout. **Neither is a runner number**; the step times itself and prints the
milliseconds into the run summary on every run, so the first push measures it. **Eleven sabotages
were watched going red** — deleting a `# gate-instrument:` declaration and deleting a
`run_instrument` line (both fail the CI step itself, exit 1), and nine against the guard. **One
defect found on the way, in the guard's own parser:** splitting the workflow into steps "up to the
next step" made the last step of `server-suite` swallow the prose header of the job below it, which
names the variable — 11.84's delimit-by-the-next-one class, on YAML. Comment lines are now dropped
before both the step and the job split.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** Adding the step is five minutes. **Guarding it is the task**, and doing
it the quick way reproduces the defect the last three tasks closed.
**Depends on:** 11.172, Done, which built the mode and deliberately did not wire it.

**The finding, and 11.172's reason for stopping is the shape of this task.**
`GATE_SMOKE_COVERAGE_ONLY=1` runs `gate_smoke_test.sh`'s derivations and nothing else — **no Docker,
no stack, no instrument — in about a second.** So *"is this gate still running all 22 of its
instruments"* could be answered **on every push**, instead of only when the gate itself runs
(nightly, and on pushes touching `scripts/`).

> **11.172 declined to wire it, and was right: adding a CI step is adding another call site nothing
> guards** — which is precisely the class tasks 11.171 and 11.172 spent themselves closing. **A
> coverage check protected by an unguarded workflow step is the joke telling itself.**

- **Wire it and guard it in the same task, or do neither.** The shape already exists —
  `server/test/security/shipped_defaults_test.dart`'s group, which 11.171 used for
  `GATE_SMOKE_SELFTEST=1`. **Copy it. Do not invent a fourth instrument.**
- **Guard the same four things 11.171 guarded**, because they were each earned: exactly one step
  sets the variable; that step runs the gate script; **the script still implements the variable**
  (a rename would make the step run something else and pass); and **the events in the step's `if:`
  are events the workflow actually declares a trigger for.**
- **Do not let the cheap mode's output read like a gate result.** 11.172 made it print *"NOTHING WAS
  RUN…"* deliberately. **Whatever surfaces in CI must carry that too** — a green tick beside the
  word "gate" in a run that exercised no control is the lying-instrument class arriving by a new
  door.
- **Say what it costs on the runner**, measured. A second locally is not a second in CI, and this
  would run on every push.
- **Watch it fail:** delete a `# gate-instrument:` declaration and see the new CI step go red.

- **Acceptance:** the coverage mode runs on every push; its workflow step is guarded the way
  `GATE_SMOKE_SELFTEST=1`'s is; its output cannot be mistaken for a gate result; the runner cost is
  measured and reported; and the failing case was watched.


### Task 11.174 — The suite-scope check counts a platform-restricted file as a file that went missing
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-06.** `scripts/assert_suite_scope.py` now reads each `*_test.dart` file's
own `@TestOn` annotation and excuses a file only on the platforms that annotation excludes —
**derived from the file, nothing declared anywhere.** On Linux the one such file is excused and
named in the log line (*"1 not loadable on this host by its own @TestOn ... needs mac-os"*); on
macOS it is demanded like any other. **The parser's horizon is stated in the file**: one bare quoted
operating-system name and nothing else — every other `@TestOn` form (`&&`, `||`, `!`, `?:`, and the
non-OS variables `vm`/`browser`/`js`/…) **fails the run loudly**, watched on four forms. A file the
parser excuses that then loads anyway also fails the run, because that means the parser is wrong.
**Both failing cases were watched**, against the real 260-suite report from a full local run:
a genuinely missing file still reddens a Linux run, and the macOS file failing to load reddens a
macOS run. **The macOS run itself is a simulation of the runner, not a runner** — the report was
taken from a real `flutter test` on Michael's Mac (260/260 suites, 2323 tests, green) and the Linux
cases were produced by forcing the host platform and removing that suite's events. ~~**The Linux gate
itself has not been re-run; that needs a push.**~~ **Confirmed on the runner 2026-09-06: Michael
pushed and every check is green.** Nothing automated runs the macOS file — recorded in
`UNEXERCISED_CONTROLS.md`, since the repository's only macOS job is `workflow_dispatch`-only and
runs `flutter build`, never `flutter test`.
~~**Above the line. It is red on `main` right now**, on the gate that runs on
every push.~~
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** The fix is small. **Choosing between deriving the annotation and
declaring the file is the task**, and one of those answers is a hand-kept list.
**Depends on:** 11.156, which built the scope check, and 11.112, which wrote the file.

**The finding, from the first push after 11.156 shipped — the check working, on its first real
exercise.** `offline-suite.yml` reports:
*"1 test file(s) under test were never loaded by the run:
`features/more/server_config_screen_macos_test.dart`"* — **259 suites loaded of 260 on disk**, with
0 undeclared skips.

**The file is `@TestOn('mac-os')`.** On a Linux runner it is **not skipped — it is never loaded**,
which is exactly the quantity the scope check counts. **Task 11.112 anticipated this in the file's
own header**, which says that runner *"reports this file as not applicable, never as passing"* —
**but nothing told the scope check that.**

> **This is not a defect in the test and not a defect in the check's intent.** 11.156 asserted the
> declared *set* of skips rather than a count, deliberately. **A file that cannot load on this
> platform is a third category it does not model** — neither run nor skipped.

- **Derive it, do not declare it.** `@TestOn(...)` is a library annotation **in the file itself**,
  so the checker can read it and exclude the file **on the platforms it excludes** — and still
  demand it on the platforms it does not. **A declared-exclusions list is the hand-kept-list defect
  this project has hit more than any other**, and here the truth is one line inside the file.
- **The exclusion must be platform-aware, not blanket.** *"This file is allowed to be missing"* is
  wrong; *"this file is allowed to be missing where its own annotation says it cannot run"* is
  right. **On a macOS run it must still be demanded.**
- **Say what the enumeration cannot see.** `@TestOn` has expression forms beyond a bare platform
  name. **Support what the repository uses and fail loudly on a form you do not parse** — a
  `@TestOn` the checker silently misreads is the same defect one level down.
- **This file has never been exercised by any automated run.** 11.112 ran it by hand on a Mac.
  **Say whether anything now runs it**, and if the answer is nothing, that belongs in
  `UNEXERCISED_CONTROLS.md` rather than in a report.
- **Watch it fail:** the scope check must still go red for a file that is genuinely missing, and
  must go red on a macOS run if this file does not load there.

- **Acceptance:** the offline suite is green on a Linux runner; the exclusion is derived from the
  file rather than listed; it is platform-aware in both directions; the parser's horizon is stated;
  and both failing cases were watched.


### Task 11.175 — Three gate instruments are red because Alpine rebuilt a package, and one may not be
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-06.** `server/backup/Dockerfile` now pins `'age=~1.3.1'` and
`'minisign=~0.12'` — apk's fuzzy match, which accepts any *packaging revision* of that upstream
version and refuses 1.3.2 or 1.4.0, so an upstream upgrade is still a deliberate edit to that line
while a rebuild is not an outage. **Both packages were changed**; `minisign` was the same shape and
is now out of the same trap. The semantics were measured rather than assumed (`age=~1` resolves,
`age=~1.4` is refused, `minisign=~0.1` does not match 0.12). The trade-off is written in the file:
the exact bytes are no longer pinned, and pinning `FROM` by digest was rejected because **it would
not have helped at all** — apk fetches the index over the network at build time, so a frozen base
image still resolves against today's rolling repository. **The image builds, and all four
instruments were run locally on macOS and all four exit 0** with real checks (42 / 17 / 11 / 7).
**The fourth was downstream of the same cause, confirmed rather than assumed** — and the mechanism
is in `verify_h6_archive_forgery.sh:88-103`, whose postgres readiness probe runs `psql` *inside the
backup container*, so an unbuildable backup image makes every probe fail and the script blames
postgres. **That misleading message is a separate finding and is in Discovered Scope**, and it is now
**task 11.176**. **Confirmed on the machine that was red:** Michael pushed 2026-09-06 and the
gate-instruments workflow came back green on the Linux runner, which is the observation Claude Code
correctly declined to claim from a macOS run.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** Making it build again is one line. **Choosing *which* one line is a
§3.8 dependency decision**, and the wrong choice buys the same outage again on a later date.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Diagnosed from the CI log by the planning session, 2026-09-06.**

**The cause, read from the run rather than inferred.**

```
ERROR: unable to select packages:
  age-1.3.1-r6:
    breaks: world[age=1.3.1-r5]
```

`server/backup/Dockerfile:24` pins `apk add --no-cache age=1.3.1-r5 minisign=0.12-r2`. **Alpine has
rebuilt that package as `-r6` and removed `r5` from the index**, so the image cannot build. Three
instruments fail because each brings up a stack that builds it: **`backup_restore_drill`,
`verify_c3_cleartext_defaults`, `verify_i1_source_identity`.**

> **No commit caused this and Michael should not go looking for one.** `git log origin/main..main --
> server/backup/Dockerfile` is **empty** — the file has not changed since 30 August, and it was
> green after that. **It broke on the calendar, on somebody else's schedule.**

**The fourth failure is NOT established as the same cause.** `verify_h6_archive_forgery` reports
**`HARNESS ERROR postgres never came up`** — a different message, on a truncated console excerpt.
**It is plausibly downstream of the same build failure and that is a hypothesis, not a diagnosis.**
The full per-instrument logs were uploaded as the run's `gate-instrument-logs.zip` artifact.

- **Fix the pin, re-run, and let the fourth answer itself.** If `verify_h6_archive_forgery` goes
  green with the build fixed, it was downstream. **If it still fails, that is a separate finding and
  it gets its own entry** — do not fold it into this one to make a tidy story.
- **The decision, and it is §3.8's rather than this task's to invent alone.** `1.3.1` is a version;
  **`-r5` is a revision of the *packaging*, which a rolling repository replaces rather than
  accumulates.** Three defensible answers, each giving something up:
  **pin the version only** (survives rebuilds, accepts whatever build the index holds);
  **pin the base image by digest** (fully reproducible, freezes security updates until somebody
  bumps it); **vendor the binaries with a checksum** (most reproducible, most work, and a new thing
  to keep current). **Pick one, implement it, and write the trade-off into the Dockerfile beside the
  line** — §3.8 says every dependency is pinned *and reviewed*, and the review is the sentence.
- **`minisign=0.12-r2` is the same shape and is not yet broken.** **Fix both or say why not** — a
  repair that leaves an identical time bomb beside it is half a repair.
- **Watch it fail:** whatever you choose, demonstrate that the image builds and that the three
  instruments pass, and say which of them you actually ran.

- **Acceptance:** the image builds; the three instruments pass; the fourth is either explained by the
  same cause or written up separately; `minisign` is addressed alongside `age`; and the pinning
  choice and its cost are written in the Dockerfile.

### Task 11.182 — The safety net is not installed, and the check that caught what it missed is red
**Status:** **Done, 2026-09-06.** Both declarations written; **the hypothesis was neither (A) nor
(B)**. The hook was invoked, read its payload correctly, and ran the suite for 88 seconds — **task
11.181's `time git commit` measurement was of the wrong quantity**, because a `PreToolUse` hook
completes *before* the command being timed starts, so `time` around a commit is structurally
incapable of containing it. **The 0.088 seconds was the commit; the hook was never in the number.**
The silent exit 0 on an unreadable payload was a real defect and is fixed and watched refusing
anyway. **No git `pre-commit` fallback was needed** — `.claude/settings.json` is committed, so the
hook has no install step to forget.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** The red is a two-line fix. **The hook is a decision about how this
repository is set up on a machine, and `.git/` is not committed**, so there is an install story to
get right rather than a file to write.
**Depends on:** 11.180, which built the script. **Diagnosed from the run logs by the planning
session, 2026-09-07.**

#### 1. The red — two lines, and the check is working exactly as designed

**`gate-instruments` and the gate coverage job both fail for one cause, and it is not a regression in
anything they test.** Every one of the 23 instruments **passed**, both sabotage self-tests caught
their sabotage, and the server suite is green at 966 tests over 58 of 58 files with none skipped.

```
FAIL: scripts/lib/suite_verdict.py carries no '# gate-instrument:' line.
FAIL: scripts/pre_commit_suite.sh carries no '# gate-instrument:' line.
```

**Task 11.180 added both files and neither declares itself.** Every `*.sh` and `*.py` under
`scripts/` must carry `# gate-instrument: <name>` or `# gate-instrument: none - <why>` on line 2.
**Write the honest `none` reason for each** — one is a pre-commit runner, one is a library imported
rather than run — and copy the shape of the existing ones (`gate_c_baseline.py`'s is the closest).

> **The irony is the finding, and it should be written down rather than enjoyed.** **The task that
> built a pre-commit hook to stop red commits was itself the commit that turned CI red**, and its
> own hook could not have caught it *even if it had been running*: the hook runs `flutter test`, and
> this check runs in a workflow. **The local gate and the push gate cover different sets, and the
> difference between them is exactly where a red gets to live.**

#### 2. The hook never runs — measured, not suspected

**Task 11.181 was asked to report whether the hook fired and reported that it did not.** A `git
commit` through the Bash tool in a fresh window completed in **0.088 seconds**; the suite takes
**96**. **The script is not the problem** — invoked by hand with a commit payload it printed
`pre-commit suite: green: 2359 tests passed (15 skipped by tag) across all 264 test files` and
exited 0. **The wiring is broken, not the instrument.**

**Michael took the reading: `/hooks` lists `PreToolUse (1)`, so the configuration IS loaded.** See
2a below for what that leaves.

- **If it is approval, say so and say what the standing instruction is**, because an approval that
  every new window needs is a hook that will be off more often than on.
- **Otherwise build the fallback 11.180 already named: a real git `pre-commit` hook** calling
  `scripts/pre_commit_suite.sh`. **`.git/` is not committed and there is no `core.hooksPath` set
  today**, so the install story has to be real: a committed hook directory plus a one-line setup
  step, **a `SETUP_OWNERSHIP.md` row naming who owns it**, and — this is the part that matters —
  **something that can tell whether it is installed.** A setup step nobody can verify is the
  hand-kept class in a new costume.

#### 2a. What Michael's `/hooks` reading settles, and the two hypotheses left

**Michael ran `/hooks` on 2026-09-07 and reports `PreToolUse (1)` listed under *before tool
execution*.** So **the configuration is loaded.** It is not missing, not malformed, and not
unparsed. That kills the simplest explanation and leaves two, **both of which produce exactly the
0.088 seconds task 11.181 measured**:

- **(A) The hook is never invoked** for this commit — a matcher, ordering or approval condition.
- **(B) The hook IS invoked, cannot read its input, and exits 0 silently.**

> **(B) deserves suspicion before (A), because the script is built so that it cannot tell the
> difference.** Its payload reader is `except Exception: sys.exit(0)` with `2>/dev/null` on the
> end, and an unreadable payload yields an **empty** `tool_command`, which fails the "is this a
> commit?" grep, which exits 0. **A parse failure and "this Bash call was not a commit" are the same
> observable**, and the second happens hundreds of times a session, so the first would never be
> noticed. **This is the project's own cannot-distinguish-success-from-its-own-failure rule, in the
> instrument built to enforce discipline.**
>
> **The detection regex is not the suspect and was checked by the planning session rather than
> assumed** — it matches `git commit`, `git commit -q -F - -- <paths>`, `git add … && git commit`,
> `cd … && git commit -am`, `git -C … commit`, `git commit --amend`, and a heredoc `-m "$(cat <<EOF
> … EOF)"`. **Eight shapes, all matched. Do not spend time there.**

- **Separate (A) from (B) with one observable before changing anything.** Make the script record
  **every** invocation — one appended line saying what it saw and which branch it took, including
  *"payload unreadable"* and *"not a commit"* — then make one commit and read the file. **Empty file
  means (A). An entry saying it could not parse means (B).** Do not reason about which is more
  likely; one commit answers it.
- **Whatever the cause, the silent-exit-0 is a defect in its own right and outlives this
  diagnosis.** **A hook that cannot read its input must not exit 0.** Fix that even if the answer
  turns out to be (A), and **watch it refuse** on a deliberately malformed payload.

#### 3. The question this red raises about the hook's scope

**A `flutter test`-only pre-commit gate would not have caught this red.** Decide, and say what it
costs: **should the hook also run the gate's coverage-only check**, which executes no instruments
and is therefore cheap? **Do not assume it is cheap — measure it and add the number to the 96
seconds.** If the answer is no, **say what else lives outside the local gate**, so the next person
who is surprised by a red finds the list rather than the surprise.

- **Acceptance:** both workflows are green; the two declarations say something true; the hook either
  runs and was **seen running**, or a git hook exists with an install step, an owner and a way to
  tell whether it is installed; and the local-versus-push gate difference is written down with a
  decision about the coverage check.

### Task 11.185 — The wedges that made a position sit on top of it
**Status:** Done 2026-09-07. **Above the line. Michael reported it from the app, 2026-09-07**, on the
main map — the screen this app exists for.
**Model:** **Sonnet.** The change is a condition on one layer and a sentence in one panel. **Both
design decisions are made below** (Michael answered them directly); do not re-open them.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Related to 11.131**, which made the wedge and the ray share one range.

**What Michael sees.** *"After a position is calculated and displayed on the map with the bearings,
when you click on the position it displays heavier with the ellipse — but the bearing wedges display
as well and it makes it hard to see the ellipse. Make it so the wedges don't display when the
ellipse gets displayed. Just show the bearing lines heavy, so it is clear which bearing lines
created the position."*

**Why it happens, read from `map_screen.dart` rather than guessed.** Selecting an estimate sets
`highlightIds` to `estimate.observationIdsUsed`. **The wedge layer then draws those wedges *more*
heavily, not less** — fill alpha goes `0.2 → 0.35` and border `0.45`, while unrelated wedges drop to
`0.08`. **The ellipse is filled at alpha `0.18`.** So the exact wedges that converge on the ellipse
are darkened above it, and the ellipse is the faintest thing in the pile. **The highlighting is
working as designed and the design is wrong for this case.**

#### The two decisions, answered by Michael on 2026-09-07 — implement, do not re-litigate

- **Hide only the wedges of the bearings that produced the selected estimate** — the ones actually
  on top of the ellipse. **Wedges for other bearings stay exactly as they are** (already dimmed to
  `0.08`), so the surrounding context is not lost.
- **The rays are untouched.** The `strokeWidth: 4` full-colour highlight on those same bearings is
  what answers *which lines made this*, and it is already there.

#### The condition, stated precisely so it cannot drift

**Suppress those wedges exactly when the ellipse is actually drawn** — that is, `ellipsePolygon !=
null`: an estimate is selected, `_showSelectedEllipse` is on, **and both axes are greater than
zero.** **An estimate whose ellipse cannot be drawn must keep its wedges**, and toggling the ellipse
off in the selection panel must bring them straight back. **Do not key this off "an estimate is
selected."**

#### Where the explanation goes, and why not on the layer toggle

Michael's answer to *"what should the Uncertainty wedges toggle show?"* was **grey it out and say
why** — **and that answer was given for a design where all wedges disappeared.** With only the used
ones hidden, **the layer toggle still governs every other wedge on the map, so disabling it would
take away real control and would itself be a lie.**

**So the sentence goes where the suppression is decided: the selection panel**, beside the ellipse
switch it already owns (`_SelectionInfoPanel`, `showEllipse` / `onToggleEllipse`). One short line
saying the wedges for these bearings are hidden while the ellipse is shown. **The layer toggle keeps
working and is not touched.** **This is a deviation from the letter of Michael's answer and it
follows its intent — the control must explain itself. It is flagged here rather than made quietly,
and he can overrule it.**

- **Watch it at phone geometry, not in a description.** Render the selected-estimate state and show
  the ellipse is legible — this is a *visual* fix and `CLAUDE.md` says a test suite cannot close a
  rendering task, so **say what you could and could not verify without a device**, and leave Michael
  a specific thing to look at.
- **Check the same collision elsewhere before calling it done.** `position_estimation_screen.dart`
  also draws ellipses and wedges. **Say whether it has this problem**; if it does, fix it here, and
  if it does not, say why not. **Silence about it is not a verdict.**

- **Acceptance:** the ellipse is unobstructed when shown; only the producing bearings' wedges are
  suppressed and only while the ellipse is actually drawn; toggling the ellipse off restores them;
  the rays' heavy highlight is unchanged; the panel says what is hidden and why; the layer toggle
  still works; and the position-estimation screen has a written verdict.

on a real iOS simulator since before any of the four tasks that asked Michael to look**, with a

measured things: a `flutter_test` golden is taken in a font about twice Roboto's width and is a
picture of a phone nobody owns; **all 20 of the outstanding questions are about a change the same task
had just made on purpose, so a regression check would have been re-blessed in that same commit —
20 of 20, not a majority**; and **every rendering defect this project has actually caught was caught

**zero by anything picture-shaped.** The record is
`test/documentation/rendering_verification_policy_test.dart`, which refuses an unargued golden under

coupling shape. Watched red in four directions: a golden added, the scan narrowed to a real but
smaller directory, the harness deleted, and its accept gate renamed. **The honest claim is written

**Depends on:** nothing. **Prompted by task 11.185, 2026-09-07.**
