### Task 11.187 — A tag's pulse modes are two words baked into the schema; they should be the biologist's
**Status:** Done 2026-09-07. Schema v12: one to three named pulse modes per tag, with rates in beats
per minute, versioned like every other measurement column; `Observations.pulse_mode` records which
mode a bearing was heard on; a device-wide bpm ↔ seconds-per-pulse display toggle. The storage shape
is the one recommended, with one refinement argued in the comms entry: **slot 1's rate stays in the
column already called `pulse_rate`**, because renaming a shipped column costs a `schemaMajorVersion`
bump. `SignalType` survives as the legacy two-valued projection and is what every pre-v12 record is
read through. Originally **above the line**, and the reason was timing rather than severity: **this
changes the data model, and a schema change is far cheaper before a beta collects data against it
than after.**
**Model:** **Opus, high. Run it alone in a fresh window.** It touches the shared client/server sync
package, a schema migration, tag versioning, two screens and a share format.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Michael asked for it 2026-09-07 and answered four design questions the
same day; those answers are decisions, not suggestions.**

**What Michael asked for, in his words.** *"There are always two pulse types currently (active and
mortality). The truth is that the person who enters the tag should be able to set those, because
some tags have only one mode and some have more than one. The user should be able to set a pulse
rate for each mode and name the mode… each named mode should have its own rate. It is important that
these named modes update in the record screen when they are changed in the tag database
(immediately). The user shouldn't have to restart the app. The default modes should be 'Normal' at 1
pulse per second and Mortality at 2 pulses per second. The user should be able to toggle on/off up
to three modes but not fewer than 1."*

#### The four answers, given by Michael on 2026-09-07 — implement, do not re-open

1. **Storage stays in bpm.** Michael corrected the planning session on this: *"I thought they were
   in pulses per second. Keep them stored as bpm but still allow users to toggle to see them in
   seconds-per-pulse."* **So there is no unit migration, no arithmetic on existing values, and no
   historical version rows to rewrite.** His defaults are **60 bpm (Normal)** and **120 bpm
   (Mortality)**.
2. **A rate or name edit asks the same question the app already asks.** *Correcting a mistake* fixes
   it everywhere; *recording a change* leaves older bearings against the old value.
3. **Records already stored as `regular_pulse` / `mortality_signal` adopt the new default names**
   — the word *Regular* leaves the app.
4. **The seconds ↔ bpm toggle is remembered everywhere**, across screens and restarts. One setting,
   one answer; no screen disagreeing with another.

#### What is actually in the way, read from the code rather than assumed

- **`SignalType` is a two-value enum in `packages/tritrack_sync/lib/src/enums.dart`**
  (`regular_pulse`, `mortality_signal`), validated by `row_validator.dart` and stored on **every
  observation**. It is the shared client/server package. **This is not a UI list; the server
  enforces it.**
- **`pulse_rate` is `TagColumnKind.measurementContext`** in `tag_column_kinds.dart` — so it is
  already versioned into `Tables.tagVersions`, and editing it already asks the mistake-or-change
  question. **Michael's answer 2 therefore costs nothing new: mode names and rates join that class
  and inherit the behaviour.** `tagColumnKinds` has no default and no fallback on purpose, so every
  new column must choose.
- **`observation_share.dart` carries `signal_type` and `tagPulseRate` across devices.** A file
  written by a new build and read by an old one, or the reverse, must **refuse honestly rather than
  guess.**
- **Today's UI labels the field `Pulse rate (bpm, optional)`** and prints `bpm` on the record screen
  and the sharing screen. Those are the strings the unit toggle now governs.

#### The storage shape — the planning session recommends, the task may overrule with an argument

**Three name/rate pairs as ordinary columns on `Tags`.** Because the maximum is three and fixed,
this keeps **every existing mechanism working untouched**: per-column `NumericBound`/`TextBound`
validation, the versioning that `measurementContext` already gives, the totality check on
`tagColumnKinds`, and the CSV columns.

> **The alternative is a child `Tag_Modes` table, and it is several times the work for a list that
> can never exceed three.** It needs a new synced table, new `RowAuthorizer` rules, new
> `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` rows, a new §4.21.2 verdict, and an answer to **how a tag version snapshots
> its child rows** — which the versioning design does not currently have. **A JSON blob is refused
> outright**: it defeats the per-column bounds this project's whole row validator is built on.
- **If you disagree after looking, say so before building it** — and the argument has to address the
  version-snapshot question, because that is the part that has no answer today.

#### What an observation records

**The observation must record which mode, not the mode's words.** The name and the rate at the time
already live on the tag version the observation points at (`tagVersionId`). **So the observation
carries the mode's identity and the version supplies the rest** — do not copy names onto
observations.

- **State what happens to an observation with no tag**, since `tagId` is nullable and today
  `signalType` defaults to `regularPulse` regardless.
- **State what happens when a mode an old observation used is later switched off.** The record must
  remain readable and must not claim a mode that no longer exists is current. **Do not delete
  history to keep a list tidy.**

#### The immediacy Michael asked for is a specific mechanism, not a hope

*"These named modes update in the record screen when they are changed in the tag database
(immediately). The user shouldn't have to restart the app."* **This project already has the machinery
and it is named** — `tag_view_refresh.dart` and `arrival_refresh.dart` enumerate what a change must
refresh. **Use it, and add a test that changes a mode and watches the record screen's picker change
without a restart.** A screen that happens to rebuild is not the same as one that must.

#### Migration

**Schema version bump, and the migration is the dangerous part.** Existing tags get Michael's two
defaults; existing observations map `regular_pulse` → mode 1 and `mortality_signal` → mode 2.
**Write the migration so that a tag with a `pulse_rate` already set keeps that value** — say
explicitly which mode it lands on and why. **And say what a project synced from a server running the
old schema does**, because the server's copy changes too.

- **Acceptance:** a tag carries 1–3 named modes with rates, never zero; the defaults are Normal
  60 bpm and Mortality 120 bpm; edits ask mistake-or-change; the record screen's picker follows a
  tag-database change **without a restart, proven by a test**; the unit toggle is remembered across
  restarts and every screen that shows a rate obeys it; observations record the mode's identity, not
  its words; the share format refuses an unreadable version honestly; the migration's treatment of
  existing `pulse_rate` values is stated; and the storage-shape choice is argued if it differs from
  the recommendation.


### Task 11.188 — The rollers put the worst answer at the top
**Status:** Done 2026-09-07. **Below the line.** Nothing was broken. **Michael asked for it 2026-09-07.**
**Model:** **Sonnet.** Small, and safe for a specific reason given below.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Can be run before or after 11.187** — it touches the same widget and
nothing else, so **run it first if 11.187 is going to be a long session**, to avoid two tasks editing
`observation_logging_screen.dart` at once.

**What Michael asked for.** *"In the record screen you generally have things ordered worst to best
from top to bottom (see bearing quality and signal strength). Generally it should be the opposite,
with better signal and bearings at the top of the list and the user rolls down for lower
quality/strength."*

**Why this is safe, and it is worth stating so the task does not reach further than it should.**
**Neither change touches a stored value or an enum declaration.** `BEARING QUALITY` already renders
from an explicit display list, `_bearingQualityOrder` in `observation_logging_screen.dart`
(`suspectedBounce, fair, good`). `SIGNAL STRENGTH` renders straight from `SignalStrength.values`,
which is declared worst-to-best. **The fix is to reverse the first list and give signal strength an
explicit display list of its own** — not to reorder either enum. The stored strings are unchanged and
nothing that reads them is affected.

- **Do not reorder the enums.** Their declaration order is a serialization-adjacent property and
  changing it to fix a picker is a change with a much larger blast radius than the problem.
- **Check whether anything else in the app renders these two in worst-first order** — the log screen,
  a filter, the observation edit dialog — and **give a verdict per site.** Michael said *"generally"*,
  which is an invitation to look rather than a licence to change every list in the app. **Say what
  you found and change only what matches what he described.**
- **This changes which value sits under the finger when the picker opens.** Say what the initial
  selection is now and whether it changed; a default that quietly moves from *fair* to *good* is a
  data-quality change wearing a layout change's clothes.

- **Acceptance:** best is at the top of both rollers; no enum declaration moved; other renderings of
  the same two values have a written verdict; and the effect on the default selection is stated.


### Task 11.189 — A bar on every screen that says what one icon could
**Status:** Done 2026-09-07. **The banner strip is gone app-wide**, sync reports as one icon above
the "+" on the Main Map and a dot on the More tab, and the cloud-backup retirement notice moved to
the More screen rather than into the icon — a stated deviation from Michael's answer 2, with the
reasoning in `cloud_backup_retired_notice.dart` for him to overrule. Every screen was handed back
**109 logical pixels at the default text size and 623 at AX5** on a 6.1-inch phone.
**Above the line.** **Michael asked for it 2026-09-07** and answered three
design questions the same day.
**Model:** **Opus, high. Run it alone in a fresh window.** It removes a shell-wide surface that
task 11.149's whole space budget is built around, and it collapses thirteen states into three
colours.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Related to 11.149**, whose measurements are the argument for doing it.

**What Michael asked for.** *"Could we get away from the bar at the top of the map window that
constantly takes up vertical space and move to some icon based system right above the + on the map…
I'd just want the icon, not a big button that reduces visible map space. The north map reorientation
is a nice model — small and selectable and out of the way, still clickable. For sync it could be a
little green check when everything is okay, a yellow warning for delayed sync and a red exclamation
point when things were bad… the map screen just needs to indicate to the user if everything is okay
or not and can click in if they need to review what's wrong."*

#### The three answers, given 2026-09-07 — implement, do not re-open

1. **The bar goes app-wide, not just on the map**, and **the status icon also lives in the tab bar**
   — a badge on the More tab's icon — so the signal is visible from every screen rather than only
   from the map.
2. **The retirement notice folds in too** (but read the recommendation below before doing it
   literally).
3. **The map's icon sits above the `+`**, in `MapNorthArrow`'s visual language.

#### Why this is worth more than map area, with the numbers already measured

`shell_banner.dart`'s own header holds the table task 11.149 measured on a 6.1-inch phone, of the
body left to whichever screen is on the tab:

| text size | body | sync bar | retirement notice | nav bar |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Large (default) | **570** | 38 | 71 | 114 |
| AX3 | **239** | 60 | **380** | 114 |
| AX5 | **56** | 73 | **550** | 114 |

**The Record screen's scrolling form was handed a viewport of zero logical pixels from AX4** (AX3 for
a viewer). **Removing both banners returns 109 pixels at the default and 623 at AX5** — and the
accessibility text sizes are the axis most of this project's open rendering questions sit on.
**Say the recovered numbers after the change rather than repeating these.**

#### Derive the severity; do not write a second list of thirteen

**`SyncStatusBanner._presentation` already assigns a colour to every one of the thirteen
`SyncHealth` states** — `Colors.red.shade800`, `Colors.orange.shade800`, or `Colors.blueGrey.shade700`
for the informational ones. **Map the icon's severity from that same switch**, so the icon and the
sentence behind it cannot disagree, and **make the mapping exhaustive so a new state has to choose**
rather than falling into a default. *(The planning session is deliberately not listing which state is
which colour: this file records sixteen occasions where a hand-written list in a brief was wrong.)*

- **`healthy` is the only green.** `running` and `offline` are neither faults nor health — **being
  offline in the field is the normal condition of this app**, and an amber warning for it would cry
  wolf on every field day. Give them their own quiet treatment and say what you chose.
- **A colour is a summary; the tap-through is the answer.** Some of these states do not mean *sync is
  behind* — they mean **a record is on this device and nowhere else**, or *your membership in this
  project ended*, or *this app build refuses the server address* (whose whole wording exists to stop
  somebody walking outside looking for signal). **Nothing may read as "a bit slow" when it means
  "your data is stranded."**

#### One invariant that a redesign is very easy to break

**A person who never configured a server must see no icon at all — not a green tick.** Task 10.2's
invariant, and `isWorthShowing` is what carries it today. **A green tick would be claiming a sync
succeeded when nothing ever tried.** Watch that case in a test.

#### The retirement notice — a recommendation against the letter of Michael's answer

**It is not a status.** It is a one-time dismissible notice about a feature that was removed, and at
AX5 it was taking **550 of the phone's 852 pixels**. **Folding a one-time notice into a live status
icon makes the icon lie** — there is no state of the app that "retirement notice pending" describes.

**Recommended: it leaves the banner strip entirely** — a one-time entry on the More screen, or a
dialog shown once — and the icon covers sync alone. **This is a deviation and Michael can overrule
it; say plainly which you built.**

#### What must not be lost on the way

- **The dismiss control** (*"Dismiss until tomorrow morning"*, task 11.114, on exactly the two
  staleness states) needs a home. **The sync status screen is the obvious one. Say where it went.**
- **`AppShellBody`, `ShellBanner` and the shedding order become dead or nearly dead.** Say what you
  did with them — **deleting is fine; leaving an unused budget mechanism that a later task will
  believe in is not.**
- **Task 11.149's floors must survive.** Those budget tests exist because banners squeezed screens.
  **Removing the squeeze does not remove the need for the floor** — it gives it headroom. **Do not
  delete a guard because the thing it was guarding against is currently gone.**

- **Acceptance:** the banner strip is gone app-wide; one icon on the map above the `+` in
  `MapNorthArrow`'s language and a badge on the More tab; severity derived from the existing
  presentation switch and exhaustive; `healthy` the only green and offline not a warning; **no icon
  at all with no server configured, watched in a test**; the dismiss control has a stated home;
  `ShellBanner`'s machinery is deleted or justified; 11.149's floors still exist; the recovered
  pixels are measured and stated; and every copy change is declared in the comms entry's
  planning-session half.

### Task 11.191 — Four small things left over, and one contradiction worth settling
**Status:** Done 2026-09-07. All five items closed: the unit control now lives on the Tag
Database app bar (as a `PopupMenuButton`, not the segmented toggle Tag details uses — that
toggle overflowed the app bar's action row at a real phone width and a large text scale) over
the same stored preference, watched staying in sync with no restart; one dead doc reference

now matches what the guard enforces; the website workflow's harmless `flutter_native_splash`
version-solving warning is now named and explained rather than left looking like a fault; and
the citation ratchet printed no fallen ceilings to lower — the tree is confirmed green without
the escape hatch (2462 tests, 0 failures). **Below the line. Nothing is broken.**
**Model:** **Sonnet.** Four unrelated small items, grouped because each alone is too small to be
worth a window.
**Depends on:** 11.187, which reported three of them.

#### 1. The unit toggle needs a second, central home — Michael asked for it

The bpm ↔ seconds-per-pulse control sits only on Tag details, at the top of the pulse-modes section.
Michael's answer on 2026-09-07: *"Yes — let's do that so there is a central place to make the change
as well."* **Put it on the Tag Database app bar beside the sort control.**

  the same stored value, and **changing it in one place must be visible in the other without a
  restart** — the same requirement 11.187 met for modes. **Watch that in a test.**

#### 2. Two doc comments name code that does not exist

- `lib/data/sharing/observation_share.dart` names **`share_column_coverage_test.dart`**, which does
  not exist. **The check it describes does exist**, under a different name, in
  `test/security/share_payload_overwrite_test.dart`.
- `lib/widgets/sync_status_banner.dart` names **`BackupHealthBanner`** twice, and
  `test/routing/tab_shell_layout_test.dart` names it once. **There is no such widget anywhere in

**Both are the names-code-it-does-not-own class.** Correct them. **And say whether anything checks
that a `[SquareBracket]` doc reference in this repository resolves** — if nothing does, that is a
finding worth one sentence, not a task.

#### 3. `CLAUDE.md` and a guard now contradict each other, and the guard wins

`CLAUDE.md` says the planning session deletes a task's command file when it resolves that task's
comms entry. **`command_file_staleness_test.dart` reads the plan's `Status:` field, so a task that
marks itself Done and leaves its command file in place puts a red on `main`** — and the pre-commit
hook then refuses the commit. **Task 11.187 hit this and deleted its own command file, correctly.**

- **Update `CLAUDE.md`: a task deletes its own command file in the commit that marks it Done.** The
  planning session deletes it only for a task it resolves on the task's behalf. **A task that stops
  short leaves its command in place**, because `Partial` and `Deferred` are legitimately re-runnable
  and the check lets them pass.
- **This is the good failure mode.** The convention was a habit; 11.179 replaced it with something

version-solving failure and then passes is a job whose next real failure gets skimmed past.

#### 5. Two citation ceilings have fallen, and one red of the planning session's own

`planning_document_citations_test.dart` **prints rather than fails** when a document's real count has

### Task 11.193 — The Record screen has run out of room, and it needs one more control
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-07.** Schema v13 adds one nullable column,
`Observations.signal_irregular`, holding 0 or 1 — a boolean, as expected, with the argument for one
bit rather than a scale written on the column. **NULL means nobody was asked** and nothing backfills
it; a note, a truth point and a no-signal sweep store NULL rather than 0, because the question has no
meaning for a record of not hearing anything. It is not `TagStatus.malfunction` and neither derives
from the other. **`AnalysisEligibility` does not read it**, watched red under a deliberate sabotage.
**It travels in a shared record and an import writes it** — unlike `pulse_mode` and `tag_version_id`,
which name rows in the *sender's* database, this names a listening moment and means the same thing on
both devices; payload version 4. On the screen it is a chip on the pulse-mode line, in a `Wrap` so it
moves to its own run rather than overflowing: **31 logical pixels at the default text size, 75 at
AX5** where it no longer fits beside the line. **The button is whole**: `Preview / set position on
map` moved from 52 pixels past the fold to 55 pixels clear of it on a 6.9-inch phone, bought by
moving the notes field and the ADVANCED disclosure below the position block (138 pixels). **On a
6.1-inch phone it is still 46 pixels short** — improved from about 153 — and closing that needs a
section taken out of the form, which is discovered scope rather than this task's call.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** **The two halves are one task on purpose** — adding a control to a
screen that already overflows, in two separate tasks, is how the second undoes the first.
**Depends on:** 11.187, which added the line that pushed the button over. **Michael asked for the
flag 2026-09-07; `/w-14` found the overflow the same day.**

#### 1. The overflow, found by the screenshot harness rather than by a person

**On a 6.9-inch phone at the default text size, `Preview / set position on map` is sliced to a green
sliver at the bottom edge of the form.** Task 11.187's per-mode rate line (*"Normal · 46 bpm"*) pushed
the form down by about one line and that button over the fold.

> **`/w-14` checked the obvious suspect before reporting, and it is not that.** It is **ordinary
> overflow, not a budget withdrawing the button** — `BudgetedColumn` is not doing this. **Do not
> spend the task looking there.**

**It is reachable by scrolling**, and **the guide's own page tells people about that button while its
screenshot shows a sliver of one.** `/w-14` committed that picture deliberately — *a truthful
picture of a rough screen beats a stale picture of a screen that no longer exists* — so **the site is
showing this until this task lands.**

#### 2. The flag Michael asked for, and what it is not

**Michael, 2026-09-07:** *"We should add a flag for all signal recordings — not for a weak tag, but
for one that seems to be malfunctioning, such as when the inter-pulse duration is irregular."*

> **This is not `TagStatus.malfunction`, and the difference is the whole design.** That status is
> `TagColumnKind.collarLife` — a current-state fact about the collar, with no per-observation copy,
> and the only useful answer to it is today's. **What Michael is asking for is a fact about one
> listening moment**: *this is what I heard, at this time, from this spot.* **Several of those are
> the evidence that would later justify setting the collar's status** — they are complementary, and
> **neither may be derived from the other.**

- **A new column on `Observations`, and a schema bump.** **Copy task 11.187's `pulse_mode` column
  comment as the model for how to write it** — in particular, **what NULL means and why nothing
  backfills it.** A bearing recorded before this column existed does not know whether the signal
  sounded irregular, and inventing an answer is the falsehood that comment exists to prevent.
- **Decide whether it is a boolean or has degrees, and argue it.** *"Sounded wrong"* is one bit of
  information a person is confident about; a scale is a thing they will guess at. **The planning
  session's expectation is a boolean; say so if you disagree.**
- **It must not silently change a position estimate.** Excluding a bearing from an estimate is
  already its own mechanism, with its own row (`Tables.observationExclusions`, task 11.7). **This
  flag records what was heard; it does not withdraw the bearing.** **Say explicitly what
  `analysis_eligibility.dart` does with it — which should be nothing — and watch that in a test.**
- **Decide whether it travels in a shared or pasted record.** Unlike `pulse_mode`, this is **not**
  relative to the sender's tag — it is a fact about the sender's listening moment, so it probably
  should travel. **`ObservationShare.writableColumns` is where that decision is written down.**

#### 3. The two halves meet here, and that is why they are one task

**The Record screen is already over its budget and you are adding a control to it.** Two previous
tasks measured this screen as crowded, 11.187 added a line, and the result is a button off the
bottom.

- **Do not add a row of furniture.** Find the space, or put the flag where it costs nothing —

- **Watch the button.** The acceptance is not "the flag exists"; it is **the flag exists and
  `Preview / set position on map` is whole at the default text size on a 6.9-inch phone.**
- **Re-run the harness.** `integration_test/screenshots/regenerate.sh` is what found this and is what
  proves it fixed. **Say which profiles you ran and what moved.**

- **Acceptance:** the button is whole on a 6.9-inch phone at the default text size; the flag exists

### Task 11.192 — Nothing checks that a doc reference points at anything
**Status:** Done, 2026-09-08. **Below the line.** Nothing was broken; one real defect found by
measuring, and 11.199's guard now checks the assumption it stated rather than merely stating it.

#### 1. `comment_references` — measured, not enabled

**169 violations across 90 files**, all with the identical message *"The referenced name isn't
visible in scope. Try adding an import for the referenced name."* That message does not
distinguish a genuinely dead symbol from a real one the file simply hasn't imported for doc
purposes — so every hit still needs the same by-hand check this task exists to replace.

**Sampled ~20 of the most-repeated symbols** (`SyncHeldRowStore`, `TagRepository`,
`BaseRepository`, `classifySyncFailure`, `refreshTagViews`, `LastOwnerRemoval`, `ObservationCsv`,
`SyncConflictStore`, `TileFetchHealth`, `ViewshedComputer`, `TabShell`, `awaitReady`, and others):
**every one is a real, currently-existing symbol**, referenced correctly, just not imported into
the file whose doc comment names it. Fixing all 169 would mean adding an import to roughly 90
files purely to satisfy documentation cross-referencing — no functional defect in ~168 of them.
**That is the "hundreds → noise" branch the task asked to watch for.**

**Decision: do not enable it.** Recorded so the question is not re-opened at the next dead
reference.

**And the hole that decision leaves is now a trip-wire rather than a note (planning session,
2026-09-08).** `comment_references` only ever saw `[bracket]` references in Dart doc comments. **A
prose sentence naming a file, or a backtick-quoted filename in a comment, is covered by nothing in
this repository** — the `share_column_coverage_test.dart` incident was exactly that shape and was
found by a person reading. **The class stands at two instances. The third one buys a
repository-wide checker for backtick-quoted filenames, not another look at this lint.** Written
into `CLAUDE.md` as well, because a threshold that lives only in a plan entry is a threshold
nobody is standing at.

**One real defect turned up anyway, while sampling** — fixed, not just noted.
`lib/features/map/services/geo_math.dart` had a docstring for a deleted-and-reinserted function
merged onto the wrong neighbor: task 2d0a062 (Phase 7) inserted `ellipsePolygonPoints` and
`bearingWedgePoints` between `distanceAndBearing`'s doc comment and `distanceAndBearing` itself,
with no blank line separating the two doc blocks, so `ellipsePolygonPoints` inherited a comment
describing `[a]`, `[b]` and "the inverse of `[destinationPoint]`" — none of which are its
parameters — while `distanceAndBearing` (still called from six screens) has carried no doc
comment since. Split back apart in this task's commit.

**Coverage — is it luck that this class was found by `[bracket]` references so far?** No, and the
two real-world incidents that motivated this task say so directly. `sync_status_banner.dart`'s
dead reference to `BackupHealthBanner` was written as `[BackupHealthBanner]` — exactly the shape
`comment_references` checks, and it would have caught it. `observation_share.dart`'s dead
reference to `share_column_coverage_test.dart` was a plain backtick filename in prose — outside
what this lint (or any Dart analyzer option) looks at at all. **So the coverage gap is real, not
luck: a prose or backtick reference to a file or symbol is never checked by anything.** No
mechanism is proposed here to close that half; it would need a repo-wide grep-style checker (find
every backtick-quoted `.dart` filename and path in `CLAUDE_DOCS/*.md` and doc comments, assert
each still exists), which is a bigger, separate task if it is ever wanted.

#### 2. 11.199's guard assumption — measured false, now asserted

11.199's `stored_value_display_test.dart` separates a display from a store by directory:
`_presentationLayer = ['lib/features', 'lib/widgets']`. Its own doc comment named the risk: *"the
day somebody writes a widget under `lib/core/`... that rule is quietly narrower than it reads."*

**Measured: it already had, twice.** `lib/app.dart` (`TriTrackApp`/`_TriTrackAppState`) and
`lib/routing/app_router.dart` (`TabShell`/`_TabShellState`) both define a widget and both live
outside `_presentationLayer` — neither is scanned by condition 1's check. Neither currently reads
a stored value, so nothing was silently wrong; but the guard's own scan could not have told you
either way.

**Fixed by assertion, not by widening condition 1's scan** (the full derivation — any file
importing `package:flutter/widgets.dart` is a display — is the better rule in principle and stays
explicitly not built here, per the brief). Added a new test to the same file: a named allowlist,
`_widgetsOutsidePresentationLayer` (these two files, each with a one-line reason), plus a scan of
all of `lib/` that fails if any *other* widget-defining file exists outside `_presentationLayer`
and outside that allowlist, and fails separately if either allowlisted file starts reading a
stored value. **Watched red twice**: injecting a `.db` read into `app_router.dart`, and dropping a
throwaway widget file under `lib/core/` — both caught by the new test, both reverted.

**Acceptance for both halves met:** violation count measured and reported before any decision;
the `comment_references` decision was "not worth it" with its reasoning recorded; nothing was
suppressed (the one real hit found was fixed); what the lint does not cover is stated; 11.199's
assumption was named, measured against the current tree (found false), and is now asserted; the
assertion was watched going red; the full-derivation alternative is named and explicitly deferred.

**Commit:** (this task's commit). Full suite: 2524 tests, 0 failures, 15 skipped.
**Model:** **Sonnet.** The mechanism is one analyzer option. **The judgement is whether the count
makes it worth turning on**, which is why the first step is to measure.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Task 11.191 asked the question and got the answer: nothing checks.**

**Two dead references surfaced by hand in one week.** `observation_share.dart` named
`share_column_coverage_test.dart`, which never existed; `sync_status_banner.dart` named
**`BackupHealthBanner`** twice, and a test's doc once, after that widget was deleted. **Both were
found by a person reading, which is not a mechanism.**

> **This is the `path:NN` class one layer over** — a document pointing at a symbol that is not there,
> with nothing to say so — and that class has now produced findings on three separate days.

- **Dart already has this check: the `comment_references` lint.** **Measure before enabling it.**
  Turn it on locally, count the violations, and report the number **before** deciding.
- **The number decides the answer, and both answers are real.** A handful means fix them and enable
  it permanently. **Hundreds means enabling it produces noise somebody will switch off**, and the
  honest outcome is either a narrower rule or a written "not worth it" — **which is worth as much as
  a yes, recorded so the question is not re-opened.**
- **Say what it does and does not cover.** It checks `[SquareBracket]` references in Dart doc
  comments. **A prose sentence naming a file, or a `.md` document naming a class, is outside it** —
  and both of this week's instances were in Dart doc comments, so say whether that is luck.

**Second item, added 2026-09-08 from task 11.199 (Michael's fold-rather-than-multiply rule).** That
task's guard separates a display from a store **by layer** — nothing under `lib/features/` or
`lib/widgets/` may read `.db`. **Correct today**, because every legitimate use of a stored spelling
lives elsewhere. **Its author stated the limitation rather than hiding it:** *"the day somebody writes
a widget under `lib/core/`, or a CSV writer under `lib/features/`, that rule is quietly narrower than
it reads."*

> **The planning session's decision: keep the layer rule and make the assumption under it
> checkable.** The full derivation — *any file importing `package:flutter/widgets.dart` is a
> display* — **is the better rule in principle and a bigger task. Not here.** **Assert the layering
> the guard depends on**, so the day it stops holding, something says so. **Measure the current tree
> first — if the assumption is already false somewhere, that is a finding and it outranks the
> check** — and **if it cannot be asserted cheaply, say so and leave 11.199's written limitation as
> the answer.** A limit somebody wrote down on purpose is not the failure this project chases.

- **Acceptance:** the violation count is measured and reported before the decision; a decision is
  made with its reasoning; if enabled, the violations are fixed rather than suppressed; and what the
  lint does not cover is stated.

focus leaves and keeping what was typed. `minLines` and `maxLines` are the same number in each state
so the box does not grow a line at a time under somebody's hands. **The keyboard half needed an
explicit line and would have been missed by anyone reasoning from the framework's defaults**: on iOS
and Android `TextField`'s default `onTapOutside` handler does *nothing* — it only dismisses on
desktop — so the field passes its own. **(3) The Record screen's tag wheel shows its centred item at
18pt**, up from 16, through a new `WheelPicker.selectedFontSize` that defaults to 16 everywhere

**And a fifth, after he saw the fourth: the opened notes box has to scroll onto the screen.**
Michael: *"the expansion of the notes pushed below the save button rather than moving the stuff
above the notes block up."* **That is what a `ListView` does on its own** — a child that grows grows
*downward*, into the fold, then the pinned bar, then the keyboard — and **Flutter's own
scroll-on-focus does not cover it**: `EditableText` asks for the *caret* to be shown, and the caret
is on the first line, so that request is already satisfied while the other three lines are
underneath. **Two wrong fixes preceded the right one and both are written into the code, because
either would be reached for again.** `Scrollable.ensureVisible` **under-scrolled by exactly the
amount the box was overflowing** — 128 → 310 where 350 was needed — because it works from the
viewport's own idea of where its children are and a `SliverList` estimates the extent of children it
has not laid out, an estimate still settling on the frame after a child changes height and the
keyboard changes the viewport. **The reveal now measures the two render boxes and scrolls by the
difference: what is on the screen is not an estimate.** And **one pass was still not enough** — the
keyboard's inset reaches the two `Scaffold`s above this form over more than one frame, so the first
measurement read a layout about to move underneath it and landed **48 pixels short**. It repeats,
measured afresh each time so it converges rather than accumulates, **bounded at four attempts**, and
**stops if the person has taken hold of the form themselves** (an interrupted `animateTo` completes
like any other, and a reveal that yanks a drag back is worse than no reveal). Measured with a
336-pixel keyboard inset: **306..422 inside a viewport ending at 430**, where it used to sit at
354..470. **The harness cannot see this** — no shot on any profile focuses the notes field, so there
is no published picture in which the box is open; the instrument is the widget test with a simulated
keyboard.
**And three more, after he tried the notes box (2026-09-07).**
**(1) A Note's box shrank to a line when the keyboard came up.** `Expanded` fills *what is left*,
and with a keyboard up there is very little left — so on the one record type where the box **is**
the record it became a sliver. A Note being written now stops filling and demands **eight lines**,
which is more than the keyboard leaves, so the column outgrows its viewport, the form scrolls, and
the record type and the tag move off the top instead of the box losing lines. At rest it still
fills the screen.
**(2) The reveal stepped instead of moving once, and the retry loop was the cause.** The keyboard
rises over a couple of hundred milliseconds and reports its height on **every frame** of that rise;
each report started a fresh 180 ms scroll animation that interrupted the one before it, **which is
what stepping is**. It jumps now, once per frame, so the content tracks the keyboard as it comes up
— the smooth motion is the keyboard's own and nothing is left to fight it. **The general form:
animating in response to something that is itself animating produces the jitter it was meant to
smooth.**
**(3) *Draft autosaves* is gone** — Michael: *"users will figure this out as they use the app."* It
explained a behaviour nobody has to act on and cost **21 logical pixels** of the form's headroom;
the pinned bar's declared height goes 85 → 64. **`BudgetedColumn` stays with one child that never
sheds**, because it is what makes rule 3 something that can refuse rather than a comment — the
mechanism armed with nothing in it, so the next line added to that bar is the one that stands down.

note's absence is supposed to guarantee. And **an assertion was caught being vacuous while it was

and on a Note the form is a `SingleChildScrollView`, so nothing in it is ever absent from the tree.

`CLAUDE.md` now carries Michael's own sentence: *simplicity and readability over verbosity, so long

### Task 11.200 — A colour token this app never defined, and everything that asks for it
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-08.** **Michael's requirement was unmet and this was a repair.** The
Irregular/Malfunctioning label was not light grey: it was `#1A1A1A`, the app's full-strength body
text, because `ColorScheme.onSurfaceVariant` was never passed and Flutter's getter falls back to
`onSurface`. **The token now resolves to the palette's `secondaryText` grey** — `#6B6B68` light,
`#9C9C98` dark, values that have been in `DesignTokens` since the design handoff with no caller,
clearing WCAG AA in both modes on both backgrounds (4.60–6.69:1). **The real call-site count is 81
across 20 files, not 86** — the planning session's number was a grep and included three comment
lines and the two sites this task moved off the token. **Three sites did not want "muted" and were
handled rather than swept along:** the map's *no signal* marker keeps `onSurface` (it is a 13-pixel
glyph over imagery, 4.69:1 against 15.25:1); the elevation chart's axis labels drop their 0.55 alpha
(fading the real grey gave 2.22:1); the Record screen's disabled-pill alpha goes 0.4 → 0.7 to hold
its old rendering (0.4 on the real grey is 1.75:1). **Two instruments, both watched red:**
`test/core/theme/color_scheme_tokens_defined_test.dart` derives which `ColorScheme` members `lib/`
reads and which the theme passes, refuses an empty derivation on either side, and fails on any member
that is neither passed nor argued for in a `_knownFallbacks` map; and 11.197's own colour test, which
**passed for its whole life comparing the label to a token whose value was wrong** — it now asserts
the label is measurably lighter than `onSurface`, which goes red on the code as it shipped. **The
guard's first run is the honest count of the rest of this class: six more members are used and never
passed**, the worst being `outlineVariant` on the Position screen's dimmed observer badge, which drew
the initials and the circle in the same colour — 1.00:1, invisible; defining `onSurfaceVariant`
lifted it to 3.26:1 and the circle is still wrong. **See Discovered Scope.** **The harness was run on
all three profiles and nothing was accepted** — `website/static/screens/` is untouched.
**Above the line.** Nothing crashes and nothing is lost. **It is here because
it may mean Michael did not get what he asked for**, on a control he specifically described, and
because the surface is far wider than the task that found it.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** **The fix is one line and it changes how a great many places look at
once**, which is the part that needs judgement and a person's eye.
**Depends on:** 11.198, which found it, and 11.197, which is the one that may be affected.

**`lib/core/theme/app_theme.dart` builds its `ColorScheme` from an explicit list, and
`onSurfaceVariant` is not on it.** Flutter falls back to **`onSurface`** — the app's full-strength
primary text colour. **So every call site asking for `onSurfaceVariant` to mean *muted*, *secondary*
or *light grey* is getting ordinary body text.**

> **The planning session counted 86 mentions of it under `lib/` and that number is not to be
> trusted** — it is a grep, it includes comments, and this file records more than a dozen occasions
> where a number taken from a report or a grep was wrong. **Derive the real call-site count and say
> what it is.** *(Task 11.199's guard found four sites nobody had reported; the same lesson applies
> here.)*

#### The question that makes this above the line

**Michael asked for the Irregular/Malfunctioning label to be *"light grey by default"* and to turn
red when checked** — his words, and the whole reason the control became a checkbox was that he could
not tell on from off. **Task 11.197 built it and 11.198 says it used this token.** **So check first
whether that label is actually light grey on a real screen, or whether it is full-strength text that
happens to sit beside an unticked box.** **If it is the latter, Michael's requirement is unmet and
this task is a repair rather than a polish.**

#### Then the wider decision, and it is a design one

- **Defining the token changes every site at once.** That is the fix and it is also the risk: **a
  single line quietly restyles a great many places**, some of which may look better full-strength.
  **Say how many sites move and group them** — a list of screens is what makes this reviewable.
- **Decide what the muted colour should be, and say where the value comes from.** `DesignTokens`
  already holds this app's palette; **inventing a grey beside it rather than in it is how a palette
  stops being one.**
- **This cannot be closed by a test.** It is the visual-hierarchy of most screens in the app.
  **Run `integration_test/screenshots/regenerate.sh`, report what moved and by how much, and accept
  nothing** — `website/static/screens/` is the content lane's. **Leave Michael a short list of the
  screens most worth his eye.**
- **A measured "leave it undefined" is a real answer.** If full-strength turns out to be what this
  app should look like, **say so, and define the token to `onSurface` explicitly** so the next person
  finds a decision rather than an omission. **An absence that happens to be right is still an
  absence.**

- **Acceptance:** the real call-site count is derived, not inherited; **whether 11.197's unchecked
  label meets Michael's "light grey" is answered first and plainly**; a decision is made with the
  colour's source named; the affected screens are listed; the harness was run and its result
  reported with nothing accepted; and if the answer is to leave it, **the token is defined
  explicitly rather than left absent.**

### Task 11.202 — The measure tool takes away the only gesture the Position screen has
**Status:** Done, 2026-09-08. **Michael's call, 2026-09-09: the measure tool is not needed on the
Position screen.** It stays on the Main Map, which is where the distance between two arbitrary
points is a question somebody actually asks.
**Model:** **Sonnet, low.** A deletion inside one file. **What makes it worth an entry is not the
deletion** — it is that two things have to be measured rather than assumed on the way out, and one
paragraph of standing prose loses its example and must not lose its rule.
**Depends on:** nothing.

#### 1. It is not only clutter — it disables the gesture the screen exists for

`_onMapTap` in `lib/features/position_estimation/screens/position_estimation_screen.dart` returns
early whenever measure mode is on. **The tap that includes or excludes a bearing ray is what this
screen is for**, and measure mode silently takes it. And the legend card's footnote — *"Tap a ray
on the map to include or exclude that bearing."* — stays readable the whole time, so **the app goes
on telling you to do a thing it has just switched off**, with nothing to say which state you are in
but one button's fill colour.

> **A mode that steals the primary gesture of the screen it sits on has to earn that**, and this one
> was never asked for. **Removing it removes a way to get stuck** — a better reason than tidiness,
> and the one to put in the commit message.

#### 2. What comes out, and what must not

Out of the Position screen only: the `MeasureButton` from the top control row, `_measureMode` and
`_measurePoints`, the measure branch in `_onMapTap`, the dashed measurement `PolylineLayer`, the two
point markers, and the `MeasureResultCard`. The `ValueKey` comment about re-creating the content on
a tag change loses its "clear measure state" clause.

**`MeasureButton` and `MeasureResultCard` stay in `lib/features/map/widgets/map_furniture.dart`
exactly as they are.** They have one caller left — the Main Map — and it keeps them. **Do not inline
them into `map_screen.dart` on the grounds that they now have one user.** That is a refactor nobody
asked for, in a file this task has no reason to open, and `map_screen.dart`'s own doc comment points
a reader at `MeasureButton`'s reasoning.

#### 3. The space budget: predict it, then measure it, and report both

**The prediction is that nothing moves.** `_mapControlRowHeight` is `8.0 + 48.0` — the height of one
48-pixel button, not a sum across the row — so taking a button out should not change it. The
`MeasureResultCard` was drawn in measure mode only and was never in the permanent reservation.

> **State the prediction, then run `test/features/position_estimation/screens/position_screen_space_budget_test.dart`
> and report what it actually says.** This screen's entire documented history — tasks 11.147 and
> 11.148 — is a constant measured once and believed afterwards. **A prediction that turns out right
> is still a prediction until something measures it.** If any number moves, that is the finding and
> it outranks the deletion: report it rather than adjusting a constant until the test agrees.

#### 4. Rule 3 of the MAP SPACE BUDGET loses its example and must keep its rule

The file header currently reads: *"A mode's own readout belongs to the mode. The measure card
appears only in measure mode and the legend card only when asked for; neither may become
permanent."*

**After this task there is no measure card here, and the rule is still true and still needed** — the
legend card is exactly what it governs. **Rewrite it so it stands on the legend card, and name the
measure card as the precedent that was removed, rather than deleting the sentence.** Deleting rule 3
would throw away a principle because its illustration left the building.

Then fix the control-row doc comment, which lists *"basemap toggle, measure, legend, and the north
arrow"*, and **read the whole file for any other prose that describes measuring on this screen.**
Task 11.192 established this week that **prose references are checked by nothing in this
repository** — no lint sees them, so a person reading on the way past is the only mechanism there is.

#### 5. Do not add a test that measure is gone

There is nothing to delete: **no test in `test/` or `integration_test/` has ever tapped the measure
button on this screen** — worth one line in the report, because that is an interactive mode on a
primary screen with no coverage at all. **Do not replace it with an assertion that `MeasureButton`
is absent here.** `CLAUDE.md`'s standing rule is that an assertion made by looking for an absence
passes for reasons that have nothing to do with the claim — a renamed widget, a moved import, a
screen that failed to build at all — and it would go green on the day this screen stopped rendering.

#### 6. The pictures move

Every Position state in the screenshot harness loses a button from its control row. **That is
`/w-13`'s item 8.** Do not re-shoot here and do not accept anything.

- **Acceptance:** the tool is gone from the Position screen and unchanged on the Main Map; both
  shared widgets are untouched; the space-budget prediction is stated **and** the test's actual
  numbers reported; rule 3 survives without its example; the control-row doc comment matches what is

### Task 11.203 — Green over the corner ink on every segmented control, and the Position map's layers square
**Status:** Done. Both items shipped; item 2 exposed a real regression in the Position map's clear
band, filed as Discovered Scope below rather than fixed here (it needs Michael's decision).
**Two things Michael saw on 2026-09-09.** The first is one line of shared
code and **it is not the map's** — it is every segmented control in the app. The second is a layout
change on one screen.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** Neither change is hard. **The work is the check on the first one**,
which is the only thing here that can silently come back.
**Depends on:** nothing.

#### 1. The fill bleeds over the rounded corners, and the reason explains the symptom exactly

**Michael, on the map-type selector:** *"the green infill of the selected map type bleeds over the
rounded corners of the selector boundary (white or black) just in the rounded corners — not on the
vertical or horizontal parts."*

**That symptom is a fingerprint, and it names the cause.** `SegmentedToggle`'s outer `Container`
carries `border: Border.all(width: 1.5)`, `borderRadius: BorderRadius.circular(10)` and
`clipBehavior: Clip.antiAlias`.

- A `BoxDecoration`'s **border is painted with the background — before the child.**
- The border also insets the child by its width, so **on the straight edges the fill stops 1.5
  logical pixels short of the ink and nothing bleeds.**
- But `clipBehavior` on a `Container` clips the child to the decoration's **outer** path — the
  *outside* of the rounded corner. **In a corner the inset rectangle reaches past the inner arc**,
  and the fill, painted after the border, covers the ink it finds there.

> **Straight edges clean, corners dirty, is exactly what that arrangement produces**, which is why
> Michael's description is worth more here than a screenshot would be. **Do not go looking for a
> map-specific cause.**

**It is not the map-type selector. It is `SegmentedToggle`, and it is used in nine places across six
files** — derived, not remembered: the Main Map and the Position map (map type), the Record screen
(record type, bearing method, ground-truth kind), the truth-point edit dialog, the bearing entry
sheet (two), and project setup (coordinate format). **Fix the widget once.**

**"White or black" is the confirmation.** On the Main Map the unselected labels' colour — and with
it the control's border, which is drawn in the same `onSurface` token — is overridden to white over
terrain and street and left dark over satellite (task 11.190). **Michael saw the same defect against
two different border colours**, which is what a shared-widget bug looks like from the outside.

**The fix: clip the child to the *inner* rounded rect** — a `ClipRRect` around the `Row` at
`radius - borderWidth`. **Derive that radius from the two values rather than typing 8.5**; a hand-
computed constant beside the two numbers it came from is the shape this project has been bitten by
repeatedly. Name both as constants in the file and compute the third.

> **The alternative, stated so it can be preferred:** paint the border in a **foreground**
> `DecoratedBox` over the child instead, so the ink is drawn last and nothing can cover it at any
> radius or width. **More robust, and it changes the layout** — the child loses the border's inset
> and every segment's contents shift 1.5 pixels. **The inner clip is chosen because it fixes the
> defect and moves nothing else.** Overrule it only with a reason written down.

**The check, and this is the part that matters.** Nothing in this repository can currently tell this
defect from its absence: **no test looks at the pixels, and the screenshot harness's own noise is
larger than the handful of pixels in question** (item 6 of `/w-13` measured seven screens drifting
20–47% untouched). **So a fix with no instrument is a fix that comes back.**

- **Render the control and sample the pixels.** Pump a `SegmentedToggle` with the first segment
  active, capture the image, and **assert that a pixel inside the top-left corner's border ink is
  the border colour and not `primary`.** Antialiasing means the outermost pixel is a blend — probe
  where the ink should be solid and **state the tolerance you used as a number.**
- **Watch it red before believing it.** Remove the clip, see the probe fail, put it back. **A check
  that has never failed is a claim, not a check.**
- **If it cannot be made to fail reliably, say so and do not ship it.** A green pixel probe that
  cannot detect the defect is worse than no probe, because it tells the next reader this is
  covered. In that case report what you tried and leave the fix verified by hand, in writing.

#### 2. The Position map's map type goes behind a layers square

**Michael:** *"in the position map, let's hide the map type selector behind one of those little
squares that has the layers on it — move the info square down a bit and put the map layer square
above it. I know this is different than the main map but there is less map room on the position
screen."*

**He is right, and the screen's own written rule already says so.** MAP SPACE BUDGET rule 4 is
**"corners before edges, edges before bands"** — a control that fits in a corner cluster costs the
clear band nothing extra, and a full-width band costs it in full. **The wide three-segment toggle is
the only reason that top strip is a band at all.** Replacing it with a 48-pixel square turns a band
into a corner cluster, which is the move rule 4 exists to recommend.

- **A new `MapLayersButton` in `lib/features/map/widgets/map_furniture.dart`**, built exactly like
  `MapLegendButton` beside it — same rounded square, same shadow, same active fill. A layers glyph.
  **It carries a tooltip and a semantics label**, because an icon-only control is silent to a screen
  reader; `SegmentedToggle`'s own `iconFor` doc comment already learned this the hard way.
- **The two squares stack in the top-right: layers above legend**, as asked.
- **The panel it opens is a card, not a bare control on the map.** Tasks 11.106 and 11.190 spent
  themselves on making plain text legible directly over terrain and satellite; **do not re-open
  that.** Put the same `SegmentedToggle` on a surface card in the shape of `MapLegendCard`.
- **The panel lives inside the same `Positioned` column as the buttons, as its third child** — so
  its position is derived from the buttons above it rather than typed as a `top:` constant that
  drifts the next time a button is added. **This screen has been bitten by exactly that.**
- **One panel at a time**: opening layers closes the legend and the reverse. They are anchored at
  opposite ends of a map whose height is a variable, and two open cards is a collision waiting for a
  short screen.

**The space budget: the prediction is that nothing moves, and rule 4 is the reason.** The buttons
are a corner cluster, so **`_mapControlRowHeight` stays `8.0 + 48.0`** and the second square hangs
into the map below the reservation — which is precisely what rule 4 licences and what the wide
toggle could never do. **Say that in the code comment, then run
`test/features/position_estimation/screens/position_estimation_screen`'s space-budget test and
report its real numbers.** If a case fails, **that is the finding** — report it rather than growing
the reservation quietly, because 56 pixels comes off an observation panel on a screen this project
has documented at zero headroom.

**What is given up, said plainly:** the current map type is no longer readable at a glance. **That
is Michael's standing instruction working as intended** — simplicity over verbosity where a person
can find the options by exploring — and the map itself is the readout. **Do not add a label to the
button to compensate.**

#### 3. The pictures move, and further than either item looks

Item 1 touches **nine controls on six screens**, item 2 touches the Position map. **That is `/w-13`'s
item 9.** Do not re-shoot here and do not accept anything.

- **Acceptance:** the clip radius is derived from the border width and the corner radius rather than
  typed; the pixel probe exists **and has been watched red**, or its absence is explained in writing;
  `SegmentedToggle` is fixed once and no call site is special-cased; the layers button carries a
  semantics label; the panel is positioned relative to the buttons rather than by a constant; only
  one of the two panels can be open; the space-budget prediction is stated **and** the test's real
  numbers reported; nothing is accepted in the harness.



### Task 11.204 — Two written rules that contradict each other, and a panel that should be able to get out of the way
**Status:** Done 2026-09-08. The clear-band contradiction is settled by measuring the largest clear
*rectangle* with a floor in both directions; rule 4 and the harness doc comment are both rewritten;
the Position map's band is **161.8** at the default text size, and the panel closes. **Two things
came out that nobody asked for.** The Main Map holds its floor **one text size higher than recorded —
AX3 to AX4 — with nothing on that screen having changed to earn it**, and the Offline Data Map's
margin grew on every row except the two task 11.162 pinned structurally: **those screens have had more
clear map than the arithmetic credited them with for as long as the instrument has existed.** And the
closed panel made the map big enough to reveal that **the observer markers had been clipping their
initials from xxxLarge up — 22 of 38 pixels at AX1** — which no text-size ladder could have seen,
because at every split those ladders measured, the map was too small to show it. Full suite green:
2545 passed, 15 skipped.
**Was:** Not started. **Above the line for its first half** — the Position map's clear band is
**49.8 logical pixels against a floor of 96** on `main` right now, down from about 96-105, and task
11.203 measured it. **Nothing is broken; the screen is worse and the arithmetic that made it worse
is the subject.**
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** The collapse is ordinary work. **The instrument change is not** — it
alters the numbers on three screens at once, and one of the ways it can go wrong is by making a
floor easier to clear.
**Depends on:** 11.203, which built the first overlay that separated the two rules.

#### 1. The contradiction, and it is the whole finding

**The planning session predicted 11.203 would cost the map nothing, and cited rule 4 of this
screen's own MAP SPACE BUDGET:** *"a control that fits in a corner cluster (the two side columns)
costs the clear band nothing extra; a new full-width band costs it in full."*

**`clearBandHeight` in `test/support/app_shell_harness.dart` says the opposite, in its own doc
comment, on purpose:** *"Every overlay is treated as blocking the subject's full width, whatever its
own width. That is deliberate and conservative... a budget that let furniture accumulate along one
edge 'for free' is the budget that produced the defect this measures."*

> **Both were written deliberately. Neither had gone stale. They cannot both stand, and nothing in
> this repository could tell until 11.203 built the first overlay that was not full width** — the
> two squares stacked in a corner are charged as a full-width band of their combined height, so the
> band fell to **49.8 at the default text size and 40.0 from xxLarge up.**

**This is not "the tool is broken."** The tool's reason is the better one on its own terms: corners
that cost nothing is how a map ends up ringed with furniture. **The task is to settle the pair, and
to delete the losing text rather than leave both standing.**

#### 2. The settlement, because it satisfies both reasons rather than picking one

**Measure the largest clear *rectangle*, and hold it to a floor in both directions.**

- An overlay blocks only the horizontal extent it actually covers.
- The clear region must be at least **96 logical pixels tall** — the existing floor, unchanged, with
  its existing reason (a ray crossing needs about three marker heights).
- **And at least a stated width**, derived from the same argument and written down beside it. **A
  width floor is what makes "corners are free" safe**, and its absence is precisely why rule 4 was
  unsafe as written. **Rule 4 has to be rewritten too, not merely kept.**

> **A 48-pixel square in a corner leaves a rectangle nearly the map's full width and the map's full
> height — it passes both floors easily. Furniture accumulating along an edge eats the width until
> the region collapses and the band goes to zero.** That is the harness's reason and rule 4's
> reason, both held, by one measurement.

**The regression requirement, and it outranks the feature.** **On every layout that existed before
11.203 — where every overlay really was full width — the new computation must reproduce the old
numbers exactly.** A measurement that cannot reproduce what the old one said about the old inputs is
**a different instrument, not a better one.** Pin the old values first, then change the code.

**Report what moves on every screen that shares this harness, not only this one.** `clearBandHeight`
and `clearBandOverStack` are used by the Main Map, the Offline Data Map and this screen. **The Main
Map has corner buttons too, so its band may go up — and a floor that got easier to clear is a
finding, not a bonus.** Name every floor whose margin grew and by how much.

#### 3. The panel should be able to get out of the way entirely

**Michael:** *"the non-map part of the screen should be minimizable if the drag on that part of the
screen is pulled all the way down... there should still be the little grey bar... that allows the
user to pull it back up."*

**A new state below the panel's current floor**, which is furniture plus one bearing row. Collapsed,
the panel is the grab-handle strip and nothing else.

- **Snap, not continuous.** Dragging below a threshold snaps closed; dragging up from closed restores
  **the height it had before**, not a default. A panel showing half a row is neither state.
- **The handle keeps a touch target of at least 48 logical pixels** even though the pill is 4 tall,
  and grows with text size like everything else on this screen.
- **The collapsed handle is a button as well as a drag target, and its semantics label changes.**
  *"Resize the bearings list"* is wrong when the list is not there. **A collapsed panel reachable
  only by a drag gesture is unreachable by assistive technology** — this is not optional.
- **One thing must not disappear with the rest: a caution.** Collapsed, if
  `_warningMessages` is non-empty the handle strip carries the same amber warning **glyph**, tappable,
  opening the same sheet. **Not a coloured dot** — `CLAUDE.md`'s rule is that colour never carries a
  meaning on its own. Michael did not ask for this and would not have thought of it; *"geometry too
  degenerate to estimate"* silently vanishing while somebody taps bearings is the reason it is here.
- **Transient, not persisted.** It survives a tag change, like the existing fraction. It does not
  survive a restart.
- **The budget test gains collapsed cases at every text size.** With the panel closed the map has the
  whole body, and that is a state nothing has ever measured.

- **Acceptance:** the old numbers are pinned before the instrument changes and reproduced after; the
  width floor is stated with its reason; **rule 4 is rewritten, and the harness's doc comment is
  rewritten, and neither still claims what it claims now**; every floor whose margin changed on every
  screen is named; the collapsed state snaps, restores its previous height, keeps a 48-pixel target,
  reads correctly to a screen reader, and shows a caution glyph when there is a caution; the budget
  test covers collapsed at every text size; the Position map's clear band is back over 96.

### Task 11.205 — Three colours on the Position screen that nobody chose
**Status:** Done 2026-09-09. All three colours fixed, the tiles band added, the header row's summary
line dropped, and the flake from 11.204 did not recur across 10 full-suite runs. **Fixing the tag
label found a real regression of its own** — see below — and closing it moved two more of this
screen's pinned text-size thresholds, which are updated with fresh measurements.
**Was:** Not started. **Below the line.** Michael, 2026-09-09, on the Position screen: the map
draws everything in blue whatever the tag's colour, the tag label at the top is green, its colour dot
is missing, and the header row reads in jargon.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** The colour work is four small changes in one file. **Three more items
came out of task 11.204's report and are folded in here rather than made into their own commands**,
per Michael's standing instruction — one of them runs first and carries a stop order.
**Depends on:** 11.204, which is done.

#### 1. The map ignores the tag's colour, and the Main Map does not

**Every ray, marker, ellipse and estimate on this screen draws in `colors.bearingRay` /
`colors.estimatedPosition` — a fixed theme blue.** The Main Map has drawn per-tag colour since Phase
4: `_tagColor(tagId, tagNames, fallback)` over `tagColorFromHex`. **So the same animal is orange on
one screen and blue on the next**, which is Michael's word for it: confusion.

**Use the tag's own colour**, from `tagColorFromHex(tag.colorHex)`, for the rays, the ray markers,
the estimate marker, the uncertainty ellipse and **the legend card's swatches** — a legend that keeps
drawing blue while the map draws orange is worse than no legend. **The excluded-bearing alpha stays
exactly as it is.**

> **No contrast pass is needed and none should be invented.** The palette is Okabe-Ito,
> colourblind-safe, two entries already darkened for legibility as a filled map marker — and **the
> Main Map has drawn these same colours over these same basemaps since Phase 4.** The precedent
> settles it.

#### 2. The tag label is green because nothing chose a colour

`_TagSelectorBar` draws the frequency and tag name in a bare `TextButton`, whose Material default
foreground is `colorScheme.primary` — **the brand green.** Nobody picked it.

> **This is the same class as the six `ColorScheme` fallbacks of tasks 11.200 and 11.201 — a colour
> arriving by default rather than by decision — in a different mechanism.** And
> `theme_contrast_test.dart` **cannot catch it, because the green is perfectly readable.** The guard
> asks whether a person can see the ink; this defect is that the ink means something it should not.

**Give it an explicit `onSurface` foreground**, and **put the `TagColorSwatch` back in front of the
label.** That widget already exists and the tag-picker sheet this bar opens already uses it as its
`leadingBuilder`, so **the dot is present in the sheet and missing on the bar it opens from** —
which is how the bar came to be the only place in the app naming a tag without its colour.

#### 3. The header row says three things and should say none of them

It reads `N=3 · Ellipse:120m · Span:45min` in 11-point monospace. **Michael's call, 2026-09-09: all
three go.**

- **`N=3` is the same number as `3 of 5 selected`, in English, one row below it.** Duplicated, in
  jargon, in the smaller font.
- **`Span:45min` earns its space only when it is a problem — and when it is a problem there is
  already a caution saying *"animal may have moved"* in words.** A number that is only interesting
  when something else already said it is not a readout.
- **`Ellipse:120m` goes at Michael's direction.** The ellipse is drawn on the map with a scale bar,
  and **the number survives where it is actually compared** — the past-estimates sheet still prints
  the semi-major and semi-minor axes for every saved estimate.

**What remains in that row: the grab handle, the caution button when there is a caution, and the
history icon.** **Do not shrink `_headerRowHeight` to reclaim the freed space.** That constant is an
input to the space budget, this screen's history is a catalogue of constants changed without
re-measuring, and 11.204 is already moving those numbers. **Report the freed pixels as an
observation and spend none of them.**

#### 4. Before anything else: one red nobody can explain, bounded

Task 11.204 saw `test/features/map/map_screen_test.dart` **fail once in a full-suite run and pass on
the re-run and in isolation** — the group *"map-type selector has no panel and a blurred halo behind

finding. **That is the correct report, and one observation is not a diagnosis.**

**Run the full suite a stated number of times — no fewer than ten — and report what happened.** Do
not theorise first. **If it does not recur, say so with the count**, and that is the whole item. **If
it does recur, stop and report** — reproducing it is this task's job; fixing it is not.

> suspect is `TileFetchHealth.instance`, a mutable singleton several budget tests poison on purpose.
> **Every file that poisons it resets it in `setUp` and `tearDown`** — checked, all of them — **and

> session's brief for task 11.181 ranked two hypotheses and told the task where not to look, and the

**Why this is worth the time at all:** the pre-commit suite gates every commit, and a red nobody
trusts is how three tasks in a row came to commit through the escape hatch in early September.

#### 5. The Position map can now say when tiles stop arriving, and it should

**That screen is the only live map in the app that says nothing when the tile service stops
answering**, and the reason written into it was a measurement rather than an oversight: the clear band

an animal is is the worst place in the app to be reading a basemap that quietly stopped updating.

> **Michael may veto this and it reverses in one commit.** The planning session made the call rather

> appears only when something is wrong.

**A floor that got easier to clear is a finding, not a bonus**, and 11.204's report says so: two
screens have had more clear map than the arithmetic credited them with for as long as the instrument

**This is measure-and-report. Change nothing.** Find the places in `CLAUDE_DOCS/` and `lib/` that

push something else off*. **Re-check each against 11.204's numbers and report which reasons no longer

> **A decision recorded with its reason can be re-opened when the reason expires; one recorded

### Task 11.206 — Numbers measured against a thing that no longer exists, and a sentence in the wrong place
**Status:** Done, 2026-09-09. Two document-drift items from task 11.205's sweep, plus
an instance Michael saw on 2026-09-09 and one loose end in 11.205's own flake report.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** Nothing here is hard. **Item 1 must be re-measured rather than
reasoned about**, which is the whole point of it.
**Depends on:** 11.205, which found the first two.

#### 1. The Main Map's space-budget prose describes an app that was deleted in August

Its doc header says, in so many words: *"Where the floor actually stands, measured (both shell
banners live, a navigation target running): 229 logical pixels at the default text size, 191 / 152 /
134 up the ordinary slider, 102 at AX1 — and then 30 at AX2, 14 at AX3 and AX4, 8 at AX5. **It does
not hold at every text size and has not since it was written.**"*

> **Task 11.189 removed the shell banners entirely.** Every one of those nine numbers was measured in
> a configuration this app no longer has. **And the verdict contradicts the file's own test**, which
> task 11.204 updated: `bandHoldsThrough` is now 47/17 — AX4 — with a full before-and-after table.
> **A reader of `map_screen.dart` alone gets the wrong answer**, and that is the same shape as the
> contradiction that cost task 11.203 half a map: prose and instrument disagreeing with nobody able
> to tell.

**Re-measure. Do not edit the sentence until the test agrees with it.** The test carries **one**
number; the prose carries **nine plus a verdict plus a claim about the tightest state** (*"with tiles
failing on a new project it is 105 against a floor of 96 — nine pixels"*). **Deriving nine numbers
from one is a guess, and a guess written as a measurement is worse than the stale text it replaces.**

**Same cause, second file:** `position_estimation_screen.dart`'s AX3–AX5 fallback block was also
computed **with both shell banners live** and through the pre-11.204 instrument. Task 11.205 updated
only the paragraph its own fix touched and said so. **Re-derive the rest of that block, or state
plainly which parts no longer describe a real constraint at all.**

> **The standing lesson, and it is procedural rather than clever:** *when a change removes something
> every screen carried, it invalidates every number that was measured with that thing live — in one
> commit, across files, silently.* **The numbers live in prose, and no test reads prose.** Task
> 11.189 was a good change that left this behind, and it took three weeks and an unrelated sweep to

#### 2. A sentence explaining the app to itself, in a card that has no room for it

**Michael, 2026-09-09:** selecting a position estimate on the Main Map pops up a card carrying two
italic lines explaining *"The bearing wedges for these bearings are hidden while the ellipse is shown
— the heavy bearing lines show which ones made this."*

**He is right, and the file already contains the rule it breaks.** Rule 5 of that screen's own SPACE
BUDGET: **"Onboarding copy never occupies permanent space — it goes in the legend card's footnote,

> **Nobody misses those wedges.** You would have to have been looking at them a second earlier and

**Then derive the class, and report it rather than acting on it.** Find the sentences in the app that
**explain why the app draws what it draws**, as opposed to telling somebody something about their own
