### Task 11.242 — A v15 app and a v16 server both say "major 3", and one of them crashes
**Status:** Done 2026-09-13. **Measured first: it does fail, one step earlier than 11.240 said and
worse.** The v15 phone's own database refuses the v16 row (`Tags.color_hex TEXT NOT NULL`), the page
rolls back, the cursor never moves, and the phone reports the wreck as a fault in *itself* — *"Sync
has failed repeatedly. If this continues, contact whoever manages your project server"* — forever.
Held by `test/data/sync/v15_device_meets_v16_row_test.dart`, which runs the shipped migrations to
exactly v15 and inserts what a v16 writer sends. **Chosen: A.** `schemaMajorVersion` is **4**,
beginning at schema v16; the v15 build is refused with "This version of TriTrack is too old to sync
with the server. Update the app to continue syncing" (asserted with the literal 3-vs-4 numbers in
`sync_transport_refusal_test.dart`; the e2e suite's "older MAJOR is refused" test now exercises
exactly this pair). Cost today: zero devices stranded — Michael's is the only one, and it is on v16.
**The class is checked:** the wire's shape is frozen at each major
(`packages/tritrack_sync/lib/src/wire_shape_freezes.dart`, written by `tool/freeze_wire_shape.dart`)
and `assertWireShapeCompatibleWithMajor` fails the app, package and server suites on any change a
device on the current major cannot survive — `NOT NULL` lost or gained, type, key, bound tightened,
column or table gone, new `NOT NULL` column — with the remedy in the message. 11.240's own change
was replayed against it and goes red. What it cannot see is written on the file (reused names;
`RowValidator`'s enum sets). **Found on the way:** the backup scripts had been labelling every
archive "major 2" since major 3 shipped — see Discovered Scope. App 3141 / package 401 / server
suite in Docker green. ~~Not started.~~ **ABOVE THE LINE, and it must land before any build reaches another
person.** **Reported by task 11.240 itself, 2026-09-13**, as *"the one risk you are carrying"*.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** The measurement is small; the choice between two fixes is a contract
decision.
**Depends on:** 11.240.

#### What the contract says, and what the code now does

`TriTrack_Technical_Context.md` §"Version skew" is unambiguous: **`schemaMajorVersion` is the
compatibility boundary — same major syncs, different major refuses.** It is checked in every
envelope, in both directions.

**Task 11.240 made `Tags.color_hex` nullable and left `schemaMajorVersion` at 3.** So a v15 client
and a v16 server both announce major 3, the check passes, they sync — **and 11.240 reports the v15
client then crashes on the null colour.**

> **That is the compatibility boundary declaring two builds compatible when they are not.** The
> codebase already argues this exact point from the other direction: `pulse_modes.dart` explains
> that every new column was made nullable precisely to avoid *"turning a minor schema difference
> into a device that cannot sync."* **This is the mirror image — a column that was non-null becoming
> nullable — and it strands an old reader just as thoroughly, but by crashing rather than refusing.**

#### 1. Measure it before choosing, and do not inherit the crash

**11.240 stated the crash; nothing in the repository demonstrates it.** Build the case: a v15-shaped
client model reading a v16 row with a null `color_hex`.

- **If it crashes, that is the finding and it is a test from then on.**
- **If it does not** — if the model tolerates null — say so plainly; the rest of this task may
  collapse to a documentation fix, and **a clean negative is a result.**

#### 2. Then choose, and the choice is the task

**Option A — bump `schemaMajorVersion` to 4.** The honest answer: the builds *are* incompatible, so
the boundary should say so and the old client should **refuse rather than crash**. **The cost is
normally that every device in the field must update — and today that cost is zero**, because
Michael's is the only device. **That will not be true after March.**

**Option B — keep `Tags.color_hex` non-null and mirror the animal's colour into it.** Old clients
read a valid colour; new clients ignore the column. **This buys compatibility with a second copy of
a value**, which 11.240's brief explicitly forbade as two sources of truth — so if it is chosen,
**the mirror must be written in exactly one place, read by nothing in the new app, and declared
`TagColumnKind.retired` with the reason.**

**Say which and why.** The planning session's inclination is **A**, on the same reasoning that put
11.240 above the line: the window in which this is free has a date on it. **But the measurement in
item 1 comes first**, because if nothing crashes there is nothing to bump for.

#### 3. Whatever is chosen, the boundary must be checkable

**The defect here is not the null column — it is that nothing noticed.** A column changing from
non-null to nullable, in a table both majors share, is a class.

- **Add a check that fails when a shared table's column loses `NOT NULL` without a major bump**, or
  — if that is too blunt — **write down why it cannot be automated**, the way
  `assertEveryTagColumnDeclaresItsKind` does for a judgement that genuinely cannot.
- **An unenforceable rule in a document is what this task exists because of.**

- **Acceptance:** the v15-reads-v16 case built and its answer reported, **including if it does not
  crash**; the choice made in writing with its cost; if a major bump, an old client **refusing
  cleanly** with a sentence a person can read, asserted; if a mirror, exactly one writer, no reader
  in the new app, and the column declared retired with its reason; and a check on the
  non-null-to-nullable class, or a written argument for why there cannot be one.


### Task 11.243 — Deployments: the dated link, and the wipe
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-20.** The device and server halves are confirmed: the server reports `schema_migrations` at **18**, and v17's wipe and its bookkeeping row land in one transaction — either both happened or neither did. Michael rebuilt the phone and re-entered collars and animals on 2026-09-16. ~~Partial 2026-09-13.~~ Built, and all three suites green — `flutter test` 3224,
`run_server_tests_docker.sh` 1010, the sync package 419. **Partial because the acceptance ends on
Michael's phone and the beta server, and neither has run this**: schema v17 deletes every collar,
bearing and animal on both, on purpose, and *"it deletes the right things"* is a claim two test
suites make and no device has confirmed. It becomes `Done` when he reports the rebuild and the
redeploy. **Specified by
`CLAUDE_DOCS/ANIMALS_AND_DEPLOYMENTS_DESIGN.md`, 2026-09-14 — read it first; this entry does not
restate it.**
**Model:** **Opus, high. Run alone.** It is schema major 5 and it deletes data on purpose.
**Depends on:** 11.240 (Individuals), 11.242 (the freeze it will trip).
**Followed by:** 11.244 (the screens), 11.245 (the cleanup).

#### 1. The model, from the document

Build **§3** (Tags loses `date_put_on`, `date_removed`, `capture_date`, `individual_id`), **§4**
(`Deployments`), **§5** (Individuals: status gains `unknown`, no capture date), and **§6** (the
interlock). **Where this entry and the document disagree, the document wins** — and say so in the
report, because a disagreement means one of them is stale and that is worth knowing.

- **The interlock is enforced on the server too, or it is advisory.** §6 says this and it is the
  half most likely to be skipped: a rule enforced on one device is a rule about that device, not
  about the record.
- **`Deployments` is project-scoped and has no `lineage_id`** — §4 gives the reason.

#### 2. Deriving an observation's animal — the load-bearing part

**The deployment whose tag matches and whose interval contains the observation's timestamp.** No
`individual_id` on `Observations`, ever.

- **A bearing with no covering deployment has no animal, and that is correct** (§2) — a collar that
  fell off still transmits. **Assert it**; the natural implementation quietly attributes it to the
  most recent animal instead.
- **A deployment with a null `attached_date` covers no interval and attributes nothing.** Also
  correct, also counter-intuitive, **also asserted** — Michael flagged it as the thing that will
  look like a bug the first time he meets it.

#### 3. The wipe — write no migration

**Michael will wipe: every device and the beta server hold development data only** (§9).

- **Drop and recreate.** Write **no** data-preserving path. **A migration that preserves nothing is
  machinery serving nothing**, and this project has spent real effort on elaborate paths for five
  test rows before.
- **Remove 11.240's one-animal-per-tag backfill** rather than compensating for it. The spurious
  animals disappear with the wipe.
- **Say plainly in the report what a person must do**: redeploy the server, rebuild the app,
  re-enter their tags and animals. **A destructive step that does not say so is the defect this
  project has been chasing all week in a new costume.**

#### 4. Schema major 5

§10. Justify it on `schemaMajorVersion` beside majors 2, 3 and 4; extend `schemaMajorFirstMinor`;
run `tool/freeze_wire_shape.dart`.

- **Re-derive the out-of-tree wire readers before the bump**, with the grep in
  `TriTrack_Technical_Context.md` §"What speaks the wire and is not the app". **The backup scripts
  were wrong for three days after the last bump because that list did not exist. It exists now;
  use it, and report what it found** — including *"nothing new"*, which is the result that proves
  the list works.
- **Server first, then the app.**

- **Acceptance:** §§3, 4, 5, 6 built as written; the interlock enforced **on the server as well as
  the client**, asserted on both; an observation's animal derived by interval, with **no covering
  deployment** and **null attached date** both asserted to attribute nothing; `Observations`
  untouched; no data-preserving migration written; the backfill removed; major 5 justified, frozen,
  and the out-of-tree readers re-derived with the result reported.

#### 5. What 11.243 built, and the four judgement calls it made — added by the task, 2026-09-13

**Where the entry and the document disagreed, the document won, and there was one disagreement
worth naming.** §5 lists *"one addition"* to `Individuals` — the `unknown` status — and **task
11.240 had already built it**, so §5 needed no code at all. `IndividualStatus` has carried
`alive`, `dead`, `unknown` since v16. Asserted in `individuals_test.dart` so the document's claim
is checked rather than assumed. **The document is stale on that line, not wrong about anything
else.**

**Four calls the design does not make, each flagged because a later reader will meet them:**

1. **`Tag_Library` is wiped too.** It is device-local and off the wire, so §9 says nothing about
   it — but §3's *"a tag is equipment"* applies to the personal inventory exactly, and the form
   that edits both would otherwise still have to ask for a `date_put_on` only one of them has.
2. **"Whose collar is this" and "which animal was this bearing about" are different questions
   with different answers**, and both are in the code by name
   (`latestAnimalForTag`, `animalForObservation`). A collar that came off Marie in June is listed
   under Marie *and* its bearings since June are attributed to nobody. The design implies the
   second; the first had to be decided, because a list of equipment has no timestamp to be asked
   with.
3. **Linking is contributor-level, where `Tags.individual_id` was owner-only.** The rung moved
   with the column: writing a `Deployments` row is an insert under the ordinary gradient, and
   which collar went on which bird is what the person holding the bird knows.
4. **The archive's v16→v17 crossing is deliberately lossy** — it drops the same four columns and
   synthesises no deployments, so an imported archive lands exactly where the device's own
   migration leaves it. `SchemaMigrator._lowestMigratableMajor`'s contract said *lossless* and now
   says so with major 5 named as the exception and a bound on it.

**§5a is not built and that is deliberate.** The app defaults `attached_date` to today (rule one);
it does **not** close the animal's previous deployment in the same act, nor confirm both changes
first (rule two). Until 11.244 the interlock refuses a link to an animal already wearing a collar,
and says which dates to fix — correct, and clumsy.

#### 5. What 11.244 built, and the four calls it made — added by the task, 2026-09-14

**§4's three handovers, all three resolved.**

1. **The two uncalled methods have callers, and one changed shape on the way.** `unlink` is *Remove
   record* on the animal's screen. The derivation's honest caller turned out to be the **Log's
   animal filter** — and the exemption's own prediction (*"find it a caller"*) was wrong about the
   shape: **every real caller asks it about a screenful of records at once**, so a per-record query
   would be one SQLite round trip per row on the UI path. It is `animalForObservationIn` now, a
   pure function over deployments the caller already holds. **The exemption list asked the right
   question and got an answer nobody had predicted**, which is the argument for keeping it.
2. **§5a is built**, confirmation included, and `DeploymentLinking` is a *plan then a write* so the
   sentence a person reads and the rows that land are the same object.
3. **The tag-library colour is gone**, which is §4's fallback rather than its preference. The
   preferred option — offer it as the new animal's starting colour when a collar is linked — has
   nowhere to land: **linking attaches a collar to an animal that already exists and already has a
   colour**, and creating an animal during linking is precisely what design §1 forbids. So the
   swatch came off the row *and* the Color section came off that screen's form, because leaving one
   without the other asks a question whose answer is invisible.

**Four calls the design does not make:**

1. **A screen, not a bigger dialog.** `IndividualEditDialog` was already a long scroll; the collar
   list adds a row per deployment with two actions each, plus link, merge and delete. The two share
   `IndividualFields`, so the animal's fields have one definition while both exist. **Task 11.245
   decides whether Project Setup's grouping — and with it the dialog — survives.**
2. **A deployment date is a local calendar day at its own midnight**, not `DateTime.now()` and not
   UTC midnight. `deploymentDateFor` carries the reasoning: UTC midnight would put a collaring at
   9am in New Zealand *before* the deployment it belongs to and lose the whole first morning of
   bearings. The cost — the same row reads a day out on a device in another zone — is the smaller
   error and is stated on the function.
3. **The Log's animal filter is exact now; the Map's is not.** The Log asks the derivation of each
   row. The Map's per-animal checkbox toggles *legend rows*, which are collars, so it still means
   "every collar she has worn". See Discovered Scope.
4. **The picker offers only collars free on the chosen date.** A pre-check more permissive than
   nothing and never stricter than the write: it hides no collar a person could link, it spares
   them a refusal they could not have avoided.

### Task 11.246 — A new synced table arrived and the permissions matrix does not know
**Status:** **Done 2026-09-15.** `flutter test`: green (one unrelated, unreproduced single failure
in a full-suite run — see the comms entry). Command file deleted.
**Below the line, but before a beta** — `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` is a gate
document, and a gate document that is out of date is worse than one that is missing.
**Found by the planning session 2026-09-14**, reviewing task 11.243's fourth judgement call.
**Model:** **Sonnet, low.** One row, one paragraph, one check. **Three rows now — see the widening
below.**
**Depends on:** 11.243. **Run before `/11-56`.**

**Done, 2026-09-15.** New §4.7 "Individuals and Deployments" in `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md`, derived
from `tableMutationRules` and the two repositories, stating the rung explicitly (both tables are
`MutationRule.anyUser`; no owner-only rung, and 11.243's reasoning is quoted for why). `Individuals`
did have no section either, confirming the widening's prediction that this is a habit rather than
one oversight. **A new §3.2 registry** maps every one of the 14 tables in `Tables.all` to the
section documenting it, checked by `test/documentation/permissions_matrix_table_coverage_test.dart`
against `Tables.all` directly (not a grep) in both directions — watched red by removing the
`Deployments` row and confirming the failure names the table and what to write, then restored.
`Project_Tags` (no longer in `Tables.all` since task 11.219) is declared excluded rather than
omitted, with its own regression test so a real gap cannot hide behind that declaration.
**Security-model sweep: clean negative** — grepped for `individual_id` and for the old
`Tags.individual_id` owner-only rule; neither appears in `TriTrack_Security_Model.md`, so there was
nothing to correct.

**Discovered scope, not asked for by this task.** Writing §4.7 surfaced a live instance of §2's own
corollary: merging two animals (`IndividualMerge.merge`, "Same animal as…" on the animal detail
screen) is owner-only on the screen and on the device, and **has no server-side check at all** —
both tables it writes are `MutationRule.anyUser`. A contributor editing their own database file
directly, or crafting the equivalent push, can perform an irreversible, cross-row, owner-only act at
the contributor rung. Recorded as §8 entries 13 and 14 (the second: the "shared tables" cross-author
test doesn't cover `Individuals` or `Deployments` either). **Ask the planning session to add both to
Phase 11** — see the comms entry for the exact ask.

#### What happened, and why the row matters more than it looks

Task 11.243 added `Deployments` and **moved a permission rung while doing it**: linking a collar to
an animal is **contributor-level**, where `Tags.individual_id` had been **owner-only**. The task's
reasoning is good and is not in question — *"which collar went on which bird is what the person
holding the bird knows"* — **but it is recorded only in a plan entry.**

**`PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` has no `Deployments` row.** Its own opening says *"nothing below is filled
from memory; every verdict was read out of the source"* — and a table arrived without one.

> **This is the hand-maintained-list defect, in the document whose whole purpose is to stop a
> permission drifting unnoticed.** Finding N-1, which that document exists to prevent, was exactly
> a rung that changed meaning while nobody was looking.

#### 1. The row, read from the code

Add `Deployments` the way every other row was made: **from `tableMutationRules` and the row
validator, not from this entry.** Say who may create, edit and delete a deployment, and what happens
when two people disagree.

- **State the rung change explicitly**, with 11.243's reasoning: owner-only for the old column,
  contributor-level for the new table, and why that is the right rung rather than an accident of
  where the data moved.
- **`Individuals` — check it too.** Task 11.240 added it four days earlier. **If it has no row
  either, that is the finding, not a second chore** — it means the gap is a habit rather than an
  oversight, and the check in item 2 becomes the point of this task rather than a nicety.

> **WIDENED 2026-09-15, and the reason strengthens this task rather than growing it.** Task 11.252
> — an ad-hoc bug fix, not a permissions task — **added a row to `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` itself**,
> for deleting a "no signal" record. It did the right thing. **But a permissions row arriving
> through a bug fix is the same shape as the two rows missing here:** the document's own process is
> not what keeps it current, and nothing notices either way. **Read that row rather than trusting
> it**, the same as every other.
>
> **And run this before `/11-56`, not after.** The season clone copies deployments into a new
> project, which is a permissions question on a table that has no row yet. **A check that exists
> first cannot be left stale by it**; a check written afterwards is one more catch-up.

#### 2. The check that makes the row unnecessary next time

**Every synced table must have a section in `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md`.** The list of synced tables is
already enumerable in code; the document's headings are greppable. **A test that compares the two
and fails on a table with no section** turns this class off permanently.

- **Fail with the table's name and what to write**, not with a diff.
- **Existing tests already read this document** (`permissions_matrix_membership_test.dart` and
  others) — **put this beside them and check whether one of them already half-does it** before
  writing a new file.
- **If some table legitimately needs no section, it declares that** rather than being omitted —
  omission and "deliberately not applicable" must not look identical, which is this project's
  assertion-by-absence rule.

#### 3. The security model, only if the rung reaches it

**Check whether `TriTrack_Security_Model.md` states the old rung anywhere** — the owner-only rule for
attaching a collar to an animal. **If it does, correct it with the date and the reason.** If it does
not, say so; **a sweep that finds nothing is a result**, and this one takes a grep.

- **Acceptance:** a `Deployments` section derived from the code, naming the rung change and its
  reasoning; `Individuals` checked and added if missing, with the result reported either way; a test
  failing when a synced table has no section, **watched red** against a table with its section
  removed; deliberate exclusions declared rather than omitted; and the security-model sweep reported
  including a clean negative.

look — Michael checked it on his device (2026-09-15) and found colours still wrong, which turned
out to be a **third, deeper bug** underneath both fixes above — see this phase's Discovered Scope,
*"A same-day handover silently misattributes bearings."* `Deployment.covers()` compares an
instant against a calendar-day boundary the wrong way round for a same-day removal, so a bearing
taken earlier the same day a collar changes hands can be excluded from the old deployment and
absorbed by the new one — exactly what Michael saw (one bearing turned grey, the other took on
the new animal's colour). **This task cannot be called Done until that is fixed**, because its
own acceptance — the Map filtering and colouring bearings correctly — depends on the same
derivation. Michael asked that the fix be a fresh task for Opus or Fable rather than continued
here, given how far the root cause reaches (also the Log's animal filter, task 11.244).
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium** for what shipped here. The still-open root cause is
algorithm-correctness work on a shared time-interval derivation — see the Discovered Scope entry
for why it needs a different model.
**Depends on:** 11.244, and now also on the new task the Discovered Scope entry above asks for.

#### The asymmetry, as measured

**The Log's animal filter is exact**: it asks which deployment covered each bearing, so *"show me
Marie"* means the bearings that were about Marie.

**The Map's is not**: its per-animal checkbox toggles legend rows, and **a legend row is a collar**.
So the Map shows *every bearing from every collar Marie has ever worn* — including the ones taken
after a collar came off her and went on something else, or after it fell in a creek and kept
transmitting.

> **Neither screen is wrong about what it is doing.** The Log filters records; the Map toggles
> layers. **But one project now answers the same question two ways, and a person will meet both in
> the same afternoon** — most likely while checking whether a position estimate used the right
> bearings, which is the worst moment to find out.

#### 1. Make the Map answer the Log's question

**Per-ray filtering**, not per-legend-row. A ray belongs to Marie if the deployment covering its
observation names Marie.

- **Reuse the Log's derivation. Do not write a second one** — two answers to *"whose bearing is
  this"* is the defect this task exists to remove, and adding a third would be funny rather than
  fixed.
- **A ray with no covering deployment belongs to nobody** and must not appear under any animal.
  **That is the case the whole deployment model was built for** (design §2): a collar that fell off
  still transmits. **Assert it** — the natural implementation attributes it to the collar's most
  recent animal.

#### 2. Decide what the legend shows, and say why

The legend is a list of collars. If the filter becomes per-animal, **the legend and the filter stop
describing the same thing.**

- **Decide: does the legend list animals, collars, or both?** Say why. **Do not leave a legend that
  implies a filter it no longer performs** — a control that lies about its own scope is this
  project's most repeated shape.
- **Colour is the animal's** (design §5), so a legend of collars already draws two rows in one
  colour for a re-collared animal. **That is a hint about the right answer, not the answer.**

#### 3. It ends on a device

A rendering change, so the standing rule applies: **one change, then a look.** Report `Partial` until
Michael has opened the Map with a re-collared animal and said the rays are the ones he expects.

- **Acceptance:** the Map filters per ray using the Log's own derivation, **shared, not copied**; a
  ray with no covering deployment appears under no animal, asserted; the legend's meaning decided in
  writing and matching what the filter does; `Partial` until a device look.

### Task 11.251 — Four answers to "which animal was wearing this collar", and on a handover day none of them can be right

**Status:** **Done 2026-09-15.** **Confirmed on Michael's phone the same day, after the second
device look: *"Tested and the colors are now correct."*** The code was complete and `flutter test`
green locally on the first commit (there is no CI until 1 October, so the local run is the only
evidence); it stayed Partial because the acceptance names Michael's phone, and his first look found
four things, below. **11.247's own status is the planning session's to move — its device check is
this same look.**
**First device look, 2026-09-15, found three defects on the animal's screen and one on the map, all
fixed the same session (second commit):** *Current* was written as "spans today", so after a swap
both the old and the new collar read Current — it now means *not yet recorded as off*; the rows
were oldest-first — newest is on top now; the row's three buttons ran off the right edge of the
phone — a wrapping bar, measured at 6.1-inch width; and **a bearing on B drew grey because the swap
time was rounded down to the minute**, which put a swap confirmed at 14:32:50 *before* a bearing
taken at 14:32:30 — the accepted time is written to the second now. That last one is a hypothesis
from the code, not a log capture; the second device look is what confirms it. What landed: a date-only deployment covers the whole of both its end days (`Deployment.coversMoment`,
the grey bearing — watched red at the model, the repository, the Log and the Map); the §5a
confirmation offers a swap time prefilled with now on any same-day swap, and *Set removed date* offers
one when the day is today, so both ends of Michael's tag move carry an instant; a moment two
deployments both cover is `AnimalAttribution.contested` and no reader picks — the Log lists it under
both animals, the Map draws it neutral and the legend says *"Contested: Alpha or Bravo"*. **The wire
decision: the time goes into the existing `attached_date`/`removed_date` columns; reasoning on
`deploymentEndHasTime` in `deployment.dart` and in this task's comms entry.** Interlock untouched and
asserted; server untouched. The derivations re-counted from the code: **six, not four** — the
instant question and the day question now sit side by side on the model as `coversMoment` and
`spansDay`; the "Link a tag" picker's busy set asks the interlock's own `overlapDays` rather than
keeping a third rule; the Dart `latestAnimalForTag` and the tag read join now run one shared
subquery (`latestDeploymentsSubquery`) instead of two hand-matched tie-breaks; and a sixth,
`latestAnimalByTag`, had no caller and the unfixed tie-break, and is deleted. **Above the line, and
it blocks 11.247 from closing.** It is wrong data on
a map a person reads to decide where to walk.
**Found by Michael on his device 2026-09-15**, after two fixes on 2026-09-14 that were both correct
and both about a different question. **Root-caused by the 11.247 session and deliberately not fixed
there, at Michael's instruction.** Read this phase's Discovered Scope entry of 2026-09-15 first —
**it is the measurement and it does not need repeating.** This entry is what to do about it.
**Model:** **Opus, high** (Fable acceptable). Michael: *"I don't believe sonnet is up to the task."*
It is algorithm correctness on a derivation four features depend on, and **the last three attempts
each fixed a real bug and left this one standing.**
**Depends on:** nothing. **Fresh window, alone.** Do not run it beside anything that edits
`map_screen.dart`, `log_screen.dart` or `deployments_provider.dart`.

#### Do not start by fixing `covers()`

**The Discovered Scope entry's suggested fix — widen the end of a same-day interval to the whole
day — is offered there as a starting point and it is not sufficient. Understand why before you
write anything.**

With a closed end, on a handover day **two deployments cover the same 2pm bearing**: the outgoing
one (removed today, now covering all of today) and the incoming one (attached today, no end).
`DeploymentRepository.animalForObservationIn` returns the **first match in a list**. So the widened
version would answer confidently and arbitrarily — **it swaps one silent wrong answer for another,
and this time with no boundary condition to find it by.**

**`covers()`'s own doc comment already saw this and chose half-open deliberately:** *"there is no
honest way to pick between them. Half-open gives the day to the incoming collar, which is the one
that is still transmitting."* **That reasoning is the real question, and it is wrong in two ways
that must both be answered, not patched:**

1. **It gives the whole handover day to the incoming collar**, including bearings recorded hours
   before the swap. That is Michael's yellow bearing.
2. **It considered only the case where there *is* an incoming collar.** When a deployment is closed
   with no replacement for that tag — which §5a does *automatically* to an animal's previous collar
   whenever a new one is attached — the removal day belongs to nobody at all. **That is Michael's
   grey bearing, and it is a plain data-loss bug independent of any handover:** every bearing taken
   on the day a collar comes off is currently attributed to no animal, forever.

#### 1. The decision, and it was made on 2026-09-15 — read design §4a, not this section's options

**Deployment dates are calendar days (§4, "nobody types this"). A bearing has an instant. On a
handover day the data genuinely cannot say which animal a 2pm bearing was about.** Any fix either
answers that honestly or guesses. Three candidates:

- **(a) Say "ambiguous", and make every reader handle it.** Close both ends at day granularity;
  when more than one deployment covers the moment, the derivation returns **ambiguous with the
  candidates**, never one of them. Each of the four readers then decides in the open: the Log shows
  the bearing under both animals, the Map draws it neutral, the legend says the day is contested.
  **This is consistent with what Michael already accepted for the Record wheel** — *"on the handover
  day the wheel shows BOTH tags, and that is correct"* — and it fixes the grey bearing outright,
  because a removal with no replacement is not ambiguous at all.
- **(b) Ask for the time, on a same-day handover only.** §5a **already stops and confirms** that
  swap in a dialog naming both collars and both dates. Adding *"roughly what time?"* to that one
  dialog removes the ambiguity where it is created, for the one case that has it. **§4's "nobody
  types this" stays true everywhere else**, because every other deployment is still a bare date.
- **(c) Freeze the animal onto the bearing when it is recorded.** **Rejected already** — design §2
  decided a bearing gets its animal from time and not a pointer, precisely so that correcting a
  deployment's dates corrects the bearings. **Do not reverse that as a side effect of a bug fix.**

> **DECIDED BY MICHAEL, 2026-09-15: (b), and it is written up as design §4a. Read that section;
> it is the authority and this paragraph is only the history.** His words: *"I'm leaning toward b…
> this will likely never happen: a tag removed from an animal one day and mounted on another on the
> same day. This is a real edge case… If asking for a time of the swap is needed to get around this
> issue so be it."*
>
> **§4a turns that into two rules, and the first is the one that fixes the bug he actually saw:**
> a date-only deployment **covers the whole of both its end days** (which is the grey bearing, and
> has nothing to do with swaps), and a same-day swap **may carry a time, prefilled with now**, which
> beats the day. **(c) is refused in §4a in writing.** The contested-day answer from (a) survives as
> the floor for the rows neither rule reaches — hand-typed dates, older rows, a skipped time — and
> **it is expected to be rare precisely because rule 2 exists**, which is Michael's own argument.
>
> **Two things §4a hands this task rather than settling:** whether the swap time goes into the
> existing `attached_date`/`removed_date` columns — which already hold instants, so this needs no
> schema change — or into new nullable columns; and the compatibility call that follows from it.
> **Storing a time in a column older builds read as a day is "a name reused for new meaning", the
> one thing `wire_shape_freezes.dart` is blind to.** Decide it and write it down.

#### 2. Count the derivations before changing one

**There are four implementations of "which animal is/was this tag on", using three different
notions of time.** Counted from the code on 2026-09-15, and **derive them again rather than trusting
this list** — this project's standing rule, and the reason the last two fixes each corrected one:

| | Notion of time | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Deployment.covers(at)` | an instant against midnight-stamped days, **half-open** | `animalForObservationIn` (Log filter, Map filter, Map colour, legend), `tagIdsOnAnAnimalAt`, the Animal Detail screen's "is this current" |
| `_deploymentSpansDay` | **calendar day, closed both ends** | `tagIdsAudibleOn` — the Record wheel and the no-signal checklist |
| `latestAnimalForTag` | **most recent row**, tie-broken on `created_at` | `Tag.individualName` |
| the `individual_name` join in `tag_repository.dart` | most recent row, in SQL | the same field, from the other side |

**Two of these are the same question in two languages and were fixed in parallel on 2026-09-14.
Two of them are different questions that look alike.** Say which is which, in writing, and **make
the ones that must agree share an implementation rather than a matching comment.**

#### 3. The finding underneath the finding, and it should not be lost

**Task 11.249 met this exact defect and routed around it.** Its comms entry says it used
`tagIdsAudibleOn` *"deliberately not `Deployment.covers`, which is half-open and would drop the
collar taken off this morning."* **It was right, it said so, and it wrote a second function instead
of filing the first as broken** — so the defect stayed live in three other readers for five days
and cost two further sessions. **This is `CLAUDE.md`'s "a workaround in a test is a defect nobody
filed", in production rather than in a test.** Name it in the fix.

#### 4. What the fix has to clear

- **`DeploymentInterlock.overlapDays` (`packages/tritrack_sync`) does its own day arithmetic on the
  same two columns**, and §6's one-day tolerance is what makes a same-day handover legal at all.
  **A change made for the attribution question must not loosen the interlock.** Assert the interlock
  unchanged, with the one-day handover still permitted and a two-day overlap still refused.
- **The day-granular callers are already right and must stay right.** `tagIdsOnAnAnimalAt` and
  `_deploymentSpansDay` pass an `at` that is itself day-normalised, so both sides agree; the
  Discovered Scope entry measured that. **Re-verify every caller rather than trusting it.**
- **The server enforces the interlock too** (§6). Say whether anything here changes what the server
  must do; if nothing does, say that in writing rather than by omission.

#### 5. Evidence

- **A regression test through each of the four readers**, not only through `covers()` — Log filter,
  Map filter, Map colour, legend. **This project's history is full of a correct derivation with a
  broken caller and the reverse**, and the last two fixes were each proved at one layer.
- **Watch each of them red first.** Reproduce Michael's exact scenario as the fixture: A yellow,
  B red, tag 1 on A, tag 2 on B, a bearing on each, tag 2 moved B → A the same day. **The grey
  bearing and the yellow bearing are two separate assertions with two separate causes.**
- **There is no CI until 1 October.** The local run is the only evidence this task will ever have.

- **Acceptance:** the removal-day data loss is fixed (a bearing on the day a collar comes off is
  attributed to the animal it came off, watched red first); **the §5a confirmation offers a swap
  time prefilled with now, and a recorded time beats the day at both ends of the swap**; a moment
  still covered by two deployments is **reported as contested and never silently resolved**; the
  four derivations are enumerated from the code, with the ones that must agree sharing an
  implementation; **the wire-meaning decision from §4a is made and written down**; the interlock is
  asserted unchanged; a test through each of the four readers; **task 11.247 re-opened and closed
  only after a device look**, since its own check cannot mean anything until this lands.

### Task 11.255 — Deleting an animal becomes an owner's decision, on the phone and on the server

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-15. Both suites green locally — 1015 server tests (Docker), 3332 Flutter
tests (15 skipped, 0 failed). **No CI until 1 October, so these local runs are the only evidence this
task has**, per its own acceptance. **Above the line for Gate C** — it was the irreversible act a
contributor could reach today, and Gate C's condition is *before anyone else's data is on it*.
**Decided by Michael, 2026-09-15**, choosing option (a) from task 11.254's three: *"I like the idea
of deleting an animal is an own only decision."*
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** The design question was answered by 11.254 and by Michael; what is
left is one rung in three places, watched red.
**Depends on:** 11.254, which measured the problem and costed this. **Read its §4.7 (IN4) and §8
entry 13 in `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` first** — they are the finding, and this entry does not repeat
them.

#### Why this is the right rung, in one paragraph, because it reverses half of an earlier decision

**Task 11.254 refuted the premise it was given, correctly.** A merge is not an operation the server
can recognise: **a contributor can produce a merge's exact end state with four ordinary buttons** —
withdraw each collar, attach it to the other animal, edit the attached date back, then *Delete
animal*. So the owner rung on *"Same animal as…"* is **a rung on one button**, and a server cannot
refuse a distinction the product does not make.

**The distinction the product does make is destruction.** Re-pointing collars is recoverable by
hand; a deleted animal is not. **So the rung goes on the delete**, and both routes close at once.

> **This half-reverses task 11.244, which said a contributor may remove an animal made by mistake —
> and 11.244's reason survives.** A contributor can still **rename** the animal and withdraw its
> collars; neither destroys a record. **A mistake stays fixable by the person who made it. What
> moves behind the owner rung is destroying a record, not correcting one.** Say this on the screen
> when the control is refused — a contributor who meets a greyed *Delete animal* must be told the
> thing they *can* do, not only what they cannot.

#### 1. Three places, and the server is the one that counts

- **`IndividualRepository.remove` asserts the owner rung**, the way the tag repository already does.
  **Before the first write, not on it** — `IndividualMerge.merge`'s own comment has the reasoning.
- **The delete control gates on `isOwner`**, not on `mayWrite`, and **explains itself when refused**
  in the plain English above. Task 11.220/11.221's tag precedent is the shape: the refusal is not
  the end of the road.
- **The server refuses a non-owner's tombstone of a stored `Individuals` row.** 11.254 established
  that `MutationRule` **cannot** hold a delete to a different rung from an edit — one rule per
  table, no operation distinction — so this is a branch in `RowAuthorizer` mirroring
  `_authorizeTagLifecycle`: refuse a non-owner's update whose `deleted_at` goes null → set.
  **Do not raise `Tables.individuals` to `owner`** — that would refuse the contributor workflow
  task 11.243 chose, which is the trap 11.254 already stepped around.

#### 2. What must not move with it

- **Creating and editing an animal stay contributor-level.** So does linking and unlinking a collar.
  **Assert that**, or the next reader will assume the whole table moved.
- **`DeploymentLinking.deleteAnimal`** is the call the screen makes; it unlinks then deletes. **The
  unlink half is contributor-level and stays so** — a contributor who is refused the delete must not
  be left having silently withdrawn every collar first. **Refuse before the first write.**
- **The merge keeps its owner rung** and now genuinely has one end to end, rather than on a button.

#### 3. Evidence

- **Watch the server refusal red** — a contributor's tombstone of an `Individuals` row must answer
  `unauthorized`, and 11.254's derived cross-author loop is where it belongs if it fits there.
- **Watch the repository refusal red**, and watch that the unlink half did not happen.
- **The screen's refusal is asserted with its sentence**, not only its greyed state.
- **No CI until 1 October** — `scripts/run_server_tests_docker.sh` and `flutter test` locally are the
  only evidence this will ever have. Say so.

- **Acceptance:** deleting an animal is refused for a non-owner at the repository and at the server,
  both watched red; **nothing is written before the refusal**; create, edit, link and unlink remain
  contributor-level and that is asserted; the screen names what a contributor *can* do instead;
  `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` §4.7 and §8 entry 13 updated from decided-and-open to closed; both suites
  green locally.

> **Met, in full — 2026-09-15.** `IndividualRepository.assertMayDelete` refuses before
> `IndividualRepository.remove`'s write; `DeploymentLinking.deleteAnimal` asks it again before the
> first deployment is unlinked, and `test/data/repositories/individual_authorization_test.dart`
> watches both refusals red and watches nothing land — the animal survives undeleted and the
> deployment survives unwithdrawn. The server's `RowAuthorizer._authorizeIndividualLifecycle`
> refuses a non-owner's `deleted_at` null→set write on `Individuals`
> (`DenialReason.deleteIndividualRequiresOwner`), watched red by
> `server/test/authz/permissions_matrix_test.dart`'s widened "shared tables" group — which now asks
> the alter and remove questions separately per table, because `Individuals` is the first one where
> they have different answers. Create, edit, link and unlink are asserted contributor-level in the
> same file. The screen's `_deleteDisabledReason` names renaming and withdrawing tags as what a
> contributor can still do, asserted by its sentence in
> `test/features/more/animals_screen_test.dart`. `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` §4.7 (IN3, IN4), the "Two
> people" note and §8 entry 13 are rewritten as closed. 1015 server tests and 3332 Flutter tests
> (15 skipped) passed locally; no CI exists to confirm it a second way before 1 October.

### Task 11.256 — Six instances fixed one at a time, and nobody has ever defined the class

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-15. **The two hazards are separated by measurement
(`test/core/providers/ref_after_await_hazards_test.dart`, ten cases), the population is derived from
the code (`test/core/providers/ref_after_await_guard_test.dart`: 48 auto-disposing providers, 8 with
the body shape, 19 reached by a bare read, 0 with all three at once), and the guard was watched red on
the real tree twice — a bare read of `snapshotProjectIds` added, and 11.236's `strandedRecordCount`
fix reverted — and on fixtures per verdict.** Nothing is condemned, so nothing was fixed;
`snapshotProjectIds` and `unsyncedMemberProjectIds` carry a written statement of why that is safe,
pointing at the check that keeps it true. `flutter test` green locally; no CI until 1 October.

#### What was measured (2026-09-15)

- **Hazard (a) — the bare read — needs three things at once:** an auto-disposing provider, a `ref` (or
  `state`) use after a completed `await`, and a read nothing keeps alive. Remove any one and the same
  body completes. The bare read's `.future` errors rather than hanging. **This is the class 11.235,
  11.236 and 11.238 were counting**, and the seven working providers differ from the broken ones on the
  third condition alone — which is why a body-shape guard fired on all eleven.
- **Hazard (b) — an invalidation landing mid-build — is not a property of the body at all.** A bare
  `keepAlive` read invalidated mid-build never completes *whether or not* the body touches `ref` after
  its gap: nothing listens, the rebuild is lazy, and the stale value is discarded silently. The same
  invalidation is harmless to anything listened to. The `currentUser` comment's "orphaned forever" is
  (b) self-inflicted, and it measures true for a bare read and false for a listened one. **So no
  predicate over provider bodies can find (b); it belongs to `ArrivalRefresh.settleFirst` (11.153),
  which already guards it.**
- **11.238's exemption — "always watched, never read bare" — is therefore complete for (a), and
  for (b) as well.** But it is a fact about *call sites*, so the guard derives it: every `.read(` of an
  auto-disposing provider anywhere in `lib/`, followed transitively through what a bare-read
  auto-dispose provider watches, stopping at `keepAlive` (11.236's one-level-down finding is the
  transitive edge).
- **The predicate's edge, written down:** a helper that stores a `Ref` and uses it later, and a
  provider read through an alias, are invisible to it. Exemptions are a map in the guard with a
  reason per entry, checked in both directions. **A second `await ref.watch(...)` after a first is the
  shape** — 11.235's "safe form" sentence is true only of an `await`'s own operand.

**The count reconciled:** 11.235's eleven, less the four 11.236 fixed, plus the two 11.238 named, less
`mayWriteProjectData` (which 11.236 found was never in shape) is eight — the number derived today.
**Original brief follows.** It was above the line not because any instance was dangerous, but
because the counting had failed and that is what this project spends its time on.
**Trigger fired 2026-09-16, one day after it was written.** The planning session's Discovered Scope
entry of 2026-09-16 said the "revisit if a fifth instance appears" trigger had no reader and *"becomes
a task the moment anybody finds a fifth by accident."* **Task 11.238 found two more the next day, by
accident, while building something else** — and called its own find *"a fifth-ish instance"*, which is
the tell.
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** The fixing is trivial and is not the job. **Defining a predicate that
separates eleven providers into the ones that are wrong and the ones that are fine is the job**, and
task 11.235 already measured that the obvious predicate cannot do it.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Fresh window, alone.**

#### The count was never four. It was four *known*.

- **11.235** fixed `_ensureOwnerMembership`'s three callers, counted as one.
- **11.236** fixed three — and found that one of the four its brief named was **safe in its own body**,
  the defect living one level down in a provider it depends on.
- **11.238** reports **two more**: `unsyncedMemberProjectIdsProvider`, which it wrote, and
  `snapshotProjectIdsProvider` (task 11.237), **which has carried the shape since it shipped and has
  never been fixed.**

**Read on 2026-09-16: `unsyncedMemberProjectIds` does `await ref.watch(...)` twice, after an earlier
`await`.** The shape is there. **So the population has been under-counted the whole time, by a hand
count with no definition behind it** — which is this project's oldest defect, arriving inside the
remedy for a different one.

#### 1. Define the class before counting it, and do not accept the existing framing

**There may be two hazards here wearing one name, and nobody has separated them.** The planning
session is not going to guess which governs; **that is the measurement this task exists to take.**

- **(a) A bare `ref.read` of an auto-disposing provider** — disposed before the rebuild that a write
  triggers finishes. That is what task 11.235 met, on a button.
- **(b) `ref.watch` after an `await` inside a provider body** — `tag_view_refresh.dart` documents
  this trap in its own words: an in-flight `Future` orphaned when something invalidates during that
  provider's build, so it never completes, **and it names `currentUserProvider`'s announcement on a
  first run as a route that reaches it in the running app rather than only in a test.**

**11.238's proposed exemption — *"always watched, never read bare"* — is only valid if (a) is the
whole hazard.** If (b) is real, the hazard lives inside the provider and the call site cannot
exempt it. **Settle this by making one of them fail, or by demonstrating it cannot.** Do not settle
it by reasoning from the two comments; they were written about different incidents.

#### 2. Then count from the code, once, in a place that has a reader

**11.235 measured that a guard on the body shape alone fires on eleven providers, seven of which work
today** — and an instrument that cries wolf about working code is one people learn to silence, which
is how this project lost `clippedTexts` to five test files. **That measurement stands and this task
must not ignore it.**

**What the predicate has to do is separate those eleven.** If it can, that is the guard, and it
should be built. **If it cannot, say so, and build the reader instead** — one named place stating the
count, listing every member with its verdict, and **carrying the query that regenerates the list**,
so the next instance is something a person discovers rather than something they must remember. A
hand-maintained list is already wrong; this one was.

#### 3. Fix what the verdict says to fix

Including `snapshotProjectIdsProvider`, which has shipped with the shape since task 11.237 — **or a
written statement that it is safe and why.** Not silence.

- **Acceptance:** the two hazards are separated by a measurement, not by argument; the population is
  derived from the code with a stated number; either a guard exists that passes the seven working
  providers and fails the wrong ones, **watched red per verdict**, or a written statement of why no
  predicate can and a reader that carries the list and its query; every instance the verdict condemns
  is fixed or exempted **in writing**; `flutter test` green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

### Task 11.258 — A deployment survives the collar and the animal it joins, and four readers have never been asked what they do with one

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-16, commit 4960b16. Every reader of `Deployments` was derived from the
code, not assumed: a tombstoned **tag** was already handled correctly everywhere (the app's own
design keeps a removed tag's deployments live on purpose, so bearings keep resolving — see
`TagRepository.removeFromProject`'s own doc comment) — that half needed nothing. A tombstoned
**animal** is different, and the app's own two writers (`IndividualMerge`, `DeploymentLinking
.deleteAnimal`) already never leave a live deployment naming one — but the read join that answers
"whose collar is this" did not know that, and would have shown a deleted animal's name and colour
forever the one time a deployment naming one arrives anyway (a sync race between an offline link
and a delete elsewhere — the case `IndividualRepository.remove`'s own doc comment already
anticipated, though the "Collars with no animal" screen it described was never built — measured by
grepping for it, found nowhere). Fixed once, in the shared derivation both readers already ran:
`DeploymentRepository.latestDeploymentsSubquery` now excludes a deployment whose animal is
tombstoned, so `latestAnimalForTag`, `TagRepository`'s read join (`Tag.individualName`,
`individualColor` — feeds `tags_screen.dart`'s "Worn by X" and the Record wheel's grouping) and
everything built on them fall through to the next live deployment, or to none, the same answer a
never-linked collar gives. **The bearing-resolution question is answered explicitly and the other
way**: `DeploymentRepository.animalForObservationIn` still resolves a bearing to the animal that
wore the collar at the time, tombstoned or not — a bearing's provenance is a historical fact, not a
question about who is on the project today, the same argument the tag side already made. A minor
related leak in the Map's contested-legend fallback (a raw UUID could show instead of a name for a
candidate whose animal had been deleted) was fixed alongside it, not independently red/green tested
— narrower than the rest and low-risk. **Watched red**: the new repository test fails on the
pre-fix code (`latestAnimalForTag` returns `'marie'` and the read join carries her name forward)
and passes after. `flutter test`: 3461 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed — the whole local suite, not
just the new group. **No CI until 1 October; this local run is the only evidence this task has.**
**Found by task 11.56, 2026-09-16**, while building the season clone — **a finding about the source
data, not about the clone.** The clone itself handles it: it skips such a link and the screen says
how many.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** The fix is small; the derivation is the work.
**Depends on:** nothing.

#### What is true, read from the code on 2026-09-16

**`TagRepository.removeFromProject` tombstones the tag row and stops.** `IndividualRepository.remove`
tombstones the animal row and stops. **Neither touches `Deployments`** — so a deployment goes on
naming a collar or an animal that is a tombstone.

**Nobody has measured what that looks like** on the Log's animal filter, the Map's colour and
legend, the Animals screen's collar list, or anywhere else that reads a deployment. Task 11.56 said
so plainly rather than guessing, which is why this is a task and not a bug report.

#### 1. Derive the readers before deciding anything

**Do not work from a list of four.** Task 11.251 counted six derivations of "which animal wore this
collar" where the planning session had written four, and the one it missed had no caller at all.
**Find every reader of `Deployments` from the code**, and for each one say what it does today with a
link whose tag or individual is deleted. **Measure it; do not reason about it.**

#### 2. Then decide, and the choice is not obviously "cascade"

- **Cascading the tombstone** is the tidy answer and may be wrong: a deployment is the record that
  *this collar was on this animal between these dates*, and that stays true after somebody removes
  the collar from the project. **A bearing still resolves its animal through it.**
- **Leaving it and making every reader skip it** keeps the history and costs a rule in N places —
  which is the shape this project keeps paying for.
- **A third possibility worth weighing:** the readers already have one shared derivation
  (`animalForObservationIn` and its siblings, unified by 11.251). **If the skip belongs anywhere, it
  belongs there, once.**

**Whichever is chosen, say what happens to a bearing whose animal is resolved through a link to a
deleted animal.** That is the question the answer must not dodge: today it presumably still resolves,
and a bearing attributed to an animal the person deleted is either right (the record is history) or
a ghost. **Decide it in writing.**

#### 3. Do not widen this into the delete semantics

**Deleting an animal is owner-only as of task 11.255 and that is settled.** This task is about what
the row leaves behind, not about who may leave it.

- **Acceptance:** every reader of `Deployments` derived from the code, with its measured behaviour
  against a deleted tag and a deleted animal; a decision recorded with its reasoning; the rule
  implemented **once** if it belongs in the shared derivation, and the reason written down if it
  cannot be; **watched red**; the bearing-resolution question answered explicitly; `flutter test`
  green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

### Task 11.259 — A carried-over estimate counts bearings that are not in this project

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-15, commit fd37886. `EstimateBearingResolution`
(`lib/core/utils/estimate_bearing_resolution.dart`) derives "carried" from whether an estimate's
stored `observation_ids_used` resolve to a bearing this device holds. Both the Main Map and the
Position Estimation screen's past-estimates sheet now say "computed in an earlier season" instead
of a false "0 bearings used"/"0 observations" when none resolve, and count only the resolvable ids
in the partial case rather than the stored list's raw length. The map's tap-to-highlight now only
ever highlights ids that can resolve to a drawn ray — the second half of the same defect, since it
used to dim every bearing on the map when a carried estimate was selected (none of its ids ever
matched a drawn ray, so every ray read as "not the highlighted one"). The carry-across design
decision is documented where the column is declared, in `schema.dart`'s `_createEstimatedPositions`
doc comment. `flutter test`: 3452 passed, 15 skipped, 0 failed, watched red first (both the map and
past-estimates cases). `check_app_quotes`: unchanged at the 9 pre-existing reds owned by `/w-19` —
this task's new copy ("computed in an earlier season") is not quoted by any guide page.
**Decided by Michael 2026-09-16** — *"agreed"* — after task 11.56's addendum named it so nobody would
file it as a defect. **A note in a comms file is not a reader; the person who meets this will not
have read it.**
**Model:** **Sonnet, low.**
**Depends on:** 11.56.

#### What is true, read on 2026-09-16

The season clone carries an estimate's `observation_ids_used` across, deliberately — *"it is what the
estimate came from, and the column is unvalidated by design."* **Those bearings stay in last
season's project.** So on the new season:

- `map_screen.dart` renders *"… · N bearings used"*, a count of records that are not here;
- tapping the estimate highlights that id set, **and nothing lights up**;
- `position_estimation_screen.dart` renders *"N observations"* from the same list.

#### 1. Keep the data. Fix the claim. — and this is a correction to what the planning session proposed

**I put this to Michael as "clear the column on a carried estimate", and he agreed to that wording.
Build the other version of it, unless he says otherwise**, because the agreement was to stop showing
a number the app cannot back — not to destroy a record.

**Clearing the column loses a real fact.** Those ids are what the estimate was computed from, and
they still identify real bearings — in the other project. **That is the same kind of fact
`lineage_id` is** (`TAG_COPY_ON_ADD_DESIGN.md` §2.3, `TagColumnKind.provenance`): *for a person
reading two exported files, or an analysis in R spanning several seasons — not for the app.* This
project has already decided once that such a fact is worth keeping and worth keeping inert. **Decide
it the same way, and say so where the column is declared.**

#### 2. Derive "carried", do not flag it

**Do not add a column or read `copied_at`.** The condition that matters is *none of these ids
resolves to a bearing in this project* — which is true of a carried estimate and of any other way a
row could end up with unresolvable ids. **Derive it; a flag would be a second source of truth for a
thing the data already says.**

#### 3. What the two screens should say instead

- **Not "0 bearings used".** That is a different false statement: the estimate did come from
  bearings.
- **Say what is true**, in the plain English the reporting rules require — *"computed in an earlier
  season"* is the shape. **Fewer words is better** (Michael's standing instruction), and the sentence
  must not imply the estimate is less trustworthy: **it is a real fix; only its working is
  elsewhere.**
- **The tap must not offer a highlight that cannot happen.** Either it does not offer one, or it says
  why — **and a control that silently does nothing is the thing being fixed here, so do not replace
  it with a quieter one.**

#### 4. The partial case, which is the one to get right

**Some ids may resolve and some may not** — an estimate is carried, then a bearing is recorded in the
new season and nothing recomputes. **Measure what happens today and decide it explicitly**: a count
of the resolvable ones is honest and a count of all of them is not, but a silent change in what the
number means between one estimate and the next is worse than either. **Say which you chose.**

- **Acceptance:** `observation_ids_used` is still carried and its reason is written where the column
  is declared; "carried" is derived from whether the ids resolve, not from a flag; both render sites
  say something true and neither says "0"; the tap offers no highlight that cannot happen; the
  partial case is measured and decided in writing; **watched red**; `check_app_quotes` names any
  guide line its new copy makes stale; `flutter test` green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

   the end of the day. Boundaries asserted in `test/core/providers/tag_ids_audible_on_test.dart`
   (rewritten) and `test/data/deployment_interval_test.dart` (the `spansDay`-specific group removed).
2. `untimedHandoverFor` (same file) finds the one remaining ambiguous case — two collars audible for
   one animal, which after item 1 can only mean an untimed same-day removal — and names the
   *outgoing* deployment (the one whose `removedDate` lacks a time), since that is the row a picked
   time actually resolves.
3. The Record screen (`observation_logging_screen.dart`) shows a full-width line above the wheel
   only when that condition holds and the person can write: *"<animal> has two collars today — set
   a removal time?"*. Tapping it opens the same time picker mechanism task 11.251 built for the §5a
   swap confirmation (`swapInstantOn`/`swapInstantNow`, reused rather than reinvented) and writes the
   time onto the outgoing deployment's `removedDate`. No label was added to the wheel row — Michael
   measured there is no horizontal room next to the name and frequency, so the fix removes the
   ambiguity at its source instead. The fallback (reorder the row, do nothing to its content) was
   **not built** — the banner is the primary design and nothing so far says it needs a fallback.
4. Measured, not assumed: `WheelPicker.itemExtent` is one fixed `double` for the whole wheel (34px
   default, unchanged), so a two-line item was never available without costing every row — this
   confirms the plan's item 2 reasoning from the code rather than a guess. The fold (previously
   186px, `record_screen_space_budget_test.dart`) is unaffected when no handover is pending (default
   fixtures, unchanged assertion) and is now separately measured *with* the prompt present: **it
   costs 78 logical pixels in `flutter_test`'s fallback font**, which task 11.133's rule says is not
   the number a phone will show — that font is roughly twice Roboto's width and this sentence is
   long enough to wrap several times in it. The wheel's own row count (3) is untouched, since the
   prompt sits above the wheel, not inside it.

**Two things only a phone can settle, per this project's own rule that a rendering change on this
screen is not closed by a test suite:**
- Whether the banner's sentence wraps to more than one line on a real 6.1-inch phone at default
  text size, and whether that reads well against the pinned SAVE bar below the fold.
- Whether the "Set time" tap target and the picker it opens feel right one-handed, which is this
  screen's whole design constraint and nothing in `flutter_test` can judge.

**For the planning session:** nothing new to scope. The Discovered Scope items already on this
task's neighbours (cross-timezone date-only ambiguity, task 11.251's Discovered Scope) are
unaffected by this change.

**For Michael:**
1. Open the Record screen on a real device with an animal wearing a collar whose removal was
   recorded as a bare day today (or ask for a quick way to set that up) and confirm the "set a
   removal time?" line reads well and the time picker it opens works one-handed.
2. If the line wraps awkwardly or crowds the fold, say so and this flips to `Done` with the
   fallback (reorder-only) built instead, per item 3 of the plan's guidance.
3. If it looks right, tell the planning session so it can mark this `Done`.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** The rule change is small; the layout question is measured, not chosen.
**Depends on:** 11.251. **Fresh window.** It edits `observation_logging_screen.dart`, which is the
screen this project treats as the one that must not get worse.

#### The rule this withdraws, and why it had no case left

**Task 11.249 made the wheel offer any collar whose deployment spans *today*, closed at both ends**,
on Michael's ruling of 2026-09-14 that on a handover day both should be listed. **That was right when
a deployment knew only calendar days.** Task 11.251 gave a swap a **time** the next day, and the Log's
filter, the Map's filter and the Map's colour all moved to asking by the moment. **The wheel did not,
and nobody re-read the ruling.** See `CLAUDE.md` on re-reading decisions that exist because the data
could not say something.

**Michael, 2026-09-16, in one question:** *"Taken off at 9 am but their bearing is at 11 am but on the
old tag. Wouldn't the old tag be with me not the animal?"* **Yes — and the planning session's defence
of the rule used exactly that example, wrongly.** The fallback defence does not exist either: **the
Record screen stamps `DateTime.now()`; there is no backdating.** Verified 2026-09-16.

#### 1. The wheel asks by the moment

**A collar is offered until the moment it comes off**, not until midnight. The no-signal checklist
beside it follows the same rule — it always has.

- **Use the derivation that already exists.** Task 11.251 unified this; **do not add a seventh.**
  `tagIdsAudibleOn` currently asks `_deploymentSpansDay`. Say in writing what it should ask instead,
  and whether `tagIdsAudibleOn` survives as a name.
- **A date-only deployment still covers the whole of both its end days** (design §4a rule 1). **That
  is unchanged and must stay** — this task narrows only the *timed* case.
- **Watch it red**: a collar removed at 09:00 must not be offered at 11:00, and must still be offered
  at 08:00 the same morning.
- **The persisted no-signal draft prunes on the same rule** — task 11.249 found that a stale draft
  could name a collar the checklist no longer shows. **Check that the repair it added still holds
  under the narrower rule**, and assert it.

#### 2. Two collars appear only when the removal has no time — and that is a missing fact, not a label

After item 1, two collars for one animal can only mean **a removal with no time**, which is the case
the app genuinely cannot resolve.

**Michael measured the constraint and it rules out the obvious answers** (2026-09-16): *"there isn't
any room horizontally adjacent to the name and frequency."* Shrinking that one line **makes the
hardest line to read the smallest**, and a double-height row means a variable item extent in a wheel
that very likely has a fixed one, against a fold pinned at 186 logical pixels with three rows
visible.

**So do not annotate the ambiguity. Remove it at its source.**

- **A full-width line above the wheel**, where there is room: *"Marie has two collars today — set a
  removal time?"*, tapping through to the removal-time picker task 11.251 already built. **One
  sentence, and it fixes the data rather than describing it.**
- **Fewer words is better** (Michael's standing instruction). The sentence above is the shape, not
  the wording.
- **It must appear only when the condition holds**, and must not be a permanent piece of furniture.

#### 3. The fallback, and the thing not to do

- **Fallback if the line proves wrong on the phone: order the current collar first and leave the row
  alone.** Position is the only free channel the row has — no new text, no height change — and the
  Animals screen already does exactly this. **Weaker, but it costs nothing.**
- **Rejected in advance: a glyph or a colour alone.** `TagForm._copyProvenance` already carries this
  project's rule — *"nothing here relies on a colour or a bare glyph: the sentence is the answer"* —
  because getting it wrong writes wrong data. **A wheel row is where that matters most.**
- **Do not shorten the line's copy to fit.** Task 11.257 established that Michael's wording is not a
  layout tool.

#### 4. Measure, do not assume

- **Say whether the wheel's item extent is fixed**, from the code. The double-height option is
  costed by that fact, and the plan entry is guessing.
- **The fold stays at 186 and the wheel keeps three rows** — both already asserted by
  `record_screen_space_budget_test.dart`. **A line above the wheel spends fold budget: measure what
  it costs and say so**, the way 11.249 measured the sort switch at 46 pixels.

- **Acceptance:** the wheel and the no-signal checklist offer a collar only until the moment it comes
  off, **watched red at 11:00 and green at 08:00 on a 09:00 removal**; the date-only whole-day rule is
  unchanged and asserted; no seventh derivation is added; the prompt appears only on an untimed
  same-day removal and leads to the time picker; the fold and row count are re-measured with the
  prompt present; `flutter test` green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

### Task 11.261 — A removal can be recorded once and never corrected, and the only way to say "I don't know when" is to cancel a dialog

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-16. `flutter test` green locally: 3467 passed, 15 skipped by tag, 0
failed. No CI until 1 October.

**What shipped.**

1. **A removed date and time can now be edited, not just set once.** The row shows *Edit removed
   date* once a removal exists, beside a new *Clear removed date* — same rung as the attached-date
   editor (contributor), same interlock re-check, watched red by a new test that back-dates a
   removal into a second deployment's interval.
2. **"Day only" is now a choice, not a cancel.** The old time picker's *"(Cancel for the day only)"*
   is gone. Picking a removal date of today now opens a small dialog — *Cancel* / *Day only* /
   *Set a time* — and only *Cancel* abandons the edit; the old behaviour (Cancel meaning "the day
   alone") is exactly what a person who mistyped a date and wanted out had no way to get before.
3. **One writer, decided the other way.** The brief's preferred option was routing the Record
   screen's same-day-handover prompt (task 11.260) to this editor. **Declined, with the reason
   written in code**: the Record screen is a field screen, and a round trip to More → Animals
   mid-bearing to set a swap time costs more than it saves. Instead both callers now go through one
   shared function, `writeRemovedDate` in `deployment_linking.dart` — one `repo.update`/catch pair
   instead of two copies of it.
4. **Clearing a removal is offered.** *"I recorded it as off and it is still on her"* now has a
   route that says so, rather than only *Remove record*, which claims the collar was never on the
   animal at all. Re-checked by the interlock like any other edit — a device look confirms this is
   the right shape, but nothing about it is device-only (see the Status rule about device-only
   acceptance).
5. **A non-zero reattribution count is named before the write**, on both callers. `deployment_linking.dart`
   gained `countReattributedBearings`, which compares the deployment against the same row with the
   proposed new end and counts which of the tag's bearings change which side of `coversMoment` they
   land on — measured against real observation timestamps rather than reasoned about by hand.
   Cancelling that dialog leaves the row untouched (watched, and asserted).

**One real red on the first full run**, not the environmental noise it first looked like:
`app_shell_harness_default_test.dart` pins how many `testWidgets` cases each bare-pumped file has
(`_bareToday`), and this task's six new cases in `animals_screen_test.dart` moved that file's count
from 23 to 29 without updating the entry — fixed in the same commit. (The interleaved reporter
output made a second, unrelated-looking failure line point at `analyzed_packages_test.dart`; that
was reporter interleaving, not a second defect — it went green with nothing touched once the real
one was fixed.)

**Found by Michael on his phone, 2026-09-16**, while trying to exercise task 11.260: *"the app
doesn't provide a way to change the removal time of a tag."*
**Depends on:** 11.251, 11.260.

#### What is true, read from the code on 2026-09-16

**`animal_detail_screen.dart` renders *Set removed date* only `if (removed == null)`.** Once a
removal is recorded — with or without a time — **no control anywhere changes the removed date or the
removed time.** The row's remaining action is *Remove record*, which says the collar was **never** on
that animal: a different claim, and a destructive one.

**Three consequences, all measured:**

1. **A mistyped removal date is permanent.** The *attached* date has an editor (*Edit attached
   date*); the removed date has none. **That asymmetry is written down nowhere as a decision**, so
   treat it as an oversight until something says otherwise — and if you find a reason for it, that
   is the finding and this task becomes documenting it.
2. **Task 11.260's *"Set time"* prompt is currently the only writer of a removal time after the
   fact** — and it is reachable only when an animal has two collars listed today. **A general
   control hiding inside an edge case.**
3. **Cancelling a dialog is the only way to express *"it came off today, I don't know when."***
   `_setRemoved`'s time picker says *"(Cancel for the day only)"*, which is honest but backwards:
   **cancelling reads as abandoning the action, not as choosing an option.**

#### 1. The editor, symmetric with the attached one

**A removed date and time that can be changed after the fact, on the animal's screen, beside *Edit
attached date*.** Same shape, same refusals.

- **The interlock still applies.** `_setRemoved` already catches `OverlappingDeployment` and shows
  its sentence; **an edit can create an overlap the original did not have.** Reuse the refusal,
  **watch it red**, and do not adjust a date silently — §6.
- **The owner rung is unchanged.** Editing a deployment is contributor-level (§4.7, task 11.243).
  **Do not move it** — task 11.255 put the rung on destruction, and this is not destruction.

#### 2. One writer, not two — decide where it lives

**11.260's prompt writes a removal time directly.** With this task there will be two places that do,
which is the shape this project keeps paying for.

- **Prefer: the prompt routes to the editor** and stops carrying its own writer. One path, one set of
  refusals, one place to fix.
- **If routing is wrong** — the Record screen is a field screen and a round trip to More → Animals
  mid-bearing may be worse than a second writer — **say so with the reason**, and make the two share
  the write rather than duplicating it.

#### 3. "Day only" becomes a choice, not a cancel

**The time picker's Cancel must stop meaning "record the day alone".** A person who genuinely wants
to abandon the action has nowhere to go today. **Offer both explicitly** — the shape is a third
button or a "Don't know" option — **and keep the wording short** (Michael's standing instruction).

#### 4. Two cases to decide, not discover

- **Can a removal be cleared entirely?** *"I recorded it as off and it is still on her."* Today the
  only route is *Remove record*, which erases the deployment rather than reopening it. **Decide it
  in writing**: either clearing is offered, or the screen says why not.
- **What happens to bearings already attributed across the moment being edited?** Moving a removal
  from 09:00 to 15:00 re-attributes every bearing in between — **which is the point** (§2: a bearing
  gets its animal from time, so correcting a date corrects the bearings). **Say it on the screen if
  the count is non-zero**, the way §5a's confirmation names the second record it touches. **This is a
  change to records the person did not open.**

- **Acceptance:** a removed date and time can be changed after the fact, by the same rung that set
  them; the interlock refusal is reused and **watched red**; the "day only" path is a choice rather
  than a cancel; one writer for a removal time, or a written reason for two that share the write;
  the clear-a-removal question answered in writing; a non-zero re-attribution count named on screen
  before it happens; `flutter test` green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.
