**Found by Michael on his phone, 2026-09-16**, closing task 11.260: *"the set removal time text came
up but when you click on 'set time' there is no indication of which tag you are setting for
removal."*
**Model:** **Sonnet, low.**
**Depends on:** 11.260, 11.261.

#### Two defects, and both are the planning session's, not 11.260's

**11.260 built what its brief specified. The brief was wrong twice.**

1. **The prompt never names the collar.** Design §5a's whole rule is that **a write to a row the
   person did not touch must name it before it happens** — the link confirmation names both collars
   and both dates for exactly this reason. **The brief wrote the prompt's sentence as *"<animal> has
   two collars today — set a removal time?"* and never asked it to say which one.** The
   re-attribution confirmation that follows names a *count*, not a collar, so nothing in the flow
   ever identifies the record being changed.
2. **With two untimed removals it picks one, and the order is not defined.**
   `untimedHandoverFor` is documented for the case it was written for — one outgoing collar with an
   untimed removal, one incoming with no removal at all — where *"the outgoing one"* is well
   defined. **Michael's test was two collars both recorded as removed today with no time**, which
   the brief did not consider. The function returns the **first** group member with an untimed
   removal, over a list whose order nothing guarantees. **Not a wrong answer — an arbitrary one.**

#### 1. Name the collar, always

**Even when there is only one candidate.** The sentence, the button, or the picker's heading must
carry the tag ID or the frequency — whichever fits the room Michael has already measured as tight.
**Fewer words is better**, and the re-attribution confirmation should name it too.

#### 2. With more than one candidate, the person chooses

**Do not pick.** Offer the candidates — two rows, each naming its collar — or route to the animal's
screen, **which now has a per-collar editor that 11.261 built.**

- **Routing was declined once, with a reason that still holds** for the one-candidate case: a round
  trip to More → Animals mid-bearing costs a field crew more than sharing the write avoids.
  **Whether it still holds when the person must choose between collars is a fresh question** — say
  which you chose and why.
- **`untimedHandoverFor` returns one deployment today.** Whatever the screen does, **the function
  must stop implying there is exactly one** — return the set, and let the caller decide. Its doc
  comment already explains the one-candidate case well; extend it rather than replacing it.

#### 3. What not to disturb

- **The rule change 11.260 made is confirmed on Michael's phone and is not in question** — a collar
  removed before now is no longer offered, and two day-only removals both show. **Do not re-open
  `tagIdsAudibleOn` or `coversMoment`.**
- **One writer stays one writer.** Both paths call `writeRemovedDate` (task 11.261). **Do not add a
  third.**

- **Acceptance:** the collar being changed is named before the write, in the one-candidate case too;
  with two or more candidates the person chooses and the app picks nothing; `untimedHandoverFor` no
  longer implies a single answer; the fold and row count re-measured if the prompt grows; **watched
  red**; `flutter test` green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

### Task 11.263 — Delete the overlap, and the two screens built to explain it

**Status:** **Done 2026-09-16, and confirmed on Michael's device the same evening** — the first time
a real phone pushed a swap through a real server since the rule changed. **What he measured:** an
ordinary recapture (bearing recorded, third collar linked, time accepted) left **one collar on the
wheel and the morning's bearing still in that animal's colour**; a cross-animal move of a free collar
onto an animal already wearing one closed the second the same instant; **and every change synced
clean, with nothing left in "Waiting to sync".** *"The scroll wheel looks right as does the map after
the tag linking and switching. Everything synced properly after all these changes."*
**The sync half is the part that matters most and had never been exercised**: the server had been
refusing the ordinary same-day swap on every push since 2026-09-14, and this task found and fixed it
because it was the first server test that ever pushed one.
**Two steps of the sequence were deliberately not exercised and this entry says so rather than
letting silence read as a pass:** the interlock's refusal sentence (step 5) and the narrowed *Day
only* dialog (step 6). **Both are covered by widget tests, both are wording rather than data, and
both move again under tasks 11.265 and 11.267** — so a device look at them tonight would have
measured copy that is about to change.
**And the legacy pairs were resolved by deletion, not repair.** Michael deleted the old projects and
built a clean one; **the count for a repair task is zero**, and no such task is owed.
Both suites green locally (app 3468 passed / 15 skipped; server 62 of
62 suites, 1030 tests). The interlock refuses any overlap, watched red on the bare-day handover
against the old body; the prompt, the chooser and `untimedHandoverFor` are deleted; *Day only* is
withheld where it would overlap; the contested path is asserted still reachable for a planted pair;
fold re-measured at 186 with and without a legacy pair, wheel rows at 3. **Two defects in the
server's enforcement were found by the first server test that ever pushed a swap, and fixed in the
same commit** — see Discovered Scope. The acceptance names no device; the comms entry names what a
phone look would settle.
**Decided by Michael 2026-09-16**, pushing back on the machinery rather than on its wording:
*"I'm realizing we may be over complicating this… What if we just enforce a rule that every animal
in the list can't have more than one tag attached and can't have more than one tag with removal
times that overlap or the same."*
**Read `ANIMALS_AND_DEPLOYMENTS_DESIGN.md` §6a first — it is the decision and this entry does not
repeat it.**
**Model:** **Opus, medium.** The change is small and it touches the interlock, the server and two
screens; **most of the work is deleting confidently.**
**Depends on:** 11.251, 11.260, 11.261, 11.262. **Fresh window, alone.**

#### This task removes more code than it adds. That is the point.

**The one-day tolerance existed because a deployment could not say when.** Task 11.251 gave a swap a
time, so a handover is now an overlap of **zero** — and the tolerance survives only as the route by
which *Day only* creates an ambiguity. **Close that route and the ambiguity cannot be created.**

#### 1. The interlock refuses any overlap

- **`DeploymentInterlock.overlapDays` in `packages/tritrack_sync`** is the shared rule and **the
  server enforces it too** (§6) — a rule on one device is a rule about that device. **Change it once,
  in the shared package.**
- **The refusal sentence already names the dates to fix and must keep doing so.** §6: never silently
  adjusted.
- **Watch it red on the case that used to pass** — a same-day handover with two day-only dates — and
  **watch a timed handover still pass at zero overlap.** Those two together are the whole change.
- **Say what happens to the server's existing rows.** Nothing is migrated (§9), but a row that would
  now be refused can already exist; **the interlock governs writes, not reads, and that must be true
  in writing rather than by accident.**

#### 2. A same-day handover requires a time; "Day only" narrows

**`Day only` stays where a time would be invented and goes where it would create an overlap.**

- **A past-day removal keeps it** (§4a) — and cannot overlap with today anyway.
- **A same-day removal that would overlap another deployment of that animal loses it.** The time is
  already defaulted to *now*: **a tap, not a typed number.**
- **Say what the dialog does when the only remaining choices are a time or cancel** — the person who
  wanted to abandon must still be able to (task 11.261's rule).

#### 3. Delete the prompt and the chooser

**Both exist to explain a state that can no longer arise.**

- **`_HandoverTimePrompt` and its "Set time" path on the Record screen** (task 11.260), and
  **the collar chooser** (task 11.262).
- **`untimedHandoverFor` goes with them** unless something else reads it — **derive that, do not
  assume it.**
- **`writeRemovedDate` stays**: the animal's own editor (task 11.261) is its remaining caller, and
  that is the one writer.
- **The fold and the wheel's row count return to what they were before 11.260.**
  `record_screen_space_budget_test.dart` pins them — **re-measure and say what came back.**

#### 4. What must not go with it

- **§4a's contested answer stays.** It is the honest reply for a row written by an older build, for
  the cross-zone case §4 records, and for any moment two rows genuinely cover. **This app can no
  longer create one; that is not the same as it never existing.**
- **No lockout on the Record screen.** Michael raised it and §6a refuses it with the reason.
  **Do not add one.**
- **The rung does not move.** Editing a deployment stays contributor-level.

- **Acceptance:** the interlock refuses any overlap, changed once in the shared package and enforced
  on the server, **watched red on the case that used to pass and green on a timed handover**; *Day
  only* is withheld exactly where it would overlap and kept where a time would be invented; the
  prompt, the chooser and any now-unread helper are deleted, with the unread-ness **derived**; the
  contested path is asserted still reachable for a pre-existing row; fold and row count re-measured;
  `flutter test` and `scripts/run_server_tests_docker.sh` green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

### Task 11.264 — Everything that exists because a deployment used to be a day

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-16. **Population: 24 decisions in production code and the design doc, derived
from every reader and writer of `attachedDate` / `removedDate` and every caller of `deploymentDateFor`

### Task 11.265 — A handover on a past day cannot be recorded, and the refusal names a control that does not exist

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-17. `_setRemoved` and `_setAttached` (`animal_detail_screen.dart`) now offer
a time on a past day exactly where the bare day would overlap another deployment — never otherwise,
never prefilled with the wall clock (a neutral noon default, `_noTimeToOffer`). The interlock's own
refusal sentence ("needs a time on both") is now an action both editors can carry out, on any day; its
doc comment says so. `flutter test` green locally (one pre-existing failure, unrelated — see this
task's comms entry and the new Discovered Scope entry below). No CI (paused until 1 October).
**Above the line, and it is blocking Michael tonight — 2026-09-16.** The app
refuses to record something that happened and tells the person to do a thing it does not let them do.
**No longer hypothetical:** his phone is holding a `Deployments` row from **2026-09-15** that the
server refuses as an overlap, and **because that pair is on a past day there is no way to repair it**
— a time cannot be set on a past day. His only routes tonight are *Remove record* on one half, or a
wipe. **Run this before task 11.266.**
**Found by task 11.264, 2026-09-16** — **the decision that sweep was written to find.**
**Decided by the planning session 2026-09-17; design §6b is the rule and this entry does not repeat
it.**
**Model:** **Sonnet, low.** One picker condition, one refusal sentence.
**Depends on:** 11.263, 11.264.

**What "recorded end to end" means in the tests, and why it is not the full worked example.**
A genuine same-day handover needs a time on *both* ends (an instant on one side, sitting inside a bare
day on the other, still overlaps — a bare day claims its whole 24 hours). Because each editor only
offers a time when it *currently* detects a conflict, and the earlier of two independent edits never
sees one (nothing else is dated to that day yet), **two bare, never-yet-timed rows cannot be walked to
zero overlap by editing them one after another** — the second edit's own write still fails even after a
time is chosen, because the first side is still a bare day. This was proven by working the arithmetic
through `DeploymentInterlock.overlaps`, not asserted. The tests therefore seed the *far* end already
correctly timed (as it would be after its own editor has been used) and exercise the *near* end's new
branch to a successful write — which is what task 11.265 actually promised: a control to name a time
where none existed, not a guarantee that any two independent edits converge. **This is worth a line in
`ANIMALS_AND_DEPLOYMENTS_DESIGN.md` §6b if the planning session wants the limitation on record**; see
the comms entry.

#### The hole §6a opened, and why its justification missed it

Collar 1 off Kea on the 10th, collar 2 on the same day, entered on the 12th. **`Set removed date`
offers no time for a past day** (§4b), **`Edit attached date` writes only bare days**, and **two bare
days on one date are refused since §6a** — with *"a tag swapped the same day needs a time on both"*,
**naming an action no control offers.**

**§6a's own justification was *"a past-day removal cannot overlap with today in any case"*. True, and
too narrow: it looked at today, and the pair it overlaps is on that past day.** 11.264 measured it at
the interlock.

#### 1. Offer a time on a past day exactly where one is needed, and never prefill it

**Asking is not inventing. Prefilling is.** That distinction is the whole decision (§6b).

- **Needed** = another deployment of that animal already covers the picked day. **Only then** — §4b's
  rule stands everywhere else, and a picker that appears on every past day would be the app asking
  for a number nobody needs.
- **Empty, not defaulted to now.** A time on the 10th prefilled with today's clock is a fabricated
  measurement. **The person who was there supplies it or cancels.**
- **Say what cancel does**, and make sure it is not the only way to express something (task 11.261's
  rule).

#### 2. The refusal must stop naming an impossible action

Where a time genuinely cannot resolve it, the sentence must name **a control the person has**. **Derive
the wording from what the screen now offers** rather than copying the current sentence.

#### 3. What not to widen

- **Do not restore any overlap tolerance.** §6a stands; this task adds a way to supply the time, not
  a way to avoid needing one.
- **Do not prefill on a past day anywhere**, including the link confirmation's third shape.

- **Acceptance:** a past-day swap can be recorded end to end, **watched red first**; the time picker
  appears on a past day only where another deployment covers it, and is **empty**; the refusal names
  only controls that exist; §4b's no-time-on-a-past-day behaviour is unchanged everywhere else and is
  asserted; `flutter test` green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

#### What is true, and the recorded price was wrong

**The server reads the bare-day sentinel in its own zone — UTC in the container.** So a hand-picked
swap time landing on UTC midnight — **17:00 in Arizona, noon in New Zealand** — reads there as a bare
day and is refused on push. **11.264 measured it: the same pair accepted with the device's zone,
refused with the server's.**

**`DeploymentInterlock`'s doc comment prices this at one minute in 1 440. That is wrong for the case
it describes.** Hand-picked times cluster on whole hours, so the real rate is **one in 24** — and 5
p.m. is a plausible hour to take a collar off. **Correct the price where it is written**; a number
that makes a defect look negligible is worse than no number.

#### 1. The server reads every end as an instant — the flag, not the column

**Decided by the planning session 2026-09-17.** Of 11.264's two fixes:

- **The nullable instant column** (§4's) touches the wire, the server schema and the shared
  interlock. **It remains the long-term answer to §4's cross-zone *display* cost — which is a
  different problem — and should not be bundled into this one.**
- **One flag on `DeploymentInterlock.overlaps`**, making the server treat every end as an instant, is
  **never wider than the device** and **gives up nothing the server catches today for a device
  outside UTC.** That is the fix.

**Say in writing what the server stops catching, if anything**, rather than asserting it stops
catching nothing.

#### 2. The held row today has no code and no sentence

**Whatever the fix, a row refused this way is currently held with nothing a person can read.** Say
what it now shows — **or, if the fix makes the refusal unreachable, assert that it is unreachable**
rather than leaving the branch unexplained.

#### 3. “Unreachable” means this route, not this path — added by the planning session 2026-09-17

**Item 2 above invites you to assert the refusal is unreachable if your fix makes it so. Do not
assert it of the whole path.** Since task 11.263 a current, single-zone build cannot normally
produce an overlapping row at all — the app refuses at the link — and this task closes the one
remaining route it has. **Two producers survive, both already named in `DeploymentInterlock`'s own
comment and design §4:**

- **a build older than task 11.263**, which is exactly the untrusted-device case the server-side
  rule exists for; and
- **a crew spanning time zones** — two devices in different zones each write a bare day their own
  interlock accepts, and the server, reading both as instants in its own zone, sees an overlap.

**So task 11.267's held card is not dead code and must not be recorded as such.** Say precisely
which route this task closes and which remain, and name that cross-zone crew as the surviving
trigger — a branch wrongly written down as unreachable is how the next person deletes the thing
that catches it.

- **Acceptance:** a swap timed at exactly UTC midnight in the device's zone is accepted by the server,

left to conflict with), the honest default (`rejectedWithoutADetail`/`rejectedRemedy`) still

end-to-end test failed exactly as expected, then passed once restored.
`scripts/run_server_tests_docker.sh` (1030/1030) and `flutter test` (3520/3520, 16 skipped) both
green locally. No CI until 1 October.
**Found by Michael on his phone, 2026-09-16**, the first time a real device pushed a deployment the
tightened interlock refused. Held card: *"Which animal wore the tag unnamed, from 2026-09-15"*,
`Deployments 0c470f37…/467365d…`, two attempts.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.**
**Depends on:** 11.263.

#### What is true, read from the code on 2026-09-16

**`sync_service.dart` refuses an overlapping deployment with no `RowRefusal` code, deliberately**, and
the reasoning is written there: every code in that vocabulary derives from **a column's declared
bound**, an interlock is not a bound, and a code picked by hand at a refusal site is the
hand-maintained list that type exists to avoid. **That argument is sound and is not what is wrong.**

**What is wrong is the sentence it leans on:** *"the device that sent this already refuses the same
row locally and owns the sentence."*

> **Task 11.263 created a population that sentence does not cover: this device's own history.** The
> pair was written under §6's one-day tolerance, **before** it was withdrawn. The device does not
> refuse it — it is already stored — so **nobody owns the sentence**, and the person gets
> `HeldRowDetail.rejectedWithoutADetail`: *"it did not say which part of it was the problem — this
> device cannot tell whether something about the record is wrong or whether this device and the
> server are on different versions."* **Both halves of that are false here.** The record is wrong, by
> a rule this build knows; the versions match.

**And the remedy is worse than the diagnosis.** `rejectedRemedy` sends the person to look for hidden
characters carried in by pasted text and to retype a name by hand — **correct for the defect task
11.84 measured, and irrelevant to an overlap.** They will do it, it will not work, and the honest
signal that something else is wrong is buried under a plausible instruction that failed.

#### 1. The interlock's refusal must reach the device as a reason

**Do not solve this by adding an interlock code to `RowRefusal`.** The existing argument against that
holds — **respect it, and say in the report that you did.**

**The distinction that makes a second channel principled rather than a second list:** a `RowRefusal`
answers *"which column's declared bound did this row break"*; an interlock answers *"which named rule
about the project's other rows did this row break"*. **They are different questions, and the
interlock is one shared function both sides already call**, so its identity is derivable rather than
hand-picked. **Derive the shape from that**; do not invent a parallel vocabulary of hand-written
strings.

#### 2. The remedy must name the repair that exists

**The device holds the other half of the pair**, so it can say which two deployments overlap and on
which dates — the same sentence the interlock already produces locally when it refuses a link.
**Reuse that sentence rather than writing a second one.**

- **And it must name a control the person has.** See task 11.265: **a pair on a past day cannot be
  repaired today at all** — no time can be set on a past day — so until 11.265 lands the only routes
  are *Remove record* or a wipe. **Say what is actually available**, and re-read this when 11.265
  lands.
- **`rejectedRemedy` stays for the case it was written for.** Do not delete it; make sure an overlap
  never reaches it.

#### 3. The default branch is still needed and must stay honest

A refusal this build genuinely cannot explain must keep saying so. **What this task removes is one
cause from that branch, not the branch.**

- **Assert the branch is still reachable**, the way task 11.263 was asked to assert the contested
  path still reachable.

- **Acceptance:** an overlapping deployment refused on push reaches the device **with a reason**;
  the held card names the two deployments and their dates, reusing the local interlock sentence; the

### Task 11.269 — `main` is red, and the next task will reach for the escape hatch

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-16, commit f65e4a6. `flutter test` is green on `main`: 3854 tests,
0 failures.
**Found by task 11.265, 2026-09-17**, which declared the escape hatch correctly and then **proved the
red was not its own** by stashing every file it touched and re-running on the clean tree.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.**
**Depends on:** nothing. **Run before anything else.**

#### What turned it red, and what was actually wrong

**The commit that turned it red is 2534ab7 (task 11.264) itself — the same commit that added the
test.** 11.264's own reported green is not reproducible; it was true only some hours of the day,
in this timezone (MST, UTC-7).

**The defect: `_setAttached`'s call to `showDatePicker` passed the row's raw stored instant —
still in UTC — as `initialDate`, instead of converting it to the local calendar day first.**
`_setRemoved`, right below it, does this correctly (`initialDate: deploymentDateFor(existing)`);
`_setAttached` was the one place that skipped the conversion. Late in the evening in a
UTC-negative timezone, the wall-clock local date and the UTC date of "now" differ — a swap
recorded two hours before "now" was 2026-09-16 in local time and 2026-09-17 in UTC — so the date
picker's calendar opened on the *wrong* day. Re-picking that (wrong) pre-filled day then correctly
counted as "a different day" rather than "the same day", so the code took the wrong branch and
either wrote a bare day (losing the swap time) or ran the overlap check against a day nobody
picked. The task's own suite ran mid-morning MST when 11.264 was written and never crossed the
UTC/local date boundary, so it read as green then and only became reliably red running the suite
in the evening.

Fixed in `lib/features/more/screens/animal_detail_screen.dart`'s `_setAttached`: `initialDate` is
now `attached != null ? deploymentDateFor(attached) : _today`, matching `_setRemoved`'s pattern.
**Watched red first** (confirmed failing on `main` before the fix, and confirmed passing after).
No test changed — 11.264's expectation was correct; the code was wrong.

#### A second, unrelated red found on the way — a test bug, not this one's commit

While re-running the full suite to confirm `main` was green, a second test went red:
`animals_screen_test.dart`'s *"Set a time then OK writes the instant, and the pair no longer
overlaps"* (task 11.263's group). **Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to 2534ab7** by testing on
a worktree checked out at the commit immediately before this task started — it failed there too,
reliably.

**The cause is in the test, not the app.** `seedTouchingPair`'s `later = DateTime.now().add(const
Duration(hours: 2))` assumes "two hours from now" stays on today's calendar date. Run within two
hours of local midnight and it silently lands on tomorrow — the seeded row's removal is no longer
"today" by `deploymentDateFor`, so `_setRemoved` correctly takes its past/future-day branch
(offering noon as a neutral starting time) instead of the today branch (offering now). The test
still taps the same buttons — both branches share the same dialog — so it appeared to run to
completion and only the final assertion caught that the written time was wrong for what the test
had set up. **This is the correct-when-written-then-time-of-day-dependent class**: it passed every
time this task's own suite had been run earlier in the day and only turned red once real
wall-clock time crossed within two hours of midnight.

Fixed by clamping `later` to one minute before local midnight (still later than `now`, still
today) whenever the two-hours-out value would cross into tomorrow. **Watched red first** on the
unmodified test at this hour, confirmed green after. This is Discovered Scope, not part of
2534ab7's regression — recorded here because leaving it in place would have reddened `main` again
the next time anyone runs the suite between roughly 22:00 and midnight local.

- **Acceptance:** the commit that turned it red is named (2534ab7); the right half was fixed
  (behaviour, not the test) and watched red first; `flutter test` green on `main`, 3854 tests;
  **no escape hatch used.** The second, unrelated red (a time-of-day-dependent test bug) was found,
  confirmed pre-existing, and fixed in the same commit rather than left for `main` to hit again.

### Task 11.270 — Two never-timed rows deadlock, and each control is correct

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-17, commit 5cad5e2. Watched red first (three new
cases failed against the pre-fix code — one with the interlock's ordinary
refusal, two on a missing widget the joint confirmation had not yet been
built); green after. `flutter test`: 3891 tests, 0 failures.
**Found by task 11.265 while building §6b** — **worked through the interlock's arithmetic rather than
guessed**, and reported as a limit of the design rather than a defect in what it shipped.
**Design §6b carries the limit; this task closes it.**
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.**
**Depends on:** 11.265.

#### The deadlock

Date collar 1's removal to the 10th when nothing else is on the 10th: **no conflict, so no time is
offered** — a bare day claiming its whole 24 hours. Attaching collar 2 on the 10th is then
**refused**, so that row is never written, so **collar 1's removal never acquires the neighbour that
would make its editor offer a time.** **Each control is correct; the pair cannot be walked to zero
overlap.**

> **Task 11.265's note to Michael — *"go set that one too"* — does not work in this shape**, and that
> is worth knowing rather than discovering: there is nothing to set it *from*.

#### 1. §5a's shape, not a wider trigger

**When a collar is attached on a past day and the animal's current collar carries a bare-day removal
on that same day, ask for both times in one confirmation** — exactly as the same-day swap already
does for today, naming both collars and both instants before writing either.

- **Do not broaden "offer a time whenever the day is past".** That reopens §4b and asks for numbers
  nobody needs. **§6b says so.**
- **One write, both rows**, so a refusal leaves neither half applied.

- **Acceptance:** a late-entered past-day swap between two never-timed rows can be recorded in one
  act, **watched red first**; the confirmation names both collars and both instants; a refusal
  applies neither row; §4b's trigger is unchanged elsewhere and asserted; `flutter test` green
  locally.

### Task 11.271 — The suite cannot see its own clock, and two evenings have now been spent on that

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-17, commit a3e8e6b. A fixed-clock harness now exists and reproduced one of
task 11.269's two defects deterministically against the pre-fix code, in both offset directions;
`flutter test` is green, 3499 tests. **What it does and does not reach is written below the fold —
it is scoped to one file's date-boundary logic, not to the clock generally.**
**Written 2026-09-17, after task 11.269 found that both of that evening's reds were time-of-day
defects.**

> **And task 11.273 corrected the premise this plan has been using for three days, which makes this
> task more important than it was written to be.** *"`main` is red again"* was the wrong words, three
> times. **The third red was not a regression at all** — the offending line has sat unchanged since
> task 11.263 (`ac1cfb4`) and only fails **within about an hour of local midnight**, which is when
> 11.273 happened to run (00:52 MST). **It did not go red. It became visible.**
>
> **So "`main` is green" has never meant what this plan took it to mean.** Task 11.269's green at
> 3854 was **green at that hour**. **Nobody currently knows whether `main` is green**, only that it
> is green at the times somebody happened to run it — **and that is the sentence this task exists to
> stop being true.**
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.** The work is a harness and a small number of fixed clocks.
**Depends on:** 11.269.

#### What two evenings established

- **`main`'s red was a timezone bug**, and **task 11.264's reported green was real** — it is simply
  true only some hours of the day in a UTC-negative zone. A date picker was handed a stored UTC
  instant where it needed the local calendar day.
- **The second red found the same evening was the same shape**: a fixture seeding *"two hours from
  now"* and assuming that stays on today's date — **false within two hours of local midnight.**
- **Two of two.**

#### The gap this opens in an instrument we already trust

**Task 11.253 ran the full suite ten times, found nothing, and closed.** Its entry honestly records
that the ten runs *"removed the one variable that separates the two conditions"* — **and the
planning session meant machine load. There was a second variable nobody named: the clock.**

> **Ten runs in one quiet evening sample one moment of the day.** A test that fails only near local
> midnight **passes ten out of ten at 9pm**, and `scripts/repeat_suite.sh` reports that with a
> straight face. **The protocol is not wrong; its denominator counts the wrong thing.**

#### 1. Run the suite under fixed clocks, not only under the wall clock

- **A small, argued set** — at minimum: **just before local midnight, just after, and a
  UTC-positive zone** (so the sign of the offset flips, which is what the `_setAttached` defect
  turned on). **Say why each one is in the set**; a list of times with no reasoning is the
  hand-maintained list this project keeps paying for.
- **Derive how to do it from what the suite already supports** — a fake clock, an injected `now`, or
  the process timezone. **Say which, and what it cannot reach.** If some tests read the real clock
  in a way no harness can intercept, **that is a finding worth more than the harness**: name those
  tests.
- **Watch it red.** Both of 11.269's defects are in history — **reproduce at least one of them under
  the new harness against the pre-fix commit**, or the harness proves nothing.

#### 2. `repeat_suite.sh` says what it does and does not sample

**It is a good tool and it is about to be trusted for something it cannot do.** One sentence in it,
and one in `README.md` beside it: **repetition samples load and ordering; it does not sample the
clock — for that, run the clock harness.**

#### 3. What not to do

- **Do not make every test timezone-parameterised.** The cost is the whole suite times N and the
  benefit is concentrated in the tests that touch dates. **Scope it, and say how you scoped it.**
- **Do not chase DST.** Michael's zone (MST) does not observe it and no beta host is planned
  elsewhere; **record it as a known gap with the trigger — the first crew or server outside
  Arizona** — which is the same trigger §4a's cross-zone entry already carries.

- **Acceptance:** the suite runs under a stated set of fixed clocks, each with its reason; **at least
  one of task 11.269's two defects reproduced under it against the pre-fix commit**; tests that
  cannot be intercepted are named; `repeat_suite.sh` and `README.md` say what repetition does and
  does not sample; DST recorded as a known gap with its trigger; `flutter test` green locally,
  **no CI until 1 October**.

#### What shipped, 2026-09-17

**Two mechanisms, because they control two different things.** `animal_detail_screen.dart`'s `_now`
getter (the one seam every date/time read on that screen already went through) now reads
`clock.now()` instead of `DateTime.now()`, so `withClock` (`package:clock`, already a transitive
dependency, now direct) pins "now" for that screen inside a test. **That mechanism cannot reach
which calendar day an already-stored instant falls on** — `DeploymentRepository` round-trips every
date through `DbCodec`'s `.toUtc()`/`.toLocal()`, which always ask the real OS timezone database,
never `clock`. Reproducing task 11.269's actual bug (a raw stored instant read as a local calendar
day) needs the *process* running under a different real `TZ`, set before the Dart VM starts — that
is what `scripts/clock_matrix_test.sh` does, launching `flutter test` once per zone.

**The fixed clocks, in `animals_screen_test.dart`'s new "clock matrix" group:**
1. Just before local midnight, America/Phoenix (UTC-7, no DST) — the zone every incident to date
   (11.269, 11.273) was found in; a swap two hours earlier sits in [17:00, 24:00) local, the window
   where a UTC-negative zone's `toUtc()` has already crossed into the next calendar day.
2. Just after local midnight, America/Phoenix — task 11.273's own window; also inside the wide
   window above.
3. Shortly after local midnight (03:00, chosen so a swap two hours earlier still falls in the
   danger window), Asia/Tokyo (UTC+9, no DST) — flips the sign, so the fixed code is asserted
   correct in the direction this project has never actually hit, not only the one it has.

**Watched red.** Reverting `_setAttached`'s one-line fix (`initialDate: attached ?? _today` in place
of `deploymentDateFor(attached)`) and running `scripts/clock_matrix_test.sh` fails both
America/Phoenix cases cleanly — not vacuously: the first seeded version paired the edited row with
a sibling deployment, and the pre-fix bug's wrong day sometimes fell inside the sibling's interval,
routing through a second dialog the test didn't drive and passing for the wrong reason. Dropped the
sibling; every case now writes directly, in either offset direction, and Asia/Tokyo does **not**
reproduce this specific historical bug shape with a two-hour-back swap (confirmed by direct
measurement, not assumed) — recorded so the comment near the Tokyo case claims only what was
checked. Fix restored; all three cases pass (Tokyo's own case runs for real only under
`TZ=Asia/Tokyo`; under Phoenix it reports itself skipped, by design).

**What this cannot reach, named rather than left implicit:**
- **72 other `DateTime.now()` call sites across 38 other files in `lib/`** (`grep -rn
  "DateTime.now()" lib --include="*.dart"` excluding `animal_detail_screen.dart`) still read the
  real clock. One is worth naming specifically for future reference:
  `observation_logging_screen.dart` also calls `deploymentDateFor(now)` — the Record screen has the
  same shape of "which calendar day" logic this task's harness controls on the Animal screen, and
  it is untouched.
- **45 other test files' `DateTime.now()` calls** are likewise unreached.
- Inside `deployment_linking.dart`, `apply()`'s and `deleteAnimal()`'s `now ?? DateTime.now()`
  fallback (used only to stamp `SyncMeta` audit timestamps, never a deployment's own date) is not
  intercepted; it doesn't feed either reproduced defect, so it was left alone rather than widened.
- A documentation test, `test/documentation/app_shell_harness_default_test.dart`, tracks a literal
  count of `testWidgets(` occurrences in `animals_screen_test.dart` and needed its own update (43 →
  45) for the two new source occurrences this task added.
- **DST recorded as a known gap, per the brief:** neither America/Phoenix nor Asia/Tokyo observes
  it, so this harness has never exercised a DST transition. Trigger: the first crew or beta host
  outside Arizona, the same trigger §4a's cross-zone entry already carries.

`flutter test`: 3499 passed, 16 skipped, 0 failed. `scripts/clock_matrix_test.sh` passes under both
`TZ=America/Phoenix` and `TZ=Asia/Tokyo`. No escape hatch used.

### Task 11.272 — The Log's rows never name the animal, and their colour is the collar's current owner

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-17. Every swatch on both Log tabs (history and team) now resolves the
animal at the row's own moment through `animalForObservationIn` — the same derivation the filter
already used — never the collar's current owner; the animal is named on the row and is a sort
option on both tabs; the "no signal" stack resolves each collar separately and the disagreement case
is documented in `_NonDetectionTile`'s doc comment. `flutter test` green locally (one pre-existing,
unrelated failure in `animals_screen_test.dart`, confirmed present before this task's changes too).
**Above the line.** It is the screen a person reads to answer *"what did we
get on Marie"*, and it answers with the wrong animal's colour and does not name her at all.
**Found by Michael on his phone, 2026-09-17:** *"The animal isn't listed or sortable. That's mainly
what the users will want to see."* And: *"a tag that used to be on animal B and was reassigned to
animal A shows animal B's colour."*
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.**
**Depends on:** 11.251. **Fresh window.**

#### What is true, read from the code on 2026-09-17

- **The Log's *filter* was fixed by task 11.251 and is correct.** `_SubjectFilter.admits` calls
  `DeploymentRepository.animalForObservationIn` at the row's own timestamp.
- **The Log's *rows* were not.** Every swatch on the screen is
  `TagColorSwatch(colorHex: tag.colorHex)` — **the collar's colour, which since schema v16 is the
  colour of the animal wearing it *now***, resolved through the latest deployment. **Three places:**
  the history row, the team-log row, and the no-signal row's `TagColorSwatchStack`.
- **And no row names the animal at all.** The title is the collar; the sort offers time, tag name,
  frequency and distance. **There is no animal anywhere on the row and no way to sort by one.**

> **This is the third time this exact pattern has been found: the filter is fixed, the colour is
> not.** The Map went the same way — task 11.247 fixed its filter, and its follow-up found that
> `_tagColor` had never been made per-ray at all. **Same screen shape, same half-fix, one screen
> over.** See the `CLAUDE.md` rule this task earned.

#### 1. Every swatch asks the moment, not the collar

**Use the derivation that exists.** `animalForObservationIn` at that row's own timestamp, exactly as
the filter beside it already does — **do not add a seventh derivation** (task 11.251 counted six and
unified them).

- **A row whose collar was on nobody at its moment draws the neutral "no individual" swatch**, the
  same as the Map. **Consistency with the Map is the requirement**, not a preference: the two screens
  answer the same question about the same bearing.
- **The no-signal stack is the awkward one** — it lists several collars for one moment. **Resolve
  each collar at that moment**, and say in writing what it draws when they disagree.
- **A contested moment (§4a) must render as the Map renders it.** Do not invent a second treatment.

#### 2. The animal goes on the row, and into the sort

**Michael: this is mainly what users will want to see.**

- **Name the animal on the row**, resolved at that row's moment — **not the collar's current owner**,
  which is the same defect in words instead of colour.
- **Add an animal option to the sort.** The sort enum is `_LogSort`; the team log has its own
  `_TeamSort`. **Say whether both get it**, and if only one, why.
- **Where a row has no animal at its moment, say so plainly** rather than leaving the space blank —
  blank reads as a rendering fault, and this app has a rule about a control that is silent for a
  reason.
- **The room is the constraint.** The row is already three-line in several states. **Measure before
  choosing where the name goes**, the way the Record wheel's line was measured.

#### 3. What not to disturb

- **The filter is correct. Do not touch `admits`.**
- **Withheld, withdrawn and irregular-signal rows keep their sentences.** Task 11.194's rule stands:
  colour never carries meaning alone on this screen.

- **Acceptance:** every swatch on the Log resolves the animal at its own row's moment, **watched red
  against the reassignment Michael described**; the neutral and contested renderings match the Map's,
  asserted; the animal is named on the row and is a sort option; the no-signal stack's disagreement

### Task 11.275 — Run the whole suite in three time zones, and find out whether `main` is green

**Status:** Done, 2026-09-17, commit `78fa7fa`. **`main` is not green outside America/Phoenix. Two
real, reproducible test-fixture defects found on the first run — both green on every machine
this project has ever run the suite on, because every one of those machines happens to sit in
America/Phoenix.** Filed as tasks 11.276 and 11.277 below rather than fixed here, because fixing
either means editing a file under `test/`, which this task's own acceptance forbids.

**The mechanism works.** `scripts/tz_matrix_suite.sh` was proved against a known time-of-day
defect first: task 11.273's fix (commit `ab277b7`) reverted in a throwaway `git worktree` at its
parent commit, `animals_screen_test.dart`'s "THE TAG'S SWAP" test run alone. Clean under
`TZ=UTC`. Failed under `TZ=Australia/Brisbane` with the exact pre-fix symptom — `change_swap_time`
button not found — because local time in Brisbane was 00:38, inside the hour-after-midnight
window the defect needs. Re-run against the fix commit, same zone: clean. **`TZ` alone reproduces
a known time-of-day defect without touching a single test.**

**The three zones, and what each run found:**

| Zone | Reason | Local time at start | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| America/Phoenix (UTC-7) | Michael's own zone — every defect to date surfaced here | 2026-09-17 07:41 MST | PASS — 3499 passed, 16 skipped, 335/335 files |
| UTC | the zone CI and most silent runs use | 2026-09-17 14:43 UTC | **FAIL — 11 tests, 2 distinct causes** |
| Australia/Brisbane (UTC+10) | a UTC-positive zone — the offset sign is what the `_setAttached` defect turned on | 2026-09-18 00:45 AEST | **FAIL — 1 test** |

**Cause 1 (10 of the 11 UTC failures — `test/data/individual_merge_test.dart`,
`test/data/tag_repository_test.dart`, `test/data/individuals_test.dart`).** Each fixture links two
bare-day deployments that touch on one calendar day — e.g. `d-2025` removed `DateTime.utc(2025, 6,
1)`, `d-2025b` attached the same instant. Since task 11.263 the interlock refuses exactly this
shape (`CLAUDE.md`, `deployment_interlock.dart`: *"removed the 15th (a bare day) and attached the
15th (a bare day) overlap"*) — **and it is refusing it correctly under `TZ=UTC`.** What hides the
refusal in every other zone is a second, independent bug: `deploymentDateFor` builds "local
midnight" with the bare `DateTime(y, m, d)` constructor, so it only agrees with a value written as
`DateTime.utc(...)` when the reading process's zone actually is UTC. Under Phoenix or Brisbane the
fixtures' UTC-midnight values misclassify as *timed* instants instead of bare days, which
happens — by luck, not by design — to compute a non-overlap. **Two bugs cancel to a false green
everywhere this suite has ever been run.** This is the accepted, documented cross-zone gap the
class comment already names (a device's local midnight is not the server's UTC midnight); nothing
here is a new production defect. The fixtures are wrong on their own terms — filed as task 11.276.

**Cause 2 (the 11th UTC failure and Brisbane's only failure —
`test/features/map/map_screen_test.dart`, "per-tag coloring… dangling tag_id falling back").**
`test/data/fixtures.dart` declares `final _localNow = DateTime(2026, 7, 16, 11, 30, 0);` — built
with the **local**, not `.utc`, constructor, alongside `final _now = DateTime.utc(2026, 7, 16, 18,
30, 0);`. The two are meant to be the same instant (11:30 in Arizona, UTC-7, is 18:30 UTC) — **and
they only are when the process reading `_localNow` happens to run in Arizona's zone.** Under UTC,
`_localNow` becomes 11:30 UTC, seven hours *before* the deployment fixture built from `_now`; under
Brisbane, seventeen hours before. `Deployment.coversMoment` then correctly says the tag's estimate,
timestamped with the wrong `_localNow`, falls before its own deployment starts, and the map falls
back to the neutral "no individual" grey instead of the animal's colour — measured: expected
`Color(0.9020, 0.6235, 0.0000)`, got `Color(0.6196, 0.6196, 0.6196)`. Filed as task 11.277.

**What this does and does not license.** The suite was clean at three distances from midnight, on
one day, in one process each — not clean at every distance, and not proof that these are the only
two zone-dependent fixture bugs in the tree. Every other one of 335 files' worth of tests passed
identically in all three zones.

**Cost:** ~5.5 minutes wall-clock for the three full runs (132s + 102s + 95s), plus the worktree
reproduction. `scripts/tz_matrix_suite.sh` is left in the repo; `README.md` now says which of the
three time instruments (`repeat_suite.sh`, `clock_matrix_test.sh`, `tz_matrix_suite.sh`) answers
which question.

**No test file changed**, per this task's own acceptance — the two defects found are real and
reproducible, and are filed as follow-up tasks rather than fixed here.
**Written 2026-09-17, resolving task 11.271.**
**Model:** **Sonnet, low.** No test changes. Three runs and a script.
**Depends on:** 11.271. **Fresh window.**

#### What 11.271 did, and what it deliberately did not

**It built a fixed-clock harness and scoped it to one file's date-boundary logic — which its brief
explicitly permitted** (*"do not parameterise every test by timezone… scope it, and say how"*). **It
scoped it and said so. That is compliance, not a shortfall.**

**But the sentence that got it promoted is still true:** *"nobody currently knows whether `main` is
green — only that it is green at the times somebody happened to run it."* **A harness over one file
does not close that**, and this entry exists so the gap is named rather than assumed closed by a task
that never claimed to close it.

#### 1. The cheap instrument nobody has tried: change the zone, not the tests

**Every defect in this class so far turns on *how far the wall clock is from local midnight*** — a
stored instant read as a local day, a fixture seeding "two hours from now", a line that fails within
an hour of midnight. **That distance is a function of the process time zone**, and Dart's
`DateTime.now().toLocal()` follows it.

**So: run the existing suite, unchanged, under several `TZ` values.** Three runs sample three
different distances from local midnight **at the same moment**, without touching a single test.

- **A stated set with reasons**, not a list. At minimum a **UTC-negative** zone (Michael's, where
  every defect so far has surfaced), **UTC itself**, and a **UTC-positive** zone — because the sign
  of the offset is what the `_setAttached` defect turned on.
- **Choose zones that put "now" at a different distance from local midnight**, and **say what time it
  was in each when you ran it** — a run at noon everywhere samples nothing.
- **Verify the mechanism before trusting the result:** **reproduce a known defect** — task 11.273's,
  or 11.269's — **by `TZ` alone, against its pre-fix commit.** If changing `TZ` cannot surface a
  defect we know is time-of-day dependent, **this instrument does not work and that is the finding.**

#### 2. Then answer the question

**Run it and report what it found**, including *"nothing"*.

- **A red found this way is a real red.** Fix it, or file it with the zone and the local time that
  produced it.
- **If nothing surfaces, say what that does and does not license** — it means the suite is clean at
  three distances from midnight on one day, **not that it is clean.**

#### 3. Leave it runnable, and say where it belongs

- **A script beside `repeat_suite.sh` and `clock_matrix_test.sh`**, and one line in `README.md`
  saying which of the three answers which question: **repetition samples load and ordering; the clock
  matrix samples one file's date logic; this samples the whole suite's distance from midnight.**
  **Three instruments, three questions, and none of them is the others.**
- **Say what it costs in wall-clock time.** Three full suites is the price, and if that is too slow to
  run before a beta, **that is worth knowing now rather than at the gate.**

#### 4. Two things not to do

- **Do not parameterise tests.** The whole point is that nothing in `test/` changes.
- **Do not fold in 11.271's item 2** — `observation_logging_screen.dart` reading the unfixed clock.
  **If this sweep surfaces a defect there, that is its evidence and it gets its own task;** if it does
  not, the trigger 11.271 wrote stands as written.

- **Acceptance:** the suite runs unchanged under a stated set of zones, each with its reason and the
  local time it ran at; **a known time-of-day defect reproduced by `TZ` alone against its pre-fix
  commit**, or a written finding that the mechanism does not work; the result reported including a
  nil result, with what it does and does not license; a script left behind and `README.md` saying
  which instrument answers which question; the wall-clock cost stated; **no test file changed.**

**Status:** Done — 2026-09-20. **The measured total is far larger than the earlier sample said:**
`find "$TMPDIR" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'tri_track_test_*'` (safe, read-only, completes in
seconds — `ls` is what hangs, not a directory walk) counted **1,830,039** matching directories plus
**294** `tritrack-gate-smoke.*` ones, not the 199,261 the earlier "first 200,000 entries" sample
implied. **And they are not all empty**: a 20,000-directory sample found 0.71% held a small test
artifact (`offline_regions.json`, a `dem_tiles` cache dir) left by tests that write into their fake
temp path — about 1.4 KiB per non-empty one, ~130 MB total estimated across all of them, all
disposable test output, none of it anything Michael recorded. `installFakePathProvider` now deletes
its directory in a tear-down (watched red, then green, in `fake_path_provider_test.dart`); the
pre-commit hook's `GATE_SMOKE_COVERAGE_ONLY=1` run of `gate_smoke_test.sh` now cleans up the same
way (watched: pre-fix left one directory per coverage-only run and the conflict-check's own early
exit, both confirmed leaking; post-fix, zero in both). **Above the line, because it is costing time
on the machine every task runs on** — `ls "$TMPDIR"` no longer returns within two minutes there.
**Found by task 11.294, 2026-09-20**, which lost about twenty minutes to it and had three attempts
to exercise the pre-commit hook stall before the cause was found.
**Model:** **Sonnet, small.**
**Depends on:** nothing. **Fresh window, and a short one.**

#### The whole defect

`test/support/fake_path_provider.dart` creates a `tri_track_test_*` directory in the system temp
folder for **every test that installs it** and deletes none. **199,261 of the first 200,000 entries
in Michael's `$TMPDIR` are these**, all empty. Three test files install it. The fix is one
`addTearDown` inside `installFakePathProvider`, which already runs in `setUp` context.

The pre-commit hook leaves `tritrack-gate-smoke.*` directories the same way, two per commit, 39
counted. **Same shape at a scale that does not matter yet** — fix it in the same pass, because the
reason it does not matter yet is only that commits are rarer than tests.

#### The part that is not one line

**Michael's machine has to be cleaned**, and that is a delete of two hundred thousand directories in
a system folder. **Do not write a task that deletes files in `$TMPDIR` by pattern without saying
exactly what it matches and having him run it himself.** Give him one command, say what it will
remove, and say how to check the count first. The directories are empty and named `tri_track_test_*`,
so the command is safe — but it is his machine and a `rm -rf` in a temp folder is the shape people
get wrong.

#### One thing to notice rather than fix

**This ran for months and nothing said so.** A test-support helper that leaks a resource per test is
invisible until the leak passes a threshold in somebody's shell, and the threshold here was `ls`
timing out during an unrelated task. **Say in the report whether anything else in `test/support/`
creates something it does not remove** — derived by reading the directory, not by memory.

- **Acceptance:** `installFakePathProvider` removes its directory in a tear-down, and the hook's
  smoke directories are cleaned too; **watched red first** on a test that counts the directory before
  and after; the rest of `test/support/` is swept for the same shape and the finding reported either
  way; Michael gets one command, with what it matches and how to count first, and **runs it himself**;
  `flutter test` green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

### Task 11.298 — A collaborator whose email the boundary allows and the sender refuses is told the link was sent

**Status:** Done — 2026-09-21, commit hash in the `TASK_COMMS.md` entry. **Reproduced first, exactly
as written**: against a live server and a Mailpit relay, `üser@example.com` answered `202`, no message
reached the relay, and the audit table held an `outcome=undelivered` row — written **2 ms before** the
`sent` row, which is the second finding measured rather than argued. **Options 2 and 3 turned out to
be one mechanism** (the only way to tell the person is a different answer, and `400 invalid_email`
already existed for malformed addresses), so that is what was built: the boundary is now *defined
as* the sender's rule on the normalized string (`isAcceptableSignInAddress`), a corpus test of
50,007 generated strings holds the two equal in both directions and was watched catching a sabotage
each way, and the app renders that `400` as a sentence about the email address rather than the
server URL. Option 1 (SMTPUTF8) costed and not built; its trigger is in Discovered Scope. The §4.5
argument is in the security model with a reopen trigger. The sender now starts every delivery in a
microtask and the route orders its two audit rows itself; live with the relay stopped, `sent` then
`undelivered`, 9 ms apart, in that order. **One correction to this entry:** `"odd name"@example.com`
was never in the gap — the old boundary refused any space — so three of the four named addresses
were. **The pre-commit hook caught what the refactor broke**: `verify_round8_broken_control.py`'s
`sanitiser` variant patched the boundary's deleted control-character regex (defect vocabulary 16), and
was re-authored against the one-line rule — its sabotage is now "anything with an `@`", confirmed to
apply and compile. Server suite green against real Postgres (1,121 tests); `flutter test` green via
the pre-commit hook.
**Was:** Not started. **Above the line** — it silently drops sign-in links for a real class of
person, and the app is aimed at *"hundreds of independent research teams worldwide"*
(`SERVER_DEPLOYMENT_PRIMER.md`'s own scale paragraph).
**Found by the planning session 2026-09-21**, reading task 11.293's code rather than its report.
Neither 11.287's brief, 11.293's brief, nor either report named this path.
**Model:** **Opus** — it is an auth path, an international-correctness question and a §4.5 argument
in one.
**Depends on:** nothing. **Fresh window.**

#### Two checks that disagree on purpose, and nobody reconciled them

`auth_routes.dart`'s `_looksLikeEmail` is **deliberately permissive**, and its own comment says why:
*"rejecting unusual but valid addresses would lock real collaborators out."* It requires 3–320
characters, one `@` not at either end, no spaces, and no control characters, commas or semicolons.

`smtp_email_sender.dart`'s `isDeliverableAddress` is **strict ASCII**: local part limited to 64
characters from a fixed set, domain `[A-Za-z0-9.-]`. No quoted local part, no bracketed domain,
**no non-ASCII character anywhere**. That strictness is right — it is the second line against header
and `RCPT TO` injection, and the doc comment explains that it is deliberately independent of the
boundary so a future route cannot bypass it.

**Both are defensible. Together they are a trapdoor.** `üser@example.com`, `josé@universidad.mx`,
`"odd name"@example.com`, `user@[192.168.1.1]` all pass the boundary and are refused by the sender.

#### What that person experiences

They get the same `202` and the same *check your email* as everybody. **The link is never sent.**
Until task 11.293 the only trace was a line in the container log; now there is also an
`outcome=undelivered` audit row — **which is an improvement for the operator and changes nothing for
the person locked out.** They will conclude the mail was slow, then that it went to spam, then that
the app is broken, and they will be right about the last one.

**The boundary comment says the permissiveness exists so collaborators are not locked out. The
sender then locks them out silently.** That is the defect: not either check, but that nothing
reconciles them and nobody is told.

#### The decision this task has to make, and it is not obvious

1. **Support internationalized addresses properly** (SMTPUTF8, RFC 6531) — the honest answer for
   software aimed at teams worldwide, and the largest. **It requires the relay to advertise the
   extension**, which NAU's may not, so it cannot be promised without measuring.
2. **Tighten the boundary to match the sender**, so the refusal happens where a caller can be told
   about it — a `400 invalid_email` instead of a silent nothing. **Honest and small, and it rejects
   addresses that are genuinely valid**, which is what the boundary's comment was written to avoid.
3. **Tell the person.** Hardest, because §4.5 forbids the response varying by address — **though
   read that carefully: §4.5 protects against distinguishing *registered* from *unregistered*, and
   an address's syntax is a fact the caller already holds.** A different answer for a
   syntactically-undeliverable address discloses nothing about who has an account. **Argue it
   explicitly rather than assuming the prohibition covers this.**

**Do not pick one because it is smallest.** Say what each costs, recommend one, and **name which
real people each choice locks out.**

#### A second, smaller finding on the same path — record it even if it is harmless

`_deliver` is `async`, and **its address check throws before the first `await`**, so on this path the
catch block — including `onOutcome?.call(false)` — runs **synchronously inside `sendMagicLink`**,
within the request's own span. Task 11.293's tests assert the callback fires only after `drain()`,
but they exercise the success path and the refused-recipient path, **both of which reach an
`await`. The third path is the one that behaves differently and it was not tested.**

**This is probably not a §4.5 oracle** and the task should say so rather than inflating it: the
timing difference keys on the *syntax the caller chose*, not on whether an account exists. But **the
asserted invariant is false as written**, and an invariant that holds on the paths somebody thought
of is the shape this project keeps finding. Make it true or make the assertion honest.

- **Acceptance:** the reproduction is run first — a request with a non-ASCII address against a live
  server, showing the `202`, the absent mail and the `undelivered` row — and reported before any
  fix; the three options are costed and one recommended, **with the people each excludes named**;
  whatever is built keeps the two checks reconciled by construction rather than by both being
  correct at the same moment, and **a test fails if they drift apart again**; the synchronous-callback
  path is either fixed or its assertion rewritten to say what it actually covers; if option 3 is
  taken, **the §4.5 argument is written out in the security model**, not asserted in a commit
  message; **watched red first**; server suite green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.

11.52-boundary answer.
**Found by task 11.295, 2026-09-20**, which corrected the two documents in its scope and enumerated
the three it was not sent to touch.
**Model:** **Sonnet, medium.**
**Depends on:** nothing. **Fresh window.**

#### The recurrence, stated plainly

The number of long-running containers is written by hand in at least five places. It has now been
wrong in all of them **twice**: task 11.79 made "four" into five and nobody carried it back, and
task 11.290 made "five" into six on 2026-09-20 — caught a day later only because task 11.287
happened to be reading those documents for another reason.

**This is task 11.52's class and 11.52 is Done.** That task built `SETUP_OWNERSHIP.md` and
`setup_step_ownership_test.dart` so that one file owns each setup *step* and the copies point at it,
watched failing in three directions. **A count is not a step, so it fell outside**, and the same
defect came back wearing a different noun. **The interesting question is not how to fix the count;
it is whether 11.52's instrument should have covered this and what its boundary should be.** Answer
that in the report.

#### What is derivable, and that is the point

The count is not an opinion. It is `docker-compose.yml` plus `docker-compose.tls.yml`, minus the
services behind a Compose profile. **A test can read those files and refuse any document whose
stated count disagrees** — which is the only version of this fix that survives the next task that
adds a service.

The planning session corrected the three documents by hand on 2026-09-21
(`SERVER_DEPLOYMENT_PRIMER.md`, `NAU_infosec_review_request.md`, `RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` D4), **so
this task is not the correction. It is the instrument.** Check the hand corrections as your first
act and report if any is wrong.

#### One distinction the instrument has to make, and it is why this is not trivial

**A superseded document must be allowed to be stale.** `NAU_infosec_review_request.md` says five
containers on purpose — it is a record of what NAU ITS was told, and correcting it would destroy the
only reason it is kept. It now carries a dated as-of note instead. **So the check cannot simply
grep every document for a number**; it needs a way for a document to declare itself a record rather
than a description, and that declaration has to be visible to a reader, not just to the test.
**Design that, and make a wrong declaration fail** — an exemption nobody can see is how the setup
exemptions went stale before 11.52 caught them.

- **Acceptance:** the count is derived from the compose files by a test, and **every live document
  stating it is checked against that derivation**; documents that are records rather than
  descriptions are declared as such, visibly to a human reader, and **a stale or wrong declaration
  fails the test**; **watched red first in three directions** as 11.52's was — a new uncovered copy,
  a live document that drifted, a declaration that no longer holds; the report answers whether
  `SETUP_OWNERSHIP.md`'s instrument should have covered this and where its boundary belongs; the
  planning session's three hand corrections are verified and any error reported; `flutter test`
  green locally, **no CI until 1 October**.
