## Phase 12 — Merging duplicate tags and their data

**Raised 2026-08-17, deliberately after the beta.** Task 11.11 makes duplicates
harder to create; it cannot make them impossible, because two people offline can
always create the same tag twice. Overwriting one with the other would destroy a
scientific record. **Merge is the only honest resolution, and the reasoning that
gets you there is sound: you cannot prevent the collision, and you must not
resolve it by discarding data.**

**Rescoped 2026-08-22 by the copy-on-add decision (task 11.34), and the effect is
counterintuitive, so it is written out.** Copying a tag into a project when it is
added creates *more* duplicate tag rows overall — and makes this phase **smaller**,
because it removes the harder half of it. **Cross-project duplicates stop mattering
by definition**: two projects each holding their own copy of the same collar is now
the intended state, not a collision, and no analysis ever spanned projects anyway.
What remains is the within-project case — two people offline creating the same tag
twice in one project — which is the only case that ever affected a result.

**Two additions, 2026-09-14, from `ANIMALS_AND_DEPLOYMENTS_DESIGN.md`:**

- **Merging two tags now has to merge their deployments.** A duplicated collar may
  carry deployments on each row; the survivor takes both, and §6's interlock decides
  whether the result is legal. **A tag merge that leaves a duplicate's deployments
  behind loses the record of who wore what.**
- **Do not confuse this with the animal merge.** *"Same animal as…"* (task 11.241)
  joins two **individuals**; this phase joins two **tags**. They are different
  operations on different rows and must not share a screen or a verb.

**So scope this phase to within-project merges only**, and do not build a
cross-project merge nobody needs. One dependency to respect: adding a tag to a
project is owner-only, which is what keeps within-project duplicates rare in the
first place. If that rule is ever relaxed, this phase gets harder again.

> **Correction, task 11.219, 2026-09-10 — the dependency sentence above is now false, and
> the design document said it would be (§1.4).** Adding a tag to a project is **no longer
> owner-only in the sense that sentence means.** Copy-on-add shipped, so anybody who may
> write to a project can put a collar from their own device library into it, and the tag
> that lands is that project's own row rather than a shared record. **Two projects holding
> the same collar is the intended state now.** What is still owner-only is *editing* a
> project's tag, which is a different rule and is not what keeps duplicates rare.
> **So the frequency of within-project duplicates is no longer bounded by a role check**,
> and the argument for holding this phase past the beta rests on a fact that has changed.
> **That is a scheduling decision and it is not this task's to take** — the planning
> session should re-take it. The engineering half is unchanged: within-project merges
> only, and the standing-rule problem below is still the hard part.

Held until after March on purpose — the beta will tell you how often this
actually happens, and with what shape. Building the merge tool first risks
solving a problem that occurs twice a season with a feature nobody trusts.

### The hard part, recorded now so it is not discovered later

**A merge is not an event. It is a standing rule.**

The obvious implementation sweeps the observations currently pointing at the
absorbed tag and re-points them at the surviving one. That works, and then a
teammate who was offline during the merge syncs three days later carrying
observations recorded against the absorbed tag — and they land pointing at a tag
that no longer means anything.

So the merge has to *keep applying* to rows that arrive afterwards: "tag A now
means tag B" is a durable fact the app consults, not a one-time migration. A
sweep alone is the "fixed where it reproduced" shape that Phase 10 found six
times.

### Requirements, when it is scheduled

- **Owner-only.** It re-parents primary scientific records.
- **Retire the absorbed tag, never delete it.** A teammate's device still
  references it, and the record of the duplicate having existed is part of the
  data's history.
- **Show exactly what will happen before it happens** — "42 observations move
  from *F12-dup* to *F12*; *F12-dup* is retired" — with counts, not a generic
  confirmation. Reuse §4.19's consent-diff thinking, including 10.109's lesson
  that a dialog nobody can read at scale is theatre.
- **Preserve original provenance.** Each moved observation records which tag it
  originally referenced. Without that the merge is unauditable and irreversible.
- **Reversible, or explicitly not** — decide, and say which in the UI.
- **Position estimates that used the old grouping** must be recomputed or
  invalidated, not left silently stale.
- **Selection UI** in the sortable tag list, as proposed: choose two or more
  tags, review the diff, confirm.
- **Tests must include the late-arrival case** — an observation recorded against
  the absorbed tag *after* the merge, arriving later, ends up on the survivor.
  That is the requirement most likely to be missed and the one that makes the
  feature trustworthy.

### Discovered Scope

- **[Found by task 11.288, 2026-09-19. A test-harness gotcha, not an app defect — recorded so the
  next task does not lose the same hours.] `pumpAndSettle()` does not wait for a `FutureProvider` to
  finish recomputing after `ref.invalidate`, when the provider already has a cached value.**
  Riverpod keeps showing the *previous* value while the new one is in flight — there is no spinner and
  nothing scheduled for a frame, so `pumpAndSettle` has nothing to wait on and returns immediately,
  even though the write the test just drove has not actually landed in what the screen renders. A
  widget test that writes, invalidates, then asserts on the very next `pumpAndSettle` can read stale
  data and pass for the wrong reason — or, worse, chase the real gap with `tester.runAsync(() =>
  Future.delayed(...))` immediately before the read and still be too early, because the delay races
  the real (non-fake-clock) database read the write itself started. **What actually closed it in
  `tag_database_screen_test.dart`: a second `runAsync(delay) + pumpAndSettle` round after the write**
  (one round is not reliably enough), and, in three of the four delete/undo cases, asserting on the
  rendered row (`tagRowContaining`) rather than re-reading the provider through `container.read` at
  all — which sidestepped a second, separate hang this same investigation hit (a `container.read` of
  the same provider, from a *second* `tester.runAsync` call issued after the widget itself had already
  settled on the correct data, would not resolve within the test, for a reason this task did not run
  down further once the UI-assertion form of the same test worked). Mixing gesture-driven callbacks
  (a `Dismissible`'s `confirmDismiss`/`onDismissed`) with this same pattern is worse still — a real
  `tester.drag` ties the gesture's own completion to its animation clock, which raced the database
  read in a way that never settled; invoking the widget's callbacks directly (found on its declared
  type via `tester.widget<Dismissible>(...)`) is the reliable way to exercise them once the picture
  above is understood.

- **[Found by task 11.288, 2026-09-19. Observed once, not reproduced in isolation — flagged rather
  than fixed or dismissed.] `position_screen_space_budget_test.dart`'s "the map keeps a clear band
  with nothing drawn over it" failed once, deep inside a full `flutter test` run (test #2041 of
  3,545), and passed cleanly every time it was run alone — both on `main` and with this task's changes
  applied. That is evidence of order-dependent state leaking between test files somewhere in the
  suite, not evidence this task's changes broke that screen: the screen and this task share no code.
  Worth a task if it recurs; nothing here points at a cause yet.**

- **[Found by task 11.264, 2026-09-16. Closed by task 11.265, 2026-09-17 — design §6b, both editors
  now offer a time on a past day where one is needed.] A handover that happened on a past day cannot
  be recorded.**
  Collar 1 came off Kea on the 10th and collar 2 went on the same day; the crew enters it on the 12th.
  *Set removed date* on collar 1 picks the 10th and offers no time (§4b: a past day gets none); *Edit
  attached date* on collar 2 writes the 10th as a bare day. Two bare days on one date overlap under
  §6a and the interlock refuses the second write with *"a tag swapped the same day needs a time on
  both"* — and nothing on a past day offers one, so the sentence names an action the person cannot
  take (the one-sentence-that-is-unrecoverable class). The only ways out misrecord a fact: date the
  removal the 9th (a day of collar 1's bearings go to nobody) or the attach the 11th (a day of collar 2's
  go to nobody). Right when written — a bare-day pair was tolerated and merely contested — and orphaned
  by 11.263 without anyone re-reading §4b's confirmation. **Number: unknown.** Michael has said a
  same-day swap will *"likely never happen"*; a same-day swap entered late is rarer still, and there is
  no query on his device that could count how many were wanted and not entered. The cheap shape: offer
  *Set a time* on a past day too, with no prefill (a time for a day nobody is standing in is typed, not
  accepted), and let *Edit attached date* keep or set one the same way. One task; owner: planning
  session.

- **[Found by task 11.264, 2026-09-16. Measured in two zones; NOT fixed — the column is not this
  sweep's.] The server refuses a hand-picked swap time that lands on UTC midnight, and the price on
  `DeploymentInterlock`'s doc comment is understated.** `deploymentEndHasTime` reads a bare day as "sits
  at local midnight"; the server's local is UTC. A swap hand-picked at **17:00 in Arizona, or noon in
  New Zealand (NZST)**, is 00:00Z, reads on the server as a bare UTC day, widens to the whole of it,
  overlaps the incoming collar's start and is refused on push — measured: the same pair is accepted
  under `TZ=America/Phoenix` and refused under `TZ=UTC`. The doc says *one minute in 1 440*; hand-picked
  times cluster on whole hours, and for a whole-hour pick it is **one in 24** in any whole-hour-offset
  zone. The device then holds the row as `invalid` with no refusal code and no sentence (11.263 chose
  that on purpose — the server may not send prose), so the person sees a held row and a swap that
  never syncs. Two fixes, both bigger than a line: the nullable instant column §4 already names (wire,
  server schema, shared interlock — a schema minor at least), or **the server reading every end as an
  instant** — narrower than the device, never wider, exact for every overlap that does not turn on the
  sentinel, and it already gives up the same-day bare-day pair for any device not in UTC. The second is
  one flag on `DeploymentInterlock.overlaps` plus tests and loses nothing the server catches today.
  Owner: planning session, to choose.

- **[Found by task 11.265, 2026-09-17. Measured, reproduces every run right now; NOT fixed — outside
  this task's scope.] `animals_screen_test.dart`'s "re-picking the same attached day keeps the swap
  time" test (task 11.264) currently fails, on `main`, with no code from task 11.265 in the tree** —
  confirmed by stashing every file this task touched and running the test unmodified. `sameDay` is
  computed as `deploymentDateFor(attached).isAtSameMomentAs(day)` where `attached` is the row's own
  swap instant and `day` is what `showDatePicker` returns for the *same, untouched* pre-filled date;
  the assertion that follows treats the write as unchanged and is currently false. The count-before-
  deciding rule applies here too: **the deterministic reproduction is the finding — not a guess at the
  mechanism.** Not something a wall-clock-relative fixture like `seedSwappedPair`'s `DateTime.now()
  .subtract(2 hours)` should be able to do to `deploymentDateFor`'s own day-only comparison, which is
  exactly why it is worth a task rather than a local patch. Owner: planning session, to assign.

- **[Found by task 11.56, 2026-09-16. For the planning session — a matrix row, not a decision.]
  `PERMISSIONS_MATRIX.md` §3 "Projects" and §4.1 have no row for starting a season from a
  project.** The operation exists now (*Start next season* on a project's ⋮ menu). Its answer is
  P1's: **anybody holding the project may do it**, whatever their standing on it, because it reads
  what §4.21.4 already lets every role read and writes only into a new project the person creates
  and owns; the source is not touched and the server is not involved. The menu item is offered to
  every row for that reason — a pre-check stricter than the write would hide a capability the
  person has (task 11.126's invariant). Recorded here rather than written into the matrix because
  that table is the planning session's and ***hand-kept***.

- **[Found by task 11.56, 2026-09-16. Measured on the fixture, not on a phone; NOT fixed — out of
  the task's scope.] Removing a tag from a project, or deleting an animal, leaves that thing's
  `Deployments` rows live.** `TagRepository.removeFromProject` and `IndividualRepository.remove`
  each tombstone one row and touch no link. A season clone skips such a link (it has no end to
  re-point) and the screen says how many it skipped; on the source project the question is what
  the Log's animal filter, the Map's colour and "Marie's collars" do with a live link whose collar

- **[Found by task 11.56, 2026-09-16. A risk Michael carries until he acts, not a defect.] A v17
  server stores only the columns it declares, so it drops a v18 device's `Projects.lineage_id`
  and `copied_at` on the way through** — `SyncService._insert` writes `spec.columns` and nothing
  else; the client-side preservation floor (`UnknownColumnStore`) has no counterpart on the server.
  A season published to the beta server before it is redeployed at v18 is stored there with no
  lineage, and every *other* device pulls it that way — correct in every other way, but an export
  from a teammate's phone, or a restore from the server's backup, no longer says the two seasons are
  one study. (The device that made the season keeps its own value: the merger patches only the
  columns a pulled row carries, and a v17 server's row carries neither.) **Redeploy the server
  before the first real clone is published.** After that, an un-updated phone pushing the row with the
  column absent does the same thing for the same reason, and that is the ordinary cost of a minor
  the freeze already accepts.

- **[Michael, 2026-09-15, while re-checking task 11.247 after the two same-day fixes below. NOT
  FIXED — Michael asked that this be handed to a fresh task, run by Opus or Fable given how deep
  it reaches, rather than patched further in this session. This entry is that hand-off.] A
  same-day handover — the ordinary case §5a and §6 were built for — silently misattributes
  bearings taken earlier the same day to the wrong animal, or to no animal at all. This is not
  new: it has been live since task 11.243/11.244 shipped, and it affects the Log's animal filter,
  the Map's animal filter, and the Map's ray/estimate/tag-location colour and legend — four
  features, one shared root cause, none of them touched today except to surface it.**
  **What Michael saw, and it is an exact, reproduced match.** Animal A is yellow, animal B is red.
  Tag 1 on A, tag 2 on B, one bearing recorded on each. Tag 2 is then moved from B to A — the
  ordinary same-day recapture. Afterward on the Map: **the bearing that was always A's (tag 1)
  drew grey — unattributed to anyone** — and **the bearing that was genuinely B's (tag 2, recorded
  hours before it ever went anywhere near A) drew yellow, A's colour.** Both tag IDs were correct;
  only the attributed animal was wrong, in two different ways on the same screen.
  **Root cause, found and reproduced in isolation — `Deployment.covers(DateTime at)`
  (`lib/data/models/deployment.dart`) compares an *instant* against a *calendar-day* boundary the
  wrong way round for same-day removals.**
  - `attached_date`/`removed_date` are calendar days, always written through `deploymentDateFor`,
    which normalises to **local midnight** of the day (§4's own documented reasoning — see that
    function's doc comment).
  - `covers(at)` asks `at.isBefore(removedDate)`. When a deployment is removed **today**,
    `removedDate` is *midnight of today* — and a bearing recorded at any point during today (2pm,
    say) is **not before midnight of today; it is after it.** So `covers()` reports the deployment
    does **not** cover a bearing taken hours before the removal actually happened. This is the
    grey bearing.
  - The replacement deployment (tag 2 → A) is `attached` at that same midnight, with **no
    `removedDate` yet** — so its own `covers(at)` check has no upper bound at all, and a bearing
    from *earlier that same day*, wrongly rejected by the old deployment, is **silently absorbed by
    the new one instead**, because "no upper bound" beats "starts at midnight today" for any
    instant later that day. This is the yellow bearing.
  - **Watched in isolation**, with no UI involved: a `Deployment` removed at `DateTime.utc(2026, 9,
    15)` (midnight) reports `covers(DateTime.utc(2026, 9, 15, 14, 0))` (2pm the same day) as
    `false`; a second `Deployment` attached at that same midnight, with `removedDate: null`,
    reports `covers` on the same 2pm instant as `true`. Both watched directly — no repository, no
    screen, no fixture in between.
  - **Some callers of `covers()` are already immune, and the fix must not break why.**
    `tagIdsOnAnAnimalAt` and `_deploymentSpansDay` (`core/providers/deployments_provider.dart`) —
    what decides which collars the Record wheel offers, and which collar a "Link a tag" dialog
    treats as free — call `covers()` with an `at` that is **itself already day-normalised**
    (`deploymentDateFor(DateTime.now())`), so both sides of the comparison agree on granularity and
    the same-day case resolves correctly there (documented and tested as "removed today is still
    offered today"). **The bug is specific to `DeploymentRepository.animalForObservationIn`**,
    which is the only caller that passes a raw *instant* — `Observation.timestampUtc`,
    `EstimatedPosition.timestampLocal`, `ActualTagLocation.timestampUtc` — as `at`. A fix that
    changes `covers()` itself must re-verify every caller, not just the broken one.
  - **Every downstream feature built on `animalForObservationIn` inherits this, unchanged by
    today's other two fixes**, because both of today's fixes corrected a *different* question
    ("which animal currently owns this collar," fixed by breaking a tie on `created_at`) — neither
    touched the *time-interval* question `animalForObservationIn` answers, which has been wrong
    since it was written:
    - **The Log's animal filter** (task 11.244, `log_screen.dart`'s `_SubjectFilter.animal.admits`)
      — a same-day handover means "show me Marie" can silently drop or wrongly include a bearing on
      her handover day, on the screen that was specifically built to be the *exact* one.
    - **The Map's animal filter** (task 11.247, `map_screen.dart`'s `_visible`) — the same
      silent mis-filter, one day after it was fixed to ask this exact question.
    - **The Map's ray/estimate/tag-location colour and legend** (task 11.248, today,
      `map_screen.dart`'s `_tagColor`/`_attributionOf`) — what Michael actually saw.
  - **Reproduced end-to-end, not only in the model class**, with the real repository write path
    (`DeploymentLinking.plan`/`apply`, `DeploymentRepository.update`) and `deploymentDateFor` in
    the loop exactly as the Animal Detail screen calls them — confirms the bug survives the whole
    stack, not just the isolated boundary case.
  - **Suggested shape of a fix, offered as a starting point and not a decision**: `covers()` most
    likely needs two distinct answers depending on what `at` is — a calendar day (as
    `tagIdsOnAnAnimalAt` and `_deploymentSpansDay` already pass, correctly) versus a real instant
    (as `animalForObservationIn` passes, incorrectly). The natural fix widens the *end* of a
    same-day-removed interval to include the whole day it ends on when asked about an instant
    (e.g. compare against `removedDate` normalised to end-of-day, or compare
    `deploymentDateFor(at)` against `removedDate` the same way the day-granular callers already do)
    — but this has to be reconciled carefully against `DeploymentInterlock.overlapDays`
    (`packages/tritrack_sync`), which does its own day arithmetic on the same two columns and must
    not be silently loosened by a change made for a different caller. **This is exactly the
    algorithm-correctness class of work `CLAUDE.md`'s model-selection guidance calls out** — hence
    Michael's request that a fresh task, not this session, take it on.
  - **What a fix task needs to do, at minimum**: correct `covers()` (or add the instant-aware
    variant `animalForObservationIn` actually needs) without changing what the day-granular callers
    already get right; add a regression test **through each of the three affected call sites**
    (Log filter, Map filter, Map colour/legend), not only through `covers()` in isolation, since
    this project's own history is full of a correct derivation with a broken caller and vice versa;
    and re-open task 11.247 (below) once done, because its device check cannot mean anything until
    this is fixed underneath it.
  - **SCHEDULED 2026-09-15 as task 11.251, Opus, above the line.** That entry takes the suggested
    fix above as a starting point and **says why it is not sufficient on its own** — a closed end
    makes the handover day cover two deployments, and `animalForObservationIn` returns the first
    match in a list, so it would answer arbitrarily rather than wrongly-but-findably. **The grey
    bearing is separated out there as plain data loss with no handover involved**, and the

- **[Michael, 2026-09-15, on his device, during task 11.251's first look. NOT FIXED — a separate
  defect, handed to the planning session.] There is no way to delete a "no signal" recording from
  the Log.** A bearing has a delete; a "no signal" entry (the list of collars somebody listened for
  and did not hear) has none, so a mistaken one stays in the record. Not measured here beyond
  Michael's report; the task that takes it should say whether the entry's own screen has a delete
  either, and whether the omission was a decision (a "no signal" is evidence of absence and somebody
  may have argued it should not be deletable) or an oversight.
- **[Task 11.256, 2026-09-16. Two edges a textual derivation cannot see, and one cell nobody has
  measured. Recorded so they are known rather than discovered.]**
  **The `ref`-after-`await` guard derives its population by reading source text**, so two shapes are
  invisible to it: **a helper that stores a `Ref` and uses it later**, and **a provider read through
  an alias or a variable** rather than by its own name. Exemptions live in a map with a reason per
  entry, checked in both directions — a condemned member needs one, and an entry whose member is no
  longer condemned fails. **When somebody finds an instance by hand, check it against these two
  edges before assuming the guard is wrong.**
  **And one cell of the table is unmeasured:** an auto-disposing provider read **bare** *and*
  invalidated **mid-build**. `ArrivalRefresh.settleFirst`'s comment says it throws *"disposed during
  loading state"*; 11.256 measured every neighbouring cell and left this one to that sentence.
  **Not a task unless somebody meets it** — recorded so that whoever does knows it was a gap on
  purpose rather than an oversight.

- **[Planning session, 2026-09-16, resolving task 11.236. Not a defect — a trigger with no reader,
  which is this project's own defect class pointed at itself.] "Revisit a guard only if a fifth
  instance appears" cannot fire, because nobody counts.**
  The decision not to build a repository-wide guard is right and measured: task 11.235 found that a
  guard on the body shape alone would fire on **eleven** providers, **seven of which work today** —
  an instrument that cries wolf about real code is one people learn to silence, which is how this
  project lost `clippedTexts` to five test files. **The trigger attached to that decision is the
  problem.** The population is **four** — three fixed by 11.236, plus `_ensureOwnerMembership`'s
  three callers from 11.235 counted as one — it is held by hand, it is spread across two Done task
  entries, and **`CLAUDE.md` already says a trigger nobody is looking for is not a trigger.**
  **What would give it a reader, and it is the "trip-wire, not a note" rule this project already
  has:** one named place — beside `no_ref_after_await_task_11_236_test.dart` is the obvious one —
  that states the count, lists the four, and **carries the grep that finds candidates**, so a fifth
  is something a person can discover rather than something they must happen to remember.
  **Deliberately not a task today:** the population is four and the cost of being wrong is a button
  that lies, not a lost record. **It becomes one the moment anybody finds a fifth by accident** —
  which is the same trigger, now with somewhere to land.

- **[Task 11.255, 2026-09-15. Not a defect — a shape to watch, recorded because the next person to
  touch that loop will not otherwise have the context.] The server's "shared tables" cross-author
  loop now carries two owner-only exception sets, and a third would not fit.**
  `permissions_matrix_test.dart` reads both out of `RowAuthorizer`'s source rather than listing
  them: `_tablesNamedByTagLifecycle` (owner owns **every** change) and
  `_tablesNamedByIndividualLifecycle` (owner owns **only the tombstone**). Two shapes fit the loop's
  `changeRefused` / `deleteRefused` pair exactly. **A third partial rung — some other split of
  create/edit/delete — would not**, and the wrong move at that moment is to bolt on a third boolean.
  **Widen the pair into something that names which operations a rung owns**, or the loop becomes a
  list of special cases, which is what deriving it from source was for.

- **[Task 11.252, 2026-09-15. Found while deriving the surface; not fixed, and it is the larger of
  that task's two findings.] A "no signal" record can now be deleted and still cannot be opened.**
  Before 11.252 a non-detection could not be reached from anywhere — the Log's row was a bare
  `ListTile` with no tap, and the Map's marker carries a comment saying it is deliberately not a
  control. **There is still no detail screen for one.** So the app now offers to destroy a record
  that a person cannot read first, which is an odd shape however defensible each half is on its
  own: a bearing can be opened and deleted; a "no signal" can only be deleted. **The next task
  touching non-detections should decide whether that is right rather than inherit it**, and should
  start by asking whether the absence of a detail screen was itself a decision — the same question
  11.252 was given, which turned out to have the answer "nobody ever decided".

- **[Task 11.251, 2026-09-15. Not fixed — recorded so the next person meets it as a known cost
  rather than a defect.] A date-only deployment end is recognised by sitting at local midnight, so
  a row written in one time zone reads as a *timed* end in another.** Design §4a's rule 2 stores a
  swap time in the same `attached_date`/`removed_date` columns a bare day lives in, and
  `deploymentEndHasTime` tells them apart by asking whether the value is at this device's midnight.
  In one zone that is exact. Across zones it is the second face of the cost §4 already records
  (*"the same row renders as the neighbouring day on a device in another timezone"*): a New Zealand
  crew's date-only removal on the 9th is 05:00 on the 8th in Arizona, so an Arizona device reads it
  as "removed at 5 a.m. on the 8th" and attributes the New Zealand 9th's bearings to nobody, where the
  New Zealand device attributes them to the animal. **Nobody has a project spanning zones today; the
  trigger is the first one that does**, and the fix on that day is the nullable instant column §4a
  named as the alternative (or an offset column beside each date) — not a cleverer sentinel.
- **[Task 11.251, 2026-09-15. Decided, not a gap.] Correcting an attached date through *Edit
  attached date* writes the picked day at midnight and so drops any swap time the row carried** —
  including when the same day is re-picked. A time recorded for one day says nothing about another,
  and a person fixing a date has said the row was wrong; the consequence of re-picking the same day
  is that the day becomes *contested* against a same-day neighbour rather than misattributed, which
  is §4a's floor. Written on `_setAttached`. If Michael finds he corrects same-day rows often enough
  to want the time kept, that is a small follow-up, not a redesign.
- **[Task 11.251, 2026-09-15.] `latestAnimalByTag` in `deployments_provider.dart` was deleted.** It
  had no reader anywhere in `lib/` or `test/`, and it carried the exact tie-break defect task 11.247
  fixed in its two siblings (`latestAnimalForTag` and the SQL join): "last row wins" over a list
  ordered by `attached_date` then `deployment_id`, which on a same-day reassignment is a random UUID.
  A fifth derivation with no caller is a copy waiting to be called; it is gone rather than fixed.
- **[Task 11.251, 2026-09-15. A pre-check widened to match the write — recorded because it reads
  like a loosening.] The "Link a tag" picker now offers a collar whose deployment ends *tomorrow*.**
  It used to hide it; the interlock has always permitted it (a one-day overlap is §6's allowance for
  the person recording a swap a day late). The picker asks `DeploymentInterlock.overlapDays` directly
  now rather than keeping a third notion of "busy", so it cannot be stricter than the write again —
  and `CLAUDE.md`'s rule is that a pre-check may be more permissive than the write, never less.
- **[Task 11.251, 2026-09-15. The finding underneath the finding, named as the plan asked.] Task
  11.249 routed around `Deployment.covers` rather than filing it.** Its comms entry said it used its
  own day function *"deliberately not `Deployment.covers`, which is half-open and would drop the
  collar taken off this morning"* — a correct diagnosis of the defect this task fixed, written as a
  design note about the new function. `covers` stayed live in the Log's filter, the Map's filter and
  the Map's colour and legend for five days and two further sessions. `CLAUDE.md`'s rule *"a
  workaround in a test is a defect nobody filed"* has been widened there to cover shipped code: when
  you route around a function because it is wrong, say so in the "For the planning session" list in
  those words.
- **[Michael, 2026-09-14, while checking task 11.247 on his device. Found and fixed the same day —
  see below.] A same-day tag reassignment named the wrong animal, everywhere that animal's name is
  read through a tag — not only the Record screen's wheel.** Michael's report: he set a removed
  date on a tag under one animal and linked it to a second, both the same day. The second animal's
  screen correctly showed the tag as current; the first animal's screen correctly showed it as no
  longer current; **and the Record screen's wheel, the Map's legend, and every other reader of
  `Tag.individualName` still named the first animal** — because force-closing the app did not fix
  it, this was never a refresh problem. First investigated as a live-refresh question (a widget
  check of `refreshTagViews`/`refreshTagViewsIn` came back clean, and a real-tap UI reproduction hit
  an unrelated test-harness hang) — that framing was wrong, and the corrected framing is below.
  **Root cause: `TagRepository`'s join named "the animal of a collar's most recent deployment" by
  `MAX(attached_date)` with a SQLite bare column, relying on a documented SQLite guarantee that
  applies only when there is no tie.** A same-day reassignment — set a removed date on one
  deployment, link a new one, both dated today — ties two deployments on `attached_date`, and which
  row's `individual_id` SQLite hands back for a tie is unspecified. Reproduced deterministically in
  an in-memory database: the tie was always broken toward the *older* deployment, i.e. exactly
  Michael's symptom. `DeploymentRepository.latestAnimalForTag`, the Dart-side twin of the same
  question, had the identical defect one layer down — it walked deployments in
  `attached_date`-ascending order and let the last one win, so a tie was broken by `deployment_id` (a
  random UUID), not by which write actually happened later.
  **Fixed both, watched red first.** `_tagRows`'s subquery is now a correlated `NOT EXISTS`
  "greatest-n-per-group" query, tie-broken by `created_at` (a real instant) and then
  `deployment_id` as a last resort — no window function, because `schema.dart`'s v4 migration
  already documents that a runtime query cannot assume `ROW_NUMBER()` is available on every
  bundled SQLite. `latestAnimalForTag` now compares `(attachedDate, createdAt)` explicitly instead
  of relying on row order. `test/data/individuals_test.dart` reproduces Michael's exact sequence —
  a removed date and a same-day relink — and was confirmed to fail against the pre-fix code before
  the fix was restored. Full suite: 3277 passed, 0 failed, 15 skipped.
  **The class this belongs to, for the next person who meets a tied date:** a bare column pinned to
  an aggregate is only as precise as the aggregate's own tie-breaking, and a calendar-day column
  (`attached_date`) ties far more often than an instant does — the fix generalises to "prefer the
  real timestamp over the day whenever the day can tie."

- **[Task 11.245, 2026-09-14 — confirms and adds to task 11.250's same-day finding, does not
  duplicate it.] `check_app_quotes` is red on `website/content/docs/managing-your-tags.md` for
  four reasons, not the one task 11.250 already reported.** 11.250 flagged that page quoting "One
  of your projects uses this collar" (now `_copyProvenance` in `widgets/tag_form.dart`, changed by
  that task). **Task 11.245 adds three more on the same page, all caused by its own wording
  changes**: "Tag Database Management" (now "Tag Library"), "+ New tag" (removed — a project's own

- **[Found by task 11.244, 2026-09-14. A real asymmetry, left deliberately, for the planning session
  to scope.] The Log's animal filter is exact and the Map's is not.** 11.244 wired design §7's
  derivation into the Log: filtering by Marie now asks *which animal was this bearing about* of each
  row, by its own timestamp, so a bearing taken on her old collar **after it came off** is no longer
  hers. **The Map still filters by collar set** — its per-animal checkbox is a tristate over legend
  rows, and a legend row is a collar. So the same project answers "show me Marie" two different ways
  on two screens. **Neither is wrong for what it is**: the Log filters records, the Map toggles
  layers. But a person will notice, and the honest fix is per-ray filtering on the map, which is a
  task rather than a line. Recorded rather than done, because it is a rendering change and this
  project's rule is to ship one of those at a time and stop for a device look.

- **[Found by task 11.244, 2026-09-14. Small, and it is a column not a control.]
  `Tag_Library.color_hex` is written and read by nothing.** The swatch and the Color section came
  off that screen (see 11.244's §5), so the column keeps whatever value a row already had and
  nothing looks at it. **It is device-local and off the wire**, so dropping it costs no major bump
  and no migration on anybody's server — it is a `Tag_Library` rebuild in a future schema version,
  whenever somebody is in that table anyway. Left because a column nobody reads is cheaper than a
  migration nobody needs.

- **[Found by task 11.244, 2026-09-14. A timezone edge nobody has met, stated because the next
  person to meet it will think it is a bug.] A deployment date is one instant and carries no
  offset.** `Observations` has the local/UTC/offset triple precisely because a bearing is a
  measurement taken somewhere; `Deployments.attached_date` is a date somebody typed, so 11.243 gave
  it one column. 11.244 pins it to **local midnight** (`deploymentDateFor`), which keeps the first
  morning's bearings inside the deployment — the failure UTC midnight would cause in New Zealand.
  **What is left is that the same row renders the neighbouring date on a device in another zone.**
  That matters to a team split across zones and to nobody else today. The fix, if it is ever wanted,
  is an offset column beside it, which is additive and needs no major bump.

- **[Found by task 11.243, 2026-09-13. A live defect in the archive reader, fixed in the same
  task because it broke an existing test.] A migration step that decides whether it has run by
  reading a value a *later* step deletes is a step that runs twice.**
  `SchemaMigrator.backfillIndividuals` (v16) wrote `Tags.individual_id` and read it back to know
  it had already run. Schema v17 takes that column off — three versions later, in different code —
  so a payload migrated twice ran the v16 step again, saw no link, and minted a **second
  `Individuals` row under the same key**; the merge then died on a UNIQUE violation and took the
  whole import with it. A payload *is* migrated twice on the ordinary path: the merger migrates
  what a caller may already have migrated, which is exactly what `forked_collar_archive_test`
  does, and that test going red is what found it. The step now asks *"is the row already there"*,
  which is the question that was always meant. **The reusable shape: a step's idempotence test
  must not depend on a column surviving a migration written after it.**

- **[Found by task 11.243, 2026-09-13. A live defect in the server migration, found by a test on a
  populated database and fixed there.] Deferred foreign keys make `DELETE` and
  `ALTER TABLE ... DROP COLUMN` incompatible in one transaction.** Every constraint in the server
  schema is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED`, for a reason that has nothing to do with migrations —
  a sync push arrives as a batch whose rows reference each other. The consequence is that after a
  `DELETE`, Postgres holds an unfired trigger event per affected row, and an `ALTER TABLE` on that
  table fails with *"cannot ALTER TABLE because it has pending trigger events"*. Schema v17 does
  both. Fixed with `SET CONSTRAINTS ALL IMMEDIATE` between the two halves. **Every statement was
  individually correct and only their combination was not**, which is precisely what a migration
  test on an *empty* database cannot see — the wipe group in
  `postgres_migration_upgrade_test.dart` runs on a populated one for that reason. **Any future
  migration that deletes rows and then alters a column needs the same line.**

- **[Found by task 11.243, 2026-09-13. Small, for task 11.244 or whoever next touches the export
  screen.] `TagLibraryEntry.color_hex` is now read by nothing at all.** Task 11.241 kept it as the
  *seed* for the animal a copy-into-project would create; 11.243 stopped creating that animal, so
  the seed has nowhere to land and a copied collar draws the neutral constant until somebody links
  it. The column is harmless and the swatch on the Tag Database screen still renders it, so a
  person sees a colour that means nothing. **Either 11.244's linking screen offers it as the new
  animal's starting colour — which is what it was for — or the swatch comes off that screen.**
  Recorded rather than decided, because it is a screen call.

- **[Found by task 11.243, 2026-09-13. For the planning session — a task entry, not a decision.]
  `Deployments` is not on the season-clone path yet.** Design §4 says a clone (task 11.56) copies
  deployments and re-points both ends at the new project's rows. 11.56 is deferred and its entry
  predates this table, so **it needs a line adding** or the first clone will produce a project with
  collars and animals and nothing joining them — which reads as "no collar was ever on anything".

- **[Found by task 11.230, 2026-09-12. Measured, not suspected. Fixed in that task because it
  blocked its own test and is one line on a screen it was already changing.] The Offline Data
  Map's download sheet could kill the app before a person confirmed anything.** Its "≈ N tiles"
  line called `GeoPolygon.tilesInPolygon(...).length` — building a `TileXY` for every tile in the
  selection at every zoom in order to count them. Task 11.103 fixed exactly this in the selection
  readout and wrote that *"the only caller of the list form is the downloader, which is bounded by
  a polygon a person has confirmed"*; **that sentence was wrong in both halves** — the sheet was a
  second caller and it opens before the confirmation. At the whole-planet framing (no fix, no
  project extent) a "New selection" box is a third of the Earth, and the first widget test to open
  the sheet died asking for **2,147,483,664 bytes**. Now the bounded estimator over the bounding
  box, as the readout already was; exact for a rectangle, high for any other shape. **Lesson for the
  file: a claim that "the only caller is X" is a grep somebody did not run** — and 11.103's own
  report said it had swept the callers.

- **[Found by task 11.230, 2026-09-12. Read, not measured; needs the planning session's decision.]
  The map's Erase tool still deletes by drawn polygon with no neighbour check, and its
  confirmation does not say so.** `_eraseSelection` on the Offline Data Map removes every tile and
  DEM file whose centre is inside the shape a person drew, whether or not a saved area still
  covers it, and says *"Removes downloaded map tiles and elevation data whose coverage falls
  inside this selection. This can be re-downloaded later."* **Deliberately left as it is by
  11.230**, because its brief was the per-area delete and this tool is a different contract — the
  person chose the shape, not an area — and a tool that erases "everything under here" has a use
  the area delete does not (pan-cache tiles no area owns). **But the sentence should say what will
  happen to a saved area it crosses** (that area drops to Partial, and getting it back needs a
  connection), and the planning session may prefer the tool to refuse or to warn per area. Two
  cheap options: name the areas the shape crosses in the confirmation, using the same
  `sharedWithPhrase` the area delete uses; or subtract saved areas the way `deleteRegion` does and
  say "kept N tiles other areas cover". One decision, one small task.

- **[Found by task 11.230, 2026-09-12, by a test passing for the wrong reason. Read and then
  measured. Low stakes today; worth one line in a future task.] `TileSources.byId` answers any
  unknown id with OpenStreetMap, so a manifest entry carrying a retired source id deletes nothing
  and reports success.** 11.230's first fixture used `'osm'` as a source id; the old delete looked
  up `'osm'`, got OpenStreetMap, and deleted under `tiles/osm_standard/` while the files sat under
  `tiles/osm/` — the neighbour "survived" because nothing at all was deleted. The new delete does
  not go through `byId` (it deletes by the region's own `sourceId` string), so the fix is not
  exposed to this; but the download path (`_runTiles`) still is, and a source renamed or removed
  in a later build would make every area recorded under the old id re-download under the new one
  while its old files stay on disk forever, uncounted and unfreeable except by "Delete all". A
  `byId` that throws, or a manifest check that flags an unknown source, closes it.

- **[Found by task 11.230, 2026-09-12. Read, not measured.] Elevation coverage and elevation
  erase use two different rules for "inside".** `DemTileStore.tilesIntersectingPolygon` (what an
  area is credited with, and what the download fetches) counts a 0.1° tile if it *touches* the
  polygon; `deleteTilesInPolygon` (the Erase tool) removes a tile only if its *centre* is inside.
  So drawing the exact shape of a saved elevation area and erasing it leaves the area's edge tiles
  on disk and the area reads Partial rather than gone. The per-area delete is consistent with
  coverage (it deletes the intersecting set, less neighbours); only the Erase tool has the
  mismatch. Same small task as the Erase item above.

  (`docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f docker-compose.e2e.yml config`, and the same for
  `docker-compose.dev-lan.yml`) and finding the volume absent from both.** Both files' comments beside
  the override say "the base `server` service declares no `volumes:` today" — true when task 10.47
  wrote the comment, false since task 11.129 added the base volume two weeks later. Neither comment
  was updated. **Lower stakes than the TLS file**: these are ephemeral test/dev stacks, not the
  deployment holding a field season, so a degradation record dying with the container costs a lost
  audit trail during a throwaway run rather than during real use. **Not fixed** — task 11.223's brief
  was the TLS file and the guard; this is the sweep's finding, reported rather than acted on. If a task
  is wanted: add `tritrack_server_state:/var/lib/tritrack` to each file's `volumes: !override` list and
  correct the now-stale comment, the same one-line-plus-comment shape as 11.223's own fix.

- **[Found by task 11.203, 2026-09-09. Measured, not suspected. Needs Michael's decision.] The

  That is a real fact about what a person sees on the map now, not only a fact about the test: the

- **[Found by task 11.197, 2026-09-07. Observed twice, cause unknown. The content lane's, not a

- **[Found by task 11.197, 2026-09-07. Suspected, not measured. Needs a task only if it is real.]

- **[Found and DONE by an ad hoc code session, 2026-09-06, at Michael's direct request, in commits
  `4b2e770` and `3e46c2c`. **It has a number now: task 11.181**, which was opened to document the

  entry are the same record; where they could disagree, **11.181 is the one that was written with
  the code open.**] The tag list row is now one line, and a viewer can read a tag at last.** Michael: *"The special notes (ie view only) should move to the tag details page. This will
  allow all the info on the tag database table be on one line (frequency name) which will allow the
  font size to be increased a bit for readability."* The row's second line (pulse rate, the status
  word, and task 11.138's "view only") is gone; the line is **18 logical pixels** instead of the
  `ListTile` default 16, capped at `maxLines: 1` with an ellipsis so it **cannot** wrap at any name
  length or text scale — which was Michael's own stated worry about the change. Non-active states
  are a grey line plus one of three icons (his choice between the treatments offered); the padlock
  stays and carries "view only" as a `semanticLabel`.
  **Three things in it are worth a later reader's time.**
  1. **The destination was unreachable by the audience the words were written for.** A viewer's tap
     on a locked row hit `_showEditDialog`'s `UnauthorizedMutation` handler, which showed the
     refusal and `return`ed — so the one person who could not edit a tag was also **the only person
     who could not read its pulse rate, pattern, notes, colour or date put on.** Nothing was wrong
     with the refusal: it explained itself, it was actionable, and
     `refusal_messages_rendered_test.dart` covered it. It was simply the *end* of the road, and
     that is invisible from inside a test that checks the message is correct. Michael chose to open
     it up; the refusal is now the banner of a read-only Tag details page, with the same wording and
     the same `tag_edit_not_permitted` key.
  2. **A first design split the line into a `Row` so only the name could ever be cut.** It
     overflowed by 13 logical pixels at a 2.0 text scale on a 6.1-inch phone: a non-flexible child
     cannot shrink, so it turned "might wrap", which is ugly, into "overflows", which is a
     yellow-and-black stripe. **The project's own rule caught it — a budget must be able to refuse,
     and a layout where one child is forbidden to shrink has no way to say no.**
  3. **The wrap guard needed three attempts and the first two passed with wrapping switched back on
     deliberately.** `getRect` on a `Text` walks *up* to the tile's title slot, whose height is
     identical either way; and comparing the long row against a short one fails because in
     `flutter_test`'s double-width font **both** rows wrap, so they move together. **A comparison
     between two things that fail identically is not a comparison.** What works is comparing each
     row's rendered height against its own `getMinIntrinsicHeight(10000)` — its height laid out in
     unlimited width, which is one line by construction, and needs no number anybody chose. **Point
     the next "prove this text did not wrap" task at
     `test/features/disabled_reason_geometry_test.dart` rather than letting it invent a threshold.**

- **[Found by 11.136 (2026-09-04), NOT FIXED — needs a task number if anybody wants it closed.]

- **[Found by 11.151 (2026-09-04), NOT FIXED — needs a task number if anybody wants it closed.]
  A tag link, membership or project rename that arrives on a *sync pull* refreshes nothing.**
  **11.151 fixed all eight user routes and did not fix this one**, deliberately: the mechanism that
  would have covered it — the three tag providers watching `recordingsRevisionProvider`, which
  `DataArrival` already bumps from inside the sync merger — **deadlocks.** A counter bumped during a
  provider's own build orphans that provider's in-flight `Future` and it never completes;
  `currentUserProvider` announces on `DataArrival` when it auto-creates a user, so the hazard is
  reachable on a first run and not only in tests. It turned `tag_database_screen_test.dart` from 11
  seconds green into a run that never finishes. **Anyone closing this must not simply add the watch
  back.** A safe shape is a listener that invalidates from *outside* any build.
  **What it costs a person:** a teammate links a collar and publishes; you sync; **your device shows
  the old tag list until you restart the app**, with nothing on screen saying so.
  The membership half of the same gap:
  Local membership writes are already safe: `membership_provider.dart`'s `_afterMembershipChange`
  is a single named function every local write calls, and it invalidates all six providers —
  exactly the shape 11.151 was asked to build for tags. **But the sync merger never calls it.** It
  announces on `DataArrival`, and none of `projectMembershipsProvider`, `projectOwnersProvider`,
  `isProjectOwnerProvider`, `myProjectRoleProvider`, `mayWriteProjectDataProvider` or
  `allProjectsProvider` watches that announcement. **What it costs a person:** an owner promotes
  you to contributor on their device, your device syncs, and **the Record screen still refuses
  your bearing and the Members screen still shows your old role until you restart the app** —
  with nothing on screen saying so. The same holds for a project renamed elsewhere.
  **Two reasons 11.151 did not extend to it**, and the second is the one that decides it. The
  watch-the-counter remedy is unavailable here for the deadlock reason above. And four of those six
  providers *gate controls* rather than fill a list, so re-running them on every announcement —
  including every bearing saved — has a blast radius that wants its own device check. **It wants
  its own task**, not a line appended to this one.

- **[Found by 11.61 (2026-09-03), NOT FIXED — needs a task number if anybody wants it closed.]
  A sync push whose *upload* stalls is bounded by a five-minute total on Android, Windows and
  Linux, not by inactivity.** `package:http`'s `Client` gives no portable hook into a request
  body as it drains, and `dart:io`'s `HttpClient` has no write-inactivity setting —
  `connectionTimeout` bounds only opening the socket, and `idleTimeout` is about pooled
  keep-alive sockets. **iOS and macOS do not have this gap**: `timeoutIntervalForRequest` is a
  true inactivity deadline and covers the upload half, and it is set. **The cost, stated:** on
  the three non-Apple platforms a 500-row push (617 KiB, measured) that stalls after 30 seconds
  of upload is not given up on until five minutes have passed. **The cost of closing it** is
  wrapping the finalized request stream, which means this app owning a `StreamedRequest`
  re-implementation of what `BaseClient` does — a real amount of code on the path every push
  takes, to shorten one failure by four and a half minutes on the platforms Michael does not
  use. **Recorded rather than done, so it is a decision somebody makes rather than a gap
  somebody finds.**
  **CORRECTION AND DECISION, planning session, 2026-09-03. "The platforms Michael does not use"
  is wrong: Android is one of the three, and it is one of his two test devices and will be in
  the beta.** So this gap is on a platform in use, and the sentence understates it.
  **The decision is still not to close it, for a different reason than the one given:** five
  minutes is **bounded**, not infinite — the condition this whole task existed to remove is
  already gone — and the price of the remaining four and a half minutes is **owning a
  re-implementation of `BaseClient` on the path every field record travels.** *A rewrite of the
  push path to shorten one failure is a bad trade on a project whose worst outcome is a season's
  records not arriving.* **Reopen trigger: a real Android push observed stalling mid-upload**,
  which the operator status command and the sync bar can now both show — not a code review, and
  not somebody re-reading this paragraph.
- **[Found by 11.61 (2026-09-03), NOT FIXED — probably never needs to be.] `cupertino_http`
  3.0.2 does not expose `timeoutIntervalForResource`**, only `timeoutIntervalForRequest`. The
  Dart `URLSessionConfiguration` wrapper omits it; the raw binding exists on a private field.
  So on iOS and macOS there is **no native total-resource ceiling**, and the ceiling is the
  Dart-side first-response deadline instead. That is the right instrument anyway — task 11.61's
  whole argument is against a wall-clock cap on a progressing transfer — so this is noted as a
  fact about the package rather than as something missing.
